primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

resources.title: Microsoft Scout FAQ
resources.description: What Scout is, what it can do across files, browser, shell and Microsoft 365, and how autonomous and scheduled work behaves.

resources.title: MCAPS Lobster Pound community
resources.description: Seller community sharing working Scout patterns, including account planning, customer language mining and recurring monitoring.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

primaryAgents.name: GitHub Copilot
primaryAgents.shortDescription: AI coding assistant available in an IDE, GitHub Copilot CLI, and the GitHub Copilot app. Repository or working-folder context supports code and configuration work rather than acting as a CRM source of record.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Write, explain, refactor and test code; scaffold infrastructure-as-code and deployment artifacts; build the smallest spike that proves or disproves an architecture assumption; generate sample data and validation scripts; and reproduce a reported failure so you can see it rather than describe it.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the next step is to build something rather than to plan or describe it. Validating an architecture assumption with a spike, standing up a demo or workshop environment, iterating a proof of concept, reproducing a deployment or integration failure, or packaging a reusable asset with tests and setup steps.
keyBenefits: Creates reviewable code and test evidence to validate an architecture assumption or reproduce a failure, giving technical and account teams a more concrete basis for the next decision. Human review and testing remain required.

resources.title: GitHub Copilot documentation
resources.description: Official GitHub Copilot documentation hub: getting started, IDE/CLI/app quickstarts, and core concepts.

resources.title: Where to use GitHub Copilot
resources.description: Choosing where to work with Copilot: IDE, CLI, GitHub.com, and the Copilot app, mapped to the stage of work.

resources.title: Best practices for using GitHub Copilot
resources.description: Official guidance on Copilot's strengths and limits, and choosing inline suggestions versus Copilot Chat for a given task.

resources.title: Adopting GitHub Copilot in your enterprise
resources.description: Governance and rollout guidance for adopting Copilot at scale: plans, policies, and codebase standards. Useful when the huddle conversation turns to customer-facing adoption or governance questions.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for customer, market or account research; that is Researcher. Do not use it to assemble a customer-facing document or deck; that is Cowork. Do not point it at production without the review your team already requires, and do not paste customer data into it. It works on code and configuration, not on the CRM record.
stepsToGetStarted: Choose the Copilot extension in your IDE, GitHub Copilot CLI for terminal work, or the GitHub Copilot app for coordinating agent-driven development. Open or select the relevant repository or working folder so the task has context. Start with: Explain what this deployment does, then write the smallest test that would prove the assumption I am least sure about. Review proposed commands and edits, run the relevant tests, and follow your approved environment and data-handling rules.

primaryAgents.name: Scout

primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

resources.title: Microsoft Scout FAQ

resources.title: MCAPS Lobster Pound community
resources.description: Seller community sharing working Scout patterns, including account planning, customer language mining and recurring monitoring.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

resources.title: Microsoft Scout FAQ
resources.description: What Scout is, what it can do across files, browser, shell and Microsoft 365, and how autonomous and scheduled work behaves.

resources.title: MCAPS Lobster Pound community
resources.description: Seller community sharing working Scout patterns, including account planning, customer language mining and recurring monitoring.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

resources.title: Sales Agent Capabilities Guide
resources.description: Detailed reference for Sales Agent components, capabilities, and example prompts.

resources.title: Role Hub
resources.description: Always-available hub for role guidance and enablement.

resources.title: Use Sales Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot
resources.description: Official overview and use guidance for Sales Agent.

resources.title: Sales Agent on mobile
resources.description: Announcement and prompt starters for Sales Agent on mobile, available through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app and in Teams and Outlook. Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

resources.title: Microsoft Scout FAQ
resources.description: What Scout is, what it can do across files, browser, shell and Microsoft 365, and how autonomous and scheduled work behaves.

resources.title: MCAPS Lobster Pound community
resources.description: Seller community sharing working Scout patterns, including account planning, customer language mining and recurring monitoring.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

resources.title: Microsoft Scout FAQ
resources.description: What Scout is, what it can do across files, browser, shell and Microsoft 365, and how autonomous and scheduled work behaves.

resources.title: MCAPS Lobster Pound community
resources.description: Seller community sharing working Scout patterns, including account planning, customer language mining and recurring monitoring.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Prioritize account action for this week
activities.description: Use Sales Agent and available sales context to rank accounts and name one next action for each.
activities.prompt: For [account scope], propose the ten accounts most deserving attention this week, or fewer if evidence is insufficient. For each show the priority driver, active opportunity stage, available renewal or whitespace signal, partner context and one seller action. Identify the dated source signal and missing context. Do not equate whitespace with customer demand; distinguish customer-confirmed need from a hypothesis. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: A proposed weekly account ranking with dated priority evidence, available stage/renewal/whitespace/partner context, missing inputs and one seller action per account.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE decides which account genuinely deserves attention this week. A ranking built from recorded signal cannot see a relationship about to open or close, and cannot know what is realistic in the days actually available.
activities.requiredContext: Your account list; access to opportunity, renewal and whitespace signals; partner coverage for those accounts.
activities.whyThisMatters: Prioritization is a decision about what will not get attention.

activities.name: Build or assess the account plan with approval gates
activities.description: Assess the current account plan and propose evidence-backed additions for AE review; any record change follows a separate, explicit approval gate.
activities.prompt: For [Account] / [TPID], assess the current account plan and supporting evidence I supply. Propose additive updates to priorities, stakeholders, opportunities and next actions, explaining the source behind each. Identify missing or conflicting evidence. Research a gap only in sources I am authorized to access and share and that this tool can actually reach; otherwise ask for a permitted extract or leave it open. Keep changes as drafts. Do not write to MSX, notify anyone or make a commitment unless I separately approve the exact content and action and an authorized tool is available; otherwise give me the accepted changes to apply through my usual process. Use only customer and commercial data I am authorized to access and disclose through this tool. Name unavailable sources instead of assuming access; the separate exact-action approval gates above remain required.
activities.expectedOutput: Account-plan assessment with proposed updates, evidence gaps, and explicit approval/rejection decisions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: AE approves or rejects each proposed change and confirms nothing is written or committed without review.
activities.requiredContext: The account and its TPID; the current account plan and approved supporting evidence; your authority to approve or reject an MSX write. A write requires an authorized tool or your usual manual process; no installed account-plan skill is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Open Scout; this practice does not require an installed account-plan skill.
2. Replace [Account] and [TPID] in the prompt with your details.
3. Supply the current account plan and approved evidence, then run the prompt.
4. Review the assessment, evidence gaps and proposed additions against your own knowledge.

5. Approve or reject each proposed change. If an authorized MSX write tool is available, approve its exact changes before execution; otherwise apply accepted changes yourself through the approved process.
6. Confirm no write or commitment occurred without your approval.
activities.whyThisMatters: Account planning becomes usable when it creates next actions, not just more content.

agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
agents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

activities.name: Pressure-test the account priority list
activities.description: Challenge whether your account priorities are driven by evidence or by habit and familiarity.
activities.prompt: Review my account priority list. For each of the top accounts, state the evidence behind the priority and whether it reflects a current signal or a standing assumption. Identify the account most likely to be wrongly prioritized, the account most likely to be wrongly ignored, and what would confirm either. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: A priority challenge showing evidence per account, plus the most likely over-prioritized and under-prioritized account.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE decides which account is genuinely mis-prioritized. A model sees only the signals that were recorded, and the account most often wrongly ignored is the one whose activity happens off-system.
activities.requiredContext: The prioritized account list; the source signal behind each priority; the accounts you have not touched recently.
activities.whyThisMatters: Challenge familiar account priorities before they consume a week that a better-supported account needed.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Prioritize account action for this week

activities.name: Create the account follow-through plan
activities.description: Convert the account priorities into named next actions and the rhythm that keeps them from decaying into a list.
activities.prompt: Turn the account priority list into a follow-through plan. For each top account, define the next action, the owner, the date, the signal you will check to know it worked, and the point at which you would drop the account down the list. Set a weekly rhythm for reviewing it. Work from the material I have supplied rather than looking it up, and where a piece of it is missing, name the gap instead of filling it. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: An account follow-through plan with next actions, owners, dates, verification signals, and a weekly review rhythm.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE sets the point at which an account drops down the list. That threshold is a judgment about where the AE own time is best spent, and no analysis can make it for them.
activities.requiredContext: The prioritized account list; the next action for each top account; your weekly planning rhythm.
activities.whyThisMatters: A weekly account plan needs both an accepted next action and a reason to stop prioritizing it when the signal fades.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Prioritize account action for this week

activities.name: Assess ECIF fit and investment momentum
activities.description: Explore eligible investment options for an approved opportunity and identify request or delivery risks to momentum.
activities.prompt: For [opportunity ID or TPID], inspect the investment context available to my authorized scope. Identify possible investment routes relevant to the documented customer barrier, summarize confirmed active-request or delivery status, and flag risks to opportunity momentum. Cite the source and date for retrieved facts, separate assumptions, and identify questions for the accountable ECIF owner. Do not determine eligibility, funding, approval or supplier selection. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Investment-fit summary with supported options, active-request status, risks, evidence gaps, and next human decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: AE confirms opportunity context and does not determine eligibility, approval, or funding. Route to the accountable ECIF owner.
activities.requiredContext: Approved opportunity ID or TPID and current opportunity context.
activitySteps: Tool/access: Open Sales Agent and ask for ECIF/investment help to engage ECIF Agent; do not assume automatic routing. Run the existing prompt with authorized inputs. If lookup is unavailable, use approved supplied evidence and flag gaps. Draft/analyze only: no eligibility determination, approval, supplier selection, record changes, or submission. Human review/submission remains outside the huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: Investment is useful only when it removes a real account or opportunity barrier.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Account planning fails when it becomes an inventory. Focus on a short operating plan that helps you decide where attention goes this week.
keyTalkingPoints: Prioritization requires saying no. AI can assemble customer, pipeline, renewal, whitespace, partner, and investment signals. You decide which account deserves action and why.
discussionQuestions: Which accounts get your attention by habit rather than evidence? Where is the account plan missing a decision? What signal would change your priority list?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Prioritize account action for this week'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from account list discussion to one AE selecting a top account and naming the next action. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Pressure-test the account priority list', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Prioritization improves when account signals change where you spend attention, not when the list grows. Separate supported priorities from assumptions before choosing the next account action. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one territory or account list and one account where the next action is unclear. For the account-plan practice, also bring its TPID, current account plan and approved supporting evidence to supply to Scout.
facilitatorQuestions: Which account deserves attention that it is not getting? Which account gets attention mostly by habit? What evidence would change your top three?
How does another AE distinguish evidence-led priority from an account that gets attention by habit?
listenFor: Planning as annual documentation, prioritization by revenue alone, unclear next actions, missing role coverage, and customer priorities not connected to pipeline.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a three-account priority table: dated signal, customer priority, role gap, next action and AE judgment. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed your priority or plan, and which assumption needs checking before the next action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, use AI to build or refine one account priority view, then choose one next action you will actually take. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share one priority you checked and whether it clarified the next action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

secondaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
secondaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

secondaryAgents.name: Sales Home
secondaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
secondaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.prompt: For [account/opportunity scope], check material changes, missing next steps, stale recorded engagement and new risk. For each item show the dated source signal, what cannot be established and one proposed seller action. First run this once, read-only, against the small named scope I supply. Use only sources I am authorized to access and disclose that are actually available to this tool; ask for a permitted extract or mark unavailable sources as gaps. Do not create a schedule until I have reviewed the first result and explicitly approved the exact scope, sources, cadence, output location and human reviewer. activitySteps: 1. Confirm the small named scope and sources this tool can actually access, or supply permitted extracts.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on restoring trust in the pipeline signal before it becomes a forecast argument.
keyTalkingPoints: Bad data creates bad inspection. Stage, close date, next step, customer engagement, and partner attach should reflect reality. AI can flag issues; you verify and decide the correction.
discussionQuestions: Where does your pipeline data most often mislead you? Which field do you trust least? Which opportunity would you hesitate to defend in a review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Ask what the certified business data says'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the individual records the check surfaced to the aggregate gap they add up to, then decide which correction would change the forecast conversation. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Tell the applied fixes apart from the ones waiting on you', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Pipeline trust comes from checking material signals and routing corrections to the record owner. An AI explanation is a hypothesis, not a verified stage or forecast change. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring the scope you normally inspect for pipeline reviews and one opportunity you suspect may be stale or misrepresented.
facilitatorQuestions: Which opportunity would you not want inspected right now? What field, date, or next step might be telling the wrong story? What correction would change the forecast conversation?
What recurring inspection check has a peer used to catch a misleading date or next step before the review?
listenFor: Manual reconciliation, stale dates, close-date optimism, missing customer engagement, and records corrected only right before reviews.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one pipeline record check: field/date, stated definition, supporting evidence, discrepancy, correction owner and verification gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did inspection reveal about the pipeline or forecast story, and which correction or caveat changes the decision?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, run one pipeline signal-quality check and correct or flag one material issue. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share the type of issue verified, corrected or routed and whether it reduced a misleading pipeline signal. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. activities.prompt: Review the outreach I have sent over the last 30 days and identify every message where I asked for something - a meeting, an introduction, a decision, or information - and did not receive a substantive reply. Do not send anything. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.

activities.humanCheckpoint: SSP reviews and edits every draft before sending, and removes any follow-up where the silence is itself the answer.
activities.requiredContext: Access to your sent messages; your current lead and opportunity list; your team's follow-up cadence norms.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the check can see your sent messages for the last 30 days.
2. Run the prompt.
3. Review the ranked list and remove any thread where the silence is itself the answer.
4. Edit every drafted follow-up so it adds a new reason to reply rather than repeating the ask.
5. Send them yourself; do not let the check send on your behalf.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most lost specialist opportunities are not rejected - they are dropped. The follow-up that would have converted was never sent because it was never surfaced.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Lead and account signals are noisy. Focus on turning them into a focused follow-up plan.
keyTalkingPoints: Qualification is evidence work. Solution relevance, owner, message, consent, and next action must be explicit.
discussionQuestions: Which lead or signal deserves attention first? What evidence makes it real? Who owns the next action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build a prioritized lead follow-up plan'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from noisy signals to one prioritized follow-up plan. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Close the loop on outreach that never got an answer', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Lead prioritization matters when credible demand leads to appropriate, consent-aware follow-up. Activity or a high AI ranking alone does not establish customer intent. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one lead or account signal, dated qualification evidence and the proposed follow-up owner. Confirm tool access and review the prior commitment and evidence.
facilitatorQuestions: Which lead has the strongest dated evidence of solution relevance, and what is only inferred? Who owns the first follow-up? How does a peer distinguish a buying signal from marketing activity before outreach?
listenFor: Undifferentiated lead lists, vague ownership, weak message fit, and missing consent/context.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a three-lead ranking: dated solution signal, customer relevance, missing context/permission, follow-up owner and next question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which signal warrants a customer action rather than just a new record, and what evidence would disprove the opportunity?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, turn your top-priority lead into an actual first contact this week. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized lead signal and whether the reviewed follow-up clarified interest or avoided a poor contact; no sent message is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

secondaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent

activities.name: Prepare the CxO technical briefing
activities.description: Build an account-grounded executive technical briefing.
activities.prompt: Prepare a CxO technical briefing for the account on the topic. Include customer outcomes, architecture direction, risks, proof points, executive talking points, likely questions, and the technical ask. State what this executive is personally backing if they say yes, and what it costs them if it goes wrong; where you have no source for that, say so and name who could tell me rather than inferring it. Present the realistic options side by side with their tradeoffs rather than one recommended path, and name the decision they are being asked to make. Where Microsoft support mechanisms apply, such as Innovation Hubs, FastTrack, Unified Support, partner capacity or ECIF, name them and cite the source for eligibility. Cite source signals where available and flag unsupported claims. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: CxO technical briefing with risks, proof points, talking points, the options and their tradeoffs, the named decision, and the Microsoft support mechanisms that apply.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The ATS owns the technical ask. A narrative can build a compelling case toward a request the customer has no mechanism to approve, and that is discovered in the room. The ATS also confirms every support mechanism named is one this account can access, because an offer of help the customer turns out not to qualify for is difficult to walk back.
activities.requiredContext: Account; topic; desired decision; available MSX and customer context; which Microsoft support mechanisms this account is eligible for and where that eligibility is recorded.
activities.whyThisMatters: The executive technical narrative needs enough evidence to be credible and enough focus to drive a decision.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on assembling an executive technical customer narrative.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is an executive-ready technical narrative with sourced claims, proof points, decision questions, and a technical ask. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: When did an executive last stop you to ask what something meant?
Which part of your technical story do you find hardest to say without jargon?
What is this executive personally putting at risk by backing your recommendation?
What decision do you actually need from the executive, and have you ever asked for it directly?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Translate architecture into business value'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the technical story to the one decision you want the executive to make, and the proof they need to make it. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Executive technical narratives translate options into customer consequences and an explicit decision. Preserve the difficult trade-off instead of hiding it behind technical detail. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming executive conversation, the desired decision, approved technical proof points and the claims that need validation. Confirm access to the named tools and review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Read your opening line aloud. Would a CFO know what you meant?
Which claim in your narrative rests on a proof point you do not have?
What are you asking the executive to decide, stated in one sentence?
How would another ATS translate your strongest technical claim without losing its caveat?
listenFor: Architecture described rather than translated, value asserted without evidence, narratives that end without an ask, and jargon that survived because nobody in the room questioned it. Also note a narrative aimed at the technical stakeholder while claiming to target the executive.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one executive technical narrative: business decision, technical option, sourced proof, caveat and one-sentence ask. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which technical trade-off became clearer in customer terms, and what proof does the executive still need?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, rewrite one technical narrative for an executive audience, state the single decision you are asking for, and give them the options with their tradeoffs. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized trade-off made clearer and whether a reviewer better understood the executive decision. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Architecture validation works best when options, criteria, assumptions, and risks are visible before the technical debate starts.
keyTalkingPoints: Compare options against the agreed decision criteria.
Name the assumptions and validation steps, not just the recommended design.
Use AI to assemble evidence and decision records while keeping architecture judgment human.
discussionQuestions: Which architecture assumption would hurt most if wrong?
What criteria will decide between options?
What validation step should happen before the customer sees the recommendation?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Compare architecture options against decision criteria'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from option comparison to creating the architecture decision record. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate architecture evidence and assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Architecture recommendations should be tested against customer criteria and the limiting constraint. A generated design remains a proposal until validation supports it. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one architecture decision, relevant customer criteria, approved technical sources, and known constraints.
facilitatorQuestions: Which option should be compared, and against what criteria?
Which assumption needs validation first?
What would make the architecture recommendation unsafe to share?
Which architecture assumption would another SE ask you to test before sharing the recommendation?
listenFor: Unchallenged assumptions, uncited guidance, missing security or operations review, and options that are not tied to criteria.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a two-option architecture record: supplied criterion, known constraint, untested assumption, evidence gap, reviewer and deferred choice. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What technical assumption did the practice test, and which proof or human decision is needed before advancing?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, design one solution and name the constraint that most limits it. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized architecture assumption checked and whether it changed the recommendation or next validation. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. activities.description: Prioritize commercial risks from approved evidence, test assumptions, and identify escalation needs; return risk rationale, evidence gaps, and the next decision/handoff.
activities.prompt: Review the approved commercial, renewal, agreement, and deal signals for the current scope. Identify the top commercial risks, the supporting source signal, likely impact, recommended intervention, owner, escalation need, and any unavailable or stale data. Identify filters, unavailable dimensions and source limits; do not invent customer causes, intent or approvals the report cannot establish. Return analysis only, not record changes or commitments. Do not invent a blocker, owner, policy requirement or stakeholder judgment outside this report's data. Mark those questions for the accountable role to verify using separate permitted sources.

activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides which commercial risks warrant action and whether the evidence supports escalation; no approval, eligibility, or customer commitment is inferred.

activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial risk found early is a conversation. The same risk found at approval becomes delay.

activities.prompt: Review the commercial risk view for unsupported assumptions, stale sources, missing owners, policy dependencies, approval needs, and customer constraints. activities.name: Set the trigger for each commercial risk
activities.description: Give each prioritized commercial risk an observable trigger, so it is acted on at a defined point rather than watched until it is late.
activities.prompt: For each prioritized commercial risk, state the observable condition that means it has to be acted on now rather than watched, who acts when that condition is met, and what they do first. Keep internal steps separate from anything the customer is asked to do. Separate the risks you can act on yourself from those that need someone with more authority, and for those name the person and what they will need from you to decide. Where a risk has no observable trigger, say so rather than inventing a threshold. Work from the material I have supplied rather than looking it up, and where a piece of it is missing, name the gap instead of filling it. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: Each commercial risk with its acting trigger, the person who acts, their first step, and the risks that have no observable trigger named as such.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE owns the escalation route and confirms it before the plan is used. An escalation that arrives through the wrong channel is slower than none, because it must be re-routed after it has already alarmed someone. The CE also decides whether each trigger is one a person would actually act on, since a threshold set where nobody would move produces a register that looks governed and changes nothing.
activities.requiredContext: The validated commercial risk view; the approval owners; the escalation route your team actually uses.
activities.whyThisMatters: A risk everyone agrees is real still waits, because nobody said what would mean now.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Risk you find this week is a conversation. The same risk found by the customer is an escalation. Focus on finding it earlier.
keyTalkingPoints: A health score can tell you something is wrong. It rarely tells you what to do.
Every risk needs an owner and a date or it is an observation.
AI is good at surfacing signal. Prioritizing it is judgment.
discussionQuestions: Which account is at risk in a way the reporting does not show?
What stops a known risk from getting an owner?
Which part of this carries policy or precedent risk?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify commercial risk and escalation priorities'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the one deal you just briefed to where commercial risk is concentrated across the book, then back to what you will act on first. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test assumptions behind the commercial risk view', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Commercial risk prioritization needs current authoritative evidence and an accountable intervention owner. Ranking risks does not authorize pricing, exceptions or commitments. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Confirm tool access for this huddle, bring one real commercial structure and policy example you are working on now, and review the commitment you made last week.
facilitatorQuestions: Which commercial risk is most consequential this week, and what dated evidence supports it? Who can act and by when? How does a colleague distinguish a risk score from a cause that changes the intervention?
listenFor: Risk described without an owner or a date; health reported by score rather than cause; and interventions discussed but never started.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one commercial-risk brief: dated fact, cause versus score, customer consequence, governed action, owner and action date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which risk is supported by current evidence, what remains uncertain, and who is accountable for the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, rank your commercial risks, then take the top one to its owner with a proposed intervention. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized commercial risk verified or routed and whether it made the intervention clearer; keep agreement and pricing details private. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.
