activities.name: Compare viable commercial structures
activities.description: Develop commercial strategy options for price and offer, documenting trade-offs and approval dependencies; hand off the options and open questions for CE review.
activities.prompt: For [opportunity], compare up to three candidate commercial structures using the approved deal context and current authoritative guidance available to me. For each show products/SKUs, term, pricing logic, customer value, Microsoft trade-offs, risks, approval requirements and assumptions. Distinguish confirmed available structures from options still requiring validation; do not invent three viable choices to fill the count. Do not create, submit or approve an offer. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Commercial structure comparison with evidence-backed availability, customer trade-offs, approval dependencies and options or policy questions still requiring validation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE verifies that each pricing and offer option is available to this customer under current authoritative guidance and keeps unapproved structures distinct from approved terms.
activities.requiredContext: Approved opportunity context.
activities.whyThisMatters: Comparing viable commercial structures surfaces the difference that actually changes the decision.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercial structure decides whether a deal can move. Focus on comparing options before the structure hardens.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is not to create an offer. The goal is to compare viable structures, surface trade-offs, and name the approval path while options still exist.
discussionQuestions: What option is the deal implicitly assuming? Which approval or exception would surprise the team later? What trade-off should be explicit before negotiation?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Compare viable commercial structures'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from possible structures to the smallest options matrix that makes the decision clearer. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Commercial options expose viable trade-offs, customer constraints and approval dependencies before negotiation narrows choice. Recommendation is separate from authority to offer terms. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live opportunity, approved commercial context, known constraints, and the current approval or exception question.
facilitatorQuestions: Which commercial option is most plausible? What trade-off would change the decision? Where would this break if an approval requirement appears late?
listenFor: One default structure being treated as the only option; approval path ambiguity; pricing, term, or concession trade-offs not stated; and assumptions that need CE or Deal Desk review.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a two-option commercial matrix: customer intent, known agreement mechanics, trade-off, authoritative source gap and approval dependency. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, build a commercial options matrix for one live deal and identify which option needs approval you do not hold. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized approval dependency or trade-off discovered and whether it prevented an unapproved offer or preserved an alternative. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

secondaryAgents.name: Sales Home
secondaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
secondaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Stress-test the assumptions the value claims depend on
activities.description: Expose what each outcome number quietly assumes, and record which assumptions the customer would have to accept.
activities.prompt: Here is our value narrative and the evidence brief behind it: the supplied information. For every outcome claim, produce a row containing: the claim, the assumption it depends on, who has to accept that assumption for the claim to hold, the evidence we currently have, and what happens to the claim if adoption is half as fast as projected. Rank the rows by how much the claim collapses when its assumption fails. Do not add claims that are not in my narrative, and do not supply evidence I have not given you. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: An assumption and risk table ranked by how much each claim depends on an unproven assumption.
activities.humanCheckpoint: SSP decides which assumptions are defensible with this customer, and owns every outcome figure before it reaches them.
activities.requiredContext: The value narrative; the evidence brief; the customer's financial context; adoption expectations already discussed with them.
activitySteps: 1. Bring the value narrative and evidence brief.
2. Paste what you gathered into the prompt where it asks for it, then run it.
3. Find the claim that collapses hardest.
4. Either find proof for its assumption or remove the claim.
5. Bring the assumption table to the huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: The value claim you cannot defend is the one the customer will ask about.

activities.name: Reduce the narrative to something the customer can forward
activities.description: Produce the short version your champion can send to people you will never meet, without you in the room to explain it.
activities.prompt: Reduce this value narrative supplied information to a single page that our champion could forward internally without us present. It must stand alone: state the business problem in the customer's own terms, the outcome, what it depends on, and what we are asking for next. Remove anything that only makes sense if a seller is explaining it. Remove any claim that is not supported by the evidence brief I gave you. Keep it under 350 words. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: A one-page, forwardable value summary with a specific next ask.
activities.humanCheckpoint: SSP verifies every claim survives without a seller present, and approves the wording before the champion receives it.
activities.requiredContext: The rehearsed value narrative; the evidence brief; who the champion is and who they would forward it to; the next ask.
activitySteps: 1. Bring the rehearsed narrative with weak claims removed.
2. Paste what you gathered into the prompt where it asks for it, then run it.
3. Read it as if you were a stranger receiving it.
4. Cut anything that needs explaining.
5. Confirm the ask is specific.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most internal customer decisions happen in rooms the seller is not in.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The conversation happens before the story is finished. Focus on turning what you heard into a customer-specific narrative the account would recognize.
keyTalkingPoints: The customer defines value. Use sourced evidence, caveats, use cases, and a clear next ask.
discussionQuestions: What customer priority does this solution map to? Which claim is supported, assumed, or missing evidence?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Tailor the solution value narrative'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from what the customer told you to the value logic and the proof it needs. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test the assumptions the value claims depend on', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Customer-specific value depends on defensible assumptions and customer-stated priorities. Removing an unsupported claim can improve trust more than polishing the narrative. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved customer conversation excerpt, the stated priority and sourced value claims with their caveats. Confirm tool access and review the prior commitment and evidence.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer-stated priority anchors the value claim? What source and assumption support it, and what remains unproved? How would a peer challenge the claim before it reaches the customer?
listenFor: Generic value claims, unsupported ROI, customer priorities inferred rather than sourced, and missing caveats.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one value-claim strip: customer-stated priority, proposed benefit, supplied evidence, assumption, caveat and validation owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which outcome can you substantiate for this audience, and what claim or next action still needs validation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, test the assumptions behind one value claim, and remove any claim you cannot defend. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized claim qualified, retained or dropped and whether checking it made the value story more credible. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Build the renewal and growth readiness view
activities.description: Connect health, consumption, adoption, value and stakeholder signals into a renewal readiness view.
activities.prompt: Build a renewal and growth readiness view for the account. Include renewal context, consumption or usage trajectory, MACC or commitment risk if applicable, adoption gaps, value evidence, support or health risks, stakeholder health, expansion hypothesis and recommended v-team next action. Separate the value already proven from the value still planned, and map the partnership forward across the next six, twelve and eighteen months so the renewal conversation is about a direction rather than a date. Flag unavailable data. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Renewal and growth readiness view separating proven value from planned value, with the partnership mapped across the next six, twelve and eighteen months.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides which signals are the AE's to raise. Renewal risk surfaced by the wrong person at the wrong moment can harden a customer position that was still movable.
activities.requiredContext: Renewal context, agreements, consumption or usage signals, adoption data, value proof, health risks and stakeholder context.
activities.whyThisMatters: Renewal risk is easier to change when it is seen through health and value before the renewal date.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal readiness starts before the renewal motion. Focus on seeing risk and growth conditions early.
keyTalkingPoints: Consumption, MACC or usage trajectory, adoption gaps, value evidence, support health and stakeholder signals all shape renewal confidence.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal are you least confident about, and what specifically drives that?
What consumption signal would you want to see six months before a renewal conversation?
Where is growth genuinely available versus where are you hoping?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the renewal and growth readiness view'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the forecast to the one early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align it with. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test the expansion hypothesis', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Consumption trajectory, evidenced value and readiness shape renewal and growth hypotheses. Early signals help inspection; they are not forecast or expansion commitments. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one account with renewal, consumption, usage or expansion relevance in the near planning horizon.
facilitatorQuestions: What is your forecast based on, and how far ahead does the signal reach?
Which growth opportunity is supported by consumption evidence?
What would you need to know now to avoid a surprise at renewal?
How does a peer distinguish customer growth intent from consumption headroom?
listenFor: Forecasts driven by relationship confidence rather than consumption evidence, growth assumed from headroom rather than intent, renewal risk surfacing late because nobody looked early, and commercial ownership blurring between CSAM and CE. Also note consumption trends read without seasonality.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one renewal/growth readiness row: dated consumption signal, seasonality/intent uncertainty, renewal event, value proof and AE/CE alignment question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, start tracking one early consumption signal and hand it to the account owner. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized early signal checked and whether it changed an evidence request or renewal action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Create the v-team orchestration brief
activities.description: Assemble execution context across workstreams, owners, handoffs, decisions, and blockers; for delivery follow-through, reconcile status and owners against the Customer Success Plan and route blockers for coordination.
activities.prompt: Analyze the approved customer-success sources I have supplied for the account across meetings, emails, notes, the CRM export, support and delivery context. List every active workstream with owner, input needed, due date, dependency, blocker, decision needed and recommended next action. Classify every workstream by the first of these rules that applies, in this order. First, where dated evidence in the sources shows something actually moved after the date I last reviewed this account, mark it confirmed progress. Second, where the record's last-modified or last-activity date falls after that review date, mark it record changed, progress unconfirmed. Third, where that date falls on or before the review date, mark it no recorded change since that review, and say plainly that this is not evidence nothing happened, only that nothing reached the record. Fourth, where there is no last-modified or last-activity date at all, or it is not precise enough to place on one side of the review date, mark it movement unknown rather than assuming there was none, even if it carries other dates such as a due date. From the same sources, flag any workstream where a specialist or partner appears to be engaged but no CSAM touchpoint is recorded, stating that this may mean the touchpoint happened and was not logged, and say what you would need to confirm it. State plainly which sources you actually had, so I can judge how complete the list is. Flag missing owners and stale dates. Reconcile each delivery workstream with the supplied Customer Success Plan outcome, milestone and next review; mark missing plan links and unconfirmed handoff acceptance explicitly. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: V-team execution-context brief listing current workstreams, owners, handoffs, decisions, blockers, delivery status, and the relevant Customer Success Plan/review connection; confirmed and unconfirmed progress are distinguished.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Orchestration is making the customer-success system observable enough to run.
keyTalkingPoints: Handoffs need an input, owner and date. Escalation is not a failure when it is used to unblock the system and protect customer outcomes.
discussionQuestions: Where does work currently stop between Microsoft, the partner, and the customer?
Who believes they own something that someone else also believes they own?
Which handoff have you personally been compensating for?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the v-team orchestration brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the coordination map to the one handoff you will make explicit, with both sides named. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build the weekly customer-success action plan', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Customer-success orchestration makes both sides of the handoff explicit and accepted. A date or listed owner is not agreement until the parties confirm it. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one workstream involving Microsoft, customer, partner, support or delivery handoffs.
facilitatorQuestions: Where exactly does work stop between the three parties?
Who thinks they own that step, and have you asked them?
What are you personally absorbing because the handoff does not work?
How does a colleague make both sides accept a handoff instead of personally compensating for it?
listenFor: The CSAM compensating for a broken handoff rather than fixing it, ownership assumed across company boundaries, partner commitments with no date, and coordination meetings that report rather than decide. Also note the customer's own team being left out of the orchestration picture.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one three-party handoff row: customer/Microsoft/partner contribution, transfer input, proposed receiver, acceptance gap and date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, make one handoff explicit this week by agreeing it with both sides rather than assuming it. Ask the receiving owner to accept the work; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized handoff gap clarified and whether both sides accepted the next step or need a specific input. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Track commercial policy and licensing changes that affect your accounts
activities.description: Set up a monitored, source-locked watch on the commercial policy and licensing guidance you rely on, so changes reach you before a customer raises them. In-huddle practice is one reviewed read-only result; recurrence is optional after approval.
activities.prompt: Run a read-only check against the fixed list of authoritative Microsoft commercial policy and licensing sources I supply and have confirmed. Each time, report only what has changed, quote the change, cite the source, and state plainly which of my accounts it plausibly affects and why. Do not interpret the change into commercial advice and do not draw on any source outside the confirmed list. Where the implication is unclear, say so and name the owner who can rule on it. First run this once, read-only, against the small named scope I supply. Use only sources I am authorized to access and disclose that are actually available to this tool; ask for a permitted extract or mark unavailable sources as gaps. Report source coverage and as-of dates. Use a previous verified result if supplied; otherwise create a dated baseline and do not claim a change. Do not create a schedule until I have reviewed the first result and explicitly approved the exact scope, sources, cadence, output location and human reviewer. If scheduling or a needed connection is unavailable, return a manual repeat procedure. Draft follow-ups only; do not send, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated first-run baseline or change digest quoting and citing each change, with plausible account impact and the named owner for anything requiring a ruling. Recurrence is a proposed configuration, or a manual repeat plan if unsupported; a scheduled result exists only after separate human approval and an actual later run.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE confirms the source list before the watch is enabled, and routes every interpretation to the accountable policy owner rather than acting on the summary.
activities.requiredContext: The authoritative policy and licensing sources your team treats as canonical; your account list; your escalation owners. A small named scope, source-access confirmation or permitted extracts, previous verified result if one exists, and a human reviewer. Recurrence needs explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence and output location; no CRM, telemetry or support connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the small named scope and sources this tool can actually access, or supply permitted extracts.
2. Run the prompt once, read-only; on the first run create a dated baseline.
3. Review actual source coverage and findings before any scheduling.
4. Agree the fixed list of authoritative policy and licensing sources with your team before you enable anything.
5. Check the first digest quotes and cites each change rather than paraphrasing it.
6. Route every interpretation to the accountable policy owner rather than acting on the summary.
7. If recurrence is useful, approve its exact scope, reachable sources, cadence, output location and reviewer before enabling it where supported; otherwise use a manual repeat review.
8. Later, verify the first actual recurring or manually repeated result before relying on it. Any message, record correction or commitment is a separate human-reviewed action.
activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial policy changes are only a problem when the customer knows before you do. A locked source list is what separates a reliable watch from confident invention.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Policy questions found at approval cost weeks. Focus on finding the question early and routing it to the authoritative owner.
keyTalkingPoints: AI can assemble the context and possible questions. It cannot interpret policy, approve exceptions, or invent authority. The useful output is a routed question with evidence, not a guessed answer.
discussionQuestions: Which policy or licensing question most often causes rework? Where did an approval path surprise you? Which interpretation must come from an authoritative source?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the investment path against policy and approval requirements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from policy categories to one live deal question and the owner who can answer it. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test policy and licensing assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Policy checks distinguish verified positions from unresolved interpretations. Use current authoritative guidance and route rulings beyond your authority instead of letting AI fill the gap. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one real commercial structure or policy example, the approved source you would check, and the decision or approval path currently unclear.
facilitatorQuestions: Which policy or licensing question changes this deal's next decision? What current authoritative source would settle it? How does another CE frame a self-contained question when the guidance is unavailable or ambiguous?
listenFor: Policy interpreted from memory; uncertainty left unflagged; approval paths discovered late; and questions that need an authoritative owner rather than a generated answer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one policy-question card: precise question, relevant deal fact, current guidance/version gap, authoritative owner and dependent commitment to hold. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which policy or commercial boundary is verified, which is still uncertain, and who can authorize the next step?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, take one open policy or licensing question to its authoritative owner rather than answering it yourself. Keep unresolved rulings pending; only the authoritative owner can confirm the position. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share the type of policy question and whether review clarified, changed or held the next step; omit restricted ruling text. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Create a technical Skill Blueprint for a repeatable SE workflow
activities.description: Describe a repeatable workflow as a draft Skill Blueprint, with implementation and testing still explicit before promotion.
activities.prompt: Create a draft reusable Skill Blueprint for [SE workflow]. Define trigger, inputs, trusted sources, ordered steps, expected output, rules, exclusions, exception behavior, human review and validation checks. Include one representative test case with expected output and pass/fail criteria, plus implementation tasks for the skill owner. Label the result as a draft specification, not an installed or tested skill. A walkthrough of the blueprint is not an execution test; do not invoke or publish an implementation that does not yet exist. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Draft technical Skill Blueprint with validation checks, representative test case, expected results, walkthrough gaps and implementation owner/tasks. No claim that a skill has been installed, executed or validated.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The SE or skill owner approves the blueprint, implements it in a supported environment, then runs and records representative execution tests. Validate access, outputs, safeguards and repository placement before approving publication or promotion; a blueprint walkthrough alone is not sufficient.
activities.requiredContext: SE workflow; trusted sources and access constraints; representative approved test case and expected outcome; the owner who will implement and validate the skill.
activitySteps: 1. Open Scout and choose one repeatable SE workflow; no installed skill is required for this drafting practice.
2. Replace [SE workflow] in the prompt and supply trusted sources and a representative, approved test case.
3. Run the prompt to generate the draft Skill Blueprint.

4. Review its steps, access assumptions, outputs and safeguards, then walk through the test case against the specification. Record expected results and gaps; do not mark this as an executed skill test.
5. Keep the blueprint as a draft and name the owner who will implement it in a supported skill format and authorized environment.
6. After an implementation is available, the owner runs the representative test, records actual results and resolves gaps. Publish or promote only after the human checkpoint is approved.
activities.whyThisMatters: A blueprint lets the team test repeatability before pretending the skill is production-ready.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Reuse only works when an asset has enough context for someone else to trust and adapt it.
keyTalkingPoints: Package purpose, prerequisites, steps, parameters, validation checks, limitations, owner, and example use.
Remove sensitive content before reuse.
Use Skill Blueprints for repeatable workflows that are not validated assets yet.
discussionQuestions: What did you build recently that another SE will rebuild?
What context would make someone trust and adapt it?
What should not be reused without review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Package a reusable technical asset with context'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect the selected asset's prerequisites, provenance and actual validation status. A blueprint or workflow walkthrough is specification review, not an installed, executed or tested skill. Name the human implementation/test owner before any promotion or publication. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Sanitize and validate the reusable asset', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Technical reuse depends on provenance, permissions, prerequisites and validation limits. A workflow outline or Skill Blueprint is a draft, not an implemented or tested capability. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one demo, script, architecture, checklist, response, or pattern that could become reusable. Supply available validation results, date and environment for asset packaging. For a Skill Blueprint, bring a representative approved test case, expected outcome and access constraints; the huddle drafts and reviews the specification rather than claiming an implementation exists.
facilitatorQuestions: Which asset is worth reusing?
What context would make it usable by another SE?
What must be removed, validated, or tested before sharing?
What did another SE need to know before reusing your asset safely?
listenFor: Assets without owner, missing prerequisites, sensitive content, unclear limitations, and reuse patterns that should become blueprints.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one reusable-asset card: purpose, prerequisites, source/provenance, sensitive detail removed, validation status, limit and implementation/test owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep reuse/publication on hold until rights, sanitization and actual validation are reviewed; no repository access is required for the draft.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which technical lesson is reusable, what needs review before others apply it, and where should it live?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review a small reuse candidate from existing work or draft a workflow outline. Check provenance, permissions, prerequisites and technical limits with its owner; keep draft status until reuse is authorized. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized reuse lesson and whether it reduced explanation or setup effort; no asset upload or distribution is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
secondaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. activities.name: Identify where customer investment could unlock the next decision
activities.description: Identify where a customer investment could remove a decision, deployment or adoption barrier, without judging eligibility.
activities.prompt: Using approved account, opportunity, customer-priority, and adoption context, identify where a customer investment could remove a decision, deployment, or adoption barrier. Separate evidence from assumptions and do not determine eligibility or approval. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. activities.whyThisMatters: Investment is worth exploring when evidence shows a customer barrier it could remove, not merely an available funding route.

activities.name: Qualify the investment before anyone builds a request
activities.description: Test whether the investment idea is worth the effort of a request, and decide who owns the next step, before work starts.
activities.prompt: Test the investment hypothesis and customer-barrier evidence I supply for [account / opportunity]. What customer outcome would it unlock, what supports that, and what remains an assumption? Name counterevidence and conditions that would support proceeding, reshaping or stopping. Identify the next accountable owner only where supplied. Distinguish non-Azure ECIF, Azure-specific offers and CSP ECIF; confirm the applicable route against current guidance rather than treating them as interchangeable. Do not assess eligibility, funding, supplier choice or approval likelihood. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: An evidence-based proceed/reshape/stop recommendation for AE decision, with assumptions, route questions and the next owner to confirm.
activities.humanCheckpoint: AE owns the judgment about whether the customer outcome is real, and routes eligibility, policy, and funding questions to the accountable owners rather than answering them.
activities.requiredContext: The investment hypothesis and its account linkage. What the customer has actually said. Who on the account team would build and own the request.
activitySteps: Tool/access: Open Sales Agent and ask for ECIF/investment help to engage ECIF Agent; do not assume automatic routing. Run the existing prompt with authorized inputs. If lookup is unavailable, use approved supplied evidence and flag gaps. Draft/analyze only: no eligibility determination, approval, supplier selection, record changes, or submission. Human review/submission remains outside the huddle.
1. Bring the investment hypothesis from the previous activity.
2. Paste what you gathered into the prompt where it asks for it, then run it.
3. Be honest about which supporting points are assumption.
4. Decide proceed, reshape, or stop.
5. If proceeding, name who builds the request and who owns the workscope.
activities.whyThisMatters: The cheapest investment request is the one you decide not to build. Qualifying early costs an hour; qualifying late costs the team weeks.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Investment should be connected to a real customer barrier, not added as a side process. Focus on your role in naming the investment hypothesis and routing the next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: Eligibility, funding, and approval are governed human decisions. AI may help assemble context, status, and evidence, but you should not overstate approval or commitment.
discussionQuestions: Where could investment remove a barrier? Which part is yours to advance? Who owns the next governed decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify where customer investment could unlock the next decision'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from investment concept to the AE’s next governed action on one live case. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Investment is useful only if it can remove an evidenced barrier. Separate the testable hypothesis from eligibility, funding and approval decisions reserved for accountable owners. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live opportunity or account barrier where investment may be relevant, plus any approved context you can safely use.
facilitatorQuestions: Where might investment remove a real barrier? What evidence supports that barrier? Who owns eligibility, funding, approval, delivery, or value proof?
What investment handoff has a peer had to return because the barrier or approval evidence was incomplete?
listenFor: Funding implied as approved, hidden open questions, unowned handoffs, and investment ideas not tied to an account priority or decision.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one investment-barrier card: account priority, evidenced obstacle, intended outcome, eligibility/approval questions and routing owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What would justify or disqualify the investment, and what must the accountable owner verify before committing?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, test whether investment could remove one real barrier, then route the next decision without implying approval. Eligibility, funding and resource commitments remain with authorized owners; a draft is not approval. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized barrier or evidence gap checked and whether the governed next action became clearer; omit request and funding details. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

WF-ORIENT-01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
WF-ORIENT-01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
WF-ORIENT-01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, connecting meaningful business outcomes to recurring workflows, responsible experimentation, and peer learning informed by evidence from real work.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

secondaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. activities.name: Test whether the qualification would survive the receiving role
activities.description: Check that an opportunity being handed on has the qualification evidence the receiving role needs, before you transfer it rather than after they reject it.
activities.prompt: I am handing over the opportunity to the specialist team. Review what is documented and tell me whether a specialist receiving this could act on it immediately. Specifically: is the customer outcome clear, are the business and technical decision makers identified, is the budget and timing evidenced, are the blockers named with a mitigation, and does the milestone carry an evidence-backed estimate and date, or an explicitly applicable non-monetary measure, rather than a placeholder. Tell me what is missing rather than summarizing what is there. Apply the qualification criteria I supply, not invented universal criteria. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: A gap list against the qualification the receiving role needs, covering outcome, decision makers, budget, timing, blockers and milestone completeness.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The sending role decides what is genuinely known versus assumed. Handing over an assumption dressed as a qualified fact is worse than handing over an acknowledged gap, because the receiving role will act on it.
activities.requiredContext: One opportunity being transferred, with its ID; the milestone attached to it; the qualification criteria your team applies.
activitySteps: 1. Choose one opportunity you are about to hand over, or one you recently received.
2. Supply your case details as inputs to the prompt.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Treat every gap as work to do before the transfer, not after.
5. Verify the date and applicable value or outcome measure from evidence; flag unknowns rather than entering an artificial non-zero value.
6. If you received this handoff, send the gap list back rather than rebuilding it silently.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most handoffs are rejected or quietly rebuilt because the receiving role cannot act on what arrived. The gap was always visible before the transfer; nobody looked.

activities.name: Write the handoff so the next role does not have to ask
activities.description: Capture the qualification, the customer context and the unwritten detail in the record itself, so the transfer survives without a meeting.
activities.prompt: Help me write the handoff notes for the opportunity moving to the receiving role. Cover what the customer is trying to achieve and in their own words where I have them, what has been agreed and what has not, who influences the decision and how, what I have already tried, and what I would warn the receiving person about. Write it so someone who has never spoken to this customer could pick it up. Flag anything I have written that is my opinion rather than something the customer said. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: Handoff notes covering customer outcome, agreed and unagreed items, decision influence, what has been tried, and warnings, with opinion separated from evidence.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The sending role decides what belongs in a permanent record. Candid relationship context may be better said than written, and the sender owns that judgment rather than transcribing everything.
activities.requiredContext: Your gap list; what the customer has said in their own words; the receiving role and who specifically will take it.
activitySteps: 1. Start from the gap list you produced in the previous practice.
2. Supply your case details as inputs to the prompt.
3. Run the prompt.
4. Separate what the customer actually said from your interpretation of it, and label both.
5. Put the notes in the record, not in a chat message. Chat is not where the next person will look.
6. Hold the handoff conversation as well. The notes make the conversation shorter, not unnecessary.
activities.whyThisMatters: The handoff conversation happens once and is forgotten. The record is what the receiving role actually works from, and what the person after them inherits.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Test whether the qualification would survive the receiving role

activities.name: Find the handoffs that stalled in the gap between roles
activities.description: Look across your opportunities and milestones for transfers that were started and never completed, where ownership is ambiguous and nothing is moving.
activities.prompt: Across my opportunities and milestones, find where a transfer between roles looks incomplete or stalled: ownership that changed but where nothing has happened since, milestones sitting at the same stage well past their estimated date, opportunities where the specialist or customer success team was engaged but no activity followed, and anything where I cannot tell from the record who currently owns the next action. Rank by how long each has been static. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: A ranked list of stalled or incomplete transfers with time static, and the ownership ambiguity named for each.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The seller confirms actual ownership with the other role directly. A record showing a transfer completed is not evidence that anyone picked it up.
activities.requiredContext: Your opportunities and milestones; the expected transfer windows your team works to; the roles you routinely hand off to.
activitySteps: 1. Run the prompt across your own opportunities and milestones.
2. For each result, establish who actually believes they own it. It is often nobody, and sometimes two people.
3. Pick the one that has been static longest and resolve ownership today.
4. Check whether the customer is waiting on any of these. That changes the priority.
5. Record the owner in the system rather than agreeing it verbally.
activities.whyThisMatters: Work does not usually stall inside a role. It stalls in the space between two, where both parties believe the other has it.

activities.prompt: I have received a handoff for the opportunity and it is thin. Play the role of the person who sent it. I will ask for what I need. Push back the way a busy colleague would, including being defensive if I imply they did it badly. Afterwards, tell me which of my questions got the most useful information, where I put them on the defensive unnecessarily, and how to ask for the missing context without making it a complaint. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: A rehearsed recovery conversation with coaching on which questions produced information and where the approach created defensiveness.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The receiving role decides how hard to push. The relationship with that colleague outlasts this opportunity, and a handoff recovered at the cost of a working relationship is a poor trade.
activities.requiredContext: A handoff you received that was insufficient; what specifically you still need; your relationship with the sending role.
activitySteps: 1. Use a real handoff you received that was not enough.
2. Supply your case details as inputs to the prompt.
3. Run the role-play.
4. Notice where you made it about the process rather than the customer.
5. Rewrite your opening so it leads with what the customer needs.
6. Have the real conversation.
activities.whyThisMatters: Nobody sends a bad handoff deliberately. Getting what you need without making it an accusation is the skill that keeps the next one better.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Write the handoff so the next role does not have to ask

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A handoff stalls when the sender considers it complete but the receiver cannot act. Focus on one live transfer: the decision, usable evidence and acceptance still needed.
keyTalkingPoints: Confirm the applicable current handoff requirements and timing with the accountable owners. A handoff is complete only when the receiving role can act and acceptance is recorded. Include the customer outcome, usable evidence, open decisions and next checkpoint; do not substitute an ownership-field change for acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What is the least useful handoff you have ever received, and what was missing?
When you hand something over, what do you assume the other person already knows?
How would you know today if a handoff you sent had gone nowhere?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Test whether the qualification would survive the receiving role'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the gap analysis to the one handoff each person will prepare, repair or chase this week. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Rehearse receiving a handoff you were given badly', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Handoffs succeed when the receiver can use qualification evidence and accepts the next action. Completeness reduces ambiguity, not legitimate questions or conversation. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one opportunity or milestone you are currently handing over or have recently received. If you have neither, bring the one that went worst.
facilitatorQuestions: Could the receiving role act on what you sent, without asking you anything?
Where in your own list has a transfer stalled with nobody owning it?
What do you know about this opportunity that is written nowhere?
What missing field has a peer receiver needed before they could accept a handoff?
listenFor: Handoffs described as notifications, ownership that changed without anyone accepting it, milestones carrying placeholder values or dates, and sellers rebuilding a thin handoff silently rather than sending it back.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or approved context is unavailable, use a sanitized supplied example or a clearly labeled synthetic case. On paper, complete one handoff acceptance check: required context, milestone evidence, proposed receiver, missing field and draft return reason. Mark evidence, assumptions and unknowns. Treat the receiver and acceptance state as proposed until confirmed; record the access gap and who must validate the handoff before use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you assume the receiving role already knew, and what will you write down next time instead of assuming?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review a handoff with the other role, clarify the consequential missing input and seek explicit acceptance of the next action; follow-up questions remain welcome. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized missing input clarified and whether the receiver could act or identified a remaining gap. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Design a technical shortfall intervention
activities.description: Connect customer context to intervention planning.
activities.prompt: Using approved consumption analysis and available context for the customer, identify technical blockers, workload milestones, stakeholders, commitments and dependencies relevant to the potential shortfall. Propose intervention options, owner candidates, customer touchpoints and evidence needed. Do not assume cause or make commitments. My delivery context is the applicable global, field, or SME&C coverage; reflect that in what you recommend. Base this on the consumption analysis I have supplied. Where it does not explain a shortfall, say what additional evidence would, rather than proposing a cause. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Intervention options with evidence, owners and gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSA confirms the cause before selecting the intervention. Consumption shortfalls have several plausible technical explanations, and the intervention for the wrong one consumes the window the right one needed.
activities.requiredContext: Approved analysis and authorized context. Your delivery context, whether global delivery, field delivery or SME&C coverage, since it changes which next action is right.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shortfall intervention needs an evidenced technical cause; unexplained movement should trigger a validation question, not a guessed remedy.

activities.name: Design the consumption intervention plan
activities.description: Build the intervention that changes the consumption trajectory, with the owner and the checkpoint that will show whether it moved.
activities.prompt: Turn the evidenced consumption causes into an intervention plan. For each, define the action, who owns it on both sides, the dependency that could block it, the date you would expect to see movement, and the telemetry that would confirm it. Separate the causes you can act on technically from the commercial or customer-driven ones, and route those to the role that owns them rather than carrying them. Rank by the size of the gap each one closes. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: A ranked consumption intervention plan with owners, blocking dependencies, expected movement dates and confirming telemetry, with non-technical causes routed to their owners.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSA confirms the customer-side owner exists before the intervention plan is used, and does not take ownership of the consumption plan itself. Consumption interventions depend on customer action, and a plan with an unconfirmed owner on the other side simply does not start. The CSA owns the technical milestones that feed the plan, not the plan.
activities.requiredContext: The validated consumption causes; the deployment and architecture levers available; the customer owners for each dependency. Your delivery context, whether global delivery, field delivery or SME&C coverage, since it changes which next action is right.
activities.whyThisMatters: Consumption intervention needs both a technical lever and a customer-owned dependency, with telemetry that can show whether it worked.
