activities.name: Identify adoption friction and next activation actions
activities.description: Map usage gaps to customer priorities and build a short activation plan.
activities.prompt: Using the certified usage/adoption extract, verified licensed or committed scope and customer-priority notes I supply for [account / workload], identify underused scope and adoption friction. Do not infer payment, entitlement or rights from usage alone. Mark each possible cause as data-supported, stated by the customer or unresolved. Compare conflicting explanations without treating a customer statement as proof by itself. Propose a four-week activation plan with owner candidates and measurable milestones, flagging unknown data and unconfirmed actions. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: Friction analysis including entitlement the customer is paying for and not using, and a four-week activation plan, with each proposed cause marked as shown by the data, stated by the customer, or still unresolved.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CSAM validates whether the adoption action is relevant to the customer priority and achievable with available owners.
activities.requiredContext: Supply an approved dated usage/adoption report extract, verified entitlement/commitment evidence, customer priorities and conversation notes, known rollout scope and available owners. No access to external dashboards or licensing systems is implied.
activities.whyThisMatters: Adoption work matters when it changes customer behavior tied to a business outcome.

activities.name: Build the value realization brief
activities.description: Assess customer health, adoption, usage, delivery, and value evidence for expansion or restart signals; return sourced next actions and unknowns for CSAM/customer validation.
activities.prompt: Using the adoption, usage, delivery and review materials I am supplying, build a value realization brief for the account. Include what changed, what evidence supports it, how it maps to the customer outcome, remaining gaps and the recommended next action. Separate measured evidence from narrative interpretation. Include health/adoption context, possible expansion or restart signals only where supplied evidence supports a question worth following up; do not treat them as customer intent or an automatic trigger. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: Value-realization brief connecting customer health, adoption, usage, delivery, and evidenced value expansion, with source-backed restart signals and gaps clearly identified.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM validates customer-recognized value and adoption evidence, removes unsupported claims, and treats restart signals as prompts for human follow-up rather than automatic decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Adoption data, usage signals, customer outcome, delivery milestones, support or health improvements and prior review notes.
activities.whyThisMatters: Value that is not evidenced is an opinion. Value that is not communicated is invisible.

resources.title: Anonymised Case Study Writer
resources.description: Turns engagement notes into a shareable case study with customer-identifying detail removed.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Adoption activity does not automatically become customer value. Focus on proving and accelerating value realization.
keyTalkingPoints: Adoption plans should link underused features, customer priorities, behavior-change actions, milestones and value evidence. AI can draft the plan and value narrative; you validate truth and relevance.
discussionQuestions: What value has this customer actually realized that you could prove today?
Where is adoption stalled, and do you know why or are you guessing?
What would the customer say they got, if asked without us in the room?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify adoption friction and next activation actions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the value picture to one claim you will evidence, and one adoption barrier you will actually diagnose. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Draft the sponsor value update', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Adoption and value are different claims: investigate barriers and verify entitlement and usage before acting. Customer statements and measures have limits that must stay visible. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one workload or solution where adoption progress, friction or value proof needs to be clarified, and the recent customer conversation where the reason was discussed, if there was one.
facilitatorQuestions: What value can you evidence today, and what are you asserting?
Where adoption stalled, do you know the cause or are you inferring it?
Would the customer describe the value the same way you just did?
What evidence would another CSAM require before describing usage as customer value?
listenFor: Value claimed from usage figures alone, adoption barriers guessed rather than investigated, realized value described in Microsoft terms rather than customer outcomes, and proof that would not survive a procurement conversation. Also note value stories that have never been said back to the customer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one adoption/value row: friction hypothesis, distinguishing evidence, customer outcome, claimed value, caveat and activation owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which adoption cause is evidenced rather than guessed, and what supports the customer-recognized value claim?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a customer-recognized value claim or adoption barrier using permitted data or conversation. Verify unused-entitlement hypotheses with the owner; finding an unused entitlement is not required. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized adoption barrier or value claim checked and whether it improved intervention or avoided an unsupported entitlement claim. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal readiness starts before the renewal motion. Focus on seeing risk and growth conditions early.
keyTalkingPoints: Consumption, MACC or usage trajectory, adoption gaps, value evidence, support health and stakeholder signals all shape renewal confidence.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal are you least confident about, and what specifically drives that?
What consumption signal would you want to see six months before a renewal conversation?
Where is growth genuinely available versus where are you hoping?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the renewal and growth readiness view'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the forecast to the one early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align it with. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test the expansion hypothesis', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Consumption trajectory, evidenced value and readiness shape renewal and growth hypotheses. Early signals help inspection; they are not forecast or expansion commitments. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one account with renewal, consumption, usage or expansion relevance in the near planning horizon.
facilitatorQuestions: What is your forecast based on, and how far ahead does the signal reach?
Which growth opportunity is supported by consumption evidence?
What would you need to know now to avoid a surprise at renewal?
How does a peer distinguish customer growth intent from consumption headroom?
listenFor: Forecasts driven by relationship confidence rather than consumption evidence, growth assumed from headroom rather than intent, renewal risk surfacing late because nobody looked early, and commercial ownership blurring between CSAM and CE. Also note consumption trends read without seasonality.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one renewal/growth readiness row: dated consumption signal, seasonality/intent uncertainty, renewal event, value proof and AE/CE alignment question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, start tracking one early consumption signal and hand it to the account owner. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized early signal checked and whether it changed an evidence request or renewal action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Build the recovery action register
activities.description: Use Cowork to turn a supplied, validated escalation brief into a recovery action register for human approval.
activities.prompt: Using the validated escalation brief and approved owner context I supply, draft a recovery action register with action, owner, customer impact, dependency, due date, escalation threshold and evidence source. Extract confirmed details from the supplied material. Mark absent owners, dates or thresholds unconfirmed and identify who needs to resolve them; do not invent commitments or retrieve incident details from an assumed live connection. Do not update a tracking system or notify anyone. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: Draft recovery action register with evidence sources, confirmed versus unconfirmed commitments, and gaps requiring owner confirmation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM confirms each owner knows they own it. A recovery register full of people who have not been told is a list rather than a plan, and recovery is exactly when that distinction shows.
activities.requiredContext: Supply the validated escalation brief from CSAM-ESCALATE-P01, approved owner context, and any agreed dates and escalation thresholds. Identify missing details for confirmation rather than assuming they are available to Cowork.
activitySteps: 1. Open Cowork from the link on this activity.
2. Supply the validated escalation brief from the briefing practice, approved owner context and any agreed dates or escalation thresholds.
3. Run the prompt to draft the recovery action register.
4. Review source evidence and resolve unconfirmed owners, dates and thresholds with the accountable people.
5. Confirm owners accept the actions and approve the register.

activities.name: Rehearse the escalation conversation before you have it

activities.prompt: Use Agent J.ai to role-play the customer stakeholder I have to tell about this escalation. Use the approved status position, the validated escalation brief and the commitment boundaries I am pasting below, and ask me for anything missing before you begin. Play them as someone who is frustrated and wants a date I cannot yet give. Push back where I over-commit, where I soften the impact, or where I explain the cause instead of saying what happens next. Pause for my response before coaching me on whether I was clear about what is known, what is not, and when they will hear from me again. Do not invent facts about the incident. Use only the scenario and material I am authorized to share here. Keep reactions explicitly simulated, not new customer facts; do not make commitments or send communications. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: A rehearsed escalation conversation, the objections raised, and coaching on where you over-committed or softened the impact.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides what can be said about cause and timing before the facts are settled. Rehearsal makes an answer fluent, and a fluent answer about an unresolved incident is easy to hear as a commitment.
activities.requiredContext: The validated escalation brief; the stakeholder and what they care about; the approved communication position; what you cannot yet commit to.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Escalations test trust. Focus on moving from scattered status to a grounded recovery plan.
keyTalkingPoints: A useful brief names customer impact, current status, owner, decision needed, next action and update cadence. AI can consolidate threads; you validate tone, accuracy and accountability.
discussionQuestions: What issue are you currently managing that should probably already be escalated?
What is holding you back: evidence, ownership, or the conversation itself?
When an escalation last worked well, what made it work?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the escalation and recovery brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the delivery risk to a recovery plan with an owner, a customer message, and a defined exit condition. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build the recovery action register', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Recovery plans need feasible delivery commitments, clear communication and work returned to its accountable owner. Escalation does not make an unaccepted date achievable. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live or recent delivery risk, incident, support issue or overdue commitment, and be ready to say which parts of it you have ended up doing yourself. For the recovery-register practice, supply the validated escalation brief and approved owner context, including any agreed dates or escalation thresholds; unresolved details stay unconfirmed.
facilitatorQuestions: What threshold would have told you to escalate this a month ago?
What does the recovery plan commit us to, and can we deliver it?
What will you tell the customer, and when?
What recovery commitment has a peer had to narrow to what delivery could actually support?
listenFor: Escalation delayed to avoid an uncomfortable conversation, recovery plans that promise more than delivery can support, customer communication planned after the internal fix rather than alongside it, and escalations raised without a defined exit. Also note the same issue recurring without anyone treating the pattern.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one recovery brief: risk, escalation trigger needing confirmation, feasible recovery action, customer-safe draft message, owner and exit condition. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which recovery commitment can delivery support, and which absorbed task should return to its accountable owner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review a delivery issue with its owner, confirm feasible recovery and agree escalation or resolution. Humans review customer communication and proposed ownership transfers. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized recovery assumption or ownership gap corrected and whether it made communication or delivery action more realistic. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

preparationChecklist: Bring one assigned signal, its source/date, applicable action-window guidance and current account or opportunity context. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which assigned signal has the earliest action window confirmed by current guidance? What account evidence warrants convert, confirm-first or close? How does a colleague triage the queue without turning a proxy into qualification?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.

bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized signal disposition and whether it improved timing or prevented low-value contact. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

DAE-ORIENT.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
DAE-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
DAE-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Establish the outcome and who is already engaged
activities.description: Avoid making the customer repeat context and choose the right participants.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the account, prepare for the upcoming conversation identified by the meeting subject on the meeting date. Summarize the customer objective, active Microsoft roles, partner involvement, and relevant interactions from the relevant time range. Return a factual conversation brief, open questions, participant recommendations, and declared assumptions so the customer need not repeat known context; leave participant selection to me.
activities.expectedOutput: A factual context brief, open questions, participant recommendation, and declared assumptions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE decides who joins and what the conversation is for.
activities.requiredContext: Upcoming conversation, customer objective, active Microsoft roles, partner involvement, and recent interactions. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Optional Sales Home access is only for enabled SME&C individual contributors; supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Avoid making the customer repeat context and choose the right participants.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm this specific task: Establish the outcome and who is already engaged.
2. Supply authorized dated inputs listed in RequiredContext; use clearly labeled synthetic data if permitted real inputs are unavailable.
3. Produce the stated ExpectedOutput using the prompt; verify claims against supplied sources and expose unknowns.
4. DAE decides who joins and what the conversation is for.
5. Keep the output as a draft for the stated human checkpoint; no sending, record update, approval or assignment is authorized by this practice.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is an optional SME&C preview for enabled individual contributors, not Enterprise Sales Agent. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. Without access, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: DAE value comes from joining customer context, business outcome, and the right contributors—not from supplying every specialist answer.

activities.name: Set the primary decision and fallback
activities.description: Convert a meeting objective into two valid customer choices.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For my conversation with the account, coach me to turn the desired outcome and the supplied customer constraints, likely objections, and DAE authority into a primary ask with a specific decision and owner plus a genuinely different fallback. Rehearse likely responses and what to say next, and state what the customer must believe for each ask; do not invent facts or decide the asks. Use a fictional or de-identified scenario. Label simulated reactions as rehearsal, not customer/partner evidence, agreement, intent or authorization.
activities.expectedOutput: A primary ask, genuinely distinct fallback, decision owner, and evidence needed.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE owns the asks and checks that the fallback is not a disguised concession.
activities.requiredContext: Desired outcome, customer constraints, likely objection, and DAE authority.
activities.bestFitJob: Convert a meeting objective into two valid customer choices.
activitySteps: 1. Open Agent J.ai and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Rehearse the likely objection, not only the version where the customer agrees.
3. Test whether the fallback changes a different axis or merely asks for less.
4. DAE chooses the opening ask and fallback; Agent J.ai does not make the decision.
5. Record only commitments actually accepted in the current system of record.
Access/fallback: Agent J.ai is optional. Use a peer or written de-identified rehearsal; simulated reactions are not evidence or accepted commitments.
activities.whyThisMatters: DAE value comes from joining customer context, business outcome, and the right contributors—not from supplying every specialist answer.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on moving one customer outcome from broad interest to a specific next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: DAE leads broad outcome discovery; DSS deepens solution-area discovery and DSE owns technical decision criteria when those triggers are present.
Current execution: Use current account, interaction, opportunity, and partner records plus direct input from active contributors.
Fallback: If records are incomplete, ask the relationship owner or partner for the missing context and label assumptions before the meeting.
System of record: MSX for account/opportunity decisions and the approved customer follow-up channel for confirmed commitments.
Optional AI boundary: Sales Home may assemble current account research where enabled; Cowork may help structure supplied notes. Neither owns the customer narrative or decision.
discussionQuestions: Which customer outcome needs a decision now?
What prior commitment must be recovered?
What must the relationship owner confirm before the meeting?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Establish the outcome and who is already engaged'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Confirm decisions and route next work', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Outcome conversations connect verified context to useful decisions and the right contributors without specialist commitments. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming customer conversation, approved outcome/commitment notes, known stakeholders and the next decision requested. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What customer outcome and prior commitment must the conversation preserve? What primary decision and fallback ask are realistic? What did a peer learn from a meeting that needed a clearer role split?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer outcome brief: prior commitment, engaged roles, primary decision, fallback ask and post-meeting handoff question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which question or fallback ask changed when you separated customer outcome from solution assumption?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, prepare or rehearse a customer conversation around its outcome and primary or fallback ask, validating claims with the relevant owner. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized ask improved and whether it focused the conversation or identified the right contributor. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on starting the work on the renewal that needs action now, not simply the agreement with the nearest date.
keyTalkingPoints: Applies where DAE owns the customer path; partner-owned CSP renewals require the partner commercial relationship to remain primary.
Current execution: Use the current agreement/renewal record, MSX opportunity, customer interactions, and available usage/value evidence; Sales Home renewal tracking is roadmap, not assumed current.
Fallback: Use a dated manual workback with CE and the relationship owner if a consolidated renewal view is unavailable.
System of record: Authoritative agreement/enrollment record for dates and mechanics; MSX for Microsoft opportunity/forecast; partner record for partner-owned renewal status.
Optional AI boundary: AI may assemble supplied evidence but must not interpret entitlement, set commercial structure, or represent roadmap renewal tracking as current.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal loses options if work waits?
Which risk is evidenced rather than assumed?
Who owns the customer path and the commercial question?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Prioritize by risk and remaining optionality'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test one same-account expansion hypothesis', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Renewal workback preserves options by checking timing, value and risk, while DAE and CE retain distinct decisions. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one renewal, authoritative agreement timing, dated value/risk evidence and the known relationship and commercial owners. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which renewal has the greatest risk and least remaining optionality? When does CE need to join before the construct hardens? How does a peer distinguish a supported expansion hypothesis from usage-based optimism?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one renewal workback: authoritative agreement date or unknown, risk, optionality, CE engagement point and supported expansion question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which timing or risk assumption changed the customer path, and what remains with CE?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a deciding timing or value gap on a renewal and seek CE or account-owner confirmation of the next handoff; expansion may remain a hypothesis. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized renewal gap checked and whether it made the next customer or CE action clearer or earlier. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

SMEC-CE-ORIENT.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on starting the commercial intervention where delay will remove the most options.
keyTalkingPoints: For partner-owned CSP renewals, CE advises on applicable Microsoft commercial dependencies without displacing the partner's customer commercial relationship.
Current execution: Use authoritative agreement/enrollment records, MSX renewal/forecast records, and value evidence from DAE/DCSA/partner sources.
Fallback: Maintain a dated renewal workback and reconcile it manually to authoritative agreements and MSX.
System of record: Agreement/enrollment source for mechanics; MSX for Microsoft renewal opportunity/forecast; partner source for partner-owned status.
Optional AI boundary: Deal Agent or Cowork may assemble supplied evidence where available; CE validates entitlement, mechanics, and forecast category.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal needs commercial intervention first?
What agreement or value evidence supports that choice?
Which partner-owned relationship must remain primary?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Rank renewal optionality and commercial risk'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate and correct the renewal record', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Renewal-book governance protects options through verified dates, risk and value evidence. Portfolio reporting cannot replace the next owned commercial decision. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one renewal, authoritative agreement timing, approved current commercial/value evidence and the account or partner relationship owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which renewal event changes the priority and remaining options? What belongs to CE, DAE or the partner? How does a colleague detect a renewal-record error before it drives a customer commitment?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or SME&C Commercial Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one renewal priority row: event/date or unknown, remaining options, commercial risk, CE/DAE/partner decision split and record-validation gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which renewal assumption threatened optionality, and what evidence or owner decision changed it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a deciding risk or agreement-timing assumption and agree a targeted evidence request or commercial review with its owner. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized renewal risk clarified and whether it preserved an option or improved review. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on choosing a commercially viable construct without promising terms or routes that authoritative guidance has not confirmed.
keyTalkingPoints: Partner-transacted shaping applies only where the partner owns the transaction; otherwise use the applicable direct route.
Current execution: Use authoritative agreement, licensing, pricing, policy, and transaction guidance plus opportunity context.
Fallback: If a required source or owner is unavailable, carry the item as an explicit assumption and stop customer commitment on that point.
System of record: Authoritative commercial systems and approved guidance; MSX retains opportunity context and agreed commercial milestones.
Optional AI boundary: Deal Agent may help organize supported scenarios, and Cowork may compare supplied options. Both are optional and maturity/access bounded.
discussionQuestions: Which commercial option fits the confirmed customer constraints?
What assumption requires authoritative confirmation?
Who can approve the route or terms?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate decide, recommend, and partner-owned elements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Make the chosen construct explainable', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Transactable constructs need authoritative agreement mechanics and transaction ownership. Plausible options are not executable offers. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one engaged deal, approved agreement/economic context, candidate constructs, known constraints and the requested commercial decision. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which construct can this customer and transaction route actually execute? Which elements can CE decide, recommend or only route to a partner? How would a peer compare the trade-offs without presenting an unapproved option as available?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or SME&C Commercial Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a two-construct comparison: transaction route, customer intent, CE versus partner decision rights, authoritative mechanics gap and trade-off. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which option depended on an unresolved agreement mechanic or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, compare a proposed construct with an authorized alternative and route its deciding agreement or policy question to the authoritative owner. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized construct assumption corrected and whether it prevented an unapproved or unworkable option. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

DSS-ORIENT.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
DSS-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
DSS-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Investment should be connected to a real customer barrier, not added as a side process. Focus on your role in naming the investment hypothesis and routing the next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: Eligibility, funding, and approval are governed human decisions. AI may help assemble context, status, and evidence, but you should not overstate approval or commitment.
discussionQuestions: Where could investment remove a barrier? Which part is yours to advance? Who owns the next governed decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify where customer investment could unlock the next decision'. facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Investment is useful only if it can remove an evidenced barrier. Separate the testable hypothesis from eligibility, funding and approval decisions reserved for accountable owners. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live opportunity or account barrier where investment may be relevant, plus any approved context you can safely use.
facilitatorQuestions: Where might investment remove a real barrier? What evidence supports that barrier? Who owns eligibility, funding, approval, delivery, or value proof?

facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What would justify or disqualify the investment, and what must the accountable owner verify before committing?

If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized barrier or evidence gap checked and whether the governed next action became clearer; omit request and funding details. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent

Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. activities.name: Build the QBR and value evidence brief
activities.description: Assemble outcomes, commitments, usage or consumption signals, risks, investments, and expansion plays into a reviewable evidence base.
activities.prompt: For the account and the relevant period, build a QBR evidence brief. Include outcomes delivered, supporting evidence, open customer and Microsoft commitments, usage or consumption signals, active investments, risks, expansion plays, and missing evidence. Separate sourced facts from interpretation. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.
activities.expectedOutput: QBR evidence brief with supported outcomes, commitments, risks, expansion plays, and evidence gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The AE decides what counts as evidence the customer would accept. Internal signals show what Microsoft can see, and a review built on measures the customer does not recognize turns into a discussion about the measures.
activities.requiredContext: Account; period; approved usage, consumption, meeting, opportunity, investment, and commitment sources.
activities.whyThisMatters: A QBR should start with evidence the customer would recognize, not slides that sound good internally.

activities.description: Convert the reviewed evidence brief into an executive-ready narrative with decisions and asks.
activities.prompt: Using the reviewed QBR evidence brief, create an executive QBR narrative for the account. Include a concise executive summary, value delivered, commitments, risks, top expansion plays, investment status if relevant, three strategic asks, and claims requiring final review. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.

activitySteps: 1. Review the evidence brief.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A QBR or executive cadence should not be a status meeting. It should make value, commitments, risks, and strategic asks visible enough for the customer to decide.
keyTalkingPoints: AI can assemble outcomes, usage signals, open commitments, risks, investments, and expansion plays. You validate what the customer would recognize as value and which ask advances the relationship.
discussionQuestions: What value has been delivered but not evidenced? Which customer commitment is still open? What strategic ask should the QBR create?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the QBR and value evidence brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from value evidence to the executive brief or QBR ask the AE would actually use. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Value stories are credible when outcomes, sources and limits travel together. Sharpen the strategic ask without converting an unsupported result into an executive promise. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one account with a QBR, SBR, renewal, or executive follow-up where value evidence matters.
facilitatorQuestions: What value would the customer recognize? Which outcome is supported by evidence, and which is only expected? What strategic ask should follow from the value story?
What value claim would another AE ask you to narrow before an executive QBR?
listenFor: Value claims without evidence, QBRs that become status readouts, unsupported causality, missing customer commitments, and expansion asks not tied to outcomes.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one QBR claim table: agreed customer outcome, observed result, source/date, supported versus assumed claim and strategic ask. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which outcome can you substantiate for this audience, and what claim or next action still needs validation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, build one executive value or QBR brief and validate which claims are supported before sharing. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized value claim qualified or removed and whether it made the review more credible. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on assessing the strategic and technical case for investment.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is a strategic and technical investment assessment with dependencies, readiness, risks, and the next governed decision named. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: What technical problem is this investment actually meant to solve?
What would tell you six months from now that it worked?
Which dependency would quietly sink it, and who owns that dependency?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Assess strategic and technical investment fit'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the investment case to the technical evidence it needs and the governed decision that comes next. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Investment cases need credible technical dependencies and observable outcomes, while funding and approval stay with governed owners. A plausible benefit cannot erase a blocking prerequisite. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one proposed investment, the technical barrier, approved readiness evidence and the next governed decision owner. Confirm access to the named tools and review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What technical outcome does this investment buy that we could not get otherwise?
What is the observable measure that proves it worked?
Which approval or eligibility question are you assuming rather than confirming?
What technical-success measure would a peer challenge before the investment review?
listenFor: The ATS drifting into eligibility, funding, or approval decisions that belong to other owners, success measures that cannot be observed, deployment paths assumed rather than validated, and handoffs to delivery with no re-engagement trigger.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one investment technical-fit brief: bounded outcome, technical prerequisite, observable measure, evidence gap and authorized approval question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which technical dependency could invalidate the investment case, and what governed owner decision is still needed?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, test one investment case against its technical dependencies, and route one approval question to its real owner. Eligibility, funding and resource commitments remain with authorized owners; a draft is not approval. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized dependency or approval question checked and whether routing it prevented an unsupported commitment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Turn the hardest review questions into a readiness edit

activities.prompt: Here is our technical contribution for a customer business review: the supplied information. Identify the three hardest questions this content invites, including about progress that has been slower than planned and any risk we have named. For each question, state what evidence the content currently offers, whether that evidence is sufficient, and the specific edit to the contribution that would answer the question before it is asked. Return the edits as a numbered change list, not as a rewritten document. Do not treat a statement of intent as evidence. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments.

activities.humanCheckpoint: ATS decides whether to strengthen the evidence, name the gap openly, or remove the claim, and owns every technical statement made to the customer.
activities.requiredContext: The technical CBR contribution; known risks and slow areas; who attends from the customer side; commitments made in prior reviews.
activitySteps: 1. Bring the reviewed CBR contribution.

3. Apply the edits where evidence exists.
4. For any question where evidence does not exist, decide whether to name the gap openly in the review or remove the claim.
5. Bring that decision to the huddle.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on preparing the technical contribution for a customer business review.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is a technical CBR contribution with roadmap points, evidence, risks, decisions, and follow-through. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: What technical progress can you evidence, rather than assert?
Where has progress been slower than the customer expected, and how will you say so?
What decision do you want the review to produce?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the technical CBR contribution'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the technical contribution to the decisions it should trigger, and the evidence each decision requires. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Technical review contributions should expose evidenced progress and areas behind plan. Honest limits make the customer decision more useful than an unsupported roadmap. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming business review, dated technical progress evidence, open risks and the decision requested. Confirm access to the named tools and review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Which technical claim in your contribution can you evidence today?
How will you present the area where progress was slower than promised?
What decision should this review produce, and who makes it?
How would another ATS explain slower progress without omitting it or committing an unsupported roadmap?
listenFor: Progress narrated rather than evidenced, slow areas omitted rather than addressed, roadmap statements that commit the product group, and reviews that end without a decision. Also note a technical contribution disconnected from the business outcome the customer cares about.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical CBR contribution: claim, source/date, progress limit, customer outcome, decision and reviewer. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which technical claim is substantiated, and how will you address the area behind plan without overstating the roadmap?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, evidence one technical claim before your next customer review, and decide how you will address the slowest area. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized claim or lagging area addressed and whether it improved the business-review discussion or next evidence request. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Raise the risk with the customer before it becomes news
activities.description: Draft the message that tells the customer about a technical risk early, in a way that keeps trust rather than spending it.
activities.prompt: We have identified this technical health risk: the supplied risk, evidence, impact, and what we are doing. Draft a short message to the customer technical owner that states the risk plainly, what we know and do not yet know, what we are already doing, what we need from them, and when we will update them next. Do not minimize the risk, do not over-apologize, and do not commit to a resolution date we have not agreed internally. Keep it under 150 words. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: A short, honest customer message with a named next update date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: ATS confirms no commitment is made that has not been agreed internally, and owns the decision to communicate and the wording.
activities.requiredContext: The identified risk and its evidence; the intervention plan; what has been agreed internally; the customer relationship and prior communications.
activitySteps: 1. Bring the ranked risk and intervention plan.
2. Confirm internally what can be committed.
3. Paste what you gathered into the prompt where it asks for it, then run it.
4. Adjust to your relationship with the customer.
5. Send, and diarize the next update.
activities.whyThisMatters: A risk the customer hears about from us early costs far less than one they discover themselves.
