activities.humanCheckpoint: DCSA retains milestone governance, not implementation.
activities.requiredContext: Handoff response, baseline, observable signal, check date, and escalation route. Supply approved dated snapshots, comparable definitions, user-maintained baseline/prior report if available, reviewer and actual approved change criteria. Missing scope, source permission, cadence, recipients, expiry/review date or future automation approval remains explicit; no persistent state or tool access is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Know whether work started and whether it is producing the intended result.
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on starting delivery with an owner who can act and a signal that shows whether the handoff landed.
keyTalkingPoints: Use a partner only when selected, capable, and accepted; otherwise use the applicable Factory, FastTrack, customer, or Microsoft route.
Current execution: Use route-specific current handoff and milestone processes; verify partner acceptance directly or in accessible partner status views.
Fallback: Hold a live handoff and record acceptance, baseline, and check date.
System of record: Delivery route system for execution status; committed-milestone/consumption record for DCSA governance.
Optional AI boundary: AI may format DCSA-authored handoff content; it must not disclose unapproved data, assign the implementer, or mark acceptance.
discussionQuestions: Can the selected implementer act from the handoff?
What proves acceptance and readiness?
Which baseline and check date will reveal whether delivery started?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Confirm the selected route and accountable implementer'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Record acceptance and monitoring signal', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Delivery handoffs need route-specific acceptance, a usable baseline and observable milestone. Sending a packet does not transfer accountability. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one accepted technical decision, approved delivery route, handoff packet, recipient acceptance evidence and the agreed baseline/check date. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What selected delivery route and implementer are actually confirmed? Could the receiver act from the technical packet alone? How does another DCSA test acceptance, baseline and the first check date?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical delivery-handoff row: selected route, implementer or unknown, executable input, baseline, acceptance evidence needed and check date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which delivery assumption stayed open until the receiver checked it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a deciding handoff input or baseline with the receiving owner and seek acceptance of the next milestone or explicit gap. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized handoff clarification and whether it reduced uncertainty or identified an acceptance condition. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on making value usable without claiming outcomes the evidence cannot prove.
keyTalkingPoints: Applies only where DCSA has coverage and accessible evidence; partner/customer evidence remains attributed to its source.
Current execution: Use accessible usage/consumption and milestone evidence plus customer/partner-confirmed outcomes.
Fallback: Create a dated evidence packet that names inaccessible or unproven outcomes.
System of record: Source telemetry/milestone systems for facts; MSX or renewal handoff for the accepted value input.
Optional AI boundary: AI may structure supplied evidence but cannot promote usage into business value or remove source attribution.
discussionQuestions: What outcome does the evidence actually support?
What remains usage rather than business value?
Who must accept the value input for the next review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Classify what the evidence proves'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Secure renewal-owner acceptance', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Adoption, usage proxies, partner reports and confirmed outcomes carry different evidence strength. Attribution must preserve those differences. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one milestone or value-review case, dated source telemetry, customer/partner-confirmed outcomes and an explicit list of unproven claims. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Does the evidence prove deployment, adoption or a customer outcome? Whose contribution does it actually support? How would a peer describe it to the renewal owner without claiming partner-delivered work as Microsoft proof?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one value-evidence strip: deployment/adoption/outcome classification, dated support, contribution attribution and renewal-owner acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which claimed outcome was a usage proxy or partner report, and how did that change the value statement?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, verify a consequential value claim with its evidence owner and revise attribution or caveats before the renewal owner uses it. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized claim qualified and whether it prevented overstated value or improved review. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PSS-ORIENT.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PSS-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PSS-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on closing or expose every material rule dependency before it becomes a customer commitment.
keyTalkingPoints: Investment content is awareness-level: CE validates contract/transaction dependencies but does not assume program eligibility or ECIF ownership.
Current execution: Use current approved policy, licensing, agreement, and route-specific program owners.
Fallback: Send a self-contained dated question to the authoritative owner and mark the construct dependent until answered.
System of record: The authoritative source or owner's recorded ruling; MSX/deal record holds the resulting dependency and decision.
Optional AI boundary: Researcher may locate published guidance, but CE must identify the deal-specific exception and obtain authoritative confirmation.
discussionQuestions: Which rule dependency could change the construct?
What current source or owner can resolve it?
What customer commitment must wait for that answer?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'List the material rule questions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile guidance, ruling, and construct', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Commercial commitment waits for verified policy and licensing positions. Open rulings must stay separate from confirmed guidance. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one candidate construct, the exact policy/licensing/program dependency, current approved guidance and the authoritative decision owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which material rule question must be answered before commitment? What dated source or authoritative ruling would settle it? How does another CE expose a dependent construct rather than filling a policy gap from memory?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or SME&C Commercial Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one material rule-question card: relevant facts, dated guidance or unavailable, authoritative owner and construct dependency to hold. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which interpretation remained open after checking source, date and authority?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, take a blocking policy or licensing question to its authoritative owner; record confirmed position or pending ruling. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on surfacing one technically credible same-account expansion while respecting customer and commercial timing.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only where the current workload is demonstrably adopted and coverage permits analysis; do not treat product adjacency as customer intent.
Current execution: Use validated adoption/value evidence and current authoritative technical prerequisites.
Fallback: Document the technical hypothesis and ask DAE/DSS to validate customer intent if system access is limited.
System of record: Source systems for adoption facts; MSX/customer plan for the accepted expansion hypothesis.
Optional AI boundary: Researcher may locate current prerequisites; DCSA validates applicability and stops short of commercial timing.
discussionQuestions: What sustained adoption supports this expansion hypothesis?
Which prerequisite could invalidate it?
Who must confirm customer intent and commercial timing?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify a workload that is genuinely adopted'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Hand the hypothesis to sales and commercial owners', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Expansion begins with a technical hypothesis and prerequisites, not headroom alone. Customer and commercial decisions remain with their owners. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one adopted workload, approved value evidence, an adjacent-outcome hypothesis and current technical prerequisites; mark intent unconfirmed where needed. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which adopted workload supports the next-workload hypothesis? What prerequisite or customer-intent gap could invalidate it? How would another DCSA hand it to DAE/DSS and CE without making a commercial commitment?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one next-workload hypothesis: adopted starting workload, technical prerequisite, customer-intent gap and DAE/DSS/CE handoff question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which prerequisite or customer need would disprove the workload hypothesis?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check the weakest prerequisite or need assumption and route a discover, defer or stop recommendation to its owner. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized hypothesis tested and whether it improved discovery or justified a hold. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.description: Compare two authorized technical-question snapshots to identify new/changed themes, using only permitted aggregate asker counts.
activities.prompt: Produce an unactivated, read-only proposal, not a running monitor. Use authorized dated snapshots, a user-maintained baseline and previous report supplied for this review; do not retrieve unsupplied records, create automation, retain agent memory or notify anyone. Missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no change. Record proposed scope, source permission, owner, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and approved change criteria without inventing values. Future monitoring requires separate explicit approval and verified access/state capabilities. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Review the supplied authorized messages and meetings from the relevant time range for technical questions answered more than once. Group by underlying problem, use authorized aggregate counts of distinct askers or customers, and compare the supplied prior report to return only new groups or groups with more distinct askers. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on reducing repeat work without applying one customer's answer to another customer's constraints.
keyTalkingPoints: Reuse is internal unless the content owner and data-sharing rules explicitly permit external or partner use.
Current execution: Use the approved team repository and current information-protection rules.
Fallback: Create a local team entry and named maintainer if no formal repository exists; do not share customer-specific content.
System of record: Approved technical asset repository and its owner/review record.
Optional AI boundary: AI may help sanitize and describe an asset, but DSE must review customer specificity, technical assumptions, and current validity.
discussionQuestions: What is genuinely reusable here?
Which customer-specific assumption must be removed?
Who can permit reuse and maintain the asset?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Sanitize and state assumptions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Catch the question that has started arriving', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Reuse assets carry source, permission, prerequisite and validation limits. Findable does not mean approved for publication or universal reuse. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one completed technical decision and approved artifact, validation/provenance notes, reuse permission and a proposed maintainer. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What assumption, permission or validation limit must travel with this technical asset? Who owns its maintenance? Which recurring question would a peer use to decide whether it is worth packaging?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one reusable technical-asset entry: sanitization, assumptions, rights gap, maintainer and evidence needed before reuse. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep reuse/publication on hold until rights, sanitization and actual validation are reviewed; no repository access is required for the draft.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What limitation would a new user miss without provenance or review status?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review a small reuse candidate for provenance, permission and validation limits; keep draft status until sharing is authorized. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized reuse boundary clarified and whether it reduced setup ambiguity or exposed a permission gap. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on removing one technical blocker without silently absorbing the partner's delivery work.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only for an active partner-led opportunity where a technical capability gap is evidenced; it is not general partner management.
Current execution: Use deal-specific evidence, partner demonstration/history, and input from PSS/PSA/PDM as applicable.
Fallback: Run a bounded technical working session and escalate route/capacity decisions to the correct partner role.
System of record: MSX/partner deal record for the blocker; approved repository for reusable enablement.
Optional AI boundary: AI may structure DSE-authored enablement. It cannot diagnose partner capability from certification or assign business ownership.
discussionQuestions: What technical blocker is evidenced?
Which enablement step could remove it?
Where must partner delivery or capacity ownership remain separate?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Evidence the deal-specific technical gap'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Leave bounded enablement and escalation', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Partner-deal gaps may need enablement, different expertise or a hold; they do not automatically justify assigned delivery work. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one active partner-led opportunity, the agreed technical criterion, evidence of the blocker and the known partner delivery/enablement owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: What deal-specific capability gap is evidenced, rather than inferred from a partner label? Should the next step be enablement, co-delivery, rerouting or escalation? How would another DSE bound the support without committing partner capacity?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one deal-specific partner gap card: demonstrated capability, missing evidence, enable/co-deliver/reroute/escalate options and correct capacity decision owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Was the gap capability, capacity or unclear scope, and what changed the treatment?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate the deciding technical gap with its partner or technical owner and agree proportionate treatment or hold without assigning unaccepted work. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized diagnosis and whether it improved routing or prevented an unrealistic commitment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.

Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Establish what the deal actually looks like
activities.description: Assemble the recorded facts that determine which investment routes are even open to this opportunity.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the opportunity in my solution area, show what is recorded: the account, the products and workloads involved, the deal value and stage, any existing agreement and its type, whether a partner is associated and any co-sell or referral record, and any consumption or usage recorded on the account. activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether there is a real barrier that money removes. Validate the barrier and its evidence; a slow deal alone does not establish funding need, and eligibility/approval stays with the accountable owner.

activities.bestFitJob: Establish what the deal actually looks like

activities.name: Find out what the routes actually require
activities.description: Establish from published guidance what each candidate investment route requires, before choosing between them.
activities.prompt: Use authorized source extracts and approved URLs I supply. Do not assume internal-document access or browse outside that boundary; keep unavailable claims unresolved and review supplied extracts manually. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. I am considering customer investment for an opportunity with these characteristics: the supplied deal facts and the barrier. Using approved Microsoft sources and authoritative internal documentation, set out what the published requirements are for each investment route that could apply, what evidence each requires, what each explicitly excludes, and where the documentation is silent. activities.expectedOutput: Each candidate route's published requirements, evidence and exclusions, cited and dated, with the silent areas identified.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS confirms every eligibility reading with the authoritative owner rather than acting on the documentation alone. activities.requiredContext: Your deal facts and the barrier you named. The routes you are considering.
activities.bestFitJob: Find out what the routes actually require
activitySteps: 1. Open Researcher, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Read current exclusions alongside requirements; flag applicability questions for the authoritative owner.
3. Check the dates. Investment guidance changes between fiscal years and last year's version is still findable.
4. Where the documentation is silent, that is a question for the authoritative owner, not a gap for you to fill.

activities.name: Draft the evidence-based request for the chosen route
activities.description: Turn the barrier and the route requirements into a request that answers what that route actually asks.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. I am requesting customer investment through the named route for an opportunity. Here are the route's published requirements: the supplied information. Here is the barrier and the deal context: the supplied information. Draft the request so that it answers each requirement in turn: what is being asked for, the barrier it removes, the evidence for that barrier, what changes if it is approved, and how that change would be observed. Mark any requirement I have not evidenced. Do not assert eligibility, do not estimate any figure I have not supplied, and do not claim approval is likely.
activities.expectedOutput: A request answering each published requirement in turn, with unevidenced requirements marked and the observable change stated specifically.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS states what will be observably different if the investment is approved. Separate supplied evidence from proposed effects; do not imply approval likelihood or claim an outcome before it is measured.
activities.requiredContext: Your chosen route and its published requirements. The barrier and the deal facts.
activities.bestFitJob: Draft the evidence-based request for the chosen route
activitySteps: 1. Open Cowork, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Look at what it marks as unevidenced. Those are the questions a reviewer will ask first.
3. Make the observable change specific. "Accelerates adoption" is not something anyone can check afterwards.
4. Keep an unsent request draft; only the accountable owner may authorize later submission through the confirmed route process.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A request mapping the customer barrier and supplied evidence to current requirements is easier to assess; completeness does not guarantee approval.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Investment in SME&C is not one thing. Focus on picking the right route before you build anything.
keyTalkingPoints: Choose the investment route before assembling a request. Check current route-specific guidance and the accountable owner for eligibility, thresholds, funding and partner requirements; historical examples are not current policy. Test whether this solution opportunity fits a direct, partner-led or voucher route. AI may organize the evidence but cannot establish eligibility or approval.
discussionQuestions: Which investment route do you reach for by default?
When did an investment request last fail, and at what stage?
Who tells you whether something is eligible?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Establish what the deal actually looks like'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the route to the eligibility question each person will route to an owner. If a participant rejects or overrides the draft, ask which evidence or workflow condition it missed and compare the correction. Discuss only permitted details; do not assume this review sends anything to a transcript service. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Draft the evidence-based request for the chosen route', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Choose the investment vehicle by the barrier it can remove and current authoritative requirements, not program familiarity. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one solution-area opportunity where customer investment might help.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the barrier the investment would actually remove?
Which route fits the size and shape of this deal?
What do you not know about eligibility?
How does another DSS confirm the current route requirements instead of borrowing eligibility from the last deal?
listenFor: One route being used for everything, eligibility being assumed from a previous deal, investment proposed before the barrier is clear, and people who have stopped requesting because a past request failed late.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one route fact base: evidenced customer barrier, scope, transaction facts, candidate route, current-rule gap and authorized eligibility question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which route-fit assumption changed after checking the barrier and current requirement?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, compare an opportunity route with its barrier and ask the program owner to verify the deciding eligibility question; keep route fit provisional until confirmed. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized route-fit question and whether checking it prevented the wrong vehicle or clarified a hold. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.description: Hand a recognized investment opportunity to its owner with enough evidence to be acted on.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. I have found an account where customer investment might remove a barrier. Here is what I found and the evidence: the supplied findings. activities.name: Decide what would count as proof
activities.description: Define observable technical success, negative-result, exit, and review-evidence criteria for the proposed work.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. A customer investment would fund this technical work: the work and customer concern already described. Define what it would need to demonstrate for the customer's doubt to be resolved: the observable success criteria, what would constitute a clear negative result, the exit criteria that end the work either way, and the evidence a reviewer would need afterwards. Do not assume the investment is approved and do not estimate cost or duration.
activities.expectedOutput: What the funded work would have to demonstrate, expressed as things somebody could observe happening.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSE decides how much the funded work must prove before the customer would act on the result. Proving too little leaves the doubt intact and the funding spent; proving too much turns a bounded piece of work into a project, and where that line sits depends on what this specific customer said they doubted.
activities.requiredContext: One proposed piece of technical work, the stated customer doubt, authorized technical evidence and the DSE/customer acceptance owner. Use supplied qualitative criteria; numeric thresholds require actual owner approval. Optional Sales Home account context is not needed to define technical proof and supplies no technical-design authority.
activities.bestFitJob: Decide what would count as proof
activitySteps: 1. Supply proposed technical work, stated customer doubt and authorized technical evidence; Sales Home is optional enabled account context, not a technical proof-design authority.
2. Separate evidenced technical facts from briefed claims; identify observable evidence needed to test the stated customer doubt.
3. Form your own view before reading anyone else's assessment.
4. Route what you find to whoever owns the request rather than acting on it yourself.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is an optional SME&C preview for enabled individual contributors, not Enterprise Sales Agent. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. Without access, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Funded technical work is assessed at closure against whatever criteria existed at the start. If none did, the assessment becomes a matter of opinion and the next request is harder.

activities.name: Write the criteria down before the work is funded
activities.description: Record the technical success and exit criteria in a form a reviewer can assess against afterwards.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. I have defined what an investment-funded piece of technical work must demonstrate. Here are my criteria: the supplied information. Write them up for the investment request: what will be demonstrated, how each will be observed, what would constitute a clear negative result, and the point at which the work stops either way. Mark anything I have written that could not actually be observed. Do not add criteria I have not stated and do not estimate effort or duration.
activities.expectedOutput: Success and exit criteria written for the request, with anything unobservable marked before it is submitted.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSE owns which criteria survive into the request. Preserve agreed success, negative-result and exit criteria with their evidence method; any change requires relevant technical-owner and customer review rather than assumed approval.
activities.requiredContext: Your assessment and the evidence behind it. Who owns the investment request.
activities.bestFitJob: Write the criteria down before the work is funded
activitySteps: 1. Open Cowork, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Check that what you could not determine is as visible as what you found. Silence on a gap reads as a clear result.
3. Say what your role would still have to do. Missing technical responsibilities may block execution and need owner clarification.
4. Prepare an unsent technical-criteria handoff for DSE and request-owner review.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Criteria that live only in your head are renegotiated at closure by people who were not there. Written into the request, they set the terms of the assessment before anyone has a stake in the answer.

activities.name: Plan how the technical proof will produce its evidence
activities.description: Turn the approved proof criteria into a bounded execution plan that identifies method, evidence sources, responsibilities, and the stop point.
activities.prompt: Use only the proof criteria and technical context I provide. Do not invent customer commitments, cost, duration, or evidence access. For each agreed success, negative, and exit criterion, state the method that would produce observable evidence, the artifact or measurement to capture, who is responsible for producing and reviewing it, dependencies, and the decision point. Mark any criterion without a feasible evidence method as unresolved. Keep the plan bounded to the stated technical work and do not add new acceptance criteria.
activities.expectedOutput: A bounded proof plan mapping each agreed criterion to an evidence method, artifact or measurement, responsible owner, reviewer, dependency, and decision point, with unresolved items visible.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSE verifies technical feasibility and that the evidence method genuinely tests the customer's stated doubt. The accountable request owner decides whether to submit or approve the plan.
activities.requiredContext: The written success, negative, and exit criteria; proposed technical work; known technical constraints and dependencies; and the human technical owner and reviewer.
activitySteps: 1. Bring the criteria and request write-up from the prior activities.
2. Run the prompt using the supplied technical context.
3. Confirm the evidence method and responsibilities with the technical owner.
4. Flag criteria that cannot be observed or dependencies that are unresolved.
5. Route the execution plan to the request owner; do not imply that investment or work is approved.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Customer investment reaches your role even though you do not own the request. Focus on the part that is yours.
keyTalkingPoints: Separate investment routing from technical proof. The request owner confirms the route and current requirements; you make the proposed technical question, success evidence and delivery dependencies explicit. Confirm criteria before work starts. AI may organize evidence but cannot establish eligibility, technical success or approval.
discussionQuestions: Where have you seen investment help, and where have you seen it wasted?
What does your role actually contribute to an investment decision?
Who owns the request once you have raised it?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Decide what would count as proof'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the assessment to the one thing each person routes or confirms this week. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Write the criteria down before the work is funded', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Funded proof should settle the customer doubt with the smallest verifiable test, including a meaningful negative result and exit. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one situation where customer investment is or was in play.
facilitatorQuestions: What customer doubt must the funded technical proof settle? Which observable success, negative-result and exit criteria bound it? How would another DSE shrink the proof without changing the investment owner's decision?
listenFor: Success criteria nobody could observe, scope that expands to fill the funding, and exit criteria being omitted entirely.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical proof contract: customer doubt, falsifiable success/negative result, minimum scope, evidence method and exit condition. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. This is a storyboard or proof contract, not an executed demo, successful test or permission to use an environment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What observed result would change the decision, and what would justify stopping proof?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, define a bounded success or failure criterion and ask the technical owner to validate scope and evidence method; do not approve execution or funds. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized proof criterion clarified and whether it avoided unnecessary work or exposed an untestable claim. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Name the dependency that would stop it
activities.description: Set out the customer-side dependencies that would block funded delivery, and who would have to resolve each.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. I have assessed whether a customer could absorb investment-funded technical work. Here is what I found: the supplied findings. Set out the customer-side dependencies that would have to be in place before the work could start or complete: what each is, who on the customer or partner side would have to provide it, and what happens to the engagement if it is not there. Separate the ones I have confirmed from the ones I am assuming. Do not assess whether the investment should proceed.
activities.expectedOutput: The customer-side dependencies that would block delivery, separated into those confirmed and those assumed.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DCSA distinguishes a dependency the customer has been told about from one they have agreed to. Preserve actual acceptance evidence and open questions; a write-up or named contact alone is not agreement.
activities.requiredContext: Your assessment and the evidence behind it. Who owns the investment request.
activities.bestFitJob: Name the dependency that would stop it
activitySteps: 1. Open Cowork, paste the prompt, and supply the relevant case details as inputs.
2. Check that what you could not determine is as visible as what you found. Silence on a gap reads as a clear result.
3. Say what your role would still have to do. Missing customer-side responsibilities may block delivery and need owner confirmation.
4. Prepare an unsent dependency handoff for DCSA and request-owner review.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Customer-side dependencies can block sound technical work. Naming required evidence and actual owner acceptance exposes risks without predicting how a future stall will be attributed.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Customer investment reaches your role even though you do not own the request. Focus on the part that is yours.
keyTalkingPoints: Connect proposed funded work to an observable adoption or consumption outcome. Verify delivery capacity and customer dependencies instead of assuming that approval makes execution feasible. The request owner confirms current eligibility, funding and route requirements. AI may organize evidence but cannot establish eligibility, delivery readiness or approval.
discussionQuestions: Where have you seen investment help, and where have you seen it wasted?
What does your role actually contribute to an investment decision?
Who owns the request once you have raised it?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the environment, not the opportunity'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the assessment to the one thing each person routes or confirms this week. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Name the dependency that would stop it', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Absorption readiness requires accepted dependencies, not just a technically eligible environment. Coverage without dedicated support cannot imply customer or partner capacity. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one situation where customer investment is or was in play.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer-environment prerequisite is actually confirmed? What customer or partner dependency is unaccepted, especially without dedicated support coverage? How would another DCSA record a readiness hold without implying funding approval?
listenFor: Prerequisites the customer has been told about but not agreed to, partner delivery capacity being assumed, and readiness judged from the opportunity rather than the environment.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer-environment readiness gate: technical prerequisite, customer/partner dependency, acceptance evidence or unknown, proposed owner and hold reason. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which recorded-ready prerequisite was not accepted by the customer or delivery partner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check the customer dependency most likely to block funded work and seek owner confirmation; recommend hold if readiness or support ownership is unclear. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized prerequisite checked and whether it changed readiness or prevented an unsupported delivery assumption. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.bestFitJob: Test whether the structure survives without the investment
activitySteps: 1. Use Sales Home only if already enabled for your SME&C individual-contributor account; otherwise use supplied records manually and paste the prompt with your account.
2. Describe the structure twice: once assuming the investment arrives and once assuming it does not.
3. If the second version does not work, the structure depends on a decision you do not own. Say so now rather than at approval.
4. Route any eligibility or investment question to the role that owns it rather than answering it.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is an optional SME&C preview for enabled individual contributors, not Enterprise Sales Agent. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. Without access, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Investment decisions sit outside the CE's authority in this segment, but the commercial consequence of one not arriving lands entirely on the structure. That exposure is worth seeing before the customer does.

activities.name: Compare authorized structures with and without approved investment
activities.description: Compare the current commercial structure with only the alternatives already authorized by the accountable commercial owner, making the effect of an unapproved investment decision explicit.
activities.prompt: Use only the commercial structure, approved terms, and alternatives I provide. Do not invent pricing, discounts, offers, precedent, or investment eligibility. Compare the current structure with each supplied authorized alternative, both with and without the investment being approved. Show which assumptions or terms change, what remains unresolved, and which option depends on an unapproved decision. If no authorized alternative is supplied, say that the comparison cannot be completed and list the information needed from the accountable commercial owner.
activities.expectedOutput: A side-by-side comparison of the current structure and supplied authorized alternatives with and without approved investment, with assumptions, dependencies, and unresolved approvals identified.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE confirms that each option and term is authorized and commercially accurate. Investment eligibility and approval remain with their designated owners.
activities.requiredContext: The current commercial structure, approved terms and options supplied by the commercial owner, the known investment decision status, and any applicable approval guidance.
activitySteps: 1. Bring the current structure and only the alternatives confirmed as authorized for consideration.
2. Run the prompt with the investment approval status clearly stated.
3. Verify every term against the approved source and separate facts from assumptions.
4. Route unresolved terms or eligibility questions to their accountable owners.
5. Do not present an unapproved alternative to a customer.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A structure that only works if unapproved investment arrives is exposed; comparing authorized alternatives makes that dependency visible before a commitment is made.

activities.name: Find the closes you cannot account for
activities.description: List recent closed-won opportunities in your book and separate the ones you closed from the ones that closed some other way.
activities.prompt: Show me the opportunities in my book that were marked closed won with a close date in the last stated short period, for example 30 days. For each, show the account, the value, the close date, the products or SKU lines attached, and the recorded close reason or status if one is set. Report what is recorded. Do not assess whether any close was correct. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Recent closed-won opportunities with the ones the seller cannot account for identified, or an explicit statement that there were none.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The seller decides which closes they can account for. A closed record can be well-formed and still describe something that did not happen, and the check is whether the value, products and date match what was actually sold.
activities.requiredContext: Your own opportunities and the date range you want to review.
activities.bestFitJob: See which of your deals closed without you closing them
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with a short recent period. Keep it small enough to read in one sitting.
2. Go down the list and mark the ones you do not remember closing. You are working from your own memory of the deal here, not from a field.
3. For each one you marked, ask whether you can account for the value, the products and the date. Mark anything you cannot.
4. Take the marked ones forward. If there are none, say so - that is a result worth the room hearing.
activities.whyThisMatters: A closed record carries your number whether or not you set it. A wrong one raises no error and blocks nothing, so it survives until somebody has to explain it.

activities.name: Work out what to do about the one you cannot explain
activities.description: Take a closed record you cannot account for and decide whether to accept it, correct it, or raise it.
activities.prompt: Here is a closed-won opportunity I cannot fully account for: the supplied record - account, value, close date, close reason, products. Here is what I know was actually happening on this account: the supplied what you know - what was sold, what was signed, what was delivered, what was still open. Lay out where the record and my account knowledge agree, where they disagree, and what would settle each disagreement. Do not tell me whether the close was correct. Use only supplied material or reachable sources I am authorized to access and share through this tool; name access gaps rather than inventing evidence. Draft or analyze only: do not send, publish, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: One questionable close resolved into accepted, corrected by the seller, routed to whoever can act on it, or held pending a specific check.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The seller decides whether the record matches what was sold, and whether the correction is theirs to make or somebody else's. Account knowledge is one input rather than the deciding one, and a correction made without the contract in front of you replaces one wrong record with another.
activities.requiredContext: One closed record you could not account for, and what you know was happening on that account.
activities.bestFitJob: Decide what to do about a close you cannot account for
activitySteps: 1. Open Cowork and paste both the record and what you know about the account.
2. Work the disagreements, not the agreements. The agreements are why you did not notice sooner.

3. Decide which of four this is: the close is right and you had forgotten; it is wrong on detail you are able to correct yourself; it is wrong in a way that needs somebody else; or you cannot yet tell and need to check something first.
4. If it is yours to correct, correct it now while you still have the context.
5. If it needs somebody else or more evidence, write down what you checked and what you found, so the next person does not start from nothing.
activities.whyThisMatters: A wrong close is easy to leave alone because nothing breaks. It shows up later as revenue that cannot be explained or a customer conversation that starts from a false position.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A closed-won record carries your number whether or not you were the one who set it. Closes arrive through your own work, through automation, and through other people acting on the account. Focus on reading your own recent closes and deciding which ones you can stand behind.
keyTalkingPoints: A wrong close raises no error and blocks nothing. It stays in the book until somebody has to explain it, and by then the context has gone.
The test is not whether the record is well-formed. It is whether the value, the products and the date describe what was actually sold.
Your account knowledge is the input here, not the verdict. A correction made without the contract in front of you replaces one wrong record with another.
Finding nothing is a real result. Say so in the room rather than treating the exercise as having failed.
discussionQuestions: When did you last read your own closed-won list rather than your open pipeline?
If a close in your book were wrong, how would you find out?
Which part of a closed record would you struggle to explain in a review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Find the closes you cannot account for'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the list of closes nobody could account for to the single record each person will resolve, and how they will resolve it. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Closed-book inspection reconciles recorded outcomes with what happened. Accept, correct, route or hold based on evidence and ownership, not pressure to find an error. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Confirm you can open Sales Agent, and choose a recent period short enough to read in one sitting. Bring what you remember about the accounts in it, because that memory is the instrument this exercise runs on.
facilitatorQuestions: Which close in your list did you not recognise straight away?
What in that record does not match what you remember selling?
Is this one yours to correct, or does it need somebody else?
What check would a peer use to notice an unexplained close even when the total looks right?
listenFor: Sellers scrolling past records they do not recognise because the totals look right. “that must have been the partner” or “that came from the team” offered as an explanation rather than as something to check. Reluctance to raise a close that flatters the number, and the assumption that a well-formed record is a correct one.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one close-verification row: record identifier in the example, stated close fact, unexplained discrepancy, evidence needed and correction owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you find in your own closed book that you had not looked at before? What would have to be true for you to notice it sooner next time?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, inspect a closed-won record you cannot explain and choose accept, correct within authority, route to its owner or hold for a named evidence check. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized manual scenario and report the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized discrepancy or confirmed record and whether its disposition improved trust or clarified ownership. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Watch the satisfaction signals across a live delivery
activities.description: Gather the delivery signals that show how the customer is experiencing the work. In-huddle practice is one reviewed read-only result; recurrence is optional after approval.
activities.prompt: For the customer and the delivery or engagement, run a read-only check on the signals that show how the customer is experiencing this delivery: open issues and how long they have been open, escalations, missed or moved dates, response times, and questions left unanswered. Report what changed since the last check rather than restating everything. Separate what the record shows from what is inferred, and state what the record cannot see. My delivery context is the applicable global, field, or SME&C coverage; reflect that in which signals you treat as material. First run this once, read-only, against the small named scope I supply. Use only sources I am authorized to access and disclose that are actually available to this tool; ask for a permitted extract or mark unavailable sources as gaps. Report source coverage and as-of dates. Use a previous verified result if supplied; otherwise create a dated baseline and do not claim a change. Do not create a schedule until I have reviewed the first result and explicitly approved the exact scope, sources, cadence, output location and human reviewer. If scheduling or a needed connection is unavailable, return a manual repeat procedure. Draft follow-ups only; do not send, change records, submit requests or make commitments. Treat any owner, date or approval not established by the sources as unconfirmed; do not convert a proposal or discussion into an agreed commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated first-run satisfaction signal watch showing what changed since the last check, separating evidence from inference. Recurrence is a proposed configuration, or a manual repeat plan if unsupported; a scheduled result exists only after separate human approval and an actual later run.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSA decides which signals reflect the customer's experience rather than internal process noise. A record with no open issues can still describe a customer who has stopped telling us about them.
activities.requiredContext: Delivery status, open issues, escalation history, milestone dates; your delivery context, whether global delivery, field delivery or SME&C coverage, since it changes which next action is right. A small named scope, source-access confirmation or permitted extracts, previous verified result if one exists, and a human reviewer. Recurrence needs explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence and output location; no CRM, telemetry or support connector is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the small named scope and sources this tool can actually access, or supply permitted extracts.
2. Run the prompt once, read-only; on the first run create a dated baseline.
3. Review actual source coverage and findings before any scheduling.
4. If recurrence is useful, approve its exact scope, reachable sources, cadence, output location and reviewer before enabling it where supported; otherwise use a manual repeat review.
5. Later, verify the first actual recurring or manually repeated result before relying on it. Any message, record correction or commitment is a separate human-reviewed action.
activities.whyThisMatters: The signals are usually already in the record. The work is looking before the survey does.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Satisfaction is decided during the delivery, not at the survey. Focus on reading it early enough to act.
keyTalkingPoints: The customer already knows how they feel. The survey only tells us.
Responsiveness, clarity and expectation-setting move scores as much as technical outcomes do.
A satisfaction risk you cannot evidence is a feeling. Name what you saw.
discussionQuestions: Where in a current delivery would the customer say we are harder to work with than we need to be?
Which satisfaction signal have you noticed and not acted on?
What would this customer say if they were asked today rather than at the end?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Watch the satisfaction signals across a live delivery'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the general idea of satisfaction to one live delivery and the specific moment that would show up in the score. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Check the risk against what the record supports', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Delivery satisfaction improves when an evidenced concern leads to timely owned response, not a survey risk guessed from an AI summary. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live delivery, any customer feedback or escalation on it, and the moment you would least like the customer to remember.
facilitatorQuestions: Which delivery are you least confident about, and what is the evidence rather than the feeling?
What would the customer say we did slowly or explained badly?
Which satisfaction risk is yours to fix and which belongs to another role?
What specific delivery moment would a peer use to test a satisfaction risk without attributing motives to a contact?
listenFor: Satisfaction inferred from the absence of complaints; technical success treated as the whole of the customer experience; risks named without a specific moment behind them; and anything the CSA plans to absorb that belongs to the CSAM or to delivery.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one delivery satisfaction-risk row: observed customer experience, evidence/date, alternative cause, CSA-owned fix and correct handoff role. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which risk is supported by current evidence, what remains uncertain, and who is accountable for the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review a satisfaction concern on a live delivery against customer and delivery evidence; personally act within your ownership or route it. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized manual scenario and report the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized concern confirmed or revised and whether the response improved clarity or follow-through. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.
