facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on assembling an executive technical customer narrative.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is an executive-ready technical narrative with sourced claims, proof points, decision questions, and a technical ask. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: When did an executive last stop you to ask what something meant?
Which part of your technical story do you find hardest to say without jargon?
What is this executive personally putting at risk by backing your recommendation?
What decision do you actually need from the executive, and have you ever asked for it directly?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Translate architecture into business value'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the technical story to the one decision you want the executive to make, and the proof they need to make it. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Executive technical narratives translate options into customer consequences and an explicit decision. Preserve the difficult trade-off instead of hiding it behind technical detail. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming executive conversation, the desired decision, approved technical proof points and the claims that need validation. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Read your opening line aloud. Would a CFO know what you meant?
Which claim in your narrative rests on a proof point you do not have?
What are you asking the executive to decide, stated in one sentence?
How would another ATS translate your strongest technical claim without losing its caveat?
listenFor: Architecture described rather than translated, value asserted without evidence, narratives that end without an ask, and jargon that survived because nobody in the room questioned it. Also note a narrative aimed at the technical stakeholder while claiming to target the executive.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one executive technical narrative: business decision, technical option, sourced proof, caveat and one-sentence ask. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which technical trade-off became clearer in customer terms, and what proof does the executive still need?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, rewrite one technical narrative for an executive audience, state the single decision you are asking for, and give them the options with their tradeoffs. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized trade-off made clearer and whether a reviewer better understood the executive decision. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on developing a technical strategy and decision trajectory.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is a technical trajectory with priority bets, proof needs, owners, risks, milestones, and open decisions. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: What is the next technical decision this customer has to make, and when?
Which of your technical bets is least supported by evidence?
What would have to be true for the customer to commit to the direction you are recommending?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Analyze consumption and technical blockers'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the technical direction to the next decision it requires, with an owner and the evidence that unblocks it. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate technical and business assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Technical strategy advances through sequenced, evidence-backed decisions. A proposed owner or date remains a proposal until the person with authority confirms it. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one technical strategy decision, approved customer context, known constraints and the next proof or decision needed. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the next decision in the trajectory, and who makes it?
Which bet would you abandon first if evidence went against it?
What proof does the customer need before they will commit, and do you have a path to producing it?
How does a peer make the next technical decision visible before it becomes a delivery blocker?
listenFor: A strategy that is a destination without a sequence, bets with no falsification condition, proof needs identified after the customer already asked, and milestones with no owner. Also note technical direction set without the customer's own objectives in the room.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical decision path: customer objective, options, next decision, proof gap, decision owner and date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption affects the technical decision sequence, and what proof or owner confirmation would change it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, clarify the next technical decision, ask its owner to confirm proposed proof and timing, and mark anything unconfirmed as open. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized technical decision or proof gap clarified and whether owner confirmation improved the next step. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on designing an executive briefing experience.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is an EBC plan with desired decisions, participants, evidence, preparation milestones, and follow-through ownership. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: What is the one thing the customer should leave the briefing believing?
Who in the room can actually approve the next step?
What is on your briefing preparation list that currently has no owner?
What would make this briefing worth their time rather than ours?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Design the executive briefing experience'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the briefing design to the single decision it is meant to produce and who must be present for that. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate briefing evidence and decisions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: A briefing earns executive time by advancing a relevant customer decision with the right evidence and contributors. An invitation is not confirmed attendance or a decision guarantee. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one planned executive briefing, its intended customer decision, proposed participants and known preparation dependencies. Use approved user-supplied inputs with source, scope and date; review the prior commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What will the customer do differently after this briefing?
Who in the room can approve that, and are they invited?
Which part of the agenda serves us rather than them?
Which agenda choice did a peer remove to make room for the customer decision?
listenFor: Agendas built around what we want to present, attendee lists without a decision maker, briefings with no ask, and content density that leaves no room for the customer to talk. Also note an experience designed for the meeting rather than for what happens after it.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or approved context is unavailable, use a sanitized supplied example or a clearly labeled synthetic case. On paper, outline the customer decision, required decision-maker role, agenda choice, supporting evidence and follow-through ask. Mark evidence, assumptions and unknowns; proposed attendance or follow-through is not confirmed. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient. Any later AI run must use project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot and approved supplied inputs.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What makes the briefing worth executive time, and which decision or contributor is still missing?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review an executive briefing around a customer decision, check who can make it and draft the reason to attend; report attendance as requested or confirmed, not guaranteed. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized change to the decision, audience or reason to attend and whether it made the briefing more purposeful; pending attendance is acceptable. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Build the v-team commitment board
activities.description: Lay the v-team's commitments out as a board the team can see and work from. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt:
Using the approved account and technical context, lay the v-team's work out as a board rather than a document: one row per commitment, showing the account, the owner, what it is waiting on, the date of the last observed activity and what that activity was, and the agreed next checkpoint. Sort the board by last observed activity, oldest first. Where a commitment has no agreed checkpoint, show it as not agreed rather than filling one in, and label any date you propose as a proposal. Mark a checkpoint as passed only where an agreed date already exists and today is later than it, and do not treat a checkpoint you are proposing as one that was missed. Cover every account I am carrying, not one. Include customer outcome, priority workloads, technical decisions, risks and required roles as supporting detail. Keep my own portfolio view separate from the per-account views I would share, so nothing from one account appears on another account's board. Format each shared view so it can be pasted into whatever that v-team already works in, and where a team has no shared tracker, give me a plain table I can paste into a message. Flag unsupported assumptions.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: A v-team commitment board covering your accounts, sorted by last observed activity, oldest first, with an owner and a last-activity date on every row, the agreed next checkpoint where one exists and not agreed where none does, any proposed date labelled as a proposal, passed checkpoints marked, and the shared per-account views kept separate from your own portfolio view.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The ATS confirms each named role has capacity to take the work. Orchestration that assigns without asking produces a plan everyone nods at and nobody starts. The ATS also agrees the human handoff structure and what may be shared, because accounts carry different teams and confidentiality boundaries; a shared record the v-team did not agree to maintain creates avoidable overhead.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. User-provided approved account and technical records for the accounts you carry, with source, scope, and as-of date; role list; decision needs; for each open commitment, the date and nature of the last observed activity and the agreed next checkpoint where one exists; today's date; and the approved source record each v-team uses to track work.
activities.whyThisMatters: Twelve commitments written as prose have to be re-read. The same twelve as rows can be sorted.

activities.name: Review v-team commitments at a human-owned checkpoint
activities.description: Compare supplied commitment snapshots; no recorded activity is an owner question, not proof of a stall.
activities.prompt:
Compare the prior/current commitment snapshots I supply using the review date and agreed checkpoints. Show source, last observed activity, agreed versus proposed date and new versus unchanged exception status from the supplied prior review. Distinguish confirmed progress, record change without progress evidence, no recorded change and unknown status. Draft one targeted owner question per exception. Do not scan mail/accounts, schedule checks or remember an unsupplied prior review.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: One-time exceptions with new/unchanged status, agreed-versus-proposed dates and owner questions; no recurring check configured.
activities.humanCheckpoint: ATS decides whether silence actually means a stall, and owns the judgment about which chases are appropriate given the relationships involved.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied prior/current snapshots, source dates, agreed checkpoints/owners, review date and prior exceptions if available.
activitySteps: 1. Supply prior/current approved snapshots, review date and previous exceptions if available.
2. Compare documented activity with agreed checkpoints manually or in Copilot if permitted.
3. Treat absent evidence as unknown until the owner confirms.
4. Review and ask the owner questions yourself.
5. Maintain the tracker separately and agree a human-owned next review.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: Technical commitments can go quiet until the customer has moved on. Keep a named owner and agree human-led follow-up so commitments remain visible between sessions.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on mobilizing the technical v-team around priorities and risks.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is a v-team commitment board with owners, dependencies, investment signals, checkpoints, and next actions. AI can assemble approved evidence and draft options; you remain accountable for strategy, technical accuracy, and next decisions.
discussionQuestions: Who on your technical v-team could not state the current priority if asked today?
Which dependency has gone quiet in the last two weeks?
Where does your v-team actually look to see what is outstanding?
What are you carrying yourself that should belong to someone else?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the v-team commitment board'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the coordination picture to one specific ask, to one named person, with a date. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Keep the v-team commitments moving between huddles', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: V-team mobilization turns a dependency into a bounded, answerable ask. Confirm accepted ownership and capacity rather than treating the board as agreement. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring the accounts you currently carry with their open commitments and review the commitment from the prior huddle.
facilitatorQuestions: If I asked each v-team member the current priority, would I get the same answer?
Which dependency is at risk, and does its owner know?
What are you doing yourself that is really someone else's accountability?
How does another ATS confirm a v-team commitment without absorbing another role's accountability?
listenFor: Priorities that live only in the ATS's head, owners assigned in a document but never agreed in a conversation, dependencies tracked without dates, and the ATS absorbing work because delegating it feels slower. Also note v-team meetings that report status without deciding anything.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one v-team commitment row: technical priority, dependency, proposed accountable role, acceptance needed, date and escalation trigger. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, use the existing board for a priority account, or a small manual note, to draft and personally send a reviewed v-team ask with the input and proposed date. Ask the receiving owner to accept the work; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a safe description of a v-team ask and whether it was accepted, clarified or held; note any reduction in handoff ambiguity. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-USPSI-ATS-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-USPSI-ATS-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-USPSI-ATS-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. PLC-USPSI-CE-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-USPSI-CE-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-USPSI-CE-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

activities.name: Build the commercial decision brief

activities.prompt:

Include contract context, proposed structure, concessions or terms requiring review, current approvals, renewal or consumption risk, likely customer questions, authority boundaries, and the next commercial decision. USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. activities.description: Give each prioritized commercial risk an observable trigger, so it is acted on at a defined point rather than watched until it is late.
activities.prompt:
For each prioritized commercial risk, state the observable condition that means it has to be acted on now rather than watched, who acts when that condition is met, and what they do first. Keep internal steps separate from anything the customer is asked to do. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercial structure decides whether a deal can move. Focus on comparing options before the structure hardens.
keyTalkingPoints: The goal is not to create an offer. The goal is to compare viable structures, surface trade-offs, and name the approval path while options still exist.
discussionQuestions: What option is the deal implicitly assuming? Which approval or exception would surprise the team later? What trade-off should be explicit before negotiation?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Compare viable commercial structures'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from possible structures to the smallest options matrix that makes the decision clearer. No Extended follow-up is listed for this placement. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Commercial options expose viable trade-offs, customer constraints and approval dependencies before negotiation narrows choice. Recommendation is separate from authority to offer terms. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live opportunity, approved commercial context, known constraints, and the current approval or exception question.
facilitatorQuestions: Which commercial option is most plausible? What trade-off would change the decision? Where would this break if an approval requirement appears late?
listenFor: One default structure being treated as the only option; approval path ambiguity; pricing, term, or concession trade-offs not stated; and assumptions that need CE or Deal Desk review.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build a two-option commercial matrix: customer intent, known agreement mechanics, trade-off, authoritative source gap and approval dependency. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, build a commercial options matrix for one live deal and identify which option needs approval you do not hold. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized approval dependency or trade-off discovered and whether it prevented an unapproved offer or preserved an alternative. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Reviewers do not need more history. They need the recommendation, options, assumptions, risks, and decision requested.
keyTalkingPoints: A commercial decision narrative should separate facts from judgment. It should show why this structure, what alternatives were considered, and who must review it.
discussionQuestions: What would a reviewer need to say yes, no, or not yet? Which assumption is unsupported? What customer impact needs to be explained plainly?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the commercial decision narrative'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from deal facts to the internal recommendation and the decision being requested. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test commercial structure assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Commercial narratives should make assumptions and customer consequences inspectable by the authorized reviewer. Reviewer questions are useful evidence, not failure. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring a reviewed deal option, known assumptions, transition considerations, and the audience for the recommendation.
facilitatorQuestions: Which recommendation would a reviewer understand quickly? What assumption needs evidence? Which reviewer or decision owner is missing?
listenFor: Narratives that bury the ask; options without trade-offs; customer impact omitted; and transition or migration risks stated without a source.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one commercial recommendation outline: decision requested, evidenced facts, options/trade-offs, customer impact, caveat and authorized reviewer. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which deal assumption changed when you inspected the evidence, and who owns the next decision or approval?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, write the commercial recommendation for one deal in a form a reviewer could act on without asking you a question. Verify claims and commercial or approval boundaries with the accountable owner; AI is advisory. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized assumption challenged or clarified and whether it improved the recommendation; no case or terms are required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.prompt:

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercial execution stalls when owners, evidence, and approval handoffs are implied. Focus on making them explicit.
keyTalkingPoints: Execution is not just follow-up. It is approval routing, evidence readiness, exception handling, ownership, and escalation without overstating authority.
discussionQuestions: Which handoff is implicit today? What evidence is missing for the next approver? Where could ECIF, Deal Desk, finance, policy, or legal review be needed?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Clarify ECIF commercial and approval dependencies'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the full execution path to the single blocker and owner that must be handled next. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test approval and execution assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Commercial execution depends on verified approval state and accepted ownership. Mapping the path matters when it exposes the next governed decision and missing evidence. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one in-flight deal or investment dependency, its known approval stage, and the evidence or owner currently missing.
facilitatorQuestions: Which handoff or approval is the deal actually waiting on? What evidence is missing? Who owns the next decision, and what should not be represented as approved?
listenFor: Approval status overstated; handoffs without owners; ECIF, finance, Deal Desk, legal, or policy dependencies hidden; and blockers described without the next governed action.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one approval-path row: required decision, evidence, current status or unknown, authorized owner, sequence dependency and next question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which handoff is still assumed rather than accepted, and what owner, request, or date would make it actionable?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, map the approval path for one deal and confirm the first owner knows it is coming. Ask the receiving owner to accept the work; do not commit their capacity or send messages automatically. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized approval or execution gap checked and whether the owner clarified the next step; a cleared blocker is not required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activitySteps: 1. Supply dated renewal and executed-date excerpts, confirmed lead times and review date.

activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial leverage is a function of how early you saw it coming. A renewal found with three weeks left is a different negotiation from the same renewal found with three months.

activities.description: Challenge the value evidence, expansion claims and approval assumptions in a renewal strategy before they reach the customer.
activities.prompt:
Review the renewal strategy for unsupported commercial assumptions, value evidence gaps, customer constraints, policy dependencies, approval needs, expansion claims, and unresolved decisions.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: Renewal assumption and risk register with evidence gaps, owners, and required decisions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE separates expansion claims that are evidenced from those that are hoped for. A renewal strategy that prices in unearned expansion negotiates from a position the customer does not recognize.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. The renewal strategy; the value evidence behind each claim; the approval requirements and customer constraints.
activities.whyThisMatters: If the renewal strategy will fail, it should fail while there is still time to change it.

activities.name: Map the renewal decision gates and who clears each one
activities.description: Turn the renewal strategy into the decision gates it must pass, with who clears each one and what missing it costs.
activities.prompt:
Turn the renewal strategy into the decision gates it has to pass, in order. For each gate, state what must be true to clear it, the person on either side who clears it, the evidence they will ask for, and what happens to the renewal date if that gate is missed. Mark the gates that can run in parallel and the ones that genuinely cannot. Where the customer controls a gate, say what I can do to make clearing it easy for them. Work from the material I have supplied rather than looking it up, and where a piece of it is missing, name the gap instead of filling it.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: The renewal decision gates in order with clearing criteria, the person who clears each, the evidence required, the date impact of missing it, and which gates can run in parallel.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE confirms timing checkpoints against the actual agreement dates before the plan is used. Renewal mechanics are date-driven, and missing an anniversary or notice window loses options that cannot be recovered. The CE also decides which gates genuinely cannot run in parallel, and confirms that anyone named as clearing a customer-side gate has agreed to that.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. The validated renewal strategy; the renewal date and approval lead times; the internal and customer owners.
activities.whyThisMatters: A renewal plan is a list until you know which gate stops it and who holds that gate.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal risk is visible before the renewal date if commercial structure, value evidence, and approval needs are inspected early.
keyTalkingPoints: A renewal is not only a date. It is a commercial strategy with structure, risk, expansion potential, concessions, and approval path.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal risk is already visible? What expansion is supported by evidence? What approval or structure question should not wait?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Review the renewal portfolio for commercial trigger dates'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from renewal principles to one renewal actually on the horizon. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Stress-test renewal strategy assumptions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Renewal strategy uses verified agreement timing, economics and value while preserving commercial options. Expansion needs evidence and authorized decisions, not headroom alone. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one renewal, approved context, current structure, risk signal, and expansion or approval question.
facilitatorQuestions: Which renewal has the least remaining room to change its commercial path? What agreement date, customer evidence or approval dependency changes the priority? How does a peer surface that risk early enough for CE intervention?
listenFor: Renewals treated as administrative; risk noticed inside the last quarter; and expansion pursued without evidence of realized value.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one renewal workback: agreement event/date, customer evidence, commercial risk, remaining options, CE/DAE/partner ownership and next check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence changes the renewal or expansion approach, and which customer or owner decision must follow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, build a renewal strategy for one account using real agreement and discount data, not recollection. Verify evidence; commercial terms, forecast commitment and approval stay with accountable owners. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized renewal assumption confirmed or changed and whether it improved timing or the next review; omit agreement and discount data. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-USPSI-CE-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-USPSI-CE-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-USPSI-CE-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

PLC-USPSI-CSA-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-USPSI-CSA-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-USPSI-CSA-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

activities.name: Analyze consumption trajectory and shortfall drivers
activities.description: Ask what certified consumption data says. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt:
Use only approved user-provided report excerpts and plan or milestone records, with source, scope, and as-of/freshness date. Identify missing records instead of assuming access. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the customer and relevant period, analyze the documented consumption trajectory and compare it with the supplied plan or milestone view. Break down the largest changes by available dimension, identify evidence-supported contributors to potential shortfall, show supporting metrics, and state what the records cannot answer. A human verifies every source and decides.
