activities.name: Design the consumption intervention plan
activities.description: Build the intervention that changes the consumption trajectory, with the owner and the checkpoint that will show whether it moved.
activities.prompt:
Turn the evidenced consumption causes into an intervention plan. For each, define the action, who owns it on both sides, the dependency that could block it, the date you would expect to see movement, and the telemetry that would confirm it. Separate the causes you can act on technically from the commercial or customer-driven ones, and route those to the role that owns them rather than carrying them. Rank by the size of the gap each one closes.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: A ranked consumption intervention plan with owners, blocking dependencies, expected movement dates and confirming telemetry, with non-technical causes routed to their owners.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSA confirms the customer-side owner exists before the intervention plan is used, and does not take ownership of the consumption plan itself. Consumption interventions depend on customer action, and a plan with an unconfirmed owner on the other side simply does not start. The CSA owns the technical milestones that feed the plan, not the plan.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. activities.whyThisMatters: A technical intervention needs customer ownership and a measurable signal, not ownership of the entire consumption plan.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Most of us have at some point defended a number we were not fully sure about. Focus on fixing the signal, not the spreadsheet.
keyTalkingPoints: A gap is usually three problems wearing one label: not enough, not moving, or dated wrong.
Certified data settles arguments opinion cannot.
Correction is judgment work. Recommendations are proposals; you decide.
discussionQuestions: Where do consumption or usage signals become technical work for you?
Which shortfall signal is most likely to hide a technical cause?
What evidence would you need before owning an intervention?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Analyze consumption trajectory and shortfall drivers'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the report signal to one technical cause or blocker that can be validated this week. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate the consumption gap analysis', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Consumption diagnosis separates technical causes from other drivers using confirmed measure definitions. Choose an owned intervention and keep unsupported causes provisional. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved, user-supplied consumption or usage report excerpt with source, scope and as-of date, plus the technical context it does not show.
facilitatorQuestions: Which consumption movement matters enough to investigate, and what baseline and period make it comparable? What technical cause is evidenced rather than inferred? How does another CSA choose an intervention that can actually test that cause?
listenFor: Report signals separated from technical cause; assumptions about customer intent; missing owners; and interventions that require architecture or workload context.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one consumption exception row: baseline/period, movement, possible technical cause, distinguishing evidence, intervention owner and next check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which consumption signal changed your interpretation, and what technical risk or owner must be checked before acting?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a consumption-gap hypothesis against permitted evidence and confirmed metric definitions, then agree or route the intervention with its owner. Keep the cause provisional if evidence is incomplete. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized consumption hypothesis checked and whether it changed the diagnosis or intervention owner. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

Second, a short internal alignment brief for the account team: what you will recommend, what they need to know before the meeting, which decisions are not yours to make, and who must agree before the customer hears it. activities.name: Rehearse the architecture recommendation
activities.description: Role-play and coach a technical advisory conversation.
activities.prompt:
Using the supplied approved advisory plan, act as a hypothetical technical stakeholder. Ask one question at a time and wait for my response for three exchanges, focusing on the highest-impact architecture tradeoff, a security or operational prerequisite, and the next decision. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A useful advisory brief makes the intended decision and supporting evidence clear. Focus on one recommendation and the questions that could change it.
keyTalkingPoints: A brief is not a summary. It is a position plus the questions that would change it.
The intended outcome is the part most preparation leaves out, and it changes how the meeting runs.
Anticipated objections are cheaper than recovered ones.
discussionQuestions: Which upcoming conversation needs a recommendation, not just a summary?
What evidence would make the advisory position credible?
What customer decision should the conversation advance?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Prepare the technical advisory conversation'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from generic preparation to one upcoming conversation and its intended customer decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate the evidence behind the advisory recommendation', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Technical advice connects a grounded recommendation and alternatives to the customer decision. Internal alignment does not establish customer agreement. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming technical advisory conversation, the intended decision, and the approved sources you would trust for preparation.
facilitatorQuestions: What technical decision should the advisory conversation advance? Which recommendation can you defend from current evidence, and what is missing? What objection did a peer use to improve the ask or fallback?
listenFor: Preparation that summarizes but does not decide; evidence gaps; customer facts needing review; and advisory recommendations without a named decision.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one advisory brief: customer decision, evidence-qualified recommendation, missing fact, likely objection, intended ask and fallback. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What evidence would make this customer conversation credible, and what decision or question still belongs to a person?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, prepare one advisory conversation around the decision you need, not the content you have. Review claims and decide personally what to say or send; do not imply customer agreement. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized recommendation or ask sharpened and whether review made the advisory conversation more useful. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

Test constraints and cross-environment dependencies before reviewers or customers rely on it. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one architecture decision or design assumption, the known constraints, and the evidence you would use to compare options.

Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A design that has not been argued against has not really been validated. Focus on the proof, and about being clear which readiness call is yours and which belongs to somebody else.
keyTalkingPoints: Design and proof are one motion. A design the customer cannot see is a document.
Success criteria set before the work are the only ones that count.
AI accelerates the assembly. The architecture judgment stays human.
discussionQuestions: Which dependency could make the design fail in production?
What proof is small enough to validate the decision?
Who owns the next technical decision after validation?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Validate the evidence behind the technical decision path'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Use the supplied prior technical decision path and approved evidence to review one assumed decision, owner or slip risk. The alternative Featured validation-path intervention practice needs the prior validation plan and reviewed gaps supplied before the session; do not run both sequentially live. Investment-readiness Extended work applies only when proposed or funded scope is relevant, never as funding approval. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Design the architecture intervention plan', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Readiness follows proportionate validation of the design and its critical dependencies. Keep technical proof distinct from delivery ownership and respect agreed stop conditions. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring the approved technical decision path, validation plan and supporting evidence from the prior design huddle, with known owners, constraints and open proof gaps. These support the Featured evidence review and validation-path plan without requiring funding. Bring approved case or proposed investment scope only if choosing an investment-specific Extended practice.
facilitatorQuestions: Which decision in the prior technical path is being assumed rather than owned and scheduled? What gap in the supplied evidence could change readiness? How would a peer define the smallest proof without expanding funded scope or treating funding as approval?
listenFor: Validation scoped too broadly; unowned prerequisites; proof criteria written after work begins; and investment-funded scope that may not be deliverable as designed.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one prior-design decision-path review: decision point, supplied evidence or unavailable, proposed owner/date, slip impact and smallest settling proof. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What technical assumption did the practice test, and which proof or human decision is needed before advancing?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, define the validation path for one design, including what would tell you to stop. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized validation criterion checked and whether it clarified readiness, a hold or a delivery-owner question. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Risk you find this week is a conversation. The same risk found by the customer is an escalation. Focus on finding it earlier.
keyTalkingPoints: A health score can tell you something is wrong. It rarely tells you what to do.
Every risk needs an owner and a date or it is an observation.
AI is good at surfacing signal. Prioritizing it is judgment.
discussionQuestions: Which technical risk is visible now but not yet owned?
What is evidence, and what is interpretation?
What intervention could prevent this from becoming customer-visible?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build a technical health evidence brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Technical health combines recorded evidence with customer and team signals. Investigate what data misses without treating a missing metric as proof of risk. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one technical health signal, risk, or dependency you are tracking, plus the source you would use to validate it.
facilitatorQuestions: Which technical-health signal is a symptom rather than a cause? What evidence makes the risk real, and who can intervene? How does another CSA separate technical action from CSAM, support, delivery or commercial ownership?
listenFor: Health scores treated as causes; risks without owners or dates; technical blockers becoming customer-visible; and actions that require CSAM, support, delivery, or commercial alignment.

Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which risk is supported by current evidence, what remains uncertain, and who is accountable for the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, find one technical health risk that is not visible in the data, name who would have known about it, and take it to its owner. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. activities.name: Create the technical progress and value narrative
activities.description: Synthesize approved technical evidence. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt:
Using the approved architecture, delivery, adoption, consumption, optimization and risk materials I am attaching for the customer, produce two linked outputs. First, the customer-facing value narrative: progress connected to supported outcomes, risks and decisions explained, commitments and owners identified, next technical actions proposed. Second, the internal governance readout for the account and delivery team: milestone status, evidence still missing and who owns producing it, risks that need a decision, and the next intervention. Separate evidence from interpretation and flag unsupported value claims. My delivery context is the applicable global, field, or SME&C coverage; reflect that in what you recommend.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: Two linked outputs: the customer-facing value narrative, and the internal governance readout for the account and delivery team.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSA confirms the link between technical progress and claimed value, and decides what belongs in the internal readout rather than the customer narrative. Those two are frequently assembled separately and joined afterwards, and a link that does not hold is what a skeptical stakeholder tests first. Evidence gaps belong internally before they are discovered externally.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Approved review sources; audience; period. Your delivery context, whether global delivery, field delivery or SME&C coverage, since it changes which next action is right.
activities.whyThisMatters: Customer and internal views should agree on evidence while respecting different audiences.

activities.name: Validate the evidence behind the customer value story
activities.description: Check that the value story is built on measured outcomes rather than activity, before the customer's finance function does it for you.
activities.prompt:
Review the technical value narrative. For each claimed outcome, state whether it is measured or projected, the baseline it is compared against, and whether the measurement basis has changed since the commitment was made. Separate delivered value from activity completed, and flag any claim a finance reviewer would reject.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: A value-claim review separating measured from projected outcomes, with baseline integrity and finance-review risk per claim.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSA separates delivered value from activity completed. Activity is easy to evidence and is not what was committed, and a value story built on it fails at the first executive question.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. The draft value narrative; the outcomes committed in the business case; the measurement basis and baseline used. Your delivery context, whether global delivery, field delivery or SME&C coverage, since it changes which next action is right.
activities.whyThisMatters: Measured outcomes are different from completed activity; preserve that distinction.

activities.name: Compare delivered value with the supplied business-case baseline
activities.description: Review measured versus projected outcomes at a human-owned checkpoint; usage alone does not prove a business result.
activities.prompt:
Compare the supplied agreed business case, baseline, current outcome evidence and prior review. Show measured versus projected status, supported change, period and measurement basis per outcome. Treat usage as outcome evidence only where the supplied model supports the link. Identify non-comparable measures and evidence still needed. Do not extrapolate without a supplied model or establish ongoing tracking.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: One-time outcome comparison with measured/projected/unknown status, baseline comparability and evidence gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CSA verifies the measurement basis has not changed and confirms every figure before it is shown to the customer as a delivered result.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied business case, outcome measures, baseline, current measured evidence, projection model if permitted and prior review; delivery context.
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved business case, baseline and current outcome evidence with dates/definitions.
2. Confirm comparability and any usage-to-outcome model.
3. Build a one-time comparison manually or in Copilot if permitted.
4. Separate observed outcomes, supported projections and unknowns.
5. Have accountable technical/financial owners verify customer claims and agree any next human checkpoint separately.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.
activities.whyThisMatters: Comparing actual outcomes with the original baseline prevents usage growth becoming an unsupported value claim.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Value without evidence tends to read as opinion. Focus on the evidence, and who needs to hear it, inside as well as outside.
keyTalkingPoints: The customer defines value. Our job is to evidence it in their terms.
Causality is easy to claim and hard to support. Say what the data supports.
A value story nobody hears is not value realized.
discussionQuestions: What value story would the customer actually recognize?
Which evidence supports the story, and which part is still only expected?
What next technical action would make the value more real?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the technical progress and value narrative'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from value language to the evidence package and next technical action. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Validate the evidence behind the customer value story', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Technical value connects progress to customer-recognized outcomes without overstating attribution. Internal alignment and customer claims need the same evidence and limits. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one technical review, business review, or value-realization example and the evidence behind it.
facilitatorQuestions: Which technical progress claim can the customer trace to an agreed outcome? What source proves realization rather than deployment or usage alone? How would a peer state the limitation and the next technical action in the review?
listenFor: Progress not connected to agreed outcomes; unsupported realization claims; missing source links; and follow-through that lacks owners.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or approved context is unavailable, use a sanitized supplied example or a clearly labeled synthetic case. On paper, draft one technical-value claim with the agreed outcome, observed progress, source/date, realization limit, reviewer and next technical action. Mark evidence, assumptions and unknowns; the draft does not establish realized value or customer agreement. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient. Any later AI run must use project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot and approved supplied inputs.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which outcome can you substantiate for this audience, and what claim or next action still needs validation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, evidence one technical outcome in terms the customer would use themselves, and name what the account team needs to see internally. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized outcome phrasing or attribution caveat improved and whether it made the value discussion more credible. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-USPSI-CSA-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-USPSI-CSA-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-USPSI-CSA-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

PLC-USPSI-CSAM-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-USPSI-CSAM-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-USPSI-CSAM-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

activities.name: Draft the outcome-anchored success-plan view
activities.description: Draft or refresh the CSP around customer outcomes, milestones, owners, risks and review points. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt:
Using approved customer priorities, recent meetings, CSP notes and delivery updates for the account, draft a Customer Success Plan view. Include outcome, success measure, milestone, owner, dependency, risk, next customer review point and evidence source. For each priority, say whether the customer has actually stated it or whether it is only recorded in the system, because the two often differ. Where the plan depends on sequencing, start, or end dates not captured in approved source records, name the record where each value is maintained and the human owner; verify the dates manually. Separate sourced facts from suggested updates.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: A human-reviewed, outcome-anchored success-plan view with evidence gaps; each priority labeled as customer-stated or present in a specified approved source record; and a named record location and human owner for items not captured in the source records.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides which outcomes the customer would recognize as their own, and does not treat a recorded priority as a confirmed one. A success plan built from Microsoft's view of the account describes what we intend to deliver, which is not the same as what the customer is trying to achieve. Planning around a priority nobody has said out loud costs the quarter it takes to find out.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Customer priorities, existing CSP or notes, recent customer meetings, delivery milestones and known risks; and what the customer has said in their own words, which may not match the recorded priority.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most success-plan toil is assembling scattered signals. The CSAM should spend judgment on the outcome and commitment.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Success planning is not documentation. It is how the customer and Microsoft agree what progress means.
keyTalkingPoints: A plan should name outcomes, milestones, owners, risks and review points. AI can draft and inspect the plan, but you validate the customer priority and commitment.
discussionQuestions: When did your success plan last change because the customer's priorities changed?
Which milestone in it would the customer not recognize as theirs?
What is in the plan because it is genuinely the outcome, and what is there because it was easy to measure?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft the outcome-anchored success-plan view'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the plan as it stands to the single outcome you will make observable this week. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Create the CSDR-ready success-plan narrative', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Governable success plans link confirmed outcomes to observable measures and accountable milestones. Simplify stale detail with the plan owner, not by dropping real obligations. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one active customer priority, its current CSP or success-plan notes and the latest review or action list.
facilitatorQuestions: Which outcome in your plan is stated in the customer's words rather than ours?
Which milestone has drifted without anyone deciding to move it?
What would you remove from the plan today to make it governable?
How does another CSAM test that the customer recognizes and accepts the stated outcome?
listenFor: Plans built around Microsoft milestones rather than customer outcomes, measures chosen because they are available rather than meaningful, owners who have never agreed to their commitment, and plans so long that nobody governs them. Also note drift being reported rather than decided.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer-success-plan row: customer-recognized outcome, measure, milestone, proposed owner, dependency and review point. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed your priority or plan, and which assumption needs checking before the next action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, make a success-plan outcome more observable and propose simplification if useful. Confirm changes with the plan owner rather than remove obligations to shorten the plan. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized outcome made more observable or plan item clarified and whether it made review easier to govern. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on moving from signal review to intervention. Scores help, but action changes the customer trajectory.
keyTalkingPoints: Health work spans adoption, usage, support, delivery, sentiment and stakeholder change. You must separate noise from the risk that matters most right now.
discussionQuestions: Which customer worries you for reasons the health score does not capture?
What did someone say in a recent conversation that has not made it into any system?
Which risk have you been watching rather than acting on, and why?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Rank customer health risks and drivers'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the ranked health view to one intervention with an owner, a due date, and an escalation threshold. If a participant rejects or overrides the draft, ask which evidence or workflow condition it missed and compare the correction. Discuss only permitted details; do not assume this review sends anything to a transcript service. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare the customer-safe health message', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Customer health judgment identifies actionable causes rather than collecting scores. Confirm a feasible intervention and established escalation guidance or an agreed review trigger. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved, user-supplied health, adoption, support or delivery-risk excerpt with source and as-of date, plus the known owner and open question. Record unavailable inputs; do not assume connected health or advisory access.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the driver behind the score, not the score itself?
Which signal came from a person rather than a system, and did it survive into the record?
Who owns the intervention, and by when does it have to start to matter?
What conversation-based signal did a peer find that the health score missed?
listenFor: Health scores treated as the diagnosis rather than the symptom, risks the team has normalized, interventions without owners, and conversation-based signals that never reached the data. Also note the customer's own view of their health being absent from the discussion.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer-health row: score/signal, evidenced driver, customer view, intervention, proposed owner/date and escalation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which risk is supported by current evidence, what remains uncertain, and who is accountable for the intervention?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review the most material actionable risk, verify its driver and ask its owner about a feasible intervention. Use confirmed escalation guidance or agree a review trigger; do not invent a policy threshold or require a minimum-size risk list. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized risk driver checked and whether the owner confirmed an intervention or held it; no risk-list quota is needed. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Executive alignment is where customer success becomes visible to the people who can sponsor, unblock or redirect it.
keyTalkingPoints: Stakeholder maps should show influence, decision rights, relationship health and the next ask. AI can assemble signals; you decide the message and timing.
discussionQuestions: Who is the most senior person at this customer you have never spoken to directly?
Which stakeholder could stop this work, and do you know what they care about?
When an executive last engaged, what did they actually want from us?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the stakeholder and influence map'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the stakeholder map to the one relationship you will build this month and the reason they would take the meeting. facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Executive alignment rests on observed priorities, relationship coverage and a useful ask. Inferred influence or sponsorship needs confirmation before guiding engagement. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one upcoming executive or sponsor conversation, current stakeholder context and an approved organizational sketch if available. If the map is missing, identify one relationship or decision-rights gap rather than trying to build the entire organization in the huddle.
facilitatorQuestions: Which stakeholder can stop this, and what do they need to believe?

What would you ask the executive for if you had fifteen minutes tomorrow?

listenFor: Stakeholder maps built from org charts rather than observed behavior, executive relationships that exist only through an intermediary, engagement plans with no ask, and blockers identified without a plan to reach them. Also note assuming a quiet stakeholder is a supportive one.

activities.name: Create the v-team orchestration brief
activities.description: Synthesize current workstreams, owners, handoffs, decisions and blockers. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt:
Analyze only approved customer-success records and excerpts that I provide, including meeting notes, email excerpts, CRM-derived fields or excerpts, support records, and delivery context, with source, scope, and as-of/freshness date. A human verifies the analysis and makes all decisions; do not include restricted customer or personal data unless policy permits. Any CRM-derived fields or excerpts must be user-provided with source, scope, and as-of/freshness date. Do not assume access to source records; a human verifies the information and makes all decisions. List every active workstream with owner, input needed, due date, dependency, blocker, decision needed, and recommended next action. Classify each workstream using the first applicable rule: (1) dated source evidence shows something actually moved after my last-review date: confirmed progress; (2) last-modified or last-activity date is after that date: record changed, progress unconfirmed; (3) that date is on/before it: no recorded change since review, explicitly not evidence that nothing happened; (4) date absent or too imprecise: movement unknown, even if other dates such as a due date exist. Flag any workstream where a specialist or partner appears engaged but no CSAM touchpoint is recorded; say the touchpoint may have happened but not been logged and what would confirm it. State which sources you actually had, flag missing owners and stale dates, and do not infer progress.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: V-team orchestration brief listing every active workstream, marking each as showing confirmed progress, as record changed with progress unconfirmed, as no recorded change since the last review, or as movement unknown where there is no comparable date, with handoffs, and any workstream where a specialist or partner appears engaged with no CSAM touchpoint recorded.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides what is still worth doing, and treats the brief as a picture that moves rather than a model that holds. Orchestration briefs accumulate actions that made sense when they were added, and carrying them forward unexamined is how a v-team stops reading the brief. The work is coordinated in conversations, so the brief is only ever as current as the last one.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. User-provided approved account records, workstream notes, delivery updates, and support context, with source, scope, and as-of date; only the minimum necessary approved CRM/MSX fields or excerpts with their last-modified or last-activity date; and the date you last reviewed the account. A human verifies the source records and decides. Do not include restricted customer or personal data unless policy permits. A human verifies every source record and claim, makes all decisions, and performs any authorized updates; Microsoft 365 Copilot does not make record changes.
activitySteps: 1. A human provides the minimum necessary approved workstream and touchpoint records, including CRM/MSX-derived fields or excerpts only when needed, with source, scope, and as-of date. This workflow uses only supplied inputs and makes no source-record changes; a human verifies and decides.
2. Export or copy only approved, permitted fields into a dated snapshot so the brief uses fixed inputs.
3. Supply that snapshot alongside meeting notes, delivery updates, and support context; otherwise review them manually.
4. Check every cited source against the materials actually supplied.

5. Distinguish confirmed progress, record changes with progress unconfirmed, no recorded change since the last review, and unknown status. Treat no recorded change as a prompt to ask the owner, not as a finding about them. Separately follow up where a partner appears engaged but no touchpoint is recorded.

If Copilot is unavailable or not permitted, complete the same bounded review manually from approved sanitized evidence or a fictional example; never bypass restrictions. Sending, publication, implementation or record updates are separate authorized human actions.

discussionQuestions: Where does work currently stop between Microsoft, the partner, and the customer?
Who believes they own something that someone else also believes they own?
Which handoff have you personally been compensating for?

facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Customer-success orchestration makes both sides of the handoff explicit and accepted. A date or listed owner is not agreement until the parties confirm it. facilitatorQuestions: Where exactly does work stop between the three parties?

activities.name: Identify adoption friction and next activation actions
activities.description: Map usage gaps to customer priorities and build a short activation plan. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt:
For the account and workload, compare current adoption or usage signals with customer priorities and licensed or committed scope. Identify unused paid entitlement only where supplied licensing, purchase and usage evidence supports it; otherwise flag missing commercial evidence. Identify the top friction points, the stakeholder owner and a four-week activation plan with measurable milestones. For each proposed cause, mark it as shown by the data, stated by the customer, or still unresolved, and do not treat a customer's explanation as proof on its own. Work from the approved report excerpts I supply and the context I supply alongside it. Where something you need sits in a surface or conversation you cannot see, say so and name what you would need, rather than reconciling it from assumption.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: Evidence-bounded friction analysis and proposed four-week activation plan; unused paid entitlement only where compatible purchase/licensing/usage evidence supports it, with each cause marked observed, customer-stated or unresolved.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CSAM validates whether the adoption action is relevant to the customer priority and achievable with available owners.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Supplied dated usage/adoption excerpts, customer priorities, workload scope, stakeholder context and prior actions; customer-stated explanations with source/date. Include permitted purchase/licensing evidence only if checking unused paid entitlement; otherwise leave that question unresolved.
activities.whyThisMatters: Adoption work matters when it changes customer behavior tied to a business outcome.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Adoption activity does not automatically become customer value. Focus on proving and accelerating value realization.
keyTalkingPoints: Adoption plans should link underused features, customer priorities, behavior-change actions, milestones and value evidence. AI can draft the plan and value narrative; you validate truth and relevance.
discussionQuestions: What value has this customer actually realized that you could prove today?
Where is adoption stalled, and do you know why or are you guessing?
What would the customer say they got, if asked without us in the room?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify adoption friction and next activation actions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the value picture to one claim you will evidence, and one adoption barrier you will actually diagnose. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Draft the sponsor value update', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Adoption and value are different claims: investigate barriers and verify entitlement and usage before acting. Customer statements and measures have limits that must stay visible. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one workload or solution where adoption progress, friction or value proof needs to be clarified, and the recent customer conversation where the reason was discussed, if there was one.
facilitatorQuestions: What value can you evidence today, and what are you asserting?
Where adoption stalled, do you know the cause or are you inferring it?
Would the customer describe the value the same way you just did?
What evidence would another CSAM require before describing usage as customer value?
listenFor: Value claimed from usage figures alone, adoption barriers guessed rather than investigated, realized value described in Microsoft terms rather than customer outcomes, and proof that would not survive a procurement conversation. Also note value stories that have never been said back to the customer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one adoption/value row: friction hypothesis, distinguishing evidence, customer outcome, claimed value, caveat and activation owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which adoption cause is evidenced rather than guessed, and what supports the customer-recognized value claim?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a customer-recognized value claim or adoption barrier using permitted data or conversation. Verify unused-entitlement hypotheses with the owner; finding an unused entitlement is not required. Verify evidence and keep the next decision with the accountable human owner. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized adoption barrier or value claim checked and whether it improved intervention or avoided an unsupported entitlement claim. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Create the escalation and recovery brief
activities.description: Consolidate incident, support, delivery and customer communication context into a grounded brief. Live huddle: choose ONE Featured practice, not the full menu; use an approved existing artifact for any prerequisite and leave additional builds for later.
activities.prompt:
Create an escalation and recovery brief for the issue. Include customer impact, current status, timeline, owners, decisions needed, risks, next action, next update cadence and what is unknown. Draw on the project record, the chat threads and what came out of one-to-one conversations with the customer, not only the incident record. For each action, name who does the work; where that is you, say what it displaces this week. Use only approved sources and separate facts from assumptions.

USPSI project practice: Use only minimum necessary supplied inputs approved for this Copilot use, account scope and audience; sanitize sensitive internal, customer, commercial or personal content before entry and withhold classified or restricted material unless explicitly permitted. Include source and as-of date. No CRM/MSX, mailbox, meeting or live-system connector access, scheduled checks, persistent memory or writes are assumed. Return draft text/tables; native artifacts are not assumed. Cite evidence; mark stale, missing or conflicting facts unknown. Label unconfirmed owners, dates, eligibility and conclusions as proposals or questions. Authorized humans retain procurement/policy judgments, commercial/investment approvals, commitments, implementation and publication. If Copilot or sharing is not permitted, use approved evidence manually or a fictional example; do not bypass restrictions.
activities.expectedOutput: Escalation and recovery brief where every action names who does the work, and anything the CSAM has taken on names what it displaces.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CSAM decides what the customer is told and when, and leads the recovery rather than absorbing it. An escalation brief assembled from internal systems holds detail that is accurate internally and damaging externally, and the sequencing of a difficult message is a relationship decision. Work the CSAM takes on personally comes out of the consumption and value work nobody else is doing.
activities.requiredContext: Supply only minimum necessary evidence approved for this use/audience, sanitized as required, with source, account scope and as-of date. Incident or support notes, delivery updates, customer communications, owners, timelines and current risks; plus the project record, relevant chat threads and what surfaced in one-to-one customer conversations.
activities.whyThisMatters: In escalation moments, clarity protects trust and reduces duplicated status chasing.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Escalations test trust. Focus on moving from scattered status to a grounded recovery plan.
keyTalkingPoints: A useful brief names customer impact, current status, owner, decision needed, next action and update cadence. AI can consolidate threads; you validate tone, accuracy and accountability.
discussionQuestions: What issue are you currently managing that should probably already be escalated?
What is holding you back: evidence, ownership, or the conversation itself?
When an escalation last worked well, what made it work?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create the escalation and recovery brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the delivery risk to a recovery plan with an owner, a customer message, and a defined exit condition. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build the recovery action register', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot. USPSI execution is Microsoft 365 Copilot only within the approved project scope, using permitted supplied inputs, or manual practice. Do not assume live retrieval, background monitoring or writeback.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: USPSI: Recovery plans need feasible delivery commitments, clear communication and work returned to its accountable owner. Escalation does not make an unaccepted date achievable. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one live or recent delivery risk, incident, support issue or overdue commitment, and be ready to say which parts of it you have ended up doing yourself. For the recovery-register practice, supply the validated escalation brief and approved owner context, including any agreed dates or escalation thresholds; unresolved details stay unconfirmed.
facilitatorQuestions: What threshold would have told you to escalate this a month ago?
What does the recovery plan commit us to, and can we deliver it?
What will you tell the customer, and when?
What recovery commitment has a peer had to narrow to what delivery could actually support?
listenFor: Escalation delayed to avoid an uncomfortable conversation, recovery plans that promise more than delivery can support, customer communication planned after the internal fix rather than alongside it, and escalations raised without a defined exit. Also note the same issue recurring without anyone treating the pattern.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one recovery brief: risk, escalation trigger needing confirmation, feasible recovery action, customer-safe draft message, owner and exit condition. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. For USPSI, the manual route is sufficient; any later AI run remains project-scoped Microsoft 365 Copilot with approved supplied inputs only.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which recovery commitment can delivery support, and which absorbed task should return to its accountable owner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review a delivery issue with its owner, confirm feasible recovery and agree escalation or resolution. Humans review customer communication and proposed ownership transfers. If inputs or access are missing, use a sanitized manual example and identify the gap rather than inventing facts. For USPSI, use Microsoft 365 Copilot only with authorized supplied information; otherwise complete the same check manually. Do not assume connected-source or MSX access.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized recovery assumption or ownership gap corrected and whether it made communication or delivery action more realistic. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.
