activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.

PLC-LDR-LDR-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-LDR-LDR-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-LDR-LDR-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

activities.name: Reconcile strategic, market, customer, and performance signals
activities.description: Prepare this bounded human-reviewed work product: A source-dated signal reconciliation with supporting/contrary evidence, strategic relevance, gaps and one priority question.
activities.prompt: I am a leader responsible for business performance across a team, portfolio, function, or organization. Help me reconcile strategic, market, customer, and performance signals. Use only governed authorized business evidence and de-identified context I supply. Do not assume connected retrieval, niche tools, persistent agent memory or permission to expose individual employee information. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Trigger: A new planning period, strategy, market signal, or material performance change requires the leader to reset priorities and choices. Separate verified evidence, missing evidence, interpretations, assumptions, recommendations, and decision authority. Return only this activity-specific work product: A source-dated signal reconciliation with supporting/contrary evidence, strategic relevance, gaps and one priority question. Identify proposed owners, authority boundaries and review questions where supplied; leave unknowns open. Decision scope varies by level and organization; contributors provide evidence and recommendations but do not become decision holders merely by attending the review. Do not use AI to rank, score, or evaluate employees; make people or HR judgments; infer intent; make approvals; commit forecasts; change records; or send messages. If a source or agent is unavailable, say so and use permitted evidence manually. Research only approved relevant source extracts/URLs I supply for the decision and review date; do not browse beyond that boundary. If Researcher/source access is unavailable, inspect supplied extracts manually and leave unsupported claims open. Cite publisher, title, source date, link, and access date for material claims. Distinguish facts, market or customer signals, policy or guidance, competing interpretations, and unresolved questions.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-dated signal reconciliation with supporting/contrary evidence, strategic relevance, gaps and one priority question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The leader validates evidence, metric definitions, authority, and the decision or recommendation. Decision scope varies by level and organization; contributors provide evidence and recommendations but do not become decision holders merely by attending the review. No AI output is approval, forecast commitment, employee evaluation, record change, external communication, or organizational commitment.
activities.requiredContext: Leader scope, business decision, governed evidence, metric definitions, accountable action owner, and known authority boundary. Approved bounded source extracts/URLs, review date and supplied options/constraints; no internal retrieval assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Reconcile strategic, market, customer, and performance signals

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A new planning period, strategy, market signal, or material performance change requires the leader to reset priorities and choices. Focus on one decision and the evidence needed to make it.
keyTalkingPoints: Leadership decision: Choose the priorities, what changes or stops, the accountable owners, and the evidence that will demonstrate progress.
Boundary: Decision scope varies by level and organization; contributors provide evidence and recommendations but do not become decision holders merely by attending the review.
discussionQuestions: What priority changes or stops?
Which governed evidence supports that trade-off?
Who owns delivery, and what proves progress?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile strategic, market, customer, and performance signals'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Challenge the trade-offs and priority narrative', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Direction-setting translates strategy into evidenced priorities and trade-offs. Decision holders retain level- and org-specific authority; participation cannot transfer it. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted planning choice and the governed evidence behind competing priorities. Identify the actual decision authority and next owner. Exclude employee/HR data and AI-generated individual performance judgments.
facilitatorQuestions: Which evidence-backed priority changes what starts, stops or receives attention? What trade-off and measure make it actionable? How would a peer leader separate recommendation from delegated decision and field execution?
listenFor: Activity reporting without a decision, local shadow data, mixed metric definitions, assumed authority, AI-generated employee evaluation, or leader takeover of field execution. Decision scope varies by level and organization; contributors provide evidence and recommendations but do not become decision holders merely by attending the review.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one priority brief: strategy link, evidence, trade-off, what changes/stops, delegated decision owner, measure and next review. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which trade-off changed the priority, and what evidence would make you reconsider?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, review a consequential priority trade-off and record your own decision or recommendation, authority boundary and review condition. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized priority assumption clarified and whether it improved direction or the next review. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

activities.name: Inspect authorized portfolio signals and missing evidence
activities.description: Prepare this bounded human-reviewed work product: A read-only portfolio evidence strip from exact authorized supplied records with identifiers, dates, metric definitions, conflicts and gaps.
activities.prompt: I am a leader responsible for business performance across a team, portfolio, function, or organization. Help me inspect authorized portfolio signals and missing evidence. Use only governed authorized business evidence and de-identified context I supply. Do not assume connected retrieval, niche tools, persistent agent memory or permission to expose individual employee information. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Trigger: A performance, forecast, portfolio, customer, partner, or execution signal no longer matches the plan or requires a leadership decision. Separate verified evidence, missing evidence, interpretations, assumptions, recommendations, and decision authority. Return only this activity-specific work product: A read-only portfolio evidence strip from exact authorized supplied records with identifiers, dates, metric definitions, conflicts and gaps. Identify proposed owners, authority boundaries and review questions where supplied; leave unknowns open. Use certified or governed sources where designated, preserve metric definitions and dates, and do not create shadow performance reports or individual employee rankings. Do not use AI to rank, score, or evaluate employees; make people or HR judgments; infer intent; make approvals; commit forecasts; change records; or send messages. If a source or agent is unavailable, say so and use permitted evidence manually. Inspect exact authorized records within the supplied Leader decision scope. Sales Agent is optional; otherwise use dated authorized extracts or labeled synthetic rehearsal data and separate access gaps from missing evidence. Use manager or leader experiences only if available; this prompt does not establish access. Use authorized account, opportunity, pipeline, renewal, milestone, consumption, or portfolio records within the stated scope. Cite identifiers and dated facts; preserve metric definitions and flag stale, missing, or conflicting records. Do not use disaggregated or functionally identifying views to compare employees.
activities.expectedOutput: A read-only portfolio evidence strip from exact authorized supplied records with identifiers, dates, metric definitions, conflicts and gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The leader validates evidence, metric definitions, authority, and the decision or recommendation. agents.name: Scout
agents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
agents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A performance, forecast, portfolio, customer, partner, or execution signal no longer matches the plan or requires a leadership decision. Focus on one decision and the evidence needed to make it.
keyTalkingPoints: Leadership decision: Select the intervention, accountable owner, evidence gap to close, and next inspection point.
Boundary: Use certified or governed sources where designated, preserve metric definitions and dates, and do not create shadow performance reports or individual employee rankings.
discussionQuestions: Which signal merits intervention rather than more reporting?
What do its date and metric definition not prove?
What owner and evidence gap should return at inspection?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile governed performance evidence into intervention candidates'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Design a change-only exception watch for explicit approval', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Business inspection reconciles governed measures before choosing intervention. Preserve definitions and dates; avoid shadow performance reports or individual rankings. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted material signal, governed baseline and current dated evidence. Identify the actual decision authority and next owner. Exclude employee/HR data and AI-generated individual performance judgments.
facilitatorQuestions: Which governed metric or customer signal changes the intervention? Are its definition and as-of date comparable? How would a peer choose an owner and next inspection without creating a shadow performance report?
listenFor: Activity reporting without a decision, local shadow data, mixed metric definitions, assumed authority, AI-generated employee evaluation, or leader takeover of field execution. Use certified or governed sources where designated, preserve metric definitions and dates, and do not create shadow performance reports or individual employee rankings.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one intervention evidence row: governed metric definition/date, comparable movement, interpretation gap, accountable owner and next inspection. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which metric definition or gap changed intervention, and what remains too uncertain to act on?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, use one suitable Featured practice or review the question manually. Check a material business variance against the governed measure, then choose an intervention, evidence request or hold within your authority. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized measure interpretation corrected and whether it improved intervention judgment; exclude employee and raw performance data. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.description: Prepare this bounded human-reviewed work product: A dated business-evidence/gap table with exact authorized references and coaching-decision questions; no employee ranking, HR inference or expanded access.
activities.prompt: I am a leader responsible for business performance across a team, portfolio, function, or organization. Help me retrieve authorized business evidence for the coaching decision. Use only governed authorized business evidence and de-identified context I supply. Do not assume connected retrieval, niche tools, persistent agent memory or permission to expose individual employee information. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Trigger: A decision is stalled, an assumption is weak, or the same execution pattern is recurring without a clear owner-led correction. Only direct or assigned managers provide formal performance coaching; other leaders coach business decisions or subordinate leaders without assuming direct people-management authority. Do not use AI to rank, score, or evaluate employees; make people or HR judgments; infer intent; make approvals; commit forecasts; change records; or send messages. If a source or agent is unavailable, say so and use permitted evidence manually. Inspect exact authorized records within the supplied Leader decision scope. Sales Agent is optional; otherwise use dated authorized extracts or labeled synthetic rehearsal data and separate access gaps from missing evidence. Use manager or leader experiences only if available; this prompt does not establish access. Use authorized account, opportunity, pipeline, renewal, milestone, consumption, or portfolio records within the stated scope. Cite identifiers and dated facts; preserve metric definitions and flag stale, missing, or conflicting records. Do not use disaggregated or functionally identifying views to compare employees.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A decision is stalled, an assumption is weak, or the same execution pattern is recurring without a clear owner-led correction. Focus on one decision and the evidence needed to make it.
keyTalkingPoints: Leadership decision: Choose the decisive coaching question, decision criteria, owner commitment, and follow-up evidence.
Boundary: Only direct or assigned managers provide formal performance coaching; other leaders coach business decisions or subordinate leaders without assuming direct people-management authority.
discussionQuestions: Which assumption can a coaching question test?
Is this business-decision coaching or formal manager-only performance coaching?
What owner commitment and follow-up evidence are needed?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Rehearse the coaching conversation and challenge the reasoning'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Retrieve authorized business evidence for the coaching decision', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Leadership coaching tests decision quality without assuming direct people-management authority. Formal performance coaching belongs only to direct or assigned managers. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted stalled business decision, the unresolved assumption and approved evidence. Identify the actual decision authority and next owner. Exclude employee/HR data and AI-generated individual performance judgments.
facilitatorQuestions: What decision criterion should the owner explain rather than defend a score? Which coaching question tests the reasoning? How would another leader stay within assigned management authority while agreeing follow-up evidence?
listenFor: Activity reporting without a decision, local shadow data, mixed metric definitions, assumed authority, AI-generated employee evaluation, or leader takeover of field execution. Only direct or assigned managers provide formal performance coaching; other leaders coach business decisions or subordinate leaders without assuming direct people-management authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one de-identified decision-coaching plan: criterion, evidence gap, reasoning question, assigned coaching authority and follow-up evidence. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Rehearse with a peer; if alone, write both sides and mark the exchange untested, not a validated customer or coaching response.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which question exposed weak reasoning, and where does your coaching authority stop?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, rehearse a decision-quality question and seek the appropriate owner next-check agreement without employee scoring or unassigned performance coaching. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a de-identified question refined and whether it improved reasoning; no employee evaluation or coaching plan is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A high-impact customer, partner, deal, renewal, or relationship decision is blocked or requires selective leader involvement. Focus on one decision and the evidence needed to make it.
keyTalkingPoints: Leadership decision: Choose whether and how to intervene, the desired decision, leader ask, field owner, boundaries, and follow-through.
Boundary: Leadership involvement is selective and does not transfer day-to-day account, opportunity, partner, delivery, or relationship ownership away from the field team.
discussionQuestions: What selective leader intervention would change the blocked decision?
Which ask stays within authority?
How will the field owner retain day-to-day ownership afterward?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect authorized account or portfolio evidence for the intervention'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Rehearse the executive intervention and likely objections', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Strategic intervention adds value to a customer or partner decision without displacing field ownership. Leadership attention is selective, not transferred daily accountability. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted high-impact blocked decision, proposed leader ask and accountable field owner. Identify the actual decision authority and next owner. Exclude employee/HR data and AI-generated individual performance judgments.
facilitatorQuestions: What customer or partner decision warrants selective leadership intervention? What ask and limit preserve the field owner's relationship? How would a peer judge whether intervention helps more than it disrupts?
listenFor: Activity reporting without a decision, local shadow data, mixed metric definitions, assumed authority, AI-generated employee evaluation, or leader takeover of field execution. Leadership involvement is selective and does not transfer day-to-day account, opportunity, partner, delivery, or relationship ownership away from the field team.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one strategic intervention brief: customer/partner decision, sourced evidence, selective leader ask, field owner and relationship boundary. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Why is leadership intervention useful, and which relationship or execution decision stays with the field?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, validate the need and bounded ask with the field owner, then personally choose act, delegate within authority or hold. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized boundary or ask clarified and whether it strengthened field-owner follow-through; no account or partner brief is needed. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A weekly, monthly, quarterly, or event-driven leadership review requires decisions, adjustments, escalation asks, and a clear performance narrative. Focus on one decision and the evidence needed to make it.
keyTalkingPoints: Leadership decision: Confirm the decisions, adjustments, owners, escalation asks, messages to cascade, and next inspection.
Boundary: Use only the cadence and decision rights established for the relevant organization; the leader confirms the forecast, commitments, narrative, and communications.
discussionQuestions: Which review decision changes the plan?
What is evidenced, forecast or assumed in the narrative?
What message, owner and next inspection follow the decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Produce the operating review, decision log, and action register'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Design a change-only signal feed for the next review', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Operating reviews turn governed evidence into human decisions and accepted follow-through. Use established org cadence; the leader validates forecast, commitments, narrative and communication. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted current review decision, governed evidence and the narrative or escalation that needs confirmation. Identify the actual decision authority and next owner. Exclude employee/HR data and AI-generated individual performance judgments.
facilitatorQuestions: Which operating-review decision actually changes the next cycle? What governed evidence, owner and approved message support it? How would another leader communicate it while preserving the organization's actual cadence and decision rights?
listenFor: Activity reporting without a decision, local shadow data, mixed metric definitions, assumed authority, AI-generated employee evaluation, or leader takeover of field execution. Use only the cadence and decision rights established for the relevant organization; the leader confirms the forecast, commitments, narrative, and communications.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one operating-review decision log: governed evidence, decision, owner, adjustment, approved-communication gap and next inspection. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which caveat changed the decision or message, and how will next review test follow-through?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, check a consequential operating-review claim or follow-through gap and personally confirm a bounded decision or communication within authority and org rhythm. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized caveat clarified and whether it improved next review; no full pack, forecast or cascade message is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-LDR-LDR-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-LDR-LDR-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-LDR-LDR-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

PLC-ENT-MGR-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-ENT-MGR-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-ENT-MGR-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. activities.name: Separate coverage facts from unanswered transition risks
activities.description: Compare the coverage evidence and relevant role guidance to identify continuity risks before an interim ownership decision.
activities.prompt: For one account transition or coverage gap in [ATU/STU/CSU remit], review the permitted coverage snapshot I supply and the authoritative role guidance I identify. Separate customer commitments with accepted owners, unconfirmed coverage and missing evidence. Cite guidance with publisher, title, date and link; do not treat general guidance as customer proof or apply CAIP assignment rules outside their documented scope. Return the three continuity risks, the evidence needed to settle each and the role that can confirm it. Use only permitted business material I am authorized to access and share in this tool. Do not include employee or HR data, score or evaluate individuals, invent inaccessible evidence, approve investments/deals, change records, send messages or make commitments. If a source is unavailable, mark the gap and use a permitted extract or manual review.
activities.expectedOutput: A source-linked continuity-risk list with confirmed versus unconfirmed coverage, evidence gaps and role-specific confirmation questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager verifies local remit and asks the named role owner to confirm coverage; research does not assign work or establish interim ownership.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted transition/coverage snapshot, customer commitments, manager remit, named authoritative role-guidance sources and known current owners.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this activity or another Featured option; use an existing relevant business artifact rather than completing every activity in sequence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: An account transition, vacancy, or at-risk customer creates a coverage decision. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU: AE vacancy and account transition. STU: SSP vacancy and specialist transition. CSU: CSAM continuity; CAIP CSA capacity rules apply only to CAIP.
Boundary: Normal AE, SSP, CSAM, and CSA execution remains with those roles; do not generalize CAIP assignment rules.
discussionQuestions: Which customer outcome is exposed by the coverage gap?
What evidence supports the proposed route in your organization?
Who must accept the assignment?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate coverage facts from unanswered transition risks'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Check authorized account context where access exists', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Coverage inspection protects continuity by separating verified assignment from gaps needing manager judgment. Normal account and delivery execution stays with AE, SSP, CSAM and CSA roles. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit. CAIP assignment rules are not universal coverage rules.
preparationChecklist: Bring one de-identified coverage case, current ownership/capacity evidence and the applicable FY27 manager guidance. Exclude employee/HR data and do not assume agent access.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer-continuity gap is evidenced and what capacity is available in your own team? What interim owner and review point can you authorize or escalate? How does a peer manager keep a proposed assignment distinct from accepted coverage?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Normal AE, SSP, CSAM, and CSA execution remains with those roles; do not generalize CAIP assignment rules.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one coverage decision card: customer continuity risk, permitted capacity evidence, interim owner proposal, authority gap and next check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which continuity risk changed after checking evidence, and what intervention can you authorize here?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, review a consequential coverage question and decide a bounded intervention or evidence request within your authority. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a de-identified coverage assumption clarified and whether it improved continuity or the next check. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Check authorized stage-specific signals and missing evidence
activities.description: Inspect a signal at the correct stage of work and formulate a source-backed question for its owner.
activities.prompt: For [team/portfolio scope] and [commercial pipeline, technical milestone or post-signature consumption stage], inspect the dated authorized record signals actually available and the stated outlook I supply. Return up to three material mismatches, each with source identifier/date, what changed, what is interpretation and the confirmation question for the record owner. Do not mix pipeline, technical proof and realized consumption as interchangeable measures. Recommend one correction request or investigation, not a forecast verdict. If access is missing, use a permitted extract or manual checklist. Use only permitted business material I am authorized to access and share in this tool. Do not include employee or HR data, score or evaluate individuals, invent inaccessible evidence, approve investments/deals, change records, send messages or make commitments. If a source is unavailable, mark the gap and use a permitted extract or manual review.
activities.expectedOutput: A stage-specific mismatch list and one evidence-backed correction/investigation request, with unavailable sources explicit.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager chooses the intervention and the accountable IC verifies and corrects records; no universal sole M1 forecast ownership is assumed.
activities.requiredContext: Named team/portfolio scope, stage of work, stated outlook, authorized dated signals and record-owner roles.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this activity or another Featured option; use an existing relevant business artifact rather than completing every activity in sequence.
2. Confirm your remit and permitted inputs, then run the prompt with the evidence listed here. If the tool/source is unavailable, use a permitted extract or manual review.
3. Check source dates, access gaps and the distinction between evidence, proposal and agreement.
4. Make the stated human decision or confirmation request, with owner-role acceptance and a review point; any real record update or communication follows the separate authorized process.
activities.whyThisMatters: Intervening on the wrong stage measure can miss the real risk while creating a correction that does not improve the customer work.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A pipeline, milestone, or consumption signal no longer matches the team's stated outlook. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU: commercial opportunity and renewal evidence. STU: technical close and uncommitted-to-committed progression. CSU: accepted milestones, consumption and delivery health.
Boundary: No source establishes sole Enterprise M1 forecast ownership; IC owners correct records and the manager decides the intervention.
discussionQuestions: What changed since the prior outlook?
Which signal needs correction by the record owner?
What intervention can you decide within your own organization?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check authorized stage-specific signals and missing evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare a concise inspection readout for human review', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Stage inspection distinguishes evidence, assumptions and the right intervention. IC owners correct records; manager review does not establish sole Enterprise M1 forecast ownership. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one de-identified outlook exception, dated opportunity/milestone/consumption evidence and the known record owner. Exclude employee/HR data and do not assume agent access.
facilitatorQuestions: Which stage-specific evidence gap could change the intervention? Who owns the record correction and who decides the manager response? How would a peer challenge the risk without assuming sole forecast ownership?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. No source establishes sole Enterprise M1 forecast ownership; IC owners correct records and the manager decides the intervention.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one stage-specific intervention card: governed signal, missing evidence, IC record owner, manager decision and review date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which stage signal changed your intervention, and what correction belongs to the IC record owner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, inspect a consequential stage signal and choose a manager intervention or evidence/correction request to its record owner. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized stage assumption checked and whether it made intervention or correction more precise. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Draft coaching questions from a de-identified business scenario
activities.description: Prepare evidence-focused coaching questions for a de-identified business decision without taking over the team member's judgment.
activities.prompt: Using the fictional or de-identified business plan, handoff or technical decision I supply, write three coaching questions: one that tests its evidence, one that exposes a material trade-off and one that lets the person choose their next action. Explain the decision criterion each question probes. Propose a team-member-owned follow-up and the work evidence to revisit. Do not rewrite the person's answer for them or assess employee ability, behavior or performance. Use only permitted business material I am authorized to access and share in this tool. Do not include employee or HR data, score or evaluate individuals, invent inaccessible evidence, approve investments/deals, change records, send messages or make commitments. If a source is unavailable, mark the gap and use a permitted extract or manual review.
activities.expectedOutput: Three judgment-focused coaching questions with decision criteria and a proposed owner-led follow-up evidence check.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager chooses questions appropriate to the situation; the team member owns the real decision and follow-up. No employee evaluation is generated.
activities.requiredContext: A fictional or de-identified business artifact, its intended customer outcome, known evidence gaps and a review point; no real employee/customer identifiers.
activitySteps: 1. Choose this activity or another Featured option; use an existing relevant business artifact rather than completing every activity in sequence.

activities.name: Rehearse a judgment-focused coaching conversation
activities.description: Rehearse an evidence-focused coaching conversation using a fictional business scenario and clearly simulated reactions.
activities.prompt: Role-play a fictional colleague discussing the de-identified business scenario I supply. I will open with a coaching question. Pause for my response in each of three exchanges, then coach whether I tested evidence, explored a trade-off and left the next action with the colleague. Label all reactions simulated; do not invent actual customer agreement or make any employee evaluation. End with one revised question and the business evidence to verify in real work. Use only permitted business material I am authorized to access and share in this tool. Do not include employee or HR data, score or evaluate individuals, invent inaccessible evidence, approve investments/deals, change records, send messages or make commitments. If a source is unavailable, mark the gap and use a permitted extract or manual review.
activities.expectedOutput: Three simulated coaching exchanges, feedback on the manager's questions, one revised question and a business-evidence verification point.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager judges the questions before any real conversation and verifies business facts separately; simulated reactions are not evidence about an employee.
activities.requiredContext: A fictional/de-identified business scenario, intended decision, coaching question and evidence boundaries; no real employee or customer data.
activitySteps: 1. Supply a fictional or de-identified business scenario with its evidence and boundaries; no real employee/customer data.
2. Rehearse three exchanges, responding yourself before the coaching.
3. Distinguish simulated reactions from verified facts and choose one question or explanation to improve.
4. The manager verifies any real-work evidence and owns the next conversation; nothing is sent or recorded by this rehearsal.
activities.whyThisMatters: Rehearsal exposes when a coaching question supplies the answer or takes ownership away from the colleague.

discussionQuestions: Which weak assumption blocks the next customer action?

facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Coaching improves decisions through evidence and questions, not seller scores. People and performance decisions stay with the manager and outside AI evaluation. preparationChecklist: Bring one de-identified account, technical or success-plan decision with approved evidence and the unresolved assumption. Exclude employee/HR data and do not assume agent access.
facilitatorQuestions: Which observable business decision needs better reasoning rather than a seller score? What question lets the owner explain their judgment? How would another manager test the reasoning without asking AI to evaluate an employee?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Never rank, score, or evaluate individual employees; keep people and performance decisions with the manager.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which question helped the team member examine a decision criterion without inferring performance or intent?
