facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A customer value claim or renewal plan is unsupported by current delivery and usage evidence. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU: review renewal/account risk. STU: verify technical commitment and residual obligations. CSU: inspect customer-success, consumption, and delivery signals.
Boundary: CAIP CSU account-health cadence is CAIP-specific; CSAM normally leads customer-facing value reviews, not every M1.
discussionQuestions: Which value claim is supported by actual delivery or usage?
What remains expected rather than realized?
Who owns the customer-facing value or renewal decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Retrieve authorized customer-risk context if accessible'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare a customer-outcome intervention for human approval', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Intervention needs customer value or renewal evidence while CSAM and field owners retain normal customer-facing execution. Do not generalize CAIP-specific cadence. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one de-identified value or renewal claim, dated delivery/usage evidence and the accountable customer-success or account owner. Exclude employee/HR data and do not assume agent access.
facilitatorQuestions: Which customer-outcome or renewal risk warrants intervention, and what source proves it? Who owns the customer-facing review and next action? How does a peer manager avoid treating a CAIP-specific cadence as a universal rule?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. CAIP CSU account-health cadence is CAIP-specific; CSAM normally leads customer-facing value reviews, not every M1.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one customer-outcome intervention card: risk evidence, customer-facing role owner, manager action, authority limit and next signal/date. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which value or renewal assumption changed intervention, and what stays with the customer-facing field role?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, check a material value or renewal assumption and agree a manager intervention or evidence request within the existing org rhythm. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized assumption checked and whether it improved field-owner follow-up or manager judgment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A coverage, delivery, or approval blocker threatens the next customer outcome. Focus on one evidence-backed decision within your organizational remit.
keyTalkingPoints: ATU/STU: cover transition or specialist vacancies. CAIP CSU: use documented capacity and investment rules. CSAM/CSA: apply only documented delivery-request approval gates.
Boundary: Do not assume universal pricing, discount, delegation, or investment approval authority.
discussionQuestions: Which resource or approval dependency blocks the outcome?
What authority do you actually hold?
What must be recommended or escalated rather than approved here?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Frame a capacity decision with the documented authority boundary'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the selected evidence or rehearsal to one human-reviewed decision, its authority limit, accountable execution owner and next check. Keep individual-contributor and receiving-owner decisions with those owners. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Design a scoped, human-reviewed exception-monitoring pilot', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Capacity and exceptions need explicit authority and a resolution path. Recommendations cannot authorize staffing, pricing, discounts or investment beyond delegation. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one de-identified coverage, capacity or approval blocker, applicable authority guidance and the next customer outcome. Exclude employee/HR data and do not assume agent access.
facilitatorQuestions: What capacity constraint is evidenced rather than assumed? Is the next step within your documented authority or an escalation? How would a peer preserve financial, staffing and investment decision rights while defining a stop condition?
listenFor: Assumed authority, unsupported evidence, or a cross-org huddle. Do not assume universal pricing, discount, delegation, or investment approval authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one capacity/exception decision card: evidenced constraint, options, formal delegation gap, authorized escalation owner and stop condition. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which capacity trade-off changed your recommendation, and what exception needs another decision owner?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Choose one Featured practice that fits the question and your authorized access and evidence; otherwise review the same question manually. Before the next huddle, frame a material capacity trade-off or exception and decide within delegation or route to the authorized owner. Keep approvals, people decisions, record changes and messages human-owned. If evidence is unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap rather than infer status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a de-identified authority or capacity assumption clarified and whether it improved escalation; exclude staffing and personnel details. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Rehearse a manager explanation of what changed and why
activities.description: Rehearse explaining an experiment's evidence and limits without claiming success or evaluating colleagues.
activities.prompt: Role-play a skeptical peer using the fictional/de-identified management-workflow experiment I supply. I will explain what changed and why. Challenge unsupported success claims, missing baseline, downstream costs and unclear human accountability. Pause for my response for three exchanges, then coach my explanation and draft a short practice note with observed evidence, caveat, owner-role follow-up and review date. Label simulated reactions and do not add results I did not supply. Use only permitted business material I am authorized to access and share in this tool. Do not include employee or HR data, score or evaluate individuals, invent inaccessible evidence, approve investments/deals, change records, send messages or make commitments. If a source is unavailable, mark the gap and use a permitted extract or manual review.
activities.expectedOutput: Three simulated peer exchanges, evidence-focused explanation feedback and a draft practice note with caveat and follow-up.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The manager verifies every real result separately before sharing a practice note; no simulated response or AI assessment becomes employee evaluation.
activities.requiredContext: Fictional/de-identified experiment plan and observed results, intended outcome, baseline, downstream effects and review point; no real employee/customer data.
activitySteps: 1. Supply a fictional or de-identified business scenario with its evidence and boundaries; no real employee/customer data.
2. Rehearse three exchanges, responding yourself before the coaching.
3. Distinguish simulated reactions from verified facts and choose one question or explanation to improve.
4. The manager verifies any real-work evidence and owns the next conversation; nothing is sent or recorded by this rehearsal.
activities.whyThisMatters: Explaining the limits as well as the gain helps peers reuse a management practice without inheriting an unsupported success claim.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

PLC-EPS-PDM-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

activities.name: Reconcile one partner growth baseline before using it
activities.description: Comparable measures prevent unsupported growth promises.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Create a working growth-baseline reconciliation for the partner over the relevant period, using only the supplied approved evidence pack available at the cutoff. Compare at most three supplied measures and retain their units, periods, definitions and source references. Separate observed actuals, partner estimates and planning assumptions. Flag incompatible denominators, stale extracts and duplicate pipeline rather than normalizing them silently. Return a compact table of measure, comparable baseline, discrepancy, source and owner question, followed by the single discrepancy most likely to change our growth choice. Do not manufacture missing values; mark NOT PROVIDED and state the smallest clarification needed. Keep this a PDM review draft, not a partner commitment or a forecast submission.
activities.expectedOutput: At most three measure rows with dates, units, discrepancy and source; one prioritized clarification with owner and review date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM checks comparability; metric owner confirms disputed values. Stop use of a measure if its definition, source or permission is unknown; record the gap instead of endorsing a target.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps; no unresolved placeholders or connector assumptions.
activitySteps: 1. choose one partner, period and three measures; bind inputs.
2. generate from approved excerpts.
3. verify one baseline against its source.
4. select the first discrepancy to resolve.
5. record owner and review date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Comparable measures prevent unsupported growth promises.

activities.name: Test one growth hypothesis against two cited market signals

activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Test the hypothesis for the partner described in the partner profile in the market as of today. Start with the approved source URLs and use at most two authoritative, dated sources; prefer official statistics or first-party published evidence. Produce a two-row evidence table with claim, supporting passage summary, publisher, date, URL and relevance limit. Distinguish a market signal from proof that the named partner can capture it. Give one disconfirming interpretation and one question for the partner. If a source is inaccessible, stale or absent, state the limitation and do not invent a citation or conclusion. End with a provisional supported, uncertain or contradicted rating; do not recommend a revenue commitment.

activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. bound one hypothesis and two references.

3. open and verify one citation.
4. decide whether a capacity check is warranted.
5. record question, owner and review date.

activities.name: Choose a growth bet using evidence and capacity constraints
activities.description: PDM makes trade-offs explicit rather than letting unsupported initiatives consume the partner plan.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Prepare a growth-choice card for the partner for review by the accountable owner. Use the options, the supplied approved evidence and the supplied confirmed constraints only. Compare no more than three bets on evidence strength, partner execution capacity, time to test and the consequence of being wrong. Explain the trade-offs in plain language rather than inventing weighted scores. Recommend one reversible next test and identify what evidence would overturn that recommendation. Return the option comparison, a proposed choice, an unresolved dependency and a named-owner question. Where inputs are missing, mark the option unassessed and ask for the minimum evidence needed; do not create financial projections. This is a PDM discussion draft awaiting partner acceptance, not an approved integrated plan.

activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM owns prioritization; the partner must accept plan changes. Stop recommendations exceeding confirmed capacity or implying investment commitment; replace unknown assumptions with an evidence request.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps. Other practices are not prerequisites.
activitySteps: 1. choose one partner and up to three options.
2. generate the constrained comparison.
3. challenge the preferred option's evidence.
4. choose one reversible test or defer.
5. record owner, evidence need and review date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.name: Extended: contrast SI and ISV growth paths before selecting one
activities.description: Partner business models require different proof, dependencies and success measures.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the partner, use the partner type, the capabilities, the growth question and the program notes to draft two contrasting growth-path sketches and select the applicable one. The SI sketch must test CustomerZero evidence, transformation delivery capacity and a proposed Majors/ATU alignment dependency. The ISV sketch must test product repeatability, Marketplace motion, MBS terminology from supplied guidance, MACC treatment questions and a co-innovation dependency. For each sketch give the first validation action, metric baseline, accountable contact and disqualifying evidence. Mark the nonapplicable sketch comparison only. If evidence or program definitions are absent, state NOT PROVIDED and ask the responsible owner; invent no eligibility thresholds, commercial treatment or program promises. Recommend discussion, not funding or partner commitment.
activities.expectedOutput: Two model-specific path sketches, one applicable, with baseline, owner, first action and disqualifying evidence.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM confirms the model; ATU or product owner validates dependencies. Stop unsupported CustomerZero claims or implied Marketplace, MBS or MACC treatment; route questions to accountable specialists.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. No partner-platform access is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Select one partner model and growth question.
2. Supply approved capabilities and official notes.
3. Generate contrasting SI and ISV sketches.
4. Verify the applicable delivery or product dependency.
5. Record one validation action and park the other path.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Name one partner and planning period. Frame this as partner strategy, not a customer opportunity stage. Outputs are working hypotheses, not approved plans.
keyTalkingPoints: Compare periods, currencies and definitions before discussing growth. Separate observed demand, partner ambition and capacity. Keep partner-reported pipeline distinct from customer-opportunity evidence. Prefer one falsifiable priority over a broad wish list.
discussionQuestions: Which number changes the growth choice if wrong? What proves this partner can execute? Whose capacity confirmation or acceptance is still missing?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile one partner growth baseline before using it'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose only one Featured practice. Move from the artifact to a human choice: pursue one evidence check or defer. Other practices are independent alternatives. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Extended: contrast SI and ISV growth paths before selecting one', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the growth question, strongest evidence and largest uncertainty. Confirm that the partner has not accepted a plan or target. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring approved dated actuals, ambition, capacity constraints and source references for one partner. Use sanitized samples if permission is unclear. Timebox: 1 minute scope, 2 generate, 2 verify, 2 decide, 1 commit.
facilitatorQuestions: Can another PDM reproduce the baseline? Which assertion is inferred? What evidence would overturn the preferred priority?
listenFor: A dated baseline; incompatible measures flagged rather than summed; an executable capacity test; a named evidence owner.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If an agent is unavailable or exceeds two minutes, use approved supplied excerpts to fill the same output columns manually. Mark unverified claims and decide what evidence to obtain. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector or source-system update is assumed. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which growth fact became an assumption after checking its denominator and source?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will ask the named owner to verify one growth assumption by the agreed date and bring evidence to the next planning discussion. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized growth assumption corrected after source or denominator checking and whether it changed the priority; partner acceptance may remain pending. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Expose one PBP target-definition conflict
activities.description: Visible conflicting definitions allow a real negotiated choice rather than artificial agreement.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Create a target-alignment issue card for the partner and the objective using the Microsoft view, the partner view and the supplied dated baseline. Preserve each party's original target, period and metric definition. Identify the single conflict that prevents meaningful comparison, then propose two clearly labeled resolution choices without changing either party's position. Explain the consequence of each choice and the evidence needed for the reviewers to decide. Return the conflict table, one proposed wording for discussion and an acceptance field set to DRAFT - NOT ACCEPTED. If a baseline or definition is missing, do not infer agreement or calculate growth; mark NOT PROVIDED and ask a precise clarification. Do not commit partner resources or approve the integrated PBP.
activities.expectedOutput: One conflict table, two resolution choices and discussion wording with draft status and paired review owners.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM confirms the conflict; partner representative must accept negotiated wording. Stop if a definition is missing or wording implies agreement; preserve both positions and request clarification.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. select one objective and both target statements.
2. generate the conflict card.
3. verify neither party's position changed.
4. select the resolution question.
5. record both review owners and date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Visible conflicting definitions allow a real negotiated choice rather than artificial agreement.

activities.name: Check one official-guidance assumption in the partner plan
activities.description: A cited guidance check prevents a program reference becoming a guarantee of support or eligibility.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Assess the planning assumption for the partner context as of today, starting with the official sources. Use at most two current official sources and cite title, publisher, date or access date, URL and the relevant section. Separate what the guidance explicitly says from what remains an interpretation for the accountable owner. Return an evidence note with confirmed wording, applicability limitations, unanswered question and the smallest change needed to keep the draft plan accurate. If sources conflict, are inaccessible or omit the requested condition, say so; do not invent eligibility thresholds or promise benefits. Do not determine funding approval, commercial treatment or partner eligibility. End with a human verification question, not an approval statement.
activities.expectedOutput: One cited guidance note separating explicit wording, applicability limits and interpretation; one conditional draft-plan correction.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM checks citations; accountable program/policy owner determines applicability. Stop reliance when currency, scope or access is uncertain; leave the claim conditional and do not assert eligibility.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED where absent.
activitySteps: 1. isolate one assumption and two references.
2. request the bounded evidence note.
3. verify one source's relevant wording.
4. decide whether conditional wording is needed.
5. record owner question and review date.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: A cited guidance check prevents a program reference becoming a guarantee of support or eligibility.

activities.name: Draft a one-question executive decision brief
activities.description: A bounded choice and consequence make executive time useful without a broad status narrative.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Draft a one-question executive decision brief for the partner using the decision, the facts, the options and the authority. Limit the brief to the requested choice, three evidence points, two alternatives, the consequence of deferral and one recommended next step. Preserve source dates and distinguish verified facts from PDM interpretation. Name the accountable decision owner only when supplied; otherwise mark NOT PROVIDED and ask who has authority. Identify any funding, discount, program or resource commitment that requires separate approval. Do not approve, send or schedule anything, and do not imply executive agreement. End with an explicit decide, defer or request-evidence response field for human use and a proposed review checkpoint.
activities.expectedOutput: One brief: single ask, three evidence points, two options, deferral consequence, authority boundary and human response field.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM verifies evidence; governance owner confirms authority. Stop treating the artifact as an approval request if rights or critical facts are unknown; seek clarification. Agent output authorizes no commitment.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for absent inputs.
activitySteps: 1. name one partner, decision and intended decider.
2. generate from supplied facts/options.
3. verify the strongest claim's source.
4. check authority and sharpen the question.
5. retain draft and record review date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A bounded choice and consequence make executive time useful without a broad status narrative.

activities.name: Resolve one POD ownership gap and escalation trigger
activities.description: Explicit ownership prevents blocked partner handoffs circulating between roles without a responsible decider.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Build an ownership-and-escalation card for the partner issue from the role notes, the dependency, the decision rights and the deadline. Limit scope to one blocked handoff and no more than four relevant roles. Distinguish the proposed accountable decider, action owner, evidence contributor and person to inform. Highlight overlapping or missing ownership without treating a generated assignment as accepted. Recommend one escalation trigger based on supplied timing or evidence and one question to resolve the gap. Return a compact responsibility table and a handoff acceptance condition. If authority or timing is missing, mark NOT PROVIDED rather than inventing it. Do not assign tasks in systems, contact the POD or commit partner resources.
activities.expectedOutput: One four-role responsibility table, one ownership question, handoff acceptance condition and evidence/time-based escalation trigger.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM validates orchestration; proposed owners must accept their roles. Stop handoffs relying on assumed authority or unaccepted capacity; retain an ownership gap instead of marking resolved.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. select one handoff and four roles at most.
2. generate the responsibility table.
3. compare proposed ownership with decision rights.
4. choose the ownership question and trigger.
5. record confirmation owner and date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Explicit ownership prevents blocked partner handoffs circulating between roles without a responsible decider.

activities.name: Separate an investment request from approval authority
activities.description: A cited boundary note helps PDM route an investment question without implying authority to approve it.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Prepare a governance-boundary note for the request in the supplied approved context as of today, using the official sources and at most two official references. Cite source title, URL, relevant section and date or access date for each supported statement. Separate documented process requirements, applicability questions and decisions reserved for the approver. Identify the smallest evidence packet the PDM should prepare for review; do not invent amounts, thresholds, eligibility or an approval chain not present in the sources. If guidance is unavailable or contradictory, state NOT PROVIDED or conflict and frame a precise owner question. This note is research support only, not funding authorization, discount approval, a program determination or a commitment to the partner.
activities.expectedOutput: One cited table of process requirements, applicability questions and reserved approvals; a minimal review-packet checklist.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM checks source accuracy; accountable approver determines authority/applicability. Stop recommendations presented as approval, eligibility or a funding promise; keep requests pending review.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. isolate one request and official references.
2. generate the bounded note.
3. verify one requirement's wording.
4. separate PDM preparation from approver decisions.
5. record owner question and minimum evidence packet.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: A cited boundary note helps PDM route an investment question without implying authority to approve it.

activities.name: Extended: tailor a POD decision for SI transformation or ISV co-innovation
activities.description: SI delivery and ISV product execution require different decision owners and evidence.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Draft a model-specific POD decision card for the partner using the specified operating model, the issue, the owner notes and the supplied approved evidence. Contrast an SI version covering CustomerZero proof, transformation delivery accountability and Majors/ATU alignment with an ISV version covering product co-innovation ownership, Marketplace readiness and separate MBS or MACC questions for specialists. In each version specify the decision, essential participants, required evidence and one escalation condition; then mark the applicable version for discussion. Do not assume that participation conveys approval authority. Missing roles, evidence or program definitions remain NOT PROVIDED with an owner question. Propose no funding, customer or commercial commitment, and do not send invitations or claim that the POD has agreed.
activities.expectedOutput: One applicable POD decision card and comparison-only variant, each with evidence, participants and escalation condition.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM confirms forum; delivery/product owner validates the ask. Stop assumed Majors/ATU involvement, co-innovation support or commercial treatment; record the dependency for human resolution.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. Select one model and execution issue.
2. Supply approved owner notes and evidence.
3. Generate both variants and select the applicable one.
4. Check the decisive owner and escalation condition.
5. Record one review ask with explicit authority limits.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask what one decision the executive or POD must make, not what slides they need. PDM recommends; authorized owners commit resources.
keyTalkingPoints: Participation does not confer approval authority. Separate decider, contributors and people to inform. Preserve no-action consequences and escalation triggers. Funding, discounts, eligibility and commitments require the accountable approver's sign-off.
discussionQuestions: What precisely must the executive decide? Who owns the consequence if the dependency fails? Which proposed commitment exceeds the forum's authority?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft a one-question executive decision brief'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. After the chosen practice, ask a peer to restate the decision without background material. If they cannot, narrow the ask before committing. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Extended: tailor a POD decision for SI transformation or ISV co-innovation', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the decision, decider and unresolved approval. Confirm nothing has been approved, sent or committed by the agent. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted partner issue, decision-rights notes, two feasible options and dated evidence. Remove unnecessary customer/personal detail. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; preserve time for human review and commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: Can the decider answer yes, no or defer? What is evidence rather than advocacy? Which request needs a separate approval route?
listenFor: A decision verb, evidenced trade-off, no-action consequence, accepted human ownership and explicit authority limits.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Use approved notes to complete the same decision/accountability card manually if agents are unavailable or exceed two minutes. Unknown authority remains a governance-owner question. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector, outbound message or assignment is required. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed when decision ownership was separated from participation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will seek the named decision owner's response to one bounded ask by the review date and route requests beyond their authority correctly. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized decision-owner boundary clarified and whether it made the executive or POD ask actionable; deferral is valid. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Read MSX evidence to select one next customer opportunity decision
activities.description: PDM focuses co-sell support on an actual customer decision rather than treating aggregate partner pipeline as verified progress.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Using only MSX evidence I am already authorized to access, review the opportunity ids at the cutoff to answer the decision question. Limit the set to three identified opportunities. Return account and opportunity ID, latest dated evidence, customer design or execution decision still needed, evidence gap and accountable account or delivery owner if recorded. Distinguish record fields from inference and do not treat CRM stage alone as customer acceptance. Mark missing information NOT PROVIDED and stop retrieval when record access is unavailable; do not seek wider access. Recommend one record for human review, not a forecast change. Do not update MSX, create tasks, certify partner referral state or imply funding, commercial or customer commitments. If existing authorized record access is unavailable, inspect a dated authorized extract of the exact identified record or clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Mark access gaps explicitly; synthetic data supports rehearsal only, never a real opportunity conclusion.
activities.expectedOutput: At most three opportunity rows with IDs, evidence/date, decision, gap and owner; one selected customer decision for review.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM checks partner relevance; account/delivery owner validates customer facts. Stop retrieval if access fails and stop all write/approval actions. Sales Agent cannot certify partner referral state; inferred status cannot become fact.
activities.requiredContext: Dependency: existing Sales Agent access, MSX authorization and visibility to named records; seek no broader permission. Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps. Read-only MSX evidence, not partner-system retrieval. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. confirm existing authorization and bind exact identifiers.
2. run read-only prompt for at most three records.
3. verify decisive dated evidence and separate inference.
4. select one customer decision for owner review.
5. record reviewer/gap without any system write.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: PDM focuses co-sell support on an actual customer decision rather than treating aggregate partner pipeline as verified progress.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Require an identified account/opportunity and actual customer decision. MCEM-02 maps to design acceptance; MCEM-03 to implementation, adoption or achievement checkpoints, never partner governance.
keyTalkingPoints: Sales Agent uses MSX-authorized evidence on named records, not partner-system discovery. CRM stage is not customer acceptance. Referral state must be verified by its authorized source owner, not certified by Sales Agent. PDM orchestrates; account/delivery owners validate customer decisions.
discussionQuestions: Which customer decision is blocked? What proves design readiness or execution progress? Is disagreement about CRM evidence, partner assertion or referral administration?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Read MSX evidence to select one next customer opportunity decision'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose one Featured route based on available authorized evidence. End with one customer checkpoint decision, not a generic pipeline list or all three practices. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile customer-opportunity facts with partner assertions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read one customer decision, evidence and account/delivery reviewer. Confirm the artifact is advisory and no MSX, referral, forecast or commitment changed. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Select one to three exact opportunity/account identifiers and evidence cutoff. Before choosing Sales Agent, confirm existing availability, MSX permission and record visibility; request read-only evidence. Prepare a dated authorized export as a separate alternative and identify the account/delivery reviewer.
facilitatorQuestions: Is the decision tied to an identified opportunity? Does missing evidence concern customer design, delivery or partner administration? Who can validate it without granting new permissions?
listenFor: Named records, dated citations, distinct evidence lanes, customer acceptance conditions and accountable owners; no connector assumptions or inferred referral certification.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Separate supplied-export alternative outside the Sales Agent practice: if Sales Agent, MSX permission or record visibility is unavailable, use Cowork with a facilitator-supplied authorized dated export for the same one to three opportunities, or complete the same columns manually. Preserve IDs, cutoff and limitations; do not ask Sales Agent to ingest an export to bypass permission. Without permitted customer evidence, use a sanitized supplied example to identify gaps. Never infer/certify referral state. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector is assumed.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which pipeline signal failed to prove the actual customer decision needed next?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will ask the identified account/delivery owner to validate one checkpoint by the agreed date and coordinate partner contribution after review. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized co-sell signal checked by its account or delivery owner and whether it changed the next customer decision; no referral or forecast writeback is implied. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask for one growth lever, not a catalog of programs. Improve the request without authorizing it.
keyTalkingPoints: Explain the growth mechanism and how it will be measured. Separate confirmed from requested capacity. Official guidance supports program facts; accountable owners determine eligibility and treatment. A proposed reversible test is not promised support.
discussionQuestions: Which baseline shows the lever worked? What assumption could make investment unnecessary? Who must approve before spending or commitments?

activities.name: Reconcile one MBR/QBR variance before explaining it
activities.description: PDM avoids corrections based on inconsistent reporting or unsupported causal stories.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Create a one-metric variance bridge for the partner in the review period using the supplied approved plan excerpt, the supplied dated actuals and the issue notes. First compare periods, units and definitions; calculate a difference only when supplied values are genuinely comparable and show the calculation. Separate observed variance, evidenced contributors and untested causal hypotheses. Return one compact table with planned value, actual value, comparable variance, source, confidence limitation and the first owner question. Do not attribute causation from timing alone or fill absent values with zero. If inputs are incompatible or missing, mark NOT PROVIDED or NOT COMPARABLE and identify the smallest reconciliation step. This is an MBR/QBR review draft, not a forecast submission or an accepted plan revision.
activities.expectedOutput: One source-linked variance table with checked calculation or noncomparability, causal-confidence limit and owner question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM/metric owner verify comparison before correction. Stop causal conclusions when definitions conflict, provenance is missing or observations only correlate; carry a reconciliation question instead.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for missing values/definitions.
activitySteps: 1. select one metric and its two sources.
2. generate the variance bridge.
3. check units, period and calculation.
4. choose first reconciliation/cause question.
5. record owner and review date.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.name: Separate a transformation claim from its actual evidence
activities.description: Traceable baselines and visible limits let PDM reuse learning responsibly.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Build a claim-evidence matrix for the partner and the claim using only the evidence pack, for the audience under the permission notes. Compare the baseline and result for period, units, population and measurement method. Separate measured change, plausible contribution and unsupported causal attribution. Return one claim row with source references, substantiation status, limitations, required redactions and the next evidence or permission question. If the baseline or result is absent or incomparable, mark the outcome unsubstantiated rather than manufacturing a benefit. Missing permission is NOT PROVIDED, not implied consent. Suggest cautious internal-review wording only for supported facts. Do not publish, upload, contact anyone or claim that the customer or partner has approved reuse.
activities.expectedOutput: One claim row with baseline/result sources, substantiation status, attribution limits, redactions and next evidence/permission question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM reviews claim; measurement owner validates proof and permission owner validates audience. Stop outcome wording if baseline, attribution or permission is unsupported; retain only a redacted review request. No publication.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Exclude unapproved sensitive detail.
activitySteps: 1. select one claim and permitted source pack.
2. generate the claim-evidence row.
3. verify comparability and references.
4. choose supported wording or evidence/permission hold.
5. record measurement reviewer and permission owner.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Traceable baselines and visible limits let PDM reuse learning responsibly.

activities.name: Draft one internal transformation case with permission boundaries
activities.description: A bounded case carries verified learning forward without an unauthorized customer success claim.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Draft a concise internal learning case for the partner alias covering the outcome, using only the approved sources, the limitations and the permission status. Structure it as starting condition, partner action, measured result, contribution limits and one reusable lesson. Preserve the baseline, result, period and evidence reference, and distinguish observed improvement from proof of causation. Remove names, quotations or metrics not permitted for the intended internal audience. If evidence is absent, provide an evidence-request outline instead of a success narrative; mark missing permission NOT PROVIDED and hold that detail. End with evidence-owner and permission-owner review fields and a NOT APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION banner. Do not publish, upload, send or imply customer or partner endorsement.
activities.expectedOutput: One five-section internal case or evidence-request outline with sources, reviewer fields and not-approved-for-publication banner.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM verifies learning; evidence/permission owners validate claims and audience. Stop narrative reuse if baseline proof or permission is missing. Do not publish or send the draft.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. No prerequisite practice.
activitySteps: 1. choose one permitted outcome and internal audience.
2. generate the structured case.
3. verify numeric claims and remove unsupported causation.
4. check redactions; choose draft or evidence outline.
5. record evidence/permission reviewers without sharing.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A bounded case carries verified learning forward without an unauthorized customer success claim.

activities.name: Test where one outcome pattern can and cannot transfer
activities.description: Distinguish reusable lessons from assumptions that another partner will repeat the same result.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Test the transferability of the pattern from the conditions to the target context as of today, starting with the official sources. Use at most two authoritative sources and cite title, publisher, URL and date for relevant guidance or market facts. Identify two enabling conditions, one material mismatch and one boundary where the pattern should not be generalized. Distinguish external evidence about context from the private outcome's substantiation; do not imply that published guidance validates that outcome or guarantees similar results. If sources or context are missing, mark the conclusion uncertain and ask for the minimum evidence. Return an internal research note only, with no customer identifiers, publication, performance promise or inferred permission to reuse the original case.
activities.expectedOutput: One cited internal note with two enablers, one mismatch, one non-generalization boundary and validation question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM tests contextual fit and keeps original proof/permission reviews separate. Stop extrapolated promises or confidential identifiers in external research; no source substitutes for permission.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for gaps.
activitySteps: 1. sanitize one pattern and select one target context.
2. run the two-source check.
3. verify one cited condition and applicability.
4. choose further investigation or retain the boundary.
5. record validation question and owner.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Distinguish reusable lessons from assumptions that another partner will repeat the same result.

activities.name: Extended: preserve SI and ISV outcome evidence in a reusable pattern
activities.description: Distinct transformation/product proof and reuse limits make future partner planning credible.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Create contrasting internal reuse cards for the partner alias using the specified operating model, the outcome pack, the permission notes and the official notes. The SI card must separate CustomerZero proof from broader transformation claims and state delivery-capacity and Majors/ATU conditions needed for reuse. The ISV card must separate product adoption or value evidence from Marketplace motion, co-innovation contribution and unverified MBS or MACC implications. For each include baseline, result, source, attribution limit, reusable mechanism and permission hold; mark the applicable card and the other comparison only. Missing evidence prevents an outcome claim, and missing permission prevents reuse of the detail. Invent no eligibility, program benefits or repeatable results. Produce review drafts only; publish or send nothing.
activities.expectedOutput: One applicable internal reuse card and comparison-only card with baseline/result proof, attribution limits, mechanism, reviewers and permission holds.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM, measurement owner and permission owner review. Stop unsupported CustomerZero scaling, implied Marketplace/MBS/MACC benefits or unauthorized detail. Neither draft is published or treated as approved for reuse.
activities.requiredContext: Use available identifiers, decision context, approved evidence, and accountable owners. Ask one concise question only if an essential detail is missing. Use NOT PROVIDED for missing inputs.
activitySteps: 1. Select one model and permitted outcome pack.
2. Identify baseline, result and intended audience.
3. Generate cards and mark the applicable one.
4. Check attribution/permission limits with proposed reviewers.
5. Record one learning and one evidence/permission hold.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Distinct transformation/product proof and reuse limits make future partner planning credible.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask for one outcome rather than a collection of success stories. Distinguish measured change from causal attribution and internal learning from publication.
keyTalkingPoints: Match periods, units and populations. Separate partner/customer contribution and avoid unsupported causation. Review permission for names, quotes, metrics and audience independently. Reusable patterns need boundaries where they do not apply.
discussionQuestions: What changed relative to which baseline? What does evidence not prove? Who can permit the metric or story for this audience?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate a transformation claim from its actual evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Decide whether the selected artifact is ready for internal human review, needs evidence or is held for permission. A draft is not publication approval. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Extended: preserve SI and ISV outcome evidence in a reusable pattern', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read one supported claim, limitation and permission decision. Confirm internal-review draft status and no publication performed. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one permitted source pack with baseline, result, dates, method and limitations. Supply audience and documented permissions; redact where necessary. No publication, upload, email or external sharing.
facilitatorQuestions: Can a reviewer reconstruct the claim? Is causation overstated? Which detail requires permission before reuse?
listenFor: Comparable measures, traceable sources, bounded attribution, redaction, named permission owner and unsupported claims removed or held.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If agents are unavailable or exceed two minutes, fill the same claim/case/transferability template manually from approved excerpts. Missing evidence or permission allows only a redacted evidence-request outline. No PMX, Partner Center or Marketplace connector is assumed; nothing is published or sent. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which evidence made the outcome credible, and which detail must remain excluded until permission is established?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will seek evidence-owner and permission-owner review of one internal reuse candidate by the agreed date before proposing broader use. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized transformation claim qualified or permission condition identified and whether it made reuse defensible; do not publish or bring the case. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.
