PLC-EPS-PDM-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-EPS-PDM-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

activities.name: Find corroborated potential signals for up to three recruits
activities.description: Concentrates recruitment attention on traceable potential rather than confident but uncorroborated market claims.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For up to three supplied named non-MPL SDC candidates, use the approved profile excerpts, the supplied qualification criteria/version, and the supplied credible source URLs. Complete one research pass. 1) Confirm the candidate scope and criteria; mark absent inputs unavailable. 2) Check only decision-relevant market, product, and adoption signals, citing links, dates, and whether each source is independent or recruit-authored. 3) Return a maximum three-row shortlist table with criterion, supporting evidence, contrary evidence, unknowns, and a provisional next question; do not invent weights. 4) Ask the PDM-R owner to verify the decisive source and accept, reject, or investigate each candidate. Stop at the evidence table or earlier if access or criteria are missing. Do not declare program qualification, contact candidates, or share externally.
activities.expectedOutput: Maximum three-candidate evidence shortlist with dated citations, source independence, unknowns, and a next question for each candidate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R checks the decisive citation and owns the shortlist decision. Missing criteria or inaccessible evidence stops ranking; no automated qualification or outreach.
activities.requiredContext: Up to three candidate names; approved profiles; criteria owner/version; two or three credible links; PDM-R decision owner. Authorized research only; protect recruit-specific data from public queries or sharing.
activitySteps: 1. Scope candidates and confirm criteria (1 min).
2. Run bounded cited research (3 min).
3. Inspect decisive and contrary evidence (2 min).
4. PDM-R records disposition or evidence request (2 min); stop before outreach.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.

activities.name: Apply supplied qualification criteria without inventing scores
activities.description: Makes recruitment prioritization reproducible and exposes where incomplete evidence would otherwise masquerade as low potential.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Build a recruit decision matrix for the maximum three candidates from the approved evidence packet and the current qualification criteria with owner/version. Use supplied material only and finish. 1) List the criteria and preserve any supplied scoring rules exactly; otherwise use Supported, Contradicted, or Unknown. 2) Match evidence to each criterion with document/page/date references, distinguishing recruit claims from verified facts. 3) Produce a compact matrix plus a provisional shortlist rationale and one decision-changing gap per candidate; label missing inputs separately from observed lack of progress. 4) Pause for the PDM-R owner to validate evidence and record accept, reject, or investigate. Stop if the criteria are absent or inconsistent. Do not manufacture scores, certify eligibility, update systems, or send the shortlist.
activities.expectedOutput: Criteria-by-candidate matrix with references, separate evidence states, provisional shortlist rationale, and one priority gap per candidate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R verifies the supplied rules and decisive evidence before deciding. Absent or conflicting criteria require clarification, not synthetic scoring or qualification.
activities.requiredContext: One approved evidence packet for up to three candidates; qualification rules with owner/version; any authorized weights; PDM-R reviewer. Cowork access and spending policy confirmed; no assumed PMX connection.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm criteria and packet scope (1 min).
2. Generate the evidence matrix (3 min).
3. Review unknowns and shortlist rationale (2 min).
4. PDM-R records a bounded decision (2 min); stop without system writes.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Makes recruitment prioritization reproducible and exposes where incomplete evidence would otherwise masquerade as low potential.

activities.description: Turns a disputed signal into a small, accountable validation task rather than a misleading shortlist decision.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the recruit, compare the two conflicting approved evidence excerpts against the supplied qualification criterion to prepare one clarification decision. 1) Identify the exact conflicting claim, source owners, dates, and scope; do not assume the newer source is correct. 2) Separate differences in definitions or reporting periods from genuine contradictions, and mark absent evidence as unavailable. 3) Return a one-page contradiction note containing what is known, what cannot be concluded, the shortlist consequence if each account is true, and one precise evidence request to the source owner. 4) Ask the PDM-R owner to choose hold, investigate, or proceed with a documented caveat. Stop before resolving an unsupported fact, changing qualification status, or sending the request; keep all material internal.

activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R decides whether the contradiction blocks recruitment attention. The source owner must validate disputed facts; AI cannot silently select a winning account.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit; two conflicting approved excerpts with references/dates; the relevant supplied criterion; source owner and PDM-R reviewer. No external discovery or source-system writes.
activitySteps: 1. Select one contradiction and criterion (1 min).
2. Compare definitions, periods, and evidence (3 min).

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: Which signal would make us invest another recruitment conversation, and can we verify it? Contrast a sourced market signal with an untested recruit claim. Keep this non-MPL recruitment work distinct from managed-partner performance reviews.
keyTalkingPoints: Qualification uses the supplied current criteria and scope; AI does not invent weights or certify eligibility. Cite source dates and separate independent corroboration from the recruit's own statements. A missing export or inaccessible source means input unavailable, not no progress. PDM-R makes the accept, reject, or investigate decision.
discussionQuestions: Which criterion changes our next decision? Where are apparent market traction and actual product evidence being conflated? What is the smallest missing fact that could reverse the shortlist?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Find corroborated potential signals for up to three recruits'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the most decision-relevant uncertainty to one Featured practice. before moving on, compare the proposed disposition with its strongest evidence and weakest assumption. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test an adjacent-segment recruit without borrowing comparators', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Have PDM-R name the candidate decision and cite one fact that supports it. Keep unsupported candidates in an investigation state rather than treating the AI scorecard as qualification. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring up to three candidate names, approved profile excerpts, qualification criteria with owner/version, and two or three credible source links. Confirm research access and sensitivity boundaries; Cowork needs approved access and an applicable spending policy. Redact unnecessary personal/customer data. Choose a single question and keep the exercise ; do not contact recruits or submit program applications.
facilitatorQuestions: What supports each candidate beyond its own marketing? Which criteria are unknown rather than unmet? Can a reviewer trace the decisive claim to a dated source? Who is authorized to decide the shortlist?
listenFor: A small candidate set, explicit criteria, dated citations, distinct claims and evidence, and a reversible human disposition. Challenge numerical scores without supplied weights and any statement that unavailable records prove inactivity.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If tools or evidence are unavailable, annotate the supplied criteria manually for one candidate with Unknown/Input unavailable labels. Produce an evidence request rather than a fabricated ranking; a clearly marked synthetic example may demonstrate format but cannot support a real decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption did we retire, and which could still change the shortlist?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate [one criterion] for [candidate] with [evidence owner] by [date], then record my shortlist disposition; I will not infer qualification from missing data. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized recruit criterion checked or unavailable and whether it changed shortlist judgment; no candidate scorecard is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What would this recruit gain that it actually values? Start with one supplied recruit priority and compare an evidence-backed capability statement with an unsupported AI promise.
keyTalkingPoints: Separate verified recruit needs, public claims, and our value hypotheses. Cite current Microsoft capability evidence and equally credible competitor sources. PDM-R approves positioning; technical owners validate fit. Internal preparation is not permission to send, promise support, or make commercial commitments.
discussionQuestions: Which recruit priority can we substantiate? What capability or outcome claim would be unsafe to repeat today? Which question would test whether our preferred angle resonates?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Choose between two evidence-backed value angles'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose the single weakest part of the planned conversation: evidence, personalization, or objection handling. Use its Featured practice, then inspect one claim before accepting the brief. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Position a bounded experiment for an incumbent-platform recruit', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Have PDM-R approve one positioning hypothesis and name its evidence and technical-validation owner. Keep unvalidated claims in the question list, not the talking track. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved recruit profile, current priority notes, two or three capability/competitor sources, and the stakeholder context. Confirm authorized Researcher or Cowork access; Cowork also needs an applicable spending policy. Keep sensitive recruit details in approved work sources, not public searches. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; no automated outreach or public reuse.
facilitatorQuestions: Can we distinguish a capability from a promised outcome? Which positioning angle has the strongest recruit-specific evidence? Who will validate technical relevance before reuse?
listenFor: Concrete recruit priorities, cited capabilities with applicability limits, honest unknowns, and a clear discovery question. Challenge invented ROI, competitive disparagement, and assertions that an architecture is already approved.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without live research, use approved source excerpts and mark freshness unverified. Without a documented recruit priority, draft a discovery question rather than a personalized claim; do not fill missing context with a generic success promise. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which statement became more credible when we replaced a promise with a question?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate [one recruit priority or capability claim] with [owner] by [date], then approve the internal agenda for [recruit conversation]. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized positioning promise replaced by evidence or a question and whether it improved credibility or the recruit agenda. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: Which part of this partnership case is evidenced today, and which is still a hypothesis? Distinguish recorded MSX opportunity state from the recruit's commitments and applicable commercial rules.
keyTalkingPoints: Sales Agent may inspect authorized MSX records only. Cowork assembles supplied inputs without assuming PMX or Partner Center connectors. MACC applicability, eligibility, discounts, funding, and terms require current evidence and authorized owner validation. PDM-R owns the case, not every commercial approval.
discussionQuestions: Which assumption could change the partnership decision? What must the recruit confirm directly? Which commitment needs a commercial, program, or technical owner's review?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect one authorized MSX opportunity for case evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R names the next case decision, one unresolved assumption, and its validator. Retain an internal draft status until the necessary commercial and partner evidence is actually reviewed. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one recruit, one authorized MSX opportunity ID or an explicitly missing-record note, supplied SPP structure, relevant current MACC/commercial criteria, and owner information. facilitatorQuestions: Can the reviewer trace each commercial statement to an applicable source? Where does recorded pipeline differ from partnership intent? Is the next action evidence collection, case review, or an authorized decision?
listenFor: Facts and assumptions in separate fields, named validators, commercial caveats, and input-unavailable labels. Challenge eligibility inferred from pipeline, unsupported revenue certainty, and partner referral conclusions derived solely from MSX.

Do not infer that a missing record means no opportunity; if commercial criteria are absent, hold that part of the case for the authorized owner. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which statement moved from an implied commitment to an explicit assumption?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate [one case assumption or commitment] with [authorized owner] by [date] and bring the cited evidence before requesting a partnership decision. activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. activities.name: Monitor one approved launch-readiness dependency
activities.description: Track one approved listing, IPCS, incentive, or co-sell dependency between reviews without converting monitoring into an eligibility decision.
activities.prompt: Produce an unactivated read-only proposal, not a running monitor. Use authorized dated snapshots, a user-maintained baseline and previous report supplied for this review; do not retrieve unsupplied records, create automation, retain agent memory or notify anyone. Missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no change. Record scope, source permission, owner, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and supplied approved change criteria without inventing values. Future monitoring requires separate explicit approval and verified access/state capabilities. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Do not activate this monitor until named PDM-R reviewer has explicitly approved approved monitoring scope, the approved cadence, the approved evidence locations, the approved recipients, access, and the approved review or expiry date. Compare supplied snapshots for the approved launch-readiness dependency only within that scope and approval window. For a baseline-only review, draft a dated baseline containing the requirement, evidence state, owner, dates, and access status. For a comparison review, compare the supplied baseline and user-maintained previous report, and return only changed wording, new or resolved evidence, changed ownership, approaching or missed dates, and access failures, with source and date. If prior state is unavailable, report that comparison is unavailable and stop until the reviewer approves a new baseline. Keep report drafts unsent; future delivery requires separate explicit approval. Do not infer eligibility, technical readiness, incentive availability, program approval, partner acceptance, or completion from silence. Do not update a portal or submit a request. The named reviewer and authorized program or technical owner validate every change and retain all readiness decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated baseline-only or change-only supplied-evidence review draft with source/history/access gaps and an unactivated proposal for the named reviewer; zero scheduled jobs or notifications.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R validates the recruit and offer context; authorized program or technical owners decide applicability and readiness. Scout does not determine eligibility, approve programs, or update systems.
activities.requiredContext: One approved launch-readiness dependency; explicit reviewer approval of monitoring scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access, and review or expiry date; named PDM-R reviewer; and authorized program or technical owner. Provide authorized dated snapshots and user-maintained baseline/prior report if available. Source permissions, scope, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and automation approval are explicit proposed fields; missing inputs remain gaps and no tool access/state retention is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one bounded dependency/action and supply authorized dated snapshots; clearly labeled synthetic evidence is rehearsal-only.
2. Check the user-maintained baseline/prior report, comparable definitions and named reviewer; leave missing history, permission or criteria explicit.
3. Compare supplied evidence manually or with one already authorized tool; no schedule, live retrieval or persistent agent memory.
4. Produce a dated baseline-only/comparison draft and unactivated proposal with source, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval fields.
5. Apply the unchanged HumanCheckpoint before interpretation/action; future automation, notifications and system changes require separate explicit authorization.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.
activities.whyThisMatters: Approved monitoring keeps time-sensitive readiness evidence visible without turning a changed page or missing artifact into a program decision.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What exactly does our evidence prove about this offer today? Contrast a supplied listing screenshot with proof of current IPCS, incentive, and co-sell requirements; avoid collapsing distinct states into a single readiness label.
keyTalkingPoints: Use current official sources and supplied Partner Center evidence with timestamps and offer identity. Do not assume PMX/Partner Center connectors. Current eligibility and technical readiness require authorized owner validation; AI cannot certify, submit, or make incentive/funding decisions.
discussionQuestions: Which readiness dimension has the weakest evidence? Does the evidence refer to the same offer/version, geography, and time period? Which missing artifact is merely unavailable rather than proof of failure?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check a bounded slice of current launch requirements'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Use the Featured practice that best fits whether the gap is the rule, the proof, or a source conflict. Review the most consequential unknown before moving on and assign its validator. facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R names one gap, its exact proof requirement, and its authorized validator. Keep readiness and eligibility decisions pending where current criteria or evidence are incomplete. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one recruit/offer ID, relevant official requirements with dates and applicability scope, and approved supplied listing/Partner Center/co-sell evidence. Confirm research access and Cowork access/spending policy; redact customer details. Identify current program and technical validators. Choose one practice ; no portal writes, eligibility decisions, public sharing, or submissions.
facilitatorQuestions: Can every checklist item point to a current applicable rule? Which status requires partner-side confirmation? Are we assuming incentive eligibility from listing existence? Who can validate a technical or program requirement?
listenFor: Separate readiness dimensions, dated offer-specific artifacts, applicability caveats, actual source owners, and precise evidence requests. Challenge blanket ready/not-ready labels, stale screenshots treated as live state, and eligibility inferred from CRM.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without official-source access, use supplied excerpts and mark currency unverified. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which status had we been treating as proof of a different requirement?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will seek and validate [one offer-specific artifact or current rule] with [program/technical/source owner] by [date], then update the internal evidence register after human review. activities.name: Inspect the recorded MSX state of one lighthouse opportunity
activities.description: Finds the real recorded next step without allowing a CRM stage to stand in for the recruit's full early-win outcome.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Read only the authorized MSX opportunity linked to the recruit lighthouse case, using the specific deal-state questions and my existing CRM permissions. Complete the inspection. 1) Confirm the correct record and stop if access or identity is unresolved. 2) Extract recorded stage, owner, dated next step, decision notes, and value/currency where available, retaining record references and freshness caveats. 3) Return a compact deal-state strip with recorded facts, contradictions, unavailable fields, and one owner question; do not equate recorded stage with verified customer acceptance, partner referral truth, or realized monetization. 4) Ask the PDM-R owner and the opportunity owner to validate the interpretation and next decision. Stop before updating MSX, submitting referrals, announcing a win, or making commitments, eligibility, discount, or funding decisions. If existing authorized record access is unavailable, inspect a dated authorized extract of the exact identified record or clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Mark access gaps explicitly; synthetic data supports rehearsal only, never a real opportunity conclusion.
activities.expectedOutput: One recorded deal-state strip with source references, dates, contradictions, unavailable fields, and a next-decision validation question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R and the opportunity owner validate recorded facts. Customer acceptance, authoritative partner referral state, and realized monetization require separate evidence; no MSX writes or outcome declarations.
activities.requiredContext: One exact MSX opportunity ID; recruit linkage; deal-state questions; existing CRM permissions; PDM-R and opportunity owner. No partner-side connector or referral authority assumed. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one exact authorized opportunity (1 min).
2. Inspect recorded MSX facts read-only (3 min).
3. Review freshness and unsupported inferences (2 min).
4. PDM-R selects the owner validation question (2 min); stop without writes.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: Finds the real recorded next step without allowing a CRM stage to stand in for the recruit's full early-win outcome.

activities.name: Reconcile customer decision, partner status, and monetization proof
activities.description: Protects early-win decisions from source mismatches and from confusing a promising deal narrative with verified monetization.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Reconcile the recruit early-win case using the approved MSX excerpt, the customer decision evidence, the supplied partner-side status artifact, and the monetization evidence with dates. Use the bracketed inputs only and finish. 1) Match opportunity, offer, customer, currency, and reporting periods where relevant; flag unmatchable or absent inputs. 2) Separate recorded deal facts, actual customer decisions, partner-side claims/records, and realized monetization proof, retaining artifact references. 3) Return a four-row evidence note with what each source proves, what it cannot prove, conflicts, and one highest-priority validation question; Microsoft-only CRM cannot establish authoritative partner referral state. 4) Ask the PDM-R owner and the authorized source owners to confirm the facts before deciding the next action. Stop before declaring a win or revenue, updating systems, submitting actions, or sharing any lighthouse story externally.
activities.expectedOutput: Four-row evidence note separating decision, recorded status, partner-side proof, and monetization, plus one priority validation question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R verifies partner-side facts with authorized source owners; monetization and customer decisions require their actual evidence. Missing artifacts cannot imply no progress or a verified win.
activities.requiredContext: One early-win case; approved MSX, customer-decision, partner-side, and monetization artifacts with dates/identifiers; PDM-R and authorized source owners. Cowork access/spending policy; no portal connectors assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one case and matched identifiers (1 min).
2. Reconcile four distinct evidence dimensions (3 min).
3. Inspect conflicts and limits of proof (2 min).
4. PDM-R assigns source-owner validation (2 min); stop before outcome claims.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Protects early-win decisions from source mismatches and from confusing a promising deal narrative with verified monetization.

activities.name: Prepare one evidence-backed lighthouse blocker escalation
activities.description: Turns early-win friction into a small accountable decision rather than a broad, unsupported escalation or commercial promise.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Prepare an internal escalation brief for the recruit lighthouse blocker using the approved win-evidence note, the actual owner responses, and the supplied escalation/approval guidance. Keep the exercise. 1) State the one decision needed and separate an evidenced blocker from an unavailable input or unverified claim. 2) Trace its impact and dependency to source references without inventing revenue loss, customer commitments, or partner-side status. 3) Return a half-page brief with known facts, disputed facts, two bounded response options, accountable decision owner, and proposed evidence/date for the next check. activities.requiredContext: One blocker; approved win-evidence note; actual owner responses; current escalation/approval guidance; PDM-R and decision owner. Customer decision evidence only if genuinely relevant; supplied sources only.
activitySteps: 1. Select one evidenced blocker and decision (1 min).
2. Trace impact and owner responses (3 min).
3. Inspect two bounded response options (2 min).
4. PDM-R chooses escalation or evidence collection (2 min); stop before sending.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: What do we mean by win here, and what evidence supports that meaning? Compare a recorded MSX stage, a customer decision note, partner-side transaction status, and monetization proof; none automatically substitutes for another.
keyTalkingPoints: Sales Agent inspects authorized MSX records only and cannot establish authoritative partner referral state. Cowork reconciles supplied evidence, not live portal truth. PDM-R verifies partner-side facts and determines escalation. This recruit lifecycle huddle has no default MCEM mapping; an actual customer decision must be evidenced before applying a customer-stage lens.
discussionQuestions: Which part of the win story has actual proof? Is the next blocker a customer decision, partner-side action, or missing monetization evidence? What would the source owner need to confirm before we call progress?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect the recorded MSX state of one lighthouse opportunity'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose whether the next decision needs CRM facts, cross-source reconciliation, or a blocker brief. After one Featured practice, ask the owner to state exactly what the evidence permits and what it does not. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile customer decision, partner status, and monetization proof', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R identifies one validated fact, one unresolved claim, and the next human decision. Separate internal evidence review from permission to announce a lighthouse win or make a commercial commitment. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one exact authorized MSX opportunity ID or approved excerpts, supplied customer decision notes, partner-side status evidence, and early monetization artifacts with dates and identifiers. Confirm permissions and Cowork spending policy. Redact unnecessary customer details. Choose one practice; no stage writes, submissions, commercial decisions, commitments, or external win sharing.
facilitatorQuestions: Are we comparing the same opportunity, offer, and reporting period? Does the source prove a decision, transaction, or realized value? Which missing field is unavailable input rather than observed lack of progress? Who validates partner-side truth?
listenFor: Precise win definitions, matched identifiers, recorded versus verified status, separate monetization proof, and a named validation owner. Challenge MSX-derived referral conclusions, forecasts described as revenue, and permissionless lighthouse publicity.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If MSX access fails, work from approved supplied excerpts or a manual evidence strip. If customer or partner-side artifacts are absent, label them unavailable and request them; do not declare no win, no progress, or realized revenue. Keep any escalation a draft until PDM-R reviews. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which success claim required a different source than the one we initially used?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate [one win, partner-side, or monetization fact] with [authorized source owner] by [date], then decide [one escalation or next action] without inferring outcomes from missing inputs. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized lighthouse or monetization claim checked and whether it improved the next human decision; no win material or publication is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Review graduation evidence against supplied current criteria
activities.description: Prevents a polished graduation packet from concealing unverified rules or an unaccepted transfer of recruit ownership.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Review the recruit's graduation evidence packet against the supplied current graduation criteria/owner/version, the transfer conditions, and the receiving-authority and actual acceptance evidence. Complete one internal review. 1) Verify the governing inputs are present; thresholds, receiving owner, and transfer point remain UNVERIFIED where no authoritative input is supplied. 2) Map each supplied criterion to artifact/page/date references, separating verified evidence, recruit claims, conflicts, and unavailable inputs; invent no thresholds. 3) Return a compact review matrix with unmet evidence needs, acceptance scope, and a provisional decision-readiness note, not a graduation verdict. 4) Ask the PDM-R owner to attest completeness and the authorized decision/receiving owners to validate criteria, authority, actual acceptance, and transfer conditions. Stop before nomination submission, graduation, or accountability transfer; absent mandatory evidence requires a documented decision hold, never assumed receiving PDM/BPA acceptance.
activities.expectedOutput: Criteria-to-evidence matrix with dated references, explicit UNVERIFIED governing inputs, acceptance scope, evidence requests, and a provisional decision-readiness/hold note.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R attests completeness; authorized owners validate current criteria, receiving authority, actual acceptance, and transfer conditions. Missing mandatory evidence blocks the decision; AI cannot graduate or transfer accountability.
activities.requiredContext: One approved recruit packet; current criteria owner/version; transfer conditions; receiving-authority evidence; actual acceptance or explicit missing-input note; PDM-R and authorized decision reviewers. Cowork access/spending policy; supplied inputs only.
activitySteps: 1. Check governing criteria and acceptance inputs (1 min).
2. Map one recruit's evidence to supplied criteria (3 min).
3. Inspect authority, acceptance scope, and gaps (2 min).
4. PDM-R records review or decision hold (2 min); stop before graduation/transfer.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Prevents a polished graduation packet from concealing unverified rules or an unaccepted transfer of recruit ownership.

activities.name: Draft a continuity package with explicit acceptance boundaries
activities.description: Keeps the recruit's open obligations owned while the actual receiving authority and acceptance conditions are resolved.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Draft a continuity handoff package for the recruit from the approved assets/decision log, the current graduation and transfer criteria, the owner-authority evidence, and the actual receiving acceptance or missing-input note. Finish. 1) Identify the confirmed current owner, proposed receiving owner, and any UNVERIFIED authority; never assume a receiving PDM/BPA. 2) Summarize no more than five open obligations with source references, artifact location, next action, and proposed versus accepted owner/date. 3) Return a one-page package plus an acceptance ledger showing exact accepted scope, unresolved conditions, and accountability pending a validated transfer; naming a recipient or sending a package is not acceptance. 4) Ask the PDM-R owner and the authorized receiving/decision owners to validate completeness, current criteria, actual acceptance, and transfer conditions. Stop at the internal draft; do not send, graduate, or transfer ownership.
activities.expectedOutput: One-page continuity package and acceptance ledger covering at most five obligations, evidence locations, accepted versus proposed ownership, and unresolved transfer conditions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R validates completeness and continuing ownership; authorized receiving/decision owners validate current criteria and actual scoped acceptance. No assumed recipient role, silent acceptance, automatic graduation, or transfer.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit; approved asset/decision log; current graduation and transfer rules; current/receiving authority evidence; actual scoped acceptance or missing note; PDM-R and authorized reviewers. Supplied sources only.
activitySteps: 1. Verify current/proposed owner authority inputs (1 min).
2. Draft up to five continuity obligations (3 min).
3. Inspect actual acceptance and pending accountability (2 min).
4. PDM-R assigns authorized acceptance review (2 min); stop before transfer or sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Keeps the recruit's open obligations owned while the actual receiving authority and acceptance conditions are resolved.

activities.name: Document a graduation decision hold without inventing rules
activities.description: Creates a safe, actionable outcome when graduation governance is incomplete without erasing real recruit progress or implying handoff acceptance.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Prepare a decision-hold note for the recruit where the specified graduation criteria, receiving-authority, acceptance, or transfer inputs are missing, using the approved available packet and the known governing source references. Limit the review. 1) List exactly which mandatory inputs are unavailable or UNVERIFIED, distinguishing missing evidence from a failed criterion or refused handoff. 2) Preserve the known progress and unresolved obligations with dated references; do not infer thresholds, receiving role, acceptance, or transfer timing. 3) Return a half-page hold note with decision blocked, minimum evidence requests, authorized confirmer needed, and current accountability requiring confirmation. 4) Ask the PDM-R owner to validate the note, identify the actual governing owner, and choose an owner-dated request. Stop before declaring ineligibility, assuming receiving PDM/BPA acceptance, submitting nomination, graduating, or transferring the recruit.
activities.expectedOutput: Half-page decision-hold note distinguishing unavailable evidence from failure/refusal, with minimum evidence requests and accountability requiring confirmation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R validates the hold and identifies authorized governing owners. Current criteria, receiving authority, actual acceptance, and transfer conditions remain mandatory; no negative eligibility or graduation verdict is inferred.
activities.requiredContext: One recruit packet; explicit missing governing/acceptance inputs; known current-source references; documented current owner if available; PDM-R reviewer. No invented graduation thresholds or default receiving role.
activitySteps: 1. Identify one decision and missing mandatory inputs (1 min).
2. Preserve evidenced progress and obligations (3 min).
3. Inspect minimum requests and continuing ownership (2 min).
4. PDM-R records the hold and validation owner/date (2 min); stop before status changes.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Creates a safe, actionable outcome when graduation governance is incomplete without erasing real recruit progress or implying handoff acceptance.

activities.name: Preview a bounded missing-artifact monitor for an incomplete handoff
activities.description: Helps an incomplete handoff stay visible without turning artifact monitoring into an unattended graduation, implied acceptance, or ownership transfer.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Preview a read-only missing-artifact check for the incomplete recruit handoff using only the approved evidence locations, the current criteria and artifact checklist, and the dated baseline. Do not schedule anything. First, confirm source permission and exact artifact scope; if Scout is unavailable, compare the approved supplied artifacts manually. Stop if permission or artifact identity is unverified. Compare accessible supplied artifacts with the baseline, distinguishing missing inputs, access failures, changed evidence, and confirmed unchanged items; unchanged evidence does not prove no progress. Return an exceptions-only preview with source/date, affected criterion, actual acceptance evidence still missing, and proposed reviewer; do not infer graduation thresholds or receiving ownership. Ask the PDM-R owner to validate the preview and request separate approval for any future schedule, cadence, sources, recipients, and expiry. Stop before scheduling, notifications, writes, graduation, or accountability transfer. Use a user-supplied dated baseline and prior report; keep missing history explicit and do not assume persistent agent memory.
activities.expectedOutput: Exceptions-only read-only preview with dated source references, evidence changes/access gaps, missing acceptance proof, and proposed reviewers; zero scheduled jobs or notifications.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PDM-R approves only the preview. Any future schedule needs separate explicit approval of cadence, source scope, recipients, and expiry; current criteria and actual acceptance remain mandatory for any human graduation/transfer decision.
activities.requiredContext: Optional Scout access must be validated; one incomplete handoff; explicitly approved supplied source list; current artifact criteria; baseline/date; PDM-R reviewer. No PMX/Partner Center connector or source expansion assumed; missing access uses manual/Cowork fallback.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm optional access and bounded source approval (1 min).
2. Run one read-only baseline comparison (3 min).
3. Inspect exceptions and unavailable inputs (2 min).
4. PDM-R validates preview only (2 min); stop before any scheduling or notifications.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.
activities.whyThisMatters: Helps an incomplete handoff stay visible without turning artifact monitoring into an unattended graduation, implied acceptance, or ownership transfer.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Ask: If we stopped owning this recruit today, what proves another authorized owner has accepted the right responsibilities? State explicitly that graduation thresholds, receiving owner, evidence standard, and transfer point are UNVERIFIED in the source; a receiving PDM/BPA must not be assumed.
keyTalkingPoints: Use supplied current graduation criteria and transfer conditions; invent no thresholds or receiving role. PDM-R attests package completeness but does not infer acceptance from a named recipient, silence, or a sent document. Actual authorized acceptance is mandatory decision evidence. The Extended Scout variant is optional, access-unverified, and read-only preview only; scheduling needs separate approval.
discussionQuestions: Which criteria and transfer conditions have a current authoritative source? What proves the actual receiving owner is authorized and has accepted the defined scope? What remains owned by PDM-R while a decision is pending?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Review graduation evidence against supplied current criteria'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Choose the decision bottleneck: evidence against supplied criteria, continuity/acceptance, or missing governing inputs. After one Featured practice, require the PDM-R owner to name the remaining decision gate rather than announce graduation. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Preview a bounded missing-artifact monitor for an incomplete handoff', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: PDM-R states package completeness and the decision's evidence limits. Record graduation/transfer as pending where mandatory evidence is missing, and name the accountable continuity owner until an authorized human decision confirms otherwise. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one recruit's approved assets, decision log, current graduation criteria with owner/version, transfer conditions, receiving-authority evidence, and actual acceptance or an explicit missing-input note. Confirm Cowork access/spending policy. Scout is optional only after access is validated, with an approved bounded source list; no source-system connector assumed. Select a Featured practice that fits the workflow and available inputs; preserve internal labels and perform no graduation, transfer, submission, sharing, or scheduling.
facilitatorQuestions: Can we distinguish package completeness from criteria satisfaction and actual acceptance? Which owner/threshold/transfer claim remains UNVERIFIED? Is unavailable acceptance evidence being mislabeled as rejection? Who retains accountability pending an authorized decision?
listenFor: Current criterion references, explicit unresolved thresholds, actual acceptance tied to scope, verified receiving authority, and a continuity owner pending decision. Challenge automatic graduation, assumed receiving PDM/BPA, or an artifact monitor that changes state or schedules itself.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without current criteria, receiving-authority evidence, transfer conditions, or actual acceptance, produce a decision-hold note and targeted request. Do not invent defaults. If Scout access or source approval is unavailable, review the supplied artifact list manually or in Cowork; no automation is required for this active huddle. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption about thresholds, ownership, or acceptance did this review expose?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will seek and validate [one current criterion, receiving-authority, acceptance, or transfer artifact] with [authorized owner] by [date], then request the appropriate human decision; I will not automatically graduate or transfer the recruit. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized graduation criterion or continuity-owner assumption checked and whether it improved transfer judgment or justified pending status. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-EPS-PDM-R-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

PLC-EPS-PMM-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-EPS-PMM-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-EPS-PMM-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.
