activities.name: Choose a segment using a three-signal market brief
activities.description: Live choice: eight minutes for one segment; an approved prior response is the retrieval fallback.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Using only the supplied approved segment brief, dated maturity excerpt and two or three market sources, create a three-signal market brief for the named partner, segment and geography. For each signal show the claim, citation, publication date, regional applicability and whether it is fact or inference. Separate market attractiveness from evidence of partner marketing capability. Propose one bounded marketing hypothesis, one disconfirming question and one missing maturity input. Do not invent market size, campaign results or readiness scores. Ask the PMM to choose pursue, narrow or defer. Stop with a draft brief and explicit gaps if citations or applicability cannot be verified; do not publish or initiate outreach.
activities.expectedOutput: Three cited signal rows, one hypothesis, one disconfirming question, one maturity gap and dated PMM decision; unsupported rows stay unknown.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM verifies dates and applicability. Stop/defer on missing critical evidence; no outreach or publication.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies exactly one approved partner/segment/geography/decision-date brief, one dated maturity excerpt and two or three approved market URLs/excerpts with dates. Only accessible supplied sources; no native system access assumed.
activitySteps: 1. confirm segment, region and sources.
2. run the prompt or inspect the approved prior response.
3. challenge one inference and maturity gap.
4. PMM records pursue/narrow/defer; stop at the draft.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Separate a marketing hypothesis from readiness or future-sales claims.

activities.name: Expose the evidence gap in a maturity assessment
activities.description: Featured alternative: three supplied maturity dimensions for one segment.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Review the supplied three-dimension maturity rubric, dated partner assessment excerpt and approved evidence snippets for one segment. Build an evidence coverage matrix with one row per dimension: rubric definition, observed evidence, source date, supported assessment, unknowns and evidence owner. Apply a rubric rating only when its stated criteria are demonstrated; otherwise write not established. Identify the single evidence request most likely to change our marketing plan and explain why. Do not infer missing capability from market interest or create a numerical score not in the rubric. Ask the PMM to confirm or defer the assessment. Stop at the reviewed matrix and draft request; do not send it or update a system record.
activities.expectedOutput: Three-row maturity matrix and one prioritized draft request with owner, due-date placeholder and decision impact.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM accepts only rubric-supported assessments. Stop on missing definitions or unsupported ratings; do not send.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies one approved rubric with three dimensions/definitions, one dated segment assessment and up to three approved evidence snippets with owners. No marketing-system query assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm three rubric definitions.
2. Map snippets to dimensions.
3. Replace unsupported ratings with not established.
4. PMM selects one request and owner; stop before sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Unknown capability needs an evidence request, not an invented score.

activities.name: Prepare a six-field referral-candidate handoff packet
activities.description: Live choice: eight minutes for one anonymized candidate; no submission.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Prepare a draft handoff packet for the single supplied anonymized campaign-response candidate using only the agreed qualification criteria, documented sharing status and receiving-owner convention. Use six fields: campaign/context, observed intent evidence and date, criteria met or unknown, sharing permission, missing information and named PSS receiving owner/requested disposition. Preserve the actual recorded status; label this a candidate unless explicit PSS acceptance is supplied. Do not convert clicks into qualified intent, invent scores or infer customer progression. Recommend hold or request PSS review and explain the decisive evidence gap. Ask the PMM to verify permissible sharing and criteria before any handoff. Stop if either is unclear; do not send, submit, update records or claim incremental sales or accepted-referral results.
activities.expectedOutput: Six-field anonymized candidate packet, one decisive gap and PMM decision; acceptance explicit or pending.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM validates sharing/evidence; PSS decides sales acceptance/progression. Stop on unclear permission, criteria or intent; no automatic handoff or status change.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies authorized anonymized response record/date, current agreed marketing-to-PSS criteria, documented consent/sharing status and receiving-owner convention. Remove unnecessary personal data; no CRM/Partner Center/Marketplace/dashboard access assumed.
activitySteps: 1. confirm anonymization, criteria and permission.
2. assemble six fields from the record.
3. challenge inferred intent/acceptance and gap.
4. PMM holds/requests-review; stop without submission.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Let PSS assess acceptance without invented qualification or progression.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Use one permissioned anonymized response record. Ask what it demonstrates and what PSS still must decide. Response, referral submission and PSS acceptance are separate; this huddle does not move customers through MCEM.
keyTalkingPoints: Use agreed criteria, never invented thresholds. Verify permissible sharing and actual intent. PMM owns marketing evidence/handoff quality; PSS owns sales qualification/progression. Correlated response is not incremental sales or acceptance. Cowork uses supplied extracts, not native CRM, Partner Center, Marketplace or dashboards. No automatic sharing/submission/status updates.
discussionQuestions: What proves intent rather than a click? Is sharing authorized? Where is PSS acceptance actually recorded?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Prepare a six-field referral-candidate handoff packet'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Carry actual PSS dispositions and definitions, not inferred acceptance, into ROB optimization. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Resolve one returned handoff without inventing customer intent', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: A marketing handoff needs permitted inputs and the applicable criteria, while PSS separately decides acceptance and sales qualification. A completed marketing packet is not an accepted referral or incremental sale. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Supply one authorized anonymized candidate, agreed criteria, consent/sharing evidence and receiving-owner convention.
facilitatorQuestions: What permitted evidence supports customer intent and the actual handoff criteria? Which candidate field remains unknown? How does another PMM distinguish a referral candidate from a PSS-accepted handoff?
listenFor: Anonymization; actual criteria; unknowns retained; candidate versus accepted; named PSS owner; no sales progression or causal attribution by PMM.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, complete one six-field referral candidate: permitted evidence/identity boundary, customer-intent support, current criteria or unknown, source/date, proposed PSS receiver, and candidate/returned/accepted evidence state manually from permitted excerpts. If none are available, use a clearly labeled synthetic campaign to practice the method only; it is not evidence of demand, eligibility, approval, customer intent or outcomes. Preserve unknowns and do not substitute historical funding amounts or invented rules. Fill six fields manually. If permission, intent or criteria are absent, use a gap-only record without personal data and hold; never manufacture a lead or acceptance.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which phrase could falsely imply sales qualification, acceptance or an incremental sale?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate one handoff gap with its named marketing/partner owner by the agreed date, then seek PSS review only through the approved process if sharing and criteria are satisfied. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized marketing handoff gap checked and whether it improved PSS review readiness; acceptance and qualification may remain pending. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Make one evidence-bounded ROB campaign decision
activities.description: Live choice: eight minutes, one decision and two supplied measures.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Create a one-page ROB decision brief for the supplied campaign using only the two-period extract, approved definitions for two selected measures, actual partner/PSS feedback and current constraints. Show each numerator, denominator, cohort, observation window and source; flag noncomparable periods or pending acceptance records. Separate observations from interpretation and include one competing explanation. Recommend one keep, adjust, pause or defer decision with an owner, review date placeholder and stop condition. Do not infer incremental sales, ROI or PSS acceptance from campaign response. Ask the PMM to validate the evidence and choose the marketing action. Stop if comparison is invalid or authority is unclear. Keep proposed changes draft until required approvers and the partner agree; do not send, alter spend or activate anything.
activities.expectedOutput: One ROB brief, two comparisons, one competing explanation, bounded decision, owner, review-date placeholder and stop condition.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM validates marketing action and data definitions; PSS confirms dispositions. Stop on invalid comparison/authority; changes remain draft pending approvers/partner.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies authorized campaign extract for two periods, approved dictionary for two measures, actual partner/PSS feedback and constraints/reviewers. Include counts/windows/cut-off; absent fields stay unknown. No native dashboard/PMX/CRM access.
activitySteps: 1. confirm decision and two measures.
2. draft brief with counts/windows/feedback.
3. inspect comparability and alternative explanation.
4. PMM records decision, owner and stop condition; do not implement.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Link observations to an accountable action without false incrementality.

activities.name: Reconcile one conflicting campaign metric before the ROB
activities.description: Featured alternative: two extracts for one disputed measure.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Reconcile the single disputed campaign measure across the two supplied authorized extracts using their timestamps, counting definitions and intended ROB window. Build a five-check comparison for unit of count, deduplication key, cohort inclusion, observation window and status cut-off. Show which difference is evidenced and which remains unknown; trace any numerical reconciliation to supplied rows or totals without manufacturing missing records. Do not average incompatible values, replace missing data with zero or infer accepted referrals from response counts. Draft one precise question for the responsible data owner and state whether the measure is usable for this ROB decision. Ask the PMM to accept the limitation or defer the decision. Stop at the comparison and unsent question; do not edit dashboards or publish corrected numbers.
activities.expectedOutput: Five-check reconciliation, one source-traced discrepancy, one owner question and ROB usability status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM decides evidence usability; data owner confirms corrections. Stop on unresolved count/window differences; no invented reconciliation, edits or published metrics.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies two authorized extracts for one campaign/measure, source timestamps, counting definitions and intended ROB window. An anonymized key sample is optional if authorized. No direct dashboard query/edit.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm disputed measure and ROB window.
2. Apply five definition checks to both extracts.
3. Trace differences and retain unknown causes.
4. PMM chooses use-with-limit/defer; keep question unsent.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Do not average incompatible metrics into a false answer.

activities.name: Design one bounded campaign adjustment test
activities.description: Featured alternative: one proposed change, no experiment launch.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Draft a one-change test card for the supplied campaign issue using only the baseline counts, approved claims sheet, channel/consent constraints and test-approval convention. Specify the hypothesis, single changed element, unchanged conditions, eligible audience, response measure with numerator/denominator/window, comparison limitations, review owner and stop rule. Use an existing approved threshold if supplied; otherwise leave the threshold for the PMM and approver to decide. Do not invent baseline results, power calculations, causal lift or ROI. Explain that observed response correlation does not establish incremental sales. Ask the PMM whether the test is worth proposing and which measurement gap must close. Stop at the draft until original/local claims are verified and required approvers plus the partner agree; do not send, publish or launch.

activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM evaluates learning value; data/approval owners confirm feasibility and claims. Stop on missing consent, invalid measurement or absent agreement; no launch or causal sales claim.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies approved issue statement, authorized baseline counts/denominator/window, current approved claims sheet, channel/consent constraints and actual test-approval convention. Use supplied approved thresholds; absent thresholds remain human decisions.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm issue, baseline and constraints.
2. Draft one change and fully defined response measure.
3. Inspect comparison limits, threshold/placeholder and stop rule.
4. PMM proposes/revises/holds; no implementation.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.name: Frame a ROB diagnosis at xPMM L100 or sPMM L200
activities.description: Extended optional variant: business or solution-area diagnostic depth.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. activitySteps: 1. Select branch; keep campaign/metric definitions.
2. Draft observation, alternatives and question at L100/L200.
3. Check subgroup denominators and remove causal/fit claims.
4. PMM validates/defers; stop before changes.

activities.name: Monitor one approved campaign adjustment
activities.description: Track evidence for an approved campaign adjustment and surface only changes for PMM review.
activities.prompt: Produce an unactivated read-only proposal, not a running monitor. Use authorized dated snapshots, a user-maintained baseline and previous report supplied for this review; do not retrieve unsupplied records, create automation, retain agent memory or notify anyone. Missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no change. Record scope, source permission, owner, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and supplied approved change criteria without inventing values. Future monitoring requires separate explicit approval and verified access/state capabilities. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Compare supplied snapshots for the approved campaign adjustment on the approved cadence using the approved evidence locations, the dated baseline, the response metric definition, and the named action owner. For a baseline-only review, record the dated adjustment, metric window, denominator, and evidence baseline. For a comparison review, compare the supplied baseline and user-maintained previous report. Return change-only findings for material measure movement, changed conditions, missing evidence, or access failures, preserving the stated attribution limits. Do not infer causation, change the campaign, or notify stakeholders. the named action owner validates execution, and PMM decides whether to continue, revise, test, or hold.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated baseline-only or change-only supplied-evidence review draft with source/history/access gaps and an unactivated proposal for the named reviewer; zero scheduled jobs or notifications.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The action owner validates execution; PMM retains campaign adjustment and attribution decisions.
activities.requiredContext: An approved adjustment, approved cadence, evidence locations, dated baseline, metric definition, action owner, and PMM reviewer. Provide authorized dated snapshots and user-maintained baseline/prior report if available. Source permissions, scope, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and automation approval are explicit proposed fields; missing inputs remain gaps and no tool access/state retention is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one bounded dependency/action and supply authorized dated snapshots; clearly labeled synthetic evidence is rehearsal-only.
2. Check the user-maintained baseline/prior report, comparable definitions and named reviewer; leave missing history, permission or criteria explicit.
3. Compare supplied evidence manually or with one already authorized tool; no schedule, live retrieval or persistent agent memory.
4. Produce a dated baseline-only/comparison draft and unactivated proposal with source, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval fields.
5. Apply the unchanged HumanCheckpoint before interpretation/action; future automation, notifications and system changes require separate explicit authorization.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.
activities.whyThisMatters: Change-only monitoring supports disciplined optimization without automating attribution or campaign decisions.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Name one campaign decision. Inspect denominators/windows before changes. PMM optimizes marketing; PSS retains sales progression and the partner its agreement role.
keyTalkingPoints: Separate observations, interpretations and decisions. State numerators, denominators, cohorts and windows; acceptance only from actual PSS records. Response correlation is not incremental sales/ROI. Cowork synthesizes supplied extracts/feedback, not native dashboards. Recommendations cannot approve spend, send communications or activate changes.
discussionQuestions: Are periods comparable? What competing explanation fits? Which action can PMM own and whose agreement is still needed?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Make one evidence-bounded ROB campaign decision'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from dashboard movement to a bounded decision; carry rationale and failure conditions into reusable insight. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile one conflicting campaign metric before the ROB', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: ROB campaign choices require valid comparison windows, definitions and denominators, with contrary evidence and a stop condition visible. Do not attribute sales causally to marketing without evidence. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Supply one two-period campaign extract, approved metric definitions, actual partner/PSS feedback and current constraints/reviewers.
facilitatorQuestions: Are the cohorts, denominators and time windows comparable? What competing explanation remains plausible? How would another PMM choose one keep, adjust, pause or defer decision and define the next evidence check?
listenFor: One decision; comparable cohorts; pending dispositions visible; no causal leap; one owned action and actual agreement status.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, use permitted excerpts to complete one campaign decision brief: cohort, denominator, window, comparable observation or unknown, competing explanation, keep/adjust/pause/defer choice, proposed owner and next test. If no excerpts are available, use a labeled synthetic campaign for practice only. Preserve unknowns. If windows or denominators do not reconcile, defer and ask the data owner; never manufacture a trend or replace unknowns with zero.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What uncertainty did we preserve, and where might language overclaim marketing-caused sales?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate one ROB decision with its named data/partner owner by the agreed date and keep changes draft until approvers and partner agree. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized metric-definition, comparison-window or denominator issue checked and whether it changed ROB continue, revise or stop judgment; do not claim marketing-caused sales. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Test one insight's transfer to a new region
activities.description: Featured alternative: one insight and one target geography.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Assess whether the supplied anonymized marketing insight can be considered for the single target region and audience using the approved claims sheet and official source URLs or excerpts. Produce a three-row transferability check covering audience/context fit, current claim or offer applicability, and local requirement differences. Cite each external assertion with date and territorial scope, and distinguish verified facts from proposed adaptations. Do not generalize the original campaign's results, promise equivalent response or infer eligibility and legal approval. Identify one non-transfer condition and one local-owner validation question. Ask the PMM to adapt, hold or reject reuse. Stop if current evidence or applicability is unclear; do not publish or activate anything, and require original/local claim verification plus approver and partner agreement before later use.
activities.expectedOutput: Three-row cited transferability check, one non-transfer condition, one local-owner question and PMM decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM checks relevance; local policy/language/technical owners verify applicability. Stop on uncertain currency/scope; no result promises, publication or activation.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies approved-for-review anonymized insight, target region/audience brief, current approved claims sheet and two or three approved official regional URLs/excerpts. No entitlement, partner-side status or legal approval inferred.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one insight and target region/audience.
2. Research three transfer dimensions from official sources.
3. Inspect dates, scope and non-transfer condition.
4. PMM adapts/holds/rejects; leave question unsent.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Check current applicability rather than assuming another region will repeat results.

keyBenefits: Produces source-cited research reports rather than unattributed summaries, combining work content and web research across multiple steps so claims can be traced.

resources.title: Get started with Researcher in Microsoft Copilot

activities.name: Capture an inconclusive campaign result as useful learning
activities.description: Featured alternative: one honest record, not a fabricated success story.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Turn the supplied inconclusive campaign review, original hypothesis, available counts and actual feedback into a four-part learning record: what was attempted, what was observed, what cannot be concluded and the next smallest evidence question. Preserve numerator, denominator and observation window where available; mark absent values unknown, not zero. Explain one plausible competing explanation without presenting it as fact. Do not invent a control group, success result, accepted referral, causal lift or ROI. Keep partner/customer identifiers out and honor the supplied reuse restrictions. Ask the PMM to choose retain the method, revise the hypothesis or stop further work. Stop if evidence is too incomplete to support any conclusion, leaving a gap-only note. Do not send, publish or launch follow-up activity.
activities.expectedOutput: Four-part learning record with unknowns, one alternative explanation, one next question and PMM retain/revise/stop decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM verifies no overstatement; evidence owner validates reuse. Stop if observations lack support; keep gap-only note, never invent success or launch follow-up.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies authorized anonymized inconclusive campaign review, original hypothesis, available counts/definitions/windows and actual partner/PSS feedback plus missing-data/reuse notes. No invented outcomes, control groups or private conversations.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm original hypothesis and inconclusive status.
2. Draft attempted/observed/not-concluded/next-question sections.
3. Inspect unknowns and competing explanation for overclaims.
4. PMM retains/revises/stops; keep record unshared.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Explicit uncertainty improves the next decision without a false performance conclusion.

activities.name: Package one reusable method for xPMM L100 or sPMM L200
activities.description: Extended optional variant: one method at appropriate technical depth.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Package the supplied single marketing insight as a three-step reusable method for the selected PMM branch, preserving evidence, limits and the shared global review process. For xPMM/L100, frame a portfolio-relevant buyer/context check, business-message decision and marketing evidence review without architecture detail. For sPMM/L200, frame the named solution-area use case, documented prerequisite/applicability check and technical-owner validation using only the approved excerpt. Add required inputs, one failure condition and a clear statement that original results do not predict new campaign results. Do not invent technical suitability, causal sales impact or ROI. Ask the PMM to approve the method for further review or hold it. Stop on missing evidence or reuse rights; do not share or activate it, and require original/local claims, approvers and partner agreement before campaign use.
activities.expectedOutput: Three-step depth-tagged recipe, required inputs, sourced applicability, failure condition and explicit non-prediction/review status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PMM validates method; technical owners confirm L200 applicability and evidence owners approve reuse. Stop on unsupported claims/rights; no publication or activation before review and partner agreement.
activities.requiredContext: Owner supplies approved-for-review anonymized insight, selected branch, current claims sheet, reuse constraints and approved technical-applicability excerpt for sPMM. One method/campaign/segment only; no portfolio expansion or invented results.
activitySteps: 1. Select branch and one method from the insight.
2. Draft three-step L100/L200 recipe with inputs.
3. Check evidence limits, failure condition and global review route.
4. PMM retains-for-review/holds; stop before sharing.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Choose one decision worth reusing and ask what could make it fail elsewhere. Reuse does not mean copying customer data, regional rules or unsupported claims; preserve evidence and limits.
keyTalkingPoints: Distinguish observation, hypothesis and validated repeatability. Retain denominators/windows and actual acceptance definitions. Response is not incremental sales, accepted referral or ROI. Remove unnecessary identifiers and honor permissions. Researcher checks current published context; Cowork uses supplied evidence, not native dashboards. Reused claims need original/local verification, approver review and partner agreement before activation. No automatic sharing/publication.
discussionQuestions: What is reusable: method, claim or result? What makes transfer inappropriate? Which evidence must remain restricted?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create a six-field reusable marketing insight card'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Close the path by reusing disciplined decisions: assess, align, govern, localize, hand off, optimize and capture. Carry only approved evidence forward. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Package one reusable method for xPMM L100 or sPMM L200', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Marketing reuse should transfer a method together with evidence limits and conditions where it will not apply. Inconclusive learning can help peers; an early response pattern is not a universal sales claim. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Supply one reviewed ROB decision, authorized anonymized evidence, metric definitions and approved reuse/sharing constraints.
facilitatorQuestions: Which observation is evidenced and which conclusion is inferred? What context or denominator would prevent transfer? What would a peer need to reuse this method safely without turning inconclusive learning into a success story?
listenFor: One decision; traceable anonymized evidence; explicit limits/failure condition; no invented success/repeatability; no restricted context exposure.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the agent or approved context is unavailable, complete one learning card: observation, separate inference, supporting denominator/window, method, transfer limit, permission/reviewer gap and next question manually from permitted excerpts. If none are available, use a clearly labeled synthetic campaign to practice the method only; it is not evidence of demand, eligibility, approval, customer intent or outcomes. Preserve unknowns and do not substitute historical funding amounts or invented rules. Without results or agent access, record method, unknowns and next question manually. Label it learning note, not success story; never fabricate outcomes or approvals.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Did we preserve uncertainty or turn one response pattern into a universal sales claim?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will review one insight with its named evidence/marketing owner by the agreed date, remove unnecessary identifiers and retain draft status until reuse/sharing conditions are satisfied. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized marketing method and non-transfer condition clarified and whether it made reuse safer; inconclusive learning is valid. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-EPS-PMM-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-EPS-PMM-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-EPS-PMM-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

PLC-EPS-PSA-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-EPS-PSA-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-EPS-PSA-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.

activities.name: Turn one intake requirement into an accept, return or reroute card
activities.description: Prevents a broad partner request from becoming an unapproved PSA delivery obligation.
activities.prompt: Use only the conversation and approved materials already supplied. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use only the approved intake excerpt, stated CSA, single requirement and owner list I paste below. Draft a six-field triage card: requirement, technical uncertainty, evidence available, missing evidence, proposed disposition and accountable reviewer. Separate PSA architecture work from PTS cross-solution strategy and partner engineering build work. Recommend accept, return or reroute for this question only; explain the recommendation using exact input references, not assumed system access. Mark unclear ownership as unresolved. Do not retrieve partner records, contact anyone, promise delivery or allocate resources. Pause for the PSA technical authority to confirm scope and routing. Stop once the card and one next evidence request are ready, even if the broader intake remains incomplete.
activities.expectedOutput: One six-field triage card plus one draft evidence request, with unknowns visible.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA technical authority confirms scope and disposition. PTS confirms a strategic reroute; partner engineering accepts build handback. Stop if the accountable reviewer is unknown.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved intake excerpt with source/date; stated CSA; one requirement; known PSA, PTS and partner engineering owners. No full account export or inferred owners.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Paste one sanitized intake requirement, CSA and owner list.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for the six-field card with input references.
3. (2 min) Have the PSA technical authority challenge scope and routing.
4. (2 min) Record accept/return/reroute and one evidence request; stop without sending.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Prevents a broad partner request from becoming an unapproved PSA delivery obligation.

activities.name: Check one intake dependency against dated authoritative guidance
activities.description: Separates authoritative constraints from optimistic intake assumptions before architecture work expands.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Investigate only the single technical dependency in my supplied intake sentence. Use the product/version and approved official source URLs I provide; if permitted, follow their official documentation links, not unrelated partner material. Produce a compact dependency note with the relevant published condition, citation, publication or update date when available, and today's access date. Distinguish what the guidance states from your inference about this requirement. If the source is unavailable, undated or version-mismatched, mark that limitation rather than substituting a confident answer. Do not claim that documentation proves our environment works or certifies compliance. Ask the PSA technical authority to confirm applicability. Stop after one supported dependency finding and one unresolved question, with no system changes.
activities.expectedOutput: One dependency note: condition, citation/date, version fit, inference boundary and unanswered question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA technical authority inspects the citation and applicability. Stop with a gap when authoritative guidance cannot be inspected; search snippets are not approval.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved dependency sentence, product/version, one or two permitted official documentation URLs and execution date. No private portal access implied.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one dependency, product/version and official URL.
2. (3 min) Ask Researcher for one cited, dated finding.
3. (2 min) Inspect the passage and version applicability with PSA.
4. (2 min) Record supported/unclear guidance and one gap; stop research.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.

activities.name: Reconcile two conflicting intake claims without inventing a third
activities.description: Turns conflicting assertions into a reviewable evidence task instead of a speculative architecture.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Compare only the two approved statements and their evidence references that I provide about one technical risk. Create a contradiction ledger with claim A, claim B, what each source actually supports, the decision affected and one discriminating evidence request. Keep dates and product versions attached to each claim. Do not average conflicting claims into a new fact or assume the newest statement is correct. Classify the risk as evidenced, contradicted or unresolved and explain why. Identify whether the next check belongs to the PSA technical authority or partner engineering owner, without assigning work on their behalf. Pause for that authority to review the ledger. Stop at one unresolved risk and its next check; do not design the whole solution.
activities.expectedOutput: One contradiction ledger with a discriminating evidence request and proposed reviewer.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA validates reasoning; partner engineering confirms feasibility of a proposed technical check. If neither claim is supported, retain unresolved status and stop.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: two approved claim excerpts with source/date/version about the same requirement or risk; named technical reviewer. Missing evidence is not invented.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Paste two authorized claims about one risk with source/date.
2. (3 min) Generate the ledger and one discriminating question.
3. (2 min) Have PSA assess whether that question resolves the conflict.
4. (2 min) Record status and proposed owner; stop without assigning or sending work.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Intake can mix partner ambition, cross-solution positioning and implementation requests. Separate those before solving anything. Today we decide whether one question is ready for PSA attention; a strategic customer-deal exception needs explicit sponsorship and must not redefine this baseline.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. One intake requirement, not the entire opportunity. 2. A claimed capability is not verified evidence. 3. PSA resolves CSA architecture questions; PTS steers cross-solution choices; partner engineers build. 4. Return and reroute are legitimate outcomes.
discussionQuestions: Which sentence is a technical requirement rather than a commercial aspiration? What evidence would change the routing decision? Who can accept the architecture question and provide the missing input?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Turn one intake requirement into an accept, return or reroute card'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At minute two, freeze one uncertainty. By minute six, review the artifact against supplied evidence. Use the last two minutes to accept, return or reroute; do not run the other practices as a sequence. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Adapt intake triage for an SI reference or ISV tenant boundary', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the disposition and evidence gap aloud. Confirm no one has silently accepted build delivery, resource allocation or customer commitments. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved, sanitized intake excerpt, the stated solution area, one requirement and known technical owners. Remove customer identifiers and secrets. Use authorized EPS research excerpts and date current technical guidance. Record any unconfirmed coverage, prioritization or regional assumption for SME review; do not treat an authored exercise as a policy mandate.
facilitatorQuestions: What single question are we accepting? What would make this a PTS decision or partner engineering task instead? Which missing input prevents a defensible recommendation?
listenFor: Bounded CSA scope, explicit evidence status and a named technical owner. Challenge invented access, automatic Partner Center/PMX retrieval, full-solution commitments and customer-deal motions presented as the baseline.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without approved intake or agent access, use a labeled synthetic requirement on paper. Produce a gap-and-owner card, not an inferred architecture or hidden search across partner systems.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Where did we nearly confuse a plausible technical idea with an intake ready for action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, name the person who will supply one missing input and agree a review date; draft the request locally for PSA approval before a human sends it. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized intake gap clarified and whether it improved PSA disposition without implying build or capacity acceptance. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Find the feasibility constraint that could invalidate the use case
activities.description: Finds a potentially fatal technical assumption before investment in the offering concept.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Research one feasibility constraint for the Customer Zero action I supply, using the named product/version and approved official documentation URLs. Return a three-part feasibility note: the relevant published limitation or prerequisite, a dated citation with access date, and the specific effect it could have on this action. Separate documented facts from assumptions about our environment. Do not expand into market research or a full solution recommendation. If guidance is unavailable, ambiguous or for a different version, record a gap and the authority needed to resolve it. Documentation alone is not executable validation or compliance approval. Pause for the PSA technical authority to check applicability, then stop with one supported finding and one test implication.
activities.expectedOutput: One feasibility note linking a cited condition to a single test implication, with applicability uncertainty.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA verifies version fit and relevance. Stop with a gap if authoritative guidance cannot be inspected; the note does not approve security or compliance.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one sanitized Customer Zero action, product/version, suspected constraint, permitted official URLs and execution date.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one action, product/version and official URL.
2. (3 min) Ask Researcher for one dated limitation or prerequisite.
3. (2 min) Inspect the cited passage with PSA.
4. (2 min) Capture one test implication or guidance gap and stop.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Finds a potentially fatal technical assumption before investment in the offering concept.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Move from accepted intake to a small offering hypothesis. Customer Zero provides a controlled partner context for learning; it does not authorize customer data, product commitments or customer-deal delivery. Identify the smallest meaningful technical question.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. One capability and intended user. 2. Separate offering promises from observable outcomes. 3. Customer Zero needs a sponsor, permitted data and acceptance owner. 4. Proposed thresholds remain drafts until approved.
discussionQuestions: What must work for this capability to matter? Which assumption can the partner test safely? What would falsify the use case, and who can approve the test?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Frame one Customer Zero hypothesis that can be disproved'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Freeze the one-capability scope by minute two. Spend four minutes drafting and challenging it; reserve two for the next technical review, not the other Featured alternatives. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Define the technical boundary of one offering capability', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the hypothesis and falsifying condition. Confirm this is a draft learning plan, not an offering launch promise or resource commitment. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved capability statement, sanitized Customer Zero scenario, sponsor/data owner and one technical constraint. Use synthetic inputs if permission is absent. Carry approved EPS research references and dates for any current technical guidance; preserve evidence status.
facilitatorQuestions: What are we not promising? Is the outcome observable rather than promotional? Who approves data and the technical acceptance condition?
listenFor: A narrow capability, testable assumption and distinct sponsor/data-owner/technical-authority roles. Challenge commercial claims as evidence, invented thresholds and assumed customer data access.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without an authorized scenario, use a clearly labeled synthetic hypothesis. Build a short approval-gap list covering the decision to test, required evidence, affected environment, accountable approver and next validation question. Separate known facts from assumptions. The exercise rehearses the method only and cannot validate a real partner or customer environment, readiness or approval.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which offering claim sounded convincing until we asked what observable evidence supports it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, seek technical approval of one acceptance condition and data-owner approval of permitted inputs by an agreed date; prepare requests for human review only. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized offering hypothesis sharpened and whether it exposed a data, feasibility or sponsorship gap before commitment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The offering hypothesis needs a technical shape. Keep the discussion small: one component, interface or trust boundary. PSA provides CSA architecture guidance; partner engineers implement, and specialist security/compliance authorities retain their approvals.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Start with a supplied requirement, not a fashionable service. 2. Explain one trade-off and unknown. 3. Published guidance constrains design but does not prove deployment. 4. Boundaries and contracts need named technical reviewers.
discussionQuestions: Which requirement drives this choice? What alternative did we reject, and why? What observation would turn the design claim into validated evidence?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft a one-component architecture decision record'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Freeze the component by minute two. At minute six, ask the authority to select, defer or reject. Use the final two minutes to name one evidence check, not expand the diagram. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test one architecture boundary for SI adaptation or ISV multitenancy', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: State select/defer/reject and the uncertainty remaining. The artifact is a design proposal, not implementation, certification or a successful test. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved requirement, sanitized component/interface sketch, two options when relevant, product/version and one constraint or evidence reference. No credentials, production code or sensitive customer architecture. Identify PSA and partner architect; pre-open permitted official guidance.
facilitatorQuestions: Which sentence is an assumption? Where does responsibility cross the interface? What specialist approval is still required?
listenFor: Requirement-to-choice traceability, explicit unknowns, one interface and partner engineering ownership. Challenge aesthetics as proof, unverified security claims, invented throughput and broader PTS strategy decisions.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without approved design inputs, draw one synthetic interface and label assumptions. If guidance is inaccessible, record the source/version gap and defer the choice rather than substituting an uncited assertion.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which trade-off became clearer when we preserved the rejected alternative or trust boundary?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, seek technical review of one decision or interface contract by an agreed date; partner engineering separately accepts proposed implementation or test work. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized architecture trade-off changed in review and whether it made select, defer or reject clearer. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Write a falsifiable proof contract for one architecture risk
activities.description: Creates a bounded evidence task without mistaking a proposed test for a result.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use only my supplied architecture risk, requirement, proposed sandbox boundary, synthetic data description and approved acceptance condition. Draft a proof contract for one assumption: hypothesis, smallest check, input, approved threshold, expected evidence and stop condition. If the threshold or environment permission is missing, mark the proof blocked rather than inventing either. Specify the run metadata an engineer would need to preserve, but do not create a result or claim execution. Keep partner engineers accountable for build and running the check, with PSA reviewing the architecture implication. Do not request resources or make environment changes. Pause for the PSA technical authority and partner engineering owner to approve the contract. Stop after the plan for this one risk.
activities.expectedOutput: One six-field proof contract with required run metadata and approved/revise/blocked status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA approves the question and acceptance condition; partner engineering approves feasibility and sandbox authorization. Stop if either approval is missing.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved risk/requirement, sandbox boundary, synthetic data description, approved threshold if available and named PSA/engineering reviewers.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one risk, sandbox boundary and approved threshold or gap.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for the six-field proof contract.
3. (2 min) Review falsifiability and permission with PSA and engineering owner.
4. (2 min) Mark approved/revise/blocked; stop without executing the plan.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Creates a bounded evidence task without mistaking a proposed test for a result.

activities.name: Classify one actual proof run without overstating the result
activities.description: Protects the difference between executable evidence and an AI explanation that only sounds plausible.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Review only the sanitized run record and approved acceptance condition I provide for one proof. Build an evidence assessment containing the command or method, version, environment, timestamp, observed output, threshold comparison and missing metadata. Classify this one check as passed, failed, blocked, not run or inconclusive only when the supplied record supports that status. Quote short input references rather than fabricating logs. A proposed command, screenshot description or expected output is not proof of execution. Do not generalize to all tests, production readiness or compliance, and do not repair or rerun anything. Pause for the partner test owner to confirm the record and the PSA technical authority to review the architecture implication. Stop after this single assessment.
activities.expectedOutput: One run-evidence assessment with supported status, metadata gaps and bounded architecture implication.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Test owner confirms actual execution; PSA approves only the bounded interpretation. Stop as inconclusive/not run when execution or threshold evidence is insufficient.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one authorized sanitized run record with available command, version, environment, timestamp and actual output; approved threshold and test owner. Missing fields remain gaps.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one actual run record and approved condition.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork to assess the record and missing metadata.
3. (2 min) Confirm execution with test owner and interpretation with PSA.
4. (2 min) Record one status and implication; stop without rerunning or repairing.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Protects the difference between executable evidence and an AI explanation that only sounds plausible.

activities.name: Optional author-designed synthetic tenant-boundary sandbox spike
activities.description: Offers inspectable synthetic coding evidence without assigning PSA default implementation delivery.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. This is an optional author-designed learning spike, not an EPS source mandate. Use only the approved isolated sandbox workspace, synthetic two-tenant sample, permitted component snippet and existing test command. Propose the smallest local assertion that could expose cross-tenant cache-key reuse; do not touch customer or production code, credentials, networks or cloud resources. First show the proposed diff and command, then wait for the partner engineer to give explicit approval before any edit or execution. Do not install dependencies. If executed with approval, preserve the actual command, version, timestamp and output; otherwise label the result not run. Pause for the PSA technical authority to review the limited architecture implication. Stop after one assertion; do not claim isolation, security or all tests are proven.
activities.expectedOutput: One reviewed minimal test/diff and actual local run record if approved/executed, otherwise not-run note; no generalized security verdict.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Partner engineering approves the diff, command and sandbox before changes or execution; PSA reviews only architecture implication. Stop on missing tools, installs, external access, real data, unauthorized code or unapproved execution.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: approved isolated sandbox folder, one permitted non-customer component snippet, synthetic tenant A/B values, existing test command, approved expected behavior and partner engineer. Optional 20-30-minute follow-on, primarily ISV; not required live.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm an approved isolated sandbox, existing command and wholly synthetic two-tenant sample.
2. Ask GitHub Copilot for one assertion and proposed diff; do not run it.
3. Partner engineer explicitly approves the local diff/command or stops the spike.
4. Only with approval, engineer owns execution and captures actual output; otherwise record not run.
5. PSA reviews the bounded implication; stop at one assertion without production/cloud changes.

Fallback: If GitHub Copilot or an approved sandbox is unavailable, review the supplied synthetic snippet/test on paper; label execution not run and preserve the explicit human approval gate before any edit or command.

activities.name: Create one requirement-to-build validation row
activities.description: Makes offering validation auditable instead of relying on a broad success narrative.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Reconcile only the single requirement, approved acceptance condition, build identifier and sanitized test excerpt I supply. Produce one validation row with requirement, build/version, observed result, evidence reference/date, threshold comparison, supported status and gap owner. Distinguish expected output from actual execution evidence and flag version mismatches. Use passed only if this exact check and approved threshold are demonstrably satisfied; otherwise record failed, blocked, not run or inconclusive as supported. Do not infer that all tests passed, the offering is production ready or security/compliance is certified. Pause for the partner test owner to verify the run and the PSA technical authority to approve the bounded conclusion. Stop at this one row without modifying code, rerunning tests or retrieving additional records.
activities.expectedOutput: One requirement-to-build validation row with traceable evidence, honest status and unresolved owner gap.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Test owner verifies the exact build/run; PSA accepts or rejects the bounded claim. Stop as inconclusive when build, threshold or execution evidence cannot be matched.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved requirement/ID, accepted threshold, build/version, one authorized sanitized actual run excerpt with reference/date and technical/test reviewers.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one requirement, threshold, build ID and actual excerpt.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for one validation row and mismatches.
3. (2 min) Verify execution with test owner and interpretation with PSA.
4. (2 min) Record status and one gap owner; stop without release verdict.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Makes offering validation auditable instead of relying on a broad success narrative.

activities.name: Verify one technical offering condition without claiming eligibility
activities.description: Grounds technical validation in current requirements while leaving eligibility and formal approvals to their authorities.
activities.prompt: Use only the conversation and approved materials already supplied. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Investigate the one deployment or operational requirement in my supplied offering note using the named product/version and permitted official documentation URLs. Produce a condition-to-evidence note with the published requirement, precise citation, update date if available, access date and evidence the partner would need to demonstrate it. Compare only the owner-supplied evidence excerpt I paste; do not retrieve Partner Center, PMX or other private records automatically. Mark unavailable guidance, outdated versions and missing evidence as gaps. A documentation match is not certification, Marketplace eligibility or proof that the implementation works. Pause for the PSA technical authority and the named evidence owner to review applicability and authenticity. Stop after one technical condition and one evidence gap, without submitting or changing anything.
activities.expectedOutput: One dated condition-to-evidence note separating published requirements, supplied evidence and gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA checks applicability; record owner confirms private evidence through supplied material or their own inspection. Stop if current guidance or authentic evidence is unavailable.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved deployment/operational condition, product/version, permitted official URL and optional authorized owner-supplied sanitized evidence with date/reference. No connector or portal access assumed.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one deployment/operational condition, version and official URL.
2. (3 min) Ask Researcher for one dated condition-to-evidence note.
3. (2 min) Inspect the citation and owner-supplied evidence with PSA.
4. (2 min) Record guidance and missing validation; stop without eligibility verdict.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
