activities.name: Separate an architecture gap from one implementation defect
activities.description: Engages the right owner without turning PSA validation into default implementation support.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Compare only my supplied interface contract, one sanitized failing observation and its build/run reference. Draft a defect handback with expected behavior, observed behavior, evidence, likely decision category, uncertainty and one next check. Distinguish an architecture ambiguity from an implementation mismatch; do not assert a root cause that the evidence does not demonstrate. If the record cannot establish execution, label it an evidence gap rather than a reproduced defect. Keep partner engineering responsible for code changes and reruns; PSA owns the architectural clarification if needed. Do not alter files, create tickets, assign work or contact anyone. Pause for the PSA technical authority and partner engineering lead to agree the routing. Stop after one reviewed handback and proposed acceptance check.
activities.expectedOutput: One defect handback with bounded evidence, uncertain cause, agreed routing and proposed acceptance check.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA owns architecture clarification; engineering lead confirms implementation responsibility and accepts handback. Stop if execution evidence or receiving ownership is missing.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved contract, sanitized observed failure, exact build/run reference/date and PSA/partner engineering lead.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one contract, failing observation and build/run reference.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for an evidence-based handback.
3. (2 min) Review architecture/implementation routing with PSA and engineering lead.
4. (2 min) Record accepted handback or gap; stop without creating or assigning a ticket.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Engages the right owner without turning PSA validation into default implementation support.

activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use only the approved before/after change note, one requirement and supplied run evidence to draft an optional regression challenge card. For an SI reference implementation, focus on one extension point affected by a local integration change. For an ISV product, focus on one existing tenant's behavior after an upgrade or shared-schema change. 2. Ask Cowork for a single invariant and regression challenge.
3. Review evidence coverage with PSA and partner release engineer.
4. Record one missing check or bounded result; stop without release approval.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Partner engineers have built or are building the capability. PSA checks whether one architectural or offering claim is supported by inspectable evidence. An unavailable, incomplete or untested build remains so; we do not write success into existence.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. One requirement and exact build/version. 2. Separate expected and observed outputs. 3. Distinguish design gaps from implementation defects. 4. Published guidance and private evidence have different access paths. 5. Engineers own fixes and reruns.
discussionQuestions: What does the evidence demonstrate? Does it match this build and acceptance condition? Is the next action architectural clarification or engineering repair?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create one requirement-to-build validation row'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Select one requirement/failure in two minutes. Reconcile evidence for four minutes; use two for accept/gap/handback with the authority. Do not expand into full release sign-off. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Challenge one reuse regression in an SI reference or ISV upgrade', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: State exactly which claim is supported and unresolved. The artifact neither certifies security/compliance nor declares the full offering launch ready. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved requirement, accepted threshold, exact build/version and sanitized actual test excerpt or explicit not-run status. For offering conditions, select one official source. Partner Center/PMX records must be authorized user-supplied or owner-inspected, never assumed retrievable.
facilitatorQuestions: Can another reviewer trace the conclusion to a run? Which missing fact prevents acceptance? Who can accept the limitation or own its correction?
listenFor: Version-specific evidence, bounded conclusions and an engineering owner. Challenge all-tests-passed generalizations, demos as certification, automatic portal retrieval and unbounded PSA bug-fixing assignments.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without actual evidence, create a gap row listing missing run metadata and owner. Inaccessible guidance remains unresolved. Never fabricate reproduction, portal status or a passed test. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which piece of version or run metadata changed our interpretation?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, agree one evidence correction, architecture clarification or engineering handback and review date, subject to receiving-owner acceptance; do not automatically assign or send it. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized version or evidence mismatch found and whether it changed the supported claim. Do not imply certification or launch readiness. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Scout
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
keyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
stepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Check one current technical publishing requirement for a handoff gap

activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Return a requirement card with the relevant condition, precise citation, publication or update date when available, access date, applicability and the evidence an authorized publishing owner must inspect. Compare only the sanitized owner-supplied excerpt I provide, if any. Do not log into or automatically retrieve Partner Center, PMX or private partner records. If guidance is missing, unavailable or not clearly applicable, mark an unresolved gap rather than declaring eligibility. Do not certify compliance, Marketplace acceptance or launch readiness. Pause for the PSA technical authority and publishing owner to review the card. Stop after one requirement and one evidence gap; do not submit anything.
activities.expectedOutput: One dated requirement card with citation, applicability limit and publishing-owner evidence gap.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA checks technical meaning; authorized publishing owner inspects private records and owns publishing. Stop without current applicable guidance/evidence; never certify eligibility.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one technical publishing requirement, offering type/version, permitted official URLs, execution date and optional authorized owner-supplied portal excerpt/inspection date.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one publishing requirement, offering type and official URL.
2. (3 min) Ask Researcher for a dated card and evidence needs.
3. (2 min) Inspect the citation with PSA and publishing owner.
4. (2 min) Record one gap or bounded match; stop without eligibility/submission claims.

activities.name: Prepare one evidence-honest demo and enablement boundary
activities.description: Lets activation teams use technical material without unsupported promises or unclear support ownership.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Reconcile my supplied single demo step, validated capability evidence, audience note and known limitation into a technical enablement card. Include what the presenter may demonstrate, what the evidence supports, the limitation they must say aloud, one likely technical question and the correct escalation owner. Do not invent a successful demo run, guarantee service levels or imply the whole offering is validated. Keep implementation troubleshooting with partner engineers and architecture clarification with PSA; commercial positioning remains with the designated commercial owner. If the demo step lacks evidence, label it a proposed demonstration and recommend a hold or narrower wording. Pause for the PSA technical authority and partner demo owner to approve the card. Stop after one step; do not schedule, send or publish material.
activities.expectedOutput: One demo-step card with allowed claim, spoken limitation, technical question and escalation owner.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA approves accuracy; partner demo owner confirms the step can be shown as described. Stop or narrow wording when actual validation evidence is missing.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved or proposed demo step, sanitized validation reference/date, audience, limitation and partner demo/technical owners.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one demo step, audience, evidence and limitation.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for an evidence-honest enablement card.
3. (2 min) Review claims/escalation with PSA and demo owner.
4. (2 min) Record allowed wording or hold; stop before presentation/distribution.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.name: Optional approval-gated monitoring of one published readiness dependency
activities.description: Provides bounded recurring monitoring without silently starting automation or communications.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Draft a monitoring proposal only; do not schedule or activate it. Use the approved official URL, the dated baseline, the partner model, and the named reviewer for the published readiness dependency. For an SI reference implementation, scope one supported-version or integration-guidance dependency; for an ISV offering, scope one technical publishing or tenant-platform requirement. Propose a bounded seven-day, once-daily check that would report only changed wording, source/access dates, possible technical impact, and a human-review flag. Treat access failures as gaps; do not assume a connector, private-portal access, or that an unavailable page is unchanged. Do not notify recipients or change readiness status. Pause for separate explicit scheduling, access, and notification approval. Stop after the proposal; no automation exists until that approval is obtained.
activities.expectedOutput: One unactivated proposal with source boundary, seven-day expiry, cadence, change criteria, access-gap behavior and approval fields.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA validates relevance; user separately approves scheduling/access/notification before automation creation. Stop on missing approval, inaccessible source, expanded scope or private portal retrieval.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one allowed public official URL, approved baseline excerpt/date, SI/ISV dependency and technical reviewer. Optional asynchronous variant; separate scheduling/access/notification approval required, no connector assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Select one SI/ISV dependency and supply one allowed public official URL/baseline.
2. Ask Scout for a seven-day proposal without scheduling or activation.
3. PSA reviews criteria; user separately approves schedule, access and notification destination.
4. Without approval, stop at proposal; if later approved, a human reviews each change/access-failure report before action.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.
activities.whyThisMatters: Provides bounded recurring monitoring without silently starting automation or communications.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercialization needs technically truthful material, not a second architecture project. PSA contributes validated capabilities, assets, limitations and support boundaries. Publishing/commercial/activation owners decide next actions; private portal status comes from authorized evidence or owner inspection.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Technical readiness is narrower than launch readiness. 2. Date and cite current requirements. 3. Partner Center/PMX evidence is supplied or owner-inspected, not silently retrieved. 4. Demonstrations show only validated scenarios. 5. No auto-sending, publishing, submission or resource commitments.
discussionQuestions: Which sentence can we defend? What limitation must travel with it? Who accepts the item and owns the separate publishing or commercial decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Convert one validation claim into a bounded readiness handoff'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Select one item in two minutes; spend four reconciling evidence and wording. Use two to record handoff/limited handoff/hold. Sending remains a separate human action. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare one evidence-honest demo and enablement boundary', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Read the qualified handoff and limitation. Confirm nothing was sent/published and broader launch was not approved on one technical item. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved capability claim, exact build/version, validation reference, limitation and receiving owner. For requirements, supply an official URL and optional owner-approved portal excerpt/date. Select one item, not a full launch checklist.
facilitatorQuestions: Would the receiving team overread the claim? Is guidance current and applicable? Has the owner inspected portal evidence, and what remains unverified?
listenFor: Evidence-qualified readiness, limitations and accepting owner. Challenge eligibility claims, guessed portal status, auto-submission and expansion into sales execution or PTS strategy.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without validation or authoritative guidance, draft a hold note with the exact gap and owner. Request owner inspection for absent private evidence; do not assume connectors or favorable status. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What might an activation owner wrongly infer without the limitation or evidence date?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, seek PSA approval of one item and receiving-owner acknowledgement by an agreed date; humans decide later sharing, publishing or submission. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized technical-readiness limitation clarified and whether the receiver understood the handoff more accurately; missing acceptance is valid. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Create a permission-aware reusable architecture pattern card
activities.description: Makes architecture learning reusable without losing context or exceeding source-material rights.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use only the approved component summary, validation references, dependency/version notes and provenance/permission status I supply. Draft a concise reusable pattern card with problem, bounded design principle, applicability, evidence limits, adaptation points, rights-review status and maintenance owner. Paraphrase the technical lesson; do not reproduce source text or code verbatim. Distinguish a validated behavior in the supplied environment from assumptions future adopters must test. Do not infer redistribution or derivative-work permission from access to a file. If licensing, permission or evidence is missing, keep the card draft and identify the blocking review. Pause for the PSA technical authority and designated rights owner to review. Stop at one pattern card without copying assets, sharing files or assigning ongoing support. Have PSA confirm the summary and referenced evidence are sanitized for the intended reuse audience.
activities.expectedOutput: One pattern card with applicability limits, adaptation points, permission gate and maintenance status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA approves the technical lesson; designated rights owner confirms reuse permission. Stop at draft if evidence or rights review is incomplete; file access is not redistribution permission. PSA also confirms audience-appropriate sanitization before reuse; stop if sensitive content remains.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved component summary, not proprietary code; actual evidence references/date/version, dependency notes, provenance, licensing/permission status and maintenance/rights reviewers.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one component summary, evidence and provenance/rights status.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for one paraphrased bounded pattern card.
3. (2 min) Review applicability with PSA and rights with designated owner.
4. (2 min) Mark reviewed reuse/draft/retire and maintenance gap; stop without redistribution.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

Return a refresh note with the current published technical condition, precise citations, source dates when available, access date and a bounded difference from the card's recorded version. Report what the published terms state without making a legal determination or declaring reuse permission. Separate a documentation change from an observed implementation failure. If authoritative guidance or terms are unavailable, mark the relevant gap and keep adoption unapproved. Do not copy source material verbatim, retrieve private assets or update the pattern automatically. Pause for the PSA technical authority and designated rights reviewer. Stop after one dependency refresh note and one adoption question.
activities.expectedOutput: One refresh note with dated citations, version delta and separate technical/rights approval gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA validates technical delta; rights reviewer decides permission implications. Stop with a gap if guidance or required terms cannot be inspected; no legal certification.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved dependency/version excerpt, permitted official documentation and applicable license/usage-terms URLs, original review date and technical/rights reviewers. No private access assumed.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one dependency/version and official guidance/terms URLs.
2. (3 min) Ask Researcher for a dated technical/rights refresh note.
3. (2 min) Inspect applicability with PSA and route terms to rights reviewer.
4. (2 min) Record one adoption question or stale-guidance gap; stop without reuse approval.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.

activities.name: Close one technical ownership gap with an accepted exit packet
activities.description: Makes exit durable instead of leaving architecture or implementation support informally with PSA.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Reconcile only the approved technical decision summary, evidence index, one open item and proposed receiving-owner note I provide. Draft a one-item exit packet containing completed scope, evidence/version limits, remaining issue, proposed next owner, acceptance needed and future escalation boundary. Do not describe an item as closed or ownership as transferred unless the supplied acknowledgement supports it. Keep partner engineering responsible for implementation maintenance, PSA responsible only for the explicitly agreed architectural follow-up, and broader strategy with PTS. Do not assign work, promise service levels, schedule support or send the packet. Pause for the PSA technical authority and receiving owner to confirm the boundary. Stop after one accepted-exit recommendation or hold note with a clear acknowledgement gap.
activities.expectedOutput: One technical exit item or hold note with evidence limits, next responsibility and acknowledgement status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA confirms completed scope; receiver explicitly accepts next responsibility. Stop as hold when acknowledgement, engineering maintenance ownership or evidence is missing.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved decision summary, short evidence index/version/date, one open issue, proposed receiver, any actual acknowledgement and agreed PSA scope boundary.
activitySteps: 1. (1 min) Supply one decision summary, evidence index, open item and owner note.
2. (3 min) Ask Cowork for a one-item exit packet.
3. (2 min) Review future responsibility with PSA and receiver.
4. (2 min) Record accepted exit/hold using actual acknowledgement; stop without sending/assigning.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Makes exit durable instead of leaving architecture or implementation support informally with PSA.

activities.name: Revalidate one pattern for a new region and partner model
activities.description: Makes regional reuse a focused technical and permission decision, not assumed universal applicability.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Create an optional regional reuse replay card from only my approved pattern summary, rights-review status, source-region evidence and one target-region change. For an SI reference implementation, examine one site-specific adapter or operational dependency; for an ISV product, examine one tenant configuration or regional deployment assumption. Separate the reusable principle from the local implementation and state one check needed before adoption. Preserve evidence/version limits and do not infer regional availability, compliance or permission to redistribute derivatives. Paraphrase rather than copying source content. If rights or authoritative regional guidance are missing, keep reuse on hold. Pause for the PSA technical authority, regional technical owner and rights reviewer. Stop after one delta and approval gap without distributing assets or approving rollout. Have PSA confirm the summary and referenced evidence are sanitized for the intended reuse audience.
activities.expectedOutput: One regional replay card with model-specific delta, bounded revalidation check and technical/permission status.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA and regional authority approve applicability; rights reviewer confirms derivative/reuse permission. Stop on missing regional guidance, unreviewed rights or unaccepted maintenance owner. PSA also confirms audience-appropriate sanitization before reuse; stop if sensitive content remains.
activities.requiredContext: Exact supplied inputs: one approved pattern summary, SI/ISV model, source-region evidence/version, target-region change, licensing/permission status and regional/rights reviewers. Optional 20-minute follow-on.
activitySteps: 1. Choose SI adapter or ISV regional-tenant variant and supply one regional change.
2. Ask Cowork for a replay card separating reusable principle and local assumptions.
3. Review applicability with PSA/regional owners and derivative rights with rights reviewer.
4. Record one revalidation/permission gap; stop without redistribution or rollout approval.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Makes regional reuse a focused technical and permission decision, not assumed universal applicability.

activities.name: Monitor one approved reusable-pattern dependency
activities.description: Track one approved technical, publishing, permission, or lifecycle dependency after handoff while keeping adoption and maintenance decisions with human owners.
activities.prompt: Produce an unactivated read-only proposal, not a running monitor. Use authorized dated snapshots, a user-maintained baseline and previous report supplied for this review; do not retrieve unsupplied records, create automation, retain agent memory or notify anyone. Missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no change. Record scope, source permission, owner, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and supplied approved change criteria without inventing values. Future monitoring requires separate explicit approval and verified access/state capabilities. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Do not activate this monitor until named PSA reviewer has explicitly approved approved monitoring scope, the approved cadence, the approved evidence locations, the approved recipients, access, and the approved review or expiry date. Compare supplied snapshots for the approved reusable-pattern dependency only within that scope and approval window. For a baseline-only review, draft a dated baseline containing the technical condition, permission or lifecycle state, owner, dates, and access status. For a comparison review, compare the supplied baseline and user-maintained previous report, and return only changed guidance, versions, terms, ownership, review dates, or access failures, with source and date. If prior state is unavailable, report that comparison is unavailable and stop until the reviewer approves a new baseline. Keep report drafts unsent; future delivery requires separate explicit approval. Do not infer reuse permission, compatibility, security, adoption approval, maintenance acceptance, or completion from silence. Do not change or publish the pattern or assign support. PSA and the designated maintenance or rights owner validate every change and retain technical, rights, adoption, and ownership decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated baseline-only or change-only supplied-evidence review draft with source/history/access gaps and an unactivated proposal for the named reviewer; zero scheduled jobs or notifications.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSA validates technical implications; the designated maintenance or rights owner decides permission, adoption, and ongoing ownership. Scout does not publish, approve reuse, or assign support.
activities.requiredContext: One approved reusable-pattern dependency; explicit reviewer approval of monitoring scope, cadence, evidence locations, recipients, access, and review or expiry date; named PSA reviewer; and named maintenance or rights owner. Provide authorized dated snapshots and user-maintained baseline/prior report if available. Source permissions, scope, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and automation approval are explicit proposed fields; missing inputs remain gaps and no tool access/state retention is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one bounded dependency/action and supply authorized dated snapshots; clearly labeled synthetic evidence is rehearsal-only.
2. Check the user-maintained baseline/prior report, comparable definitions and named reviewer; leave missing history, permission or criteria explicit.
3. Compare supplied evidence manually or with one already authorized tool; no schedule, live retrieval or persistent agent memory.
4. Produce a dated baseline-only/comparison draft and unactivated proposal with source, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval fields.
5. Apply the unchanged HumanCheckpoint before interpretation/action; future automation, notifications and system changes require separate explicit authorization.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.
activities.whyThisMatters: Approved monitoring prevents a reusable pattern from silently becoming stale while preserving technical, rights, adoption, and maintenance decisions with accountable owners.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Do not archive everything indiscriminately. Select one useful pattern and make its limits clear, or close one ownership gap. PSA contributes reusable CSA architecture/readiness learning; partner engineers and designated owners maintain implementations and accept ongoing responsibilities.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Reusable is not universally validated. 2. Preserve provenance and evidence/version limits. 3. Review licensing and permission before reuse; paraphrase instead of copying verbatim. 4. Regional and SI/ISV changes need revalidation. 5. Exit is accepted responsibility, not abandonment or indefinite support.
discussionQuestions: What can another partner reuse, and what must they revalidate? Do we have adaptation/redistribution permission? Who owns maintenance, limitations and future technical questions?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Create a permission-aware reusable architecture pattern card'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Select one asset/open item in two minutes. Spend four on provenance/evidence or ownership; use two for reviewed reuse/draft/retire or accepted exit/hold. Do not package the portfolio live. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Close one technical ownership gap with an accepted exit packet', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: State the reuse/exit decision and boundary. Confirm no redistribution, verbatim source copying or unaccepted maintenance/support assignment. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved component summary, validated build/run references, dependency/version, provenance and licensing/permission status. For exit, supply one open item and receiving owner. No proprietary code or copied protected research; use authorized summaries and references. PSA must confirm reusable summaries and evidence are appropriately sanitized for the intended audience before reuse.
facilitatorQuestions: What might a future adopter wrongly assume? Which permission/evidence gap blocks reuse? Has the next owner actually accepted responsibility?
listenFor: Bounded reuse, provenance, rights-review status and acknowledged ownership. Challenge copied source content, inferred redistribution rights, stale requirements, universal regional/tenant claims and unaccepted PSA support obligations.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: With unknown reuse rights or validation, make a draft entry and permission/evidence gap without redistribution. If the receiver is unconfirmed, create an exit hold note rather than claiming closure. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which limitation or ownership detail makes this safer and more useful than a context-free template?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, seek rights review and technical acceptance for one asset/handoff by an agreed date. Human owners decide sharing; retain draft/hold until approvals are recorded. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized reuse or exit condition checked and whether it improved rights clarity or ownership continuity; held drafts are valid. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-EPS-PSA-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-EPS-PSA-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-EPS-PSA-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent

activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Inspect only these three authorized MSX opportunities: the opportunity ID 1, the opportunity ID 2, the opportunity ID 3. Scope: the partner customer territory solution scope; review date: today. 1. Resolve each exact ID within scope; label inaccessible records as missing access, never missing pipeline. 2. Extract available record facts on stage, next step, owner and timing with record references and dates. 3. Return a three-row execution-priority table with evidence, uncertainty, proposed owner question and next decision; do not retrieve partner-system status. 5. activities.expectedOutput: Three-row execution-priority table: ID, record fact/date/reference, uncertainty, priority rationale, proposed owner question and next decision.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS accepts or holds execution focus; the AE and partner seller confirm their own actions. Stop at unresolved ID/scope, freshness or ownership. Missing access is not missing pipeline.
activities.requiredContext: Exactly OPP_ID_1, OPP_ID_2, OPP_ID_3; PARTNER_CUSTOMER_TERRITORY_SOLUTION_SCOPE; AS_OF_DATE. Existing authorized MSX access only, not native partner-system retrieval. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A partner-sales plan is useful when a named seller can act on a defensible priority. Focus on one execution choice, using current opportunity evidence and the partner strategy as context.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Use three identified opportunities, not the entire territory. Separate PSS execution priorities from PDM strategy changes. Marketing visibility, accepted referral and customer commitment are different evidence categories. In Asia name the country and covered solution areas; validate cross-solution applicability rather than generalizing.
discussionQuestions: Which priority changes when an undated partner claim is removed? Which issue belongs to PDM strategy rather than PSS execution? Which named seller must confirm the next action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile partner plan claims into a three-opportunity execution slice'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in a reviewed three-opportunity execution slice with dated support, priority rationale, proposed owner/action and an explicit unresolved decision. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'ISV variant: test Marketplace assumptions in a territory execution slice', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: A territory priority becomes executable only when record evidence, partner claims, accountable owners and the next review decision are separated. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring an approved three-opportunity territory slice, exact MSX IDs where available, a short partner-strategy excerpt and dated seller notes. If choosing the one-deal discussion, bring its meeting notes and roster. Label each input with ID, scope, source and date; use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Show one priority and its supporting evidence date. Where did a partner aspiration become a supposed record fact? What would make you hold the execution slice? Who must confirm the proposed seller action?
listenFor: A bounded territory slice; explicit source dates; PSS execution rather than PDM strategy substitution; no inferred agreement; missing access not interpreted as an empty territory.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete three opportunity rows with source/date, partner assertion, customer evidence, conflict, proposed owner/action and review date manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed about your territory choice when you separated record facts from partner claims?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate [one priority or owner assumption] with [named accountable owner] by [date] and bring my accept/hold decision and rationale. This is my validation action, not another seller's commitment. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized territory assumption checked and whether it changed PSS accept/hold judgment or clarified a separately owned action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Check the MSX record linked to one referral without inferring referral state
activities.description: Independent choice: only identified authorized MSX records under existing CRM roles; if unavailable use a supplied-evidence Cowork alternative, not a wider query. Uses record grounding without masquerading as complete partner referral evidence.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Inspect only the authorized MSX opportunity, supplied as the known link for the referral, within the partner customer solution scope as of today. 1. Resolve the exact opportunity and report identity or access gaps without treating them as absent pipeline. 2. Extract available customer need, partner involvement, owner and next-step facts with record references and dates. 3. Identify missing or contradictory record evidence relevant to referral quality; recorded partner assertions remain claims. 4. Return a linked-record evidence table and three questions for the referral source owner; do not retrieve or infer Partner Center acceptance or full referral state. 5. Ask PSS to use or hold this record evidence for quality review; stop on a linkage mismatch or unresolved freshness. Draft only: no referral acceptance, stage approval, messages, updates, promises or funding decisions. If existing authorized record access is unavailable, inspect a dated authorized extract of the exact identified record or clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Mark access gaps explicitly; synthetic data supports rehearsal only, never a real opportunity conclusion.
activities.expectedOutput: Linked-record table with customer need, partner involvement, next step, source/date, gaps and three source-owner questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS decides use/hold for quality review. Stop on linkage mismatch or unresolved freshness; only the accountable source owner verifies partner-side acceptance.
activities.requiredContext: OPP_ID, REFERRAL_ID, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE. OPP_ID is an already known linked authorized MSX record, not a request to search partner referrals. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: Uses record grounding without masquerading as complete partner referral evidence.

activities.name: Build a one-referral quality decision packet
activities.description: Independent supplied-evidence choice: Cowork uses only the approved inputs and applicable permissions/spending policy. Makes quality inspection explainable and returns weak evidence with a concrete correction.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use only the referral packet, the supplied linked record extract and the quality review criteria for the referral. Scope: the partner customer solution scope; date: today. 1. Check identifiers, evidence owners and dates, marking missing access separately from missing fields. 2. Compare the supplied customer need, seller contact and next step against the supplied criteria; do not invent eligibility rules. 3. Distinguish partner claims, record facts and explicit customer evidence; marketed status does not prove referral acceptance or customer commitment. 4. Produce a ready/return/hold review packet with evidence per criterion, unresolved exception, owner question and proposed follow-up date. 5. Ask PSS to choose the quality disposition after the source owner verifies disputed facts; stop if identity, permission or a decisive criterion remains unresolved. No native partner-system lookup, automatic acceptance, messages, writebacks, promises or funding decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: One-referral ready/return/hold packet with criterion evidence/date, exception, owner question and proposed follow-up date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS makes the quality disposition; source owners verify disputed status. Stop on unresolved identity, permission or decisive criterion. No eligibility or referral-status approval by AI.
activities.requiredContext: REFERRAL_PACKET, SUPPLIED_LINKED_RECORD_EXTRACT, QUALITY_REVIEW_CRITERIA, REFERRAL_ID, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE. If the extract is unavailable explicitly supply that access limitation; criteria must come from an accountable owner.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Makes quality inspection explainable and returns weak evidence with a concrete correction.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A referral is actionable only when its customer need, evidence and next owner are clear. Focus on one quality or acceptance gap without treating a linked CRM record as proof of partner-side acceptance.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Marketed offer, accepted referral and customer agreement require different evidence. A partner-side acceptance claim is not proven by an MSX reference. If no linked MSX ID is known, use supplied evidence rather than asking Sales Agent to discover all referrals.
discussionQuestions: What makes this referral actionable? Which source can verify acceptance? What missing field would change ready to hold?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Check the MSX record linked to one referral without inferring referral state'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one quality-review packet with identity link, customer need, evidence gaps, verification owner and a PSS ready/return/hold rationale. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'ISV variant: separate offer marketing from referral acceptance', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Referral quality requires identifiable, dated evidence; marketing visibility and an MSX mention do not prove partner-side acceptance or customer commitment. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved referral packet: ID, partner/customer/solution scope, date, source owner, stated need, next step and explicit acceptance evidence if available. For P1 also bring the exact known linked MSX opportunity ID; otherwise choose P2/P3. Use supplied local quality criteria rather than invented gates. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Show the identity link. Which assertion is still partner-supplied? Does the proposed disposition assume acceptance or customer intent? Who can resolve the first exception?
listenFor: Clear ready/return/hold rationale; marketing/referral/customer evidence separated; exact source-owner question; no automatic acceptance or stage approval.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one referral packet with identity link, customer need, source/date, unknown, verification owner and proposed ready/return/hold rationale manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which apparent referral fact became only a claim when you checked source and date?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will ask [named source owner] to verify [one referral field or mismatch] by [date] and bring the evidence and my ready/return/hold rationale; I will not accept a referral or promise customer action for someone else. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized referral-field mismatch checked and whether it improved quality judgment; no referral packet or identifying customer data is required. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Shared pipeline does not become qualified pipeline by appearing in two systems. Focus on one qualification or duplication question and the evidence needed for the next customer action.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Qualification needs customer need, engagement and next-decision evidence. Referral acceptance is not customer commitment. Repeated shared signals may overlap but similar names do not prove duplication. Do not merge records or change stage through the AI draft.
discussionQuestions: What supports progress rather than verification? What proves two signals refer to the same opportunity? Who owns the next qualification conversation?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect three identified MSX opportunities for qualification gaps'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in a reviewed qualification or reconciliation artifact with customer evidence, possible overlap, next owner action and progress/hold question. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'SI variant: untangle partner-seller and AE qualification handoffs', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Qualify the customer opportunity and reconcile shared signals before acceleration; access gaps and similar partner claims do not prove absent pipeline or duplicates. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring three exact MSX IDs for P1, one inbound packet for P2, or supplied rows for three identified opportunities for P3. Include source owners/dates, customer need, engagement, next step and local qualification criteria. For the SI variant bring sending/receiving seller roster and acceptance evidence. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Which fact supports qualification? Is a partner claim being counted as customer engagement? What corroboration resolves possible overlap? Which action still lacks seller confirmation?
listenFor: Evidence-based priority without invented scoring; possible overlap not labeled confirmed duplicate; exact scope/date; PSS prioritization distinct from AE stage authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one qualification row with customer evidence, possible overlap, identity gap, proposed seller action and progress/hold question manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed when partner-reported pipeline was separated from identifiable customer evidence?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will verify [one qualification gap or possible overlap] with [named AE/partner source owner] by [date] and return with a progress/hold rationale. Each seller accepts and completes their own next action. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized qualification gap or overlap checked and whether it prevented double counting or premature progress. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.
