facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A top deal needs a customer decision, not just a new stage label. Focus on the evidence, blocker and seller conversation that can move one deal forward.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Name one deal and the decision it faces. Top-deal importance does not override missing evidence. Supplied stage guidance is input, not permission for AI to invent gates. Partner sellers own their commitments; you own the opportunity decision.
discussionQuestions: What decision is blocked beyond changing the stage label? What customer evidence changes readiness? Which seller must confirm the next action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect one opportunity for evidence behind the next stage-2/3 decision'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one reviewed next-decision brief identifying decisive evidence, blocker, accountable owner, proposed action and hold condition. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Reconcile one deal's meeting actions against the actual blocker', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Move the next human deal decision, not the stage label: test evidence, expose the blocker and confirm seller-owned actions. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one exact authorized opportunity ID or supplied deal extract, partner/customer scope/date, applicable stage-2/3 guidance, customer evidence, dated meeting notes, blocker and owner roster. ISV variant requires supplied owner-verified offer/procurement evidence. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Which cited fact supports progression and which is a partner claim? Does the action resolve the actual blocker? What remains for the AE? When must the draft be held?
listenFor: One concrete decision; customer evidence distinct from enthusiasm; supplied rather than invented gates; owners confirming their actions; explicit stop on decisive evidence gaps.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one decision brief with dated evidence, blocker, accountable role, proposed action and hold condition manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: How did replacing advance the deal with a specific decision change the next action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will validate [one blocker or evidence gap] with [named AE/partner seller] by [date] and bring the revised decision brief. I will not approve a stage or commit another seller through the AI draft. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized deal blocker clarified and whether it improved the seller-owned decision; do not infer acceleration from AI classification. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Marketing activity and offer visibility do not establish a sales outcome. Focus on one deal-to-GTM link or current requirement, with the source owner verifying partner-side facts.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Marketed status, referral acceptance and customer commitment need different evidence. Only accountable owners verify current partner-system status. PSS sales follow-through does not authorize campaign, funding, eligibility or MACC treatment decisions. Permission review precedes outcomes claims and reuse.
discussionQuestions: Which signal is actual customer evidence? Who verifies current offer or referral status? Which action is sales coordination versus PMM marketing?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Verify one current Marketplace or GTM requirement'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one reviewed action card or reconciliation packet separating marketing signals, referral status and customer evidence, with verification owner and hold condition. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Turn one GTM handoff into a seller-owned next action', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: A marketed offer is not an accepted referral or customer commitment; translate GTM signals into verified sales decisions and accountable actions. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one deal ID, scope/date, relevant supplied GTM excerpt, dated customer/deal evidence and owner roster. Any Marketplace or referral excerpt needs ID, verifying owner and date. Unknown status remains unknown; marketing activity alone is not a sales outcome. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Does the draft claim sell-through from marketing alone? Is the customer next step dated? Who checks the disputed status at source? Which proposed seller action is still unaccepted?
listenFor: Distinct marketing/referral/customer evidence; bounded one-deal action; named verifying owner/date; PMM/PDM ownership preserved; no eligibility inference or borrowed customer commitment.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one requirement check with offer/context, official rule/date or unavailable, applicability, source owner and hold question manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which apparent success signal was downgraded after separating promotion, referral acceptance and customer commitment?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will verify [one sell-through assumption] with [named accountable source owner] by [date], then agree my coordination action with the AE/partner seller. I will not promise an offer outcome, funding or another owner's action. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized GTM or Marketplace signal checked and whether it changed the sell-through action; distinguish promotion, referral acceptance and customer commitment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Inspect one identified renewal MSX opportunity for a decision-changing risk
activities.description: Independent choice: only identified authorized MSX records under existing CRM roles; if unavailable use a supplied-evidence Cowork alternative, not a wider query. Finds the evidence gap changing renewal priority while preserving the narrow Sales Agent record boundary.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Inspect only the authorized MSX renewal opportunity within the partner customer solution scope as of today. 1. Resolve the exact record; label missing access separately from absent pipeline evidence and do not retrieve agreements or quotes. 2. Extract available renewal timing, customer next step, owner and risk facts with record dates and references. 3. Separate recorded partner assertions from supported facts and flag any MACC-related statement as requiring authorized commercial verification, not inferred treatment. 4. Return a renewal-risk card with evidence, uncertainty, one intervention question and proposed accountable seller; MCEM-05 is renewal context only. 5. Ask PSS to prioritize a verification action and the AE to judge use in account planning; stop if timing, identity or decisive evidence is unresolved. No commercial approval, partner-system retrieval, messages, writebacks, promises or funding decisions. If existing authorized record access is unavailable, inspect a dated authorized extract of the exact identified record or clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Mark access gaps explicitly; synthetic data supports rehearsal only, never a real opportunity conclusion.
activities.expectedOutput: One-renewal card: timing/next-step facts/date/reference, partner claims, commercial-verification flag, uncertainty and intervention owner question.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS prioritizes verification; AE judges account-planning use. Stop on unresolved timing, identity or decisive evidence. Authorized commercial owner verifies MACC; no AI forecast/renewal approval.
activities.requiredContext: OPP_ID, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE. Known authorized MSX renewal opportunity only; no broader renewal-agent agreement, pricing, quote or commercial-action capabilities. A dated authorized extract of the exact scoped record suffices; existing CRM access is optional. Synthetic records are practice-only.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

Fallback: If existing authorized Sales Agent/CRM access is unavailable, use a dated authorized extract of the exact specified opportunity or a clearly labeled synthetic practice record. Distinguish access gaps from absent pipeline; no broader retrieval, record update or real factual conclusion from synthetic data.
activities.whyThisMatters: Finds the evidence gap changing renewal priority while preserving the narrow Sales Agent record boundary.

activities.name: Reconcile renewal timing and risk across three supplied opportunities
activities.description: Independent supplied-evidence choice: Cowork uses only the approved inputs and applicable permissions/spending policy. Makes small-sample renewal inspection usable without turning partner expectations into committed forecast.
activities.prompt: Use only information you are authorized to access and share. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use only the three specified renewal record extracts, the partner renewal notes and the review criteria for the three specified opportunity ids. Scope: the partner customer solution scope; date: today. 1. Match the three identities, owners and dates, distinguishing unavailable access from missing pipeline evidence. 2. Compare renewal timing, next steps and risk statements, labeling record facts, partner expectations and explicit customer evidence separately. 3. Apply only the supplied review criteria to flag contradictions and unverified MACC assumptions; do not invent probabilities, forecast amounts or treatment. 4. Return a three-row intervention shortlist with evidence, uncertainty, priority rationale, proposed owner question and review date. 5. Ask PSS to accept or hold the prioritization and each AE to confirm account facts; stop where decisive timing or commercial authority is unresolved. No native system queries, forecast approval, messages, writebacks, promises or funding decisions.
activities.expectedOutput: Three-opportunity intervention shortlist with timing conflicts, fact/expectation/customer distinctions, risk rationale, commercial unknowns and owner questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PSS accepts/holds priority, not forecast; each AE confirms account facts. Stop on unresolved decisive timing or commercial authority; no invented probabilities or MACC treatment.
activities.requiredContext: THREE_RENEWAL_RECORD_EXTRACTS, PARTNER_RENEWAL_NOTES, REVIEW_CRITERIA, exactly THREE_OPPORTUNITY_IDS, PARTNER_CUSTOMER_SOLUTION_SCOPE, AS_OF_DATE. Evidence needs source owner/date; commercial claims need explicit authorized verification status.
activitySteps: 1. Supply the exact identifiers, scope, dates and required evidence listed below. 2. Run the five-step prompt, staying within its one-deal/referral or three-opportunity boundary. 3. Inspect the artifact against the supplied or cited record evidence and challenge one unsupported assumption. 4. Complete the named human decision and stop condition below; leave any owner action unconfirmed until that owner accepts it.

agents.whenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A renewal plan is credible when timing, risk and the next seller action are evidenced. Focus on one renewal intervention without assuming commercial treatment or partner commitments.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Distinguish renewal intent, record facts, partner expectations and owner-verified commercial facts. Sales Agent here is restricted to identified MSX opportunities, not broader agreement, quote or partner-system retrieval. No AI treatment calculations, eligibility approvals, financial commitments or forecast acceptance.
discussionQuestions: What evidence changes renewal risk? Is timing recorded, partner-expected or customer-confirmed? Who verifies the MACC assertion and who decides whether to use it?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect one identified renewal MSX opportunity for a decision-changing risk'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one renewal-risk card or three-opportunity reconciliation with dated facts, commercial unknowns, intervention owner and accept/hold decision. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'ISV variant: challenge the MACC assumption behind one renewal deal', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Prioritize renewal evidence gaps and accountable interventions; a MACC claim is not verified treatment, committed consumption or approved forecast. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one exact renewal MSX ID or dated supplied evidence for three renewal opportunities, scope/date, source owners, timing/risks and existing review criteria. For the one-deal intervention/ISV variant bring owner roster and explicitly supplied commercial evidence; avoid unnecessary agreement details. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Where is expected renewal treated as committed? Which statement lacks commercial authority? Is missing access being called missing pipeline? What can PSS coordinate without making a forecast or funding decision?
listenFor: Bounded renewal view; facts distinct from claims; exact authorized-owner question; no inferred MACC treatment; seller-confirmed actions; PSS priority distinct from AE forecast authority.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one renewal-risk card with agreement date or unknown, customer evidence, commercial uncertainty, verifying owner and hold reason manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which commercial assumption changed from usable evidence to a verification request?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will verify [one renewal or MACC claim] with [named AE/authorized commercial owner] by [date] and bring an updated risk/hold rationale. I will not promise renewal, treatment, funding or another seller's action. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized renewal or MACC assumption checked and whether it changed risk or hold judgment; omit terms and do not imply approved treatment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. activities.name: Monitor agreed ROB actions
activities.description: Watch agreed sales actions on an approved cadence and report only changes or exceptions for PSS review.
activities.prompt: Produce an unactivated read-only proposal, not a running monitor. Use authorized dated snapshots, a user-maintained baseline and previous report supplied for this review; do not retrieve unsupplied records, create automation, retain agent memory or notify anyone. Missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no change. Record scope, source permission, owner, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and supplied approved change criteria without inventing values. Future monitoring requires separate explicit approval and verified access/state capabilities. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Compare supplied snapshots for the agreed RoB actions on the approved cadence using the approved evidence locations, the dated baseline, and the named action owners. For a baseline-only review, record each dated action, owner, due date, and evidence state. For a comparison review, compare the supplied baseline and user-maintained previous report. Return change-only findings for new completion evidence, changed dates or owners, missed actions, missing context, or access failures. Do not infer seller intent, score performance, send reminders, or close actions. Each owner validates their action, and PSS decides the coaching focus and next-review test.
activities.expectedOutput: A dated baseline-only or change-only supplied-evidence review draft with source/history/access gaps and an unactivated proposal for the named reviewer; zero scheduled jobs or notifications.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Action owners validate status; PSS retains coaching and next-review decisions.
activities.requiredContext: Agreed ROB actions, approved cadence, evidence locations, dated baseline, named owners, and PSS reviewer. Provide authorized dated snapshots and user-maintained baseline/prior report if available. Source permissions, scope, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and automation approval are explicit proposed fields; missing inputs remain gaps and no tool access/state retention is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm one bounded dependency/action and supply authorized dated snapshots; clearly labeled synthetic evidence is rehearsal-only.
2. Check the user-maintained baseline/prior report, comparable definitions and named reviewer; leave missing history, permission or criteria explicit.
3. Compare supplied evidence manually or with one already authorized tool; no schedule, live retrieval or persistent agent memory.
4. Produce a dated baseline-only/comparison draft and unactivated proposal with source, owner, cadence, recipients, expiry and approval fields.
5. Apply the unchanged HumanCheckpoint before interpretation/action; future automation, notifications and system changes require separate explicit authorization.

Fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied dated snapshots manually and retain the baseline/report yourself; no connector, persistent agent memory, scheduled job or notification permission is assumed.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Execution coaching starts with observable evidence, not a judgment about a seller. Focus on one accepted action, its follow-through and the question that could improve the next decision.
keyTalkingPoints: PSS owns partner-sales execution; PDM owns partner strategy and PMM marketing. The partner seller and AE remain accountable for their own actions. Require exact IDs, partner/customer/solution scope and evidence dates; distinguish record facts from partner claims and missing access from missing pipeline. Observe evidence before judging behavior; an overdue record field does not prove poor performance. Meeting attendance does not prove action acceptance. PSS coaches execution, not PDM strategy or PMM performance. Compare only stated country/solution scope; three opportunities do not describe total partner performance.
discussionQuestions: What behavior can the evidence support and what context is missing? Did the receiving owner accept the action? What evidence at the next ROB shows follow-through rather than another meeting?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Inspect three MSX records for evidence-led ROB coaching questions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. At eight minutes stop generating. Select the most decision-relevant unresolved item in one coaching card or three-opportunity ROB exception sheet with evidence, context gaps, owner-confirmed action and next-review test. Ask which owner can verify it and what finding would change the next decision. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Prepare one deal's coaching conversation from observable evidence', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Coach one observable execution behavior using dated evidence and a seller-confirmed action; notes and CRM records do not establish full partner context. Separate PSS coordination from actions still awaiting another owner's confirmation. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring three exact MSX IDs or supplied evidence for three opportunities; use one deal for coaching/relay choices. Include scope/date, prior/current observations, agreed action notes and roster. State country/solution coverage, especially Asia cross-solution context. Permission-review or de-identify evidence. Each input requires exact ID, scope and evidence date. Use only approved data and remove unnecessary personal details.
facilitatorQuestions: Which statement is an observation rather than a personal judgment? What proves acceptance/completion? Which missing context should the seller explain? What will the next ROB test?
listenFor: Respectful evidence-led coaching; clear scope/date; no inferred motives or performance scores; proposed/accepted/completed actions distinct; PSS cadence ownership and individual seller accountability.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected agent or permitted record is unavailable, complete one coaching card with observable business fact, context gap, proposed/accepted/completed distinction, seller question and next ROB test manually from approved de-identified supplied evidence. If there are no permitted inputs, use a labeled synthetic case only to practice the method; current status and acceptance remain unknown. Sales Agent does not grant MSX permissions, and an export is not a workaround for denied access. Partner Center, PMX, Marketplace and referral status require supplied evidence or accountable-owner verification, not an assumed connector. PSS reviews the coordination choice; AE/PDM, commercial and individual seller decisions remain with their owners. No source-system update, message or publication is part of this fallback.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: How did checking missing context change your coaching language or proposed action?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, I will review [one execution behavior or relay gap] with [named partner seller/AE] by [date] and bring the agreed next-review evidence test. I confirm only my own coordination action; other owners accept their own actions. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a de-identified execution question clarified with its seller and whether it improved follow-up; do not assess employee performance. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

PLC-EPS-PSS-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-EPS-PSS-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-EPS-PSS-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

PLC-EPS-PTS-W01.todayObjective: Explore how peer-led huddles connect business outcomes, recurring workflows, and responsible AI experimentation, including what to try and share between sessions.
PLC-EPS-PTS-W01.whyItMatters: Access and usage do not equal transformation. Teams build durable capability when managers connect outcomes to the work, peers experiment together, and evidence from practice improves the next cycle.
PLC-EPS-PTS-W01.desiredOutcome: Participate confidently in the motion, starting with a meaningful workflow and testing improvements in real work while retaining human judgment and learning from evidence.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Welcome to the Frontier Accelerator Huddle motion. This shared 30-minute Orientation starts a continuing peer-learning path: begin with recurring work, surface friction, and consider one useful next test. It is not a tool demo or performance assessment.
keyTalkingPoints: Start with the workflow and real friction, not a product. Compare approaches before choosing a tool; tools and AI are optional. Use only authorized, non-sensitive inputs and permitted tools. Treat outputs as drafts for human review; people retain authority over decisions and actions.
discussionQuestions: Where does a familiar workflow slow down? What makes that step difficult? What have peers found helpful? What would we need to understand before trying a small change?
suggestedTransitions: Move from a workflow example to peer comparison, then consider a bounded next test. Offer a permitted tool or AI only if useful; otherwise continue manually. Before moving on, distinguish observations, assumptions, and drafts needing human review.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Return to the workflow and name what peer learning clarified. Invite an optional next test or question, with appropriate authorization and human review. This begins a continuing learning motion; no deliverable, performance proof, or reporting obligation is created.
preparationChecklist: No prework, tool access, or artifact is required. A familiar or synthetic example is helpful but optional. Use only supplied or otherwise authorized non-sensitive inputs; never share sensitive customer or employee information. Listening or a manual explanation is enough to join.
facilitatorQuestions: What happens at this step, handoff, or decision? Where is the friction? How does someone else approach it? What small change might help, and what human review would be needed before using it?
listenFor: Listen for specific friction, useful peer comparisons, and clearly labelled assumptions. Keep privacy, permission, and human authority visible. Tool use, speed, and polished outputs are not measures of participation; a useful question or clearer workflow understanding also matters.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If access or suitable inputs are unavailable, stop the tool attempt and use a synthetic, non-sensitive example, manual walkthrough, or peer discussion. Do not bypass permissions or use sensitive information. Clearly label anything not executed; discussion remains valid participation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did another perspective help you notice? Which assumption still needs checking? What would you like to understand better before changing this workflow?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: If useful, choose a small next test or question within your authority. Tools and AI remain optional, and any output stays a draft until appropriate human review. You may also keep reflecting or defer; no deadline, artifact, or follow-up report is required.
bringBackEvidence: If you return to the conversation, optionally share an observation, question, or peer insight using authorized, non-sensitive information. No artifact, completed practice, performance result, or report is required. Never share sensitive customer or employee information.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Separate demonstrated capability from roadmap aspiration
activities.description: A traceable baseline prevents ambition or incomplete reporting from silently becoming technical strategy.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Using only my approved packet for the partner, build a technical landscape from the dated capability inventory, planning excerpt and up to three project summaries below. First reconcile duplicate capability names; then distinguish demonstrated capability, stated ambition and unknown. Produce a table with capability, cross-solution relevance, source/date, constraint and validation question, followed by the single uncertainty most likely to alter our roadmap. Preserve conflicting claims rather than choosing a convenient version. Treat supplied exports as snapshots, not live PMX or Partner Center access. I, the PTS, will validate that uncertainty and the evidence classification. Stop if the partner scope or evidence provenance is missing. Draft only; no writeback, outreach or readiness approval.
activities.expectedOutput: One-page landscape table plus one prioritized evidence uncertainty, with conflicting and missing claims explicitly labeled.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS checks that capability classifications match the supplied evidence and selects the one uncertainty worth validating. Stop if partner identity, provenance or permission is unclear; do not infer readiness from missing data.
activities.requiredContext: One partner; approved capability inventory with dates; PBP technical excerpt or equivalent notes; zero to three project summaries; source labels and sharing limits. Supply extracts manually; no connector assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Select one partner and paste approved, dated excerpts with source labels.
2. Ask Cowork to reconcile names and classify claims before synthesizing the map.
3. Trace the most consequential row to its supplied evidence and correct any inference presented as fact.
4. Retain the map with one PTS-owned validation question and a named human evidence owner.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A traceable baseline prevents ambition or incomplete reporting from silently becoming technical strategy.

activities.name: Test one cross-solution opportunity hypothesis with citations
activities.description: Cited counterevidence helps the PTS avoid converting an attractive technology trend into an unsupported partner priority.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Research the supplied hypothesis for the partner using only the approved source links or extracts I provide, alongside the attached capability baseline. Assess technical relevance across the named solution areas and distinguish current facts from forward-looking possibilities. Return a short evidence brief with supporting signals, counterevidence, dependencies and a now/next/later implication using my supplied horizon definitions. Cite each factual claim with source and date; if a source cannot be reached or citations are unavailable, label that explicitly rather than substituting unapproved research. Recommend one validation question, not an investment commitment. The PTS will decide whether the hypothesis belongs in the landscape. Stop before recommending direction if its key dependency is unsupported. No messages, publication or system updates.
activities.expectedOutput: Cited hypothesis brief containing supporting and contrary evidence, dependency gaps, horizon implications and a retain/qualify/park recommendation for PTS review.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS verifies source relevance and decides whether the hypothesis merits planning attention. Stop at an evidence-gap brief when the critical dependency or citation cannot be verified; no claim of validated feasibility.
activities.requiredContext: One partner; one cross-solution hypothesis; a dated capability baseline; user-defined planning horizons; an explicit approved source list or extracts, with source dates where known.
activitySteps: 1. State one opportunity hypothesis and define now, next and later for this partner.
2. Supply approved research links or extracts and the capability baseline to Researcher.
3. Check one supporting claim and one counterclaim against their citations.
4. Decide as PTS whether to retain, qualify or park the hypothesis and record the reason.

Fallback: If Researcher is unavailable, inspect supplied approved extracts or approved official URLs manually. Preserve citations/dates and mark inaccessible claims unresolved; do not broaden the source boundary.
activities.whyThisMatters: Cited counterevidence helps the PTS avoid converting an attractive technology trend into an unsupported partner priority.

activities.name: Choose the technical gap worth resolving first
activities.description: Selecting one evidence question protects strategic attention from a long, undifferentiated backlog of technical unknowns.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. From my approved technical landscape for the partner, compare no more than three unresolved gaps using the decision criteria and constraints I supply. Work in two passes: identify which roadmap decision each gap blocks, then compare the value of obtaining evidence against effort and reversibility. Do not invent weights, delivery capacity or partner willingness; show any missing input explicitly. Return a gap-choice memo with the recommended first question, the minimum evidence needed to answer it, the human evidence owner and what we can safely defer. I, the PTS, own the ordering and will confirm the owner's involvement separately. Stop if the comparison depends on an unsupported capacity or strategic-priority assumption. Draft only; no task assignment, messages or system writeback.
activities.expectedOutput: Gap-choice memo with a comparison table, one minimum evidence question, proposed human owner and a reason for deferring the other gaps.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS confirms that resolving the selected gap could change a real roadmap decision. Stop if criteria conflict or an owner/capacity assumption is unsupported; retain a question rather than fabricate a ranking.
activities.requiredContext: One partner; one approved landscape; at most three gaps; PTS-supplied decision criteria; known effort constraints; evidence-owner names or explicitly unknown owners.
activitySteps: 1. Paste up to three gaps and the roadmap decisions they appear to block.
2. Add approved prioritization criteria, known constraints and available human evidence owners.
3. Review Cowork's comparison for invented weights or assumed capacity.
4. Select one gap as PTS and capture its minimum evidence request without sending it.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Start with one partner whose technical direction is harder to explain than its activity list. Ask what is actually demonstrated today and what is merely planned. This week establishes the evidence baseline for a cross-solution roadmap, not a customer-sales stage or an architecture review. AI can reconcile approved material and expose gaps; the PTS decides which gap matters. A partner's business ambition is useful context, but it is not proof of technical readiness. In the live practice, choose one bounded artifact, not the whole landscape-to-roadmap process.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Distinguish current technical capability, roadmap intent and unsupported assertion. Date the evidence and retain the partner's own description alongside Microsoft-side visibility.

2. Map across solution areas and planning horizons without assigning detailed architecture or delivery tasks. PTS sets direction; PSA executes scoped CSA-specific work; the partner owns delivery and operation.
3. Use PMX, PBP and Partner Center material only when the participant supplies an approved export or extract. Access, completeness and permission are not implied by naming a system.
discussionQuestions: Where does our current partner view confuse certification, stated capability and demonstrated delivery?
Which uncertainty could change the direction of the technical plan?
What must come from the partner rather than from Microsoft-side reporting?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Separate demonstrated capability from roadmap aspiration'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Give one minute to define the partner and question, five minutes to run one Featured practice, and two minutes to inspect the most consequential evidence gap. Treat the other practices as alternatives or later follow-ons. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Choose the technical gap worth resolving first', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Ask each participant to identify one claim they downgraded, retained or need to validate. Close on the evidence question rather than the apparent completeness of the AI output. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one partner identifier, a dated approved technical-plan excerpt or equivalent notes, a capability inventory and at most three project or offering summaries. Remove unnecessary customer identifiers. Mark source, date and disclosure permission; missing material is a valid starting point. Choose whether the immediate input supports a capability map, an opportunity hypothesis or a gap decision.
facilitatorQuestions: Which row is evidence and which is inference?
Does the proposed opportunity connect more than one technical capability, or simply restate a product name?
What can the PTS decide now without implying PSA capacity or partner commitment?
listenFor: An evidence gap being presented as a weakness, access to PMX being assumed, or a partner claim becoming a readiness score without corroboration. Ask participants to preserve an unknown rather than make the map look complete. Redirect implementation detail to a future scoped PSA handoff.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If approved data or agent access is unavailable, draw four columns: capability, evidence/date, uncertainty and next validation question. Populate one row from a clearly marked sanitized example. Do not imply the example describes the real partner and do not browse unapproved sources to fill the gap.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption looked credible until you asked for its source, and how could it have distorted the roadmap?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate one roadmap-relevant claim with an authorized evidence owner. Record the source/date, your PTS judgment and whether the claim changes the planning conversation; obtain the evidence through normal human channels, not automated outreach. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized roadmap claim checked and whether it improved the planning judgment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Draft a traceable multi-horizon plan slice

activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Return a table of horizon, outcome, evidence gate, cross-solution dependency, proposed owner and unresolved decision. Distinguish PTS strategy from PSA execution and partner delivery. Label unsupported assumptions and unconfirmed commitments visibly, including any missing feasibility or capacity input. I, the PTS, will choose the proposed plan and seek stakeholder review separately. Stop before recommending a baseline when a critical dependency has no evidence or owner. Do not write back, message reviewers or approve commitments.

activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS owns the proposed outcome set and horizon ordering. Stop if a critical prerequisite or owner cannot be established; leave the plan as a review draft with that blocker visible.
activities.requiredContext: One partner; approved ambition/PBP excerpt; technical baseline; horizon definitions; up to three candidate outcomes; known constraints and stakeholder roles. No live system access required.

2. Limit the plan slice to three candidate outcomes and run the synthesis.
3. Trace every outcome to a supplied priority and inspect its evidence gate.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Bring the landscape forward, but do not require last week's exercise as a prerequisite: an existing approved technical baseline is equally valid. Today connects one partner ambition to a small number of technical outcomes and the order in which they could become credible. The PTS owns cross-solution direction and planning choices. PDM contributes business alignment; PSA reviews feasibility and eventual scoped execution; the partner must validate its own priorities and responsibilities. AI prepares the conversation. It cannot make the conversation happen or turn proposed ownership into agreement.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Give each planning horizon a meaning for this partner; do not manufacture fiscal dates, funding or resource commitments. Link each technical outcome to the approved business ambition that justifies it.
2. Separate outcomes, evidence gates and dependencies. A roadmap milestone is not complete merely because a slide or activity exists.

3. Co-creation requires explicit human review. Mark proposed owners and unconfirmed partner commitments, and keep the resulting draft out of systems of record until the appropriate human process is complete.
discussionQuestions: Which technical outcome actually advances the partner's stated ambition?
Where does our plan depend on PSA feasibility input or partner capacity that has not been confirmed?
What should the next review decide rather than merely acknowledge?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Draft a traceable multi-horizon plan slice'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Use one minute to name the planning decision, five minutes for one Featured plan, dependency or review-agenda practice, and two minutes to inspect the proposed human decision. Do not try to finish the partner plan live. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Add a regional activation delta to a global plan', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by distinguishing what the PTS has drafted from what the partner and reviewers have confirmed. The next useful step is one resolved planning question, not more roadmap detail. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring an approved partner ambition or PBP excerpt, the current technical baseline, existing horizon definitions, and at most three candidate outcomes. Add known constraints and the current review stakeholders. A manually supplied PMX/PBP export is a dated input, not permission to retrieve or update the system. Have one unresolved planning decision ready.
facilitatorQuestions: Can you trace the proposed outcome to a partner priority?
What evidence would distinguish an achieved outcome from completed activity?
Which proposed owner has not yet agreed, and how is that visible?
listenFor: Technical activities being labeled outcomes, an AI-proposed date becoming a commitment, or a partner role being silently assigned to Microsoft. Help participants express the disputed dependency rather than hide it behind a confident roadmap graphic.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: With no usable packet, outline one row: partner ambition, technical outcome, evidence gate, dependency, proposed owner and decision needed. Mark all unsupplied fields unknown. Use the row as a co-creation question, not a completed plan. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which proposed milestone changed when you required an outcome and an evidence gate rather than an activity description?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, take one technical-plan decision through the normal human review with the relevant partner, PDM or PSA stakeholder. Record confirmed versus proposed ownership and the PTS decision or remaining blocker; do not automatically distribute the draft. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized milestone or ownership assumption changed in plan review and whether its evidence gate clarified the next decision. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Make an evidence-based priority or hold decision
activities.description: A conditional comparison makes the opportunity cost and uncertainty behind prioritization visible to the technical-plan owner.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Compare the two or three approved technical candidates I supply for the partner against my stated criteria, constraints and any explicit weights. First assemble a fact-and-gap table; then provide a conditional priority order with rationale and the cost of deferring each candidate. Use no invented scores, weights, effort estimates or partner commitments. Distinguish strategic fit, technical readiness evidence and the credibility of a build-to-consume path. Show how the order changes under the single uncertainty I identify. If evidence cannot distinguish the candidates, recommend a hold and the minimum question needed to proceed. The PTS makes the priority decision. Stop before recommending allocation where capacity is unconfirmed. Draft only; no funding, eligibility approval, messages or system writeback.
activities.expectedOutput: Conditional portfolio comparison and PTS decision template covering priority/hold, defer consequences, gaps and a reconsideration trigger.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS owns the ordering and validates the criteria and capacity evidence. Stop at hold if a decisive input is missing; do not let a generated score authorize allocation.
activities.requiredContext: One partner; two or three candidate briefs; approved technical-plan priorities; PTS criteria and optional weights; known constraints; one uncertainty to test. All system material is user-supplied.
activitySteps: 1. Supply two or three candidate summaries for one partner and explicit criteria.
2. Add known constraints, optional human-chosen weights and one uncertain assumption.
3. Inspect the evidence table and conditional ordering for unsupported numeric precision.
4. Record the PTS priority or hold decision, one defer consequence and a revisit trigger.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: A conditional comparison makes the opportunity cost and uncertainty behind prioritization visible to the technical-plan owner.

activities.name: Choose a sequence under a real capacity constraint
activities.description: Sequencing reveals tradeoffs that a ranked list alone cannot show when several projects depend on the same scarce capability.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use my approved candidate dependency notes and dated capacity statements for the partner to compare two sequencing options for no more than three projects. Separate confirmed capacity from requests and unknowns, including PSA specialist time and partner delivery capacity. Identify the shared bottleneck, the effect of sequencing on the technical plan and the work deliberately deferred under each option. Do not invent hours, assign people or turn a capacity request into acceptance. Return a sequence tradeoff card with assumptions, evidence references and one question that would change the choice. I, the PTS, will select a proposed sequence after owner validation. Stop if neither option is supported by the available capacity evidence. No task creation, outreach, commitments or updates.

activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS confirms the strategic ordering; PSA and partner owners separately confirm their capacity. Stop when either option depends on unsupported availability; no resource assignment by inference.
activities.requiredContext: One partner; up to three project candidates; approved dependency notes; dated PSA/partner capacity statements or explicit unknowns; the constraint PTS wants to test.
activitySteps: 1. Bound the scope to at most three projects and one shared constraint.
2. Supply dated capacity statements and prerequisite relationships, marking requests separately.
3. Review two sequencing options and verify the bottleneck against the packet.
4. Select a proposed PTS sequence or hold, leaving resource confirmation with the actual owners.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

activities.name: Challenge a candidate's build-to-consume bridge
activities.description: Testing the bridge prevents technical investment from being justified by an assumed consumption outcome that the evidence does not support.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the single candidate project/offering at the partner, use only the approved concept, activation notes and usage-evidence extracts I supply. Map the proposed bridge from build output to partner activation and eventual consumption evidence. At each link, show the required artifact or behavior, supplied evidence, partner-dependent assumption and human owner. Distinguish a successful build, activation readiness, actual activation and observed consumption; do not infer one from another or forecast unsupported revenue or usage. activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS validates that the evidence gate informs technical prioritization rather than claiming customer adoption. Stop when partner-side evidence is absent; do not substitute Microsoft visibility for partner truth.
activities.requiredContext: One partner and one candidate; approved build concept; dated activation notes; user-supplied usage or Partner Center extracts if available; known partner evidence owners. Missing extracts must stay missing.
activitySteps: 1. Choose one candidate and supply its build concept and available activation/usage evidence.
2. Ask Cowork to separate the bridge into distinct evidence-bearing links.
3. Challenge any leap from build success to adoption or consumption.
4. Record the PTS evidence gate and retain, qualify or hold recommendation for portfolio review.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.

2. Compare build value with the path to activation and consumption; label hypotheses, partner-dependent steps and evidence gaps instead of forecasting unsupported outcomes.
3. Record the defer choice and revisit trigger as carefully as the top priority. Preserve PSA capacity confirmation and partner delivery decisions as separate human checkpoints.
discussionQuestions: Which candidate would we defer if available capacity fell tomorrow?
Where are we rewarding build activity without evidence of a usable offering or consumption path?
What new evidence would legitimately reverse our ordering?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Make an evidence-based priority or hold decision'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Start with one offering idea that could materially change the partner's technical roadmap. The question is not whether AI can describe an exciting solution; it is whether the supplied evidence supports choosing this direction over a plausible alternative. Researcher can test a specific signal against an approved source list. Cowork can connect the evidence, capability baseline and partner comments into a decision brief. PTS selects technical direction; PSA determines detailed architecture and scoped execution later; partner leaders validate their own intent and commitments. Keep exercise to one evidence test or one decision artifact.
keyTalkingPoints: 1. Separate market or technology signals from verified partner demand. A cited source may support a trend without proving that this partner should invest in it.
2. State technical differentiation as a hypothesis and expose the dependency that could invalidate it. Do not turn a draft direction into promised features, timelines or revenue.
3. Partner commitment is human evidence. Prepare the questions needed to confirm priorities, sponsorship or operating ownership; never interpret a positive comment or absent objection as agreement.
discussionQuestions: What makes this direction technically distinctive for this partner rather than generically interesting?
What evidence would lead us to choose a different offering direction?
Which commitment are we assuming instead of asking the partner to confirm?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Test the signal behind an offering hypothesis'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Spend one minute naming the offering choice, five minutes running one Featured evidence, direction or commitment-question practice, and two minutes checking the strongest claim against its source. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Choose between two technical offering directions', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close on one direction to test or one reason to defer, not a list of exciting possibilities. Restate that the partner has not committed merely because the draft uses confident language. Use the next real case to test this habit, then compare what helped and what failed with the huddle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved offering concept, a partner capability baseline, the technical-plan priority it supports and either an approved source list or approved stakeholder comments. Include a real alternative where possible. Mark source dates and distinguish external signals from partner statements. No public research beyond the user-approved list is required.
facilitatorQuestions: Does the citation support this claim or only a nearby idea?
Which feature or operating assumption remains a hypothesis?
Is the next step a PTS direction decision or a partner commitment question?
listenFor: Generic innovation language, current capability confused with a future roadmap, and market signals substituted partner intent. Ask for a counterargument and insist that unsupported claims remain visible.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: Without accessible research, label citations unavailable and create a hypothesis card with the claim, supplied evidence, counterargument and minimum validation question. Do not invent market proof or use unapproved browsing to make the brief appear finished. If no permitted inputs are available at all, sketch a clearly labeled synthetic version of the selected artifact to practice the review questions only. Leave real status, program criteria, authority and acceptance unknown; the example is not evidence for a live decision.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which sentence would have overstated our confidence if it had reached the partner unchanged?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate one technical-direction assumption through the appropriate human evidence owner or approved source. Record the PTS retain, revise or defer judgment and the partner confirmation still needed; do not publish the offering brief. If input or access is missing, use a permitted sanitized example or document the verification gap; do not infer approval, agreement or status.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized direction hypothesis qualified and whether it prevented an overstated partner commitment. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Scope regional activation without rebuilding the global solution
activities.description: A regional handoff variant preserves global technical investment while making genuine local activation needs explicit.
activities.prompt: If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Use the approved global solution package, regional delta and owner notes for the partner solution in the region. Draft a local PSA activation scope that inherits global architecture decisions and limits new work to evidenced regional prerequisites or validation needs. Show inherited artifacts, allowed local checks, explicit rebuild exclusions, partner delivery/operation boundaries and exceptions requiring PTS/global-owner review. Do not assume regional coverage, service availability, compliance clearance or access to global sources beyond my packet. Mark missing evidence and proposed acceptance explicitly. PTS will validate local scope against global technical intent. Stop if a local requirement contradicts a global decision or needs unsupported coverage. No deployment, eligibility approval, commitments, messages or system writeback.
activities.expectedOutput: Local activation scope with inherited artifacts, bounded checks, rebuild exclusions, exit evidence and global/local exceptions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: PTS confirms that local scope extends the global solution rather than redesigning it. Stop on a conflicting requirement or unverified coverage; PSA and partner owners must separately accept their responsibilities.
activities.requiredContext: One partner/solution and one region; approved global solution package; regional activation delta; known regional coverage; global/local decision-owner notes and partner responsibilities.
activitySteps: 1. Choose one region and supply the approved global package plus regional delta.
2. Ask Cowork to identify inherited artifacts before defining local checks.
3. Inspect any new-build request and route strategic exceptions to PTS/global-owner review.
4. Retain a bounded PTS-reviewed local scope with acceptance still subject to human confirmation.

Fallback: If the named assistant is unavailable, complete the same bounded evidence table or draft manually from the approved supplied packet. No additional assistant, connector, private-system access or automatic execution is required.
