PLC-USPSI-SSP-W09.todayObjective: Reflect on evidence from the guided Role Path and choose the team's next workflow priorities, using relevant existing topics or a custom huddle.
PLC-USPSI-SSP-W09.whyItMatters: Teams sustain change when they use evidence from practice to set their next learning priorities rather than continuing a fixed path by default.
PLC-USPSI-SSP-W09.desiredOutcome: Sustain a team-owned cycle of workflow improvement, using shared experience to choose relevant huddles, test changes in real work, and revisit priorities as evidence develops.

activities.name: Reconnect to the Huddle Motion
activities.description: Reconnect to the shared purpose and move from guided activation into continuing, team-owned learning.
activities.expectedOutput: Shared understanding of how the team will carry learning into its next work priority.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Keep the transition non-evaluative. Participants choose what they share; do not use AI adoption or survey completion as an individual performance measure.
activities.requiredContext: An example or question about real work, if available. No separate role-specific preparation; use a sanitized or hypothetical example when the group cannot discuss the underlying details.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about three minutes reconnecting to why the Huddle Motion matters to the work.
2. Recognize the shift from guided Weeks 1-8 to team-owned learning, not the end of the motion.

3. Preview the shared transition: reflect on experience, choose the next focus, and close with participant feedback. These are coordinated session components, not four alternative practices to complete.
activities.whyThisMatters: A shared purpose helps the team connect prior learning to future work.

activities.name: Share Your Experience: look back on real work
activities.description: Compare current work with the start of the guided path; identify a useful change, a continuing friction point, or where support is still needed.
activities.expectedOutput: A practical learning insight and a support need that inform what the team should try next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Separate workflow benefit from tool usage. Share only permitted details and do not evaluate participants or collect individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: A permitted work example, attempted practice, or unanswered workflow question. Remove customer, partner, personnel, or commercial details the group is not authorized to receive.
activitySteps: 1. Spend about ten minutes comparing experiences using examples the group may discuss.
2. Explain what changed in the workflow or why a practice did not help yet; no success story is required.
3. Identify a habit worth repeating and a friction point or support need.
4. Use these observations to inform the next-focus discussion, without ranking participants.
activities.whyThisMatters: Concrete examples show what to repeat and where the motion needs support.

activities.name: AI in Action: choose the next team focus
activities.description: Choose a next work priority and an existing or custom huddle starting point, using tools and content permitted for the team.
activities.expectedOutput: An agreed next priority, a suitable huddle or draft starting point, and an owner; optional backlog ideas remain separate.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Use only tools and data permitted in the team project setting. AI assistance does not authorize access, policy changes, commercial commitments, or publishing. A named owner reviews a custom draft for accuracy, audience permissions, and privacy before distribution or publication.
activities.requiredContext: The work priorities raised in the reflection and the team project tool/data restrictions. App access is useful but not required to agree a priority; use permitted, sanitized, or hypothetical examples.
activitySteps: 1. Use the ten-minute AI-in-Action segment to connect the reflection to work where a change would be useful.
2. Choose the priority to try first; keep up to two other ideas as an optional backlog rather than simultaneous commitments.

3. In All Topics, compare relevant outcomes and activities, filtering by Segment, Role, Focus Area, and tools permitted for the team and project. Select one Featured practice for the next ordinary huddle; Extended practices remain optional.
4. If no topic fits, use Huddle in a Box to outline a draft for later review, not to create or publish a finished huddle in this session.
5. Confirm an owner and a practical next step. Without app access, record the priority and locate the content later.
activities.whyThisMatters: Starting from work value and team permissions makes the continuing motion useful rather than tool-led.

activities.name: Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey
activities.description: Confirm the next work focus and invite participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey themselves.
activities.expectedOutput: A clear next-focus commitment and a participant-owned feedback opportunity, with any unfinished survey completed after the huddle.
activities.humanCheckpoint: Participants complete their own survey; do not collect individual responses or require proof of completion. Record only permitted team-level learning and next steps, never sensitive work examples or individual performance judgments.
activities.requiredContext: The agreed next priority and a participant-accessible survey link; survey access is not required to confirm the next work step.
activitySteps: 1. Use the final five minutes to restate the useful habit, friction point, and chosen next focus.
2. Confirm who will take the next step and when the team will revisit what it learned.
3. Open the Team Member Impact Survey and let participants complete their own responses. If time or access is insufficient, finish after the huddle rather than extending the live session.
4. Continue the team-owned motion; this transition is not a final huddle.
activities.whyThisMatters: A clear next step and participant feedback sustain learning without turning the transition into a scorecard.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Week 9 is the shared transition from guided activation to team-owned practice. The team has completed the eight-week activation journey. Use this huddle to recognize what changed, address friction, and choose what to focus on next.
keyTalkingPoints: This is the same participant experience for every role. Overview: 3 minutes - reconnect to the motion and the transition to team ownership. Share Your Experience: 10 minutes - reflect on useful changes, friction, and support needs. AI-in-Action: 10 minutes - choose the next team priority and a relevant existing or custom huddle starting point. Closing & Next Steps: 5 minutes - confirm the owner and next action, then allow participants to complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
discussionQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent?
Which two or three team priorities would be most useful next?
suggestedTransitions: Use the coordinated Transition agenda: Overview, Share Your Experience, AI-in-Action, and Closing & Next Steps. Reflect on real work, agree the next focus and owner, and use the final five minutes for participant-owned survey completion. Review All Topics or a custom-huddle idea only if time and access permit.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close the guided path by naming one useful habit, one unresolved friction point, and two or three priorities for team-owned huddles. Assign a follow-up owner for each priority. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately; if access is blocked, record the blocker for follow-up.
preparationChecklist: Before joining, bring one concrete example where AI changed your work, one friction point or challenge, and one idea for what comes next. Keep examples appropriate to share. No separate role-specific Week 9 preparation is needed.
facilitatorQuestions: Where has AI changed the way you work?
What do you do now that you did not do eight weeks ago?
Which example shows an impact worth repeating?
Where are you stuck or inconsistent, and what support or practice would help?
Which two or three priorities are most useful now?
Which All Topics huddle or custom huddle could help with each priority?
listenFor: Concrete examples of work changed, one useful habit to keep, and a specific friction point. Keep reflection conversational, not a scorecard. priorities grounded in team work and an owner or next step. Remind the group to share only information it is authorized to discuss.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If examples are vague, compare one task before and after and keep tool discussion anchored to the work. If the app, search, download or survey is inaccessible, capture the useful habit, friction point, next priority and follow-up owner manually; do not require Create your own huddle or Huddle in a Box to complete the conversation. A sanitized or clearly labeled synthetic task can demonstrate the reflection method, but is not personal impact evidence or a substitute survey response. Record the access gap and use the approved link/process later.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which habit should the team keep, what evidence supports it, and what friction remains? Which two or three priorities should shape the next huddles?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next team-owned huddle, test one chosen habit on real work and decide what to keep, revise or stop. Agree the next topic and owner. Use the Frontier Accelerator topic library or Huddle in a Box if useful; otherwise plan manually. Use approved tools and permitted inputs only. Complete the Team Member Impact Survey separately, or record an access blocker.
bringBackEvidence: At the next huddle, share one brief, anonymized observation: what changed, what remains uncertain, and what to adjust next. Keep restricted details in approved systems. If untested, share the blocker and next check. Survey completion is not evidence of workflow benefit.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Define the support need before choosing a program
activities.description: State the outcome, missing capability, timing, and economics.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the opportunity, prepare a bounded support need from supplied customer outcome, workload, MCEM stage, transaction route, economics, partner status, and delivery gap. Return the missing capability, timing, success evidence, and required date; label unknowns and do not imply funding or program eligibility.
activities.expectedOutput: A bounded support need with success evidence and required date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE owns customer context and does not turn a support need into a funding promise.
activities.requiredContext: Customer outcome, workload, MCEM stage, transaction route, expected revenue/usage, partner status, and delivery gap. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on selecting the next routing conversation before the opportunity hardens around an ineligible or uneconomic path.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only when external delivery, proof, assessment, deployment, or funding support is needed; partner-led and zero-cost routes should be tested before discretionary ECIF.

Who must resolve the funding or delivery question before a promise?

listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.

Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. If current authoritative guidance or a required owner is unavailable, retain a decision hold or exact owner question; do not substitute remembered policy or a plausible ruling.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which route-fit assumption changed after checking requirements and acceptance?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a deciding route requirement or input and seek receiving-owner disposition or a documented hold. activities.name: Extract executable commercial conditions
activities.description: Separate binding conditions from context and rationale.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Separate conditions from context and rationale and preserve CE verification.
activities.expectedOutput: A condition register with source and consequence.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE verifies fidelity to the approved decision.
activities.requiredContext: Final approval, construct version, terms, expiry, credits/investment dependencies, and negotiation commitments.
activities.bestFitJob: Separate binding conditions from context and rationale.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm this specific task: Extract executable commercial conditions.
2. Supply authorized dated inputs listed in RequiredContext; use clearly labeled synthetic data if permitted real inputs are unavailable.
3. Produce the stated ExpectedOutput using the prompt; verify claims against supplied sources and expose unknowns.

activities.name: Set commercial re-engagement triggers
activities.description: Compare supplied approval conditions and execution snapshots for changes that may require CE commercial revalidation.
activities.prompt: Produce an unactivated, read-only proposal, not a running monitor. Use authorized dated snapshots, a user-maintained baseline and previous report supplied for this review; do not retrieve unsupplied records, create automation, retain agent memory or notify anyone. Missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no change. Record proposed scope, source permission, owner, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and approved change criteria without inventing values. Future monitoring requires separate explicit approval and verified access/state capabilities. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Compare the supplied approval conditions, customer or partner dependencies, expiry dates, execution evidence, and agreed CE re-entry routes. If two comparable dated snapshots are supplied, return only triggers that are new, changed, resolved, or overdue, with source date and threshold status. Do not reopen a commercial decision, assign action, or update a system.
activities.expectedOutput: A conditions/expiry/dependency delta register or baseline-only note with evidence dates, supplied approved triggers and CE re-entry questions; thresholds/approvals missing remain open and no monitor runs.
activities.humanCheckpoint: CE decides whether a change requires commercial revalidation.
activities.requiredContext: Approval conditions, customer/partner dependencies, expiry, and execution plan. Supply approved dated snapshots, comparable definitions, user-maintained baseline/prior report if available, reviewer and actual approved change criteria. Missing scope, source permission, cadence, recipients, expiry/review date or future automation approval remains explicit; no persistent state or tool access is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Define what change invalidates or reopens the commercial decision.
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.
2. Confirm scope, comparable definitions, evidence permission, access gaps and named human reviewer.
3. Compare only supplied state; missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no progress.
4. Apply the existing HumanCheckpoint to interpret changes; proposed owners, actions and thresholds are not accepted decisions.
5. Keep an unactivated proposal with approval gaps; do not schedule, retain agent memory, send reports or change records.
Access/fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied snapshots manually; no recurring job, retained agent memory or notification is required or authorized.
activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial ownership continues through accurate transfer of conditions; it does not make CE the transaction, delivery, or consumption owner.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on preventing the approved deal from failing because downstream owners received a narrative instead of executable conditions.
keyTalkingPoints: Apply only to execution dependencies created by the commercial construct; delivery, technical, consumption, and partner execution remain with their accountable owners.
Current execution: Use the approved case, authoritative contract/transaction route, and named downstream owners.
Fallback: Run a live handoff and record acceptance if no integrated workflow exists.
System of record: Approved commercial record remains authoritative; each receiving system records its execution task.
Optional AI boundary: AI may format the approved facts into audience-specific packets but must not add terms, reinterpret approval, or assign unaccepted owners.
discussionQuestions: Which approved condition must the receiver execute?
What evidence proves acceptance?
What remains with the commercial owner rather than delivery?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Extract executable commercial conditions'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Set commercial re-engagement triggers', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Execution carries the approved construct version and conditions to an accepting owner. Terms approval does not establish downstream delivery acceptance. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one approved commercial case, route-specific execution conditions, downstream owners and recipient acceptance or an explicit gap. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which approved commercial condition must the receiver execute? What transaction or delivery dependency remains open? How does another CE confirm acceptance and re-engagement triggers without claiming delivery completion?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or SME&C Commercial Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one commercial execution handoff: approved condition or unverified, transaction dependency, proposed receiver, acceptance gap and re-engagement trigger. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which condition or version mismatch would change readiness?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check an approved condition or version with the execution owner and seek acknowledgement or document the acceptance gap. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. Funding, terms, eligibility and approvals remain with authorized owners. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized condition clarified and whether it prevented wrong-construct execution or exposed a gap. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on making the Stage 4 plan buildable without turning DSE into the standing delivery owner.
keyTalkingPoints: The receiving owner depends on coverage and delivery route; DSE does not imply universal DCSA or partner involvement.
Current execution: Use the accepted technical decision, approved design repository, and current delivery/milestone route.
Fallback: Conduct a live handoff, record recipient acceptance, and retain an explicit gap if no owner is available.
System of record: Technical decision/design record for technical intent; receiving delivery or milestone system for execution.
Optional AI boundary: AI may format DSE-approved content but cannot invent configuration, assign ownership, or declare readiness.
discussionQuestions: Can the receiver build from the accepted design?
Which dependency is still unresolved?
What proves the technical handoff was accepted without transferring ongoing delivery to you?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Build the implementation decision packet'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Set re-entry and escalation boundaries', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Technical handoffs make dependencies, operating assumptions and re-entry conditions usable to the receiver. A plan is not accepted implementation work. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one accepted technical decision, approved design references, actual delivery route, known recipient and unresolved build dependencies. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Could the implementer act on this packet with the supplied evidence and constraints? Which receiving route and owner are confirmed? How does another DSE set re-entry boundaries without becoming indefinite delivery capacity?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one implementation decision packet: accepted technical intent or unknown, constraints, receiving route, owner gap and re-entry boundary. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which assumption needed receiver confirmation before use?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check the deciding delivery dependency or assumption with the receiving owner and seek acceptance or document the gap. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized handoff input clarified and whether it reduced delivery ambiguity. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on moving one applicable partner-led opportunity without mistaking partner silence for progress or failure.
keyTalkingPoints: Use only when a partner is actively co-selling, transacting, or expected to deliver; use the direct-account route otherwise.
Current execution: Reconcile MSX with current partner-reported status from Partner Center, Partner Timeline, or the named partner seller.
Fallback: If partner-system access is unavailable, obtain a dated partner confirmation and record it as partner-reported rather than Microsoft-verified.
System of record: MSX is the Microsoft opportunity and forecast record; Partner Center/Partner Timeline is the partner-side status source when accessible.
Optional AI boundary: An approved assistant may compare supplied evidence or draft the partner ask; it must not infer partner stage, update MSX, or disclose unapproved account data.
discussionQuestions: Which deal decision is stalled?
What partner status is actually confirmed?
Which next ask can move the deal without guessing stage or intent?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile Microsoft and partner deal evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Correct stage, close date, and risk', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Partner-led progress follows evidenced customer decisions and accepted actions, not unsupported stage or date changes. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one active partner-led opportunity, its MSX record, dated partner-reported status and the blocker or next decision. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which Microsoft and partner facts disagree about this deal? What next customer decision and co-sell ask follow from the verified evidence? How does a peer retain partner-reported status without treating it as Microsoft-verified forecast proof?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one co-sell reconciliation: dated Microsoft/partner facts, partner-reported status, contradiction, next decision and responsible record owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which partner signal failed to support the recorded deal state or next decision?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, inspect deciding deal evidence and ask the seller or record owner to confirm the next action or authorized correction. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized assumption corrected and whether it improved forecast discussion or the partner ask. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Identify changes that alter the plan
activities.description: Compare dated authorized portfolio snapshots to identify movement that may change account priority or intervention needs.
activities.prompt: Produce an unactivated, read-only proposal, not a running monitor. Use authorized dated snapshots, a user-maintained baseline and previous report supplied for this review; do not retrieve unsupplied records, create automation, retain agent memory or notify anyone. Missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no change. Record proposed scope, source permission, owner, cadence, recipients, review/expiry and approved change criteria without inventing values. Future monitoring requires separate explicit approval and verified access/state capabilities. Compare the supplied authorized assigned-account, opportunity, activity, usage, and support signals. If two comparable dated snapshots are supplied, return only new movement, materially growing or shrinking risk, resolved items, or changed evidence since the previous report, with source date and confidence. Exclude unchanged background risk and do not decide, assign, or write anything.
activities.expectedOutput: A portfolio-change table or baseline-only view with source dates, comparability limits, changed risks/evidence and questions for DAE; no inferred cause or running monitor.
activities.humanCheckpoint: DAE decides which movement is material.
activities.requiredContext: Assigned accounts, recent opportunity/activity changes, separately accessible usage/support evidence, and prior review. Supply approved dated snapshots, comparable definitions, user-maintained baseline/prior report if available, reviewer and actual approved change criteria. Missing scope, source permission, cadence, recipients, expiry/review date or future automation approval remains explicit; no persistent state or tool access is assumed.
activities.bestFitJob: Separate new movement from unchanged background risk.
activitySteps: 1. Supply approved dated snapshots for this activity, a user-maintained baseline and previous report if available.
2. Confirm scope, comparable definitions, evidence permission, access gaps and named human reviewer.
3. Compare only supplied state; missing history is baseline-only or comparison unavailable, not no progress.
4. Apply the existing HumanCheckpoint to interpret changes; proposed owners, actions and thresholds are not accepted decisions.
5. Keep an unactivated proposal with approval gaps; do not schedule, retain agent memory, send reports or change records.
Access/fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Compare supplied snapshots manually; no recurring job, retained agent memory or notification is required or authorized.
activities.whyThisMatters: Portfolio scale requires exception-based attention, but movement becomes useful only after the DAE assigns meaning and ownership.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on acting on the one portfolio change that materially alters the territory plan.
keyTalkingPoints: Use accessible signals only and route by actual coverage; DCSA leads applicable post-sale consumption work and partners may own delivery.

discussionQuestions: Which portfolio change materially alters the plan?
What source proves the movement?
Which role has actual coverage for the resulting action?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Identify changes that alter the plan'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Portfolio inspection focuses on material change and owned intervention. A new view matters only if it changes coverage, forecast or follow-through. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one dated territory exception, its source records, the current plan assumption and the actual covered or partner owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which portfolio change actually alters the coverage or growth plan? Which accountable role should carry the intervention? How does another DAE close the evidence loop before changing the forecast?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Account Executive absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.

A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which change warranted action rather than another status update?

If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized change and whether action became clearer or a weak hypothesis was rejected. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Agent
primaryAgents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.

Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.

EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings permitted sales data and supported record actions into the flow of work, including on mobile. Deal Agent can assemble renewal facts and Deal Books from supported source systems; verify freshness, completeness, and current scenario availability. Review each proposed MSX write and your authority before confirming it.

activities.name: Read demand in evidence order
activities.description: Combine the available evidence without allowing the loudest or most convenient source to determine priority.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the account, review the available installed-base and approved telemetry, contract or renewal events, direct customer and account-team evidence, partner evidence, and marketing engagement in that order. Return an account-outcome evidence card that labels what each item directly supports, only suggests, or leaves unknown, and identify the customer outcome that may warrant action or state that evidence is insufficient. Do not infer business value from usage or buying intent from engagement.
activities.expectedOutput: An account-outcome evidence card showing direct evidence, proxies, unknowns, timing, and whether action is warranted.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether the combined evidence warrants attention. Telemetry can show activity without value, a contract date can create timing without need, and marketing engagement can show curiosity without intent.
activities.requiredContext: One account; installed-base or telemetry evidence where available; contract or renewal timing; direct customer or team evidence; partner and marketing evidence where applicable. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Optional Sales Home access is only for enabled SME&C individual contributors; supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Gather only evidence you are authorized to use.
2. Order it by customer proximity rather than by tool.
3. Separate direct evidence, proxy evidence, and unknowns.
4. Name the customer outcome that may warrant action.
5. Record insufficient evidence rather than filling gaps with assumptions.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is an optional SME&C preview for enabled individual contributors, not Enterprise Sales Agent. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. Without access, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: A stable hierarchy makes the job solution-neutral while allowing each solution area to supply its own valid telemetry and contract events.

activities.name: Assign the action, owner, and route
activities.description: Turn warranted demand into a time-bound action owned by the DSS, account team, another specialist, or partner.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. From the supplied completed evidence card, coverage model, seller capacity, and timing event, recommend one route: DSS pursues; DSS and account owner pursue together; another solution specialist; partner acceptance; hold for named evidence; or close as not actionable. Return the proposed owner, acceptance requirement, due date, customer-safe next action, and rationale; do not treat routing as accepted until the recipient confirms.
activities.expectedOutput: A recorded action with route, accountable owner, acceptance requirement, due date, and rationale.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS owns the solution-area routing recommendation but cannot invent another person's capacity or acceptance. Closing or holding is valid only when the evidence and reason are explicit.
activities.requiredContext: A completed evidence card; actual account and partner coverage; seller capacity; relevant timing event.
activitySteps: 1. Check who currently owns the customer path.
2. Decide whether the DSS should lead, join, route, hold, or close.
3. For partner routing, name the acceptance needed.
4. Give the action a date tied to the customer event.
5. Record the reason and owner.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Demand dies when it is analyzed but not owned, or when a partner is named without accepting the work.

activities.name: Open the conversation without exposing internal signals
activities.description: Prepare a customer-safe opening grounded in the likely business situation rather than in how Microsoft detected it.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Draft a customer-safe opening for the account about the solution-area outcome, addressed to the intended recipient, for review by the accountable seller. Use only public or customer-provided context from the customer-safe context. Return the opening, open questions, assumptions to avoid, and the answer that would disconfirm active need. Do not expose internal telemetry, engagement tracking, scoring, propensity, or contract surveillance, and do not send or treat the draft as approved until the accountable seller confirms it.
activities.expectedOutput: A customer-safe opening, open questions, assumptions to avoid, and a clear disconfirming answer.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS and accountable seller decide what the customer hears. Internal telemetry and engagement data are not customer messaging, and a polished draft does not authorize outreach.
activities.requiredContext: The account, plausible customer outcome, customer-safe context, intended recipient, and accountable seller.
activitySteps: 1. Start from the recorded customer-safe next action.
2. Remove internal signal details from the input.
3. Turn assumptions into open questions.
4. Check that the opening would not reveal monitoring the customer did not expect.
5. Have the accountable seller approve the outreach.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Using a signal without exposing it preserves trust while still allowing timely discovery.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Demand rarely arrives as one perfect signal. Focus on combining the evidence the DSS can legitimately use and deciding where action is warranted.
keyTalkingPoints: Use an evidence hierarchy rather than a tool hierarchy: installed base and telemetry where available; contract and renewal events; direct customer and account-team evidence; partner evidence; then marketing engagement. No one source proves intent. A DSS decides the customer outcome, owner, and action. Tool availability and signal thresholds vary by solution area and geography.
discussionQuestions: Which evidence has preceded real pipeline in your solution area?
Which contract or usage event is easy to miss?
When is marketing engagement useful corroboration rather than the starting point?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Read demand in evidence order'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from evidence quality to the owner and action the DSS will record. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Open the conversation without exposing internal signals', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Solution-area demand needs credible account-outcome signals and actionable routing; marketing activity is not qualified demand. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one account with at least two forms of demand evidence. Remove customer-sensitive detail that should not be shared in the huddle.
facilitatorQuestions: What changed for the customer, and when?
Which evidence is direct and which is only a proxy?
What outcome and owner make this actionable?
What early signal has a peer used without confusing telemetry or marketing activity with demand?
listenFor: Marketing activity treated as intent, telemetry treated as value, contract events considered too late, local tool outputs treated as universal truth, and accounts prioritized without an owner or action date.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one demand evidence row: customer change/date, direct versus proxy signal, solution relevance, action owner and next validation. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which signal did you initially overweight, and what changed your judgment?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate a demand signal for a priority account-outcome pair and personally choose an evidenced next action or hold with its owner. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized signal reweighted and whether it improved prioritization or avoided a weak pursuit. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.name: Qualify, merge, route, or close the demand item
activities.description: Make the pipeline decision before creating or updating an opportunity.

If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the account, assess the supplied demand evidence card and current qualification criteria against related opportunities already recorded. Return a create, update, merge, route, hold, or close recommendation with supporting evidence, related-record disposition, and the single missing customer fact most likely to change it. Do not treat propensity, engagement, or installed base alone as qualification or write any record.
activities.expectedOutput: A qualification decision with supporting evidence, related-record disposition, and the single fact most likely to change it.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS makes the qualification decision. AI or propensity can organize evidence but cannot choose the stage, create customer commitment, or resolve contradictory account context.

activitySteps: 1. Search for related open opportunities.
2. Apply the current solution-area qualification criteria.
3. Separate customer gaps from internal gaps.
4. Decide create, update, merge, route, hold, or close.
5. Record the decisive evidence and missing fact.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is an optional SME&C preview for enabled individual contributors, not Enterprise Sales Agent. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. activities.whyThisMatters: Qualification before record creation reduces duplicate, speculative, and wrong-workload pipeline.

activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A demand item becomes pipeline only when somebody can execute from the record. This session moves from interest to a qualified and routed opportunity.
keyTalkingPoints: The DSS owns solution-area qualification and progression, not every account or commercial decision. Check for an existing opportunity before creating another. Route cross-solution needs explicitly. Stage and forecast are human judgments supported by evidence; CRM is the system of record even when planning begins elsewhere.
discussionQuestions: What evidence changes an account from target to qualified opportunity?
Where do duplicate or wrong-SKU opportunities begin?
What would another seller need to act from your record without calling you first?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Qualify, merge, route, or close the demand item'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the qualification decision to the exact CRM change and recipient handoff. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Route a multi-workload need without fragmenting the customer', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Qualified pipeline reflects customer evidence and owner-controlled disposition, not a new AI-generated opportunity or stage. Make that evidence check part of recurring work; share a safe example of what changed so peers can adapt the habit.
preparationChecklist: Bring one demand item and its current MSX or local CRM record, including any related opportunity.
facilitatorQuestions: Does this warrant a new opportunity, an update, a merge, or a route?
Which solution area should lead?
What evidence supports the stage and forecast treatment?
How would another DSS decide update, merge, route or close without creating a duplicate opportunity?
listenFor: Duplicate opportunities, propensity used as qualification, cross-SKU needs left ownerless, stale next steps, and stage or forecast chosen to satisfy cadence rather than evidence.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one demand disposition row: create/update/merge/route/close hypothesis, duplicate check, evidence, proposed stage and CRM owner. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Could another seller execute from this opportunity without asking you to translate it?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check a qualification gap and recommend advance, merge, route or close; reconcile the record only through an authorized owner. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized disposition and whether it reduced duplication or made the next action executable. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

preparationChecklist: Bring one live customer conversation, the known commitments, the intended outcome, and any stated decision criteria.
facilitatorQuestions: What has already been said or promised?
What customer outcome connects the stakeholders?
Which criteria will decide, and which might we concede?
Which discovery check has a peer used to expose a criterion Microsoft assumed but the customer did not?

facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which part of your original narrative was Microsoft language rather than customer language?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate a deciding customer criterion or commitment with the customer or account owner, then revise the relevant narrative point. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.

activities.name: Name the combined decision and preserve distinct owners
activities.description: Separate solution, technical, commercial, customer, and delivery decisions without pretending they progress independently.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS owns solution-area progression but cannot accept technical risk, make unauthorized concessions, or take over the customer relationship. Each accountable owner confirms their decision.
activities.requiredContext: One opportunity awaiting a customer decision; criteria map; current blockers; actual team and partner coverage.
activitySteps: 1. Start with the customer decision and date.
2. Name only dependencies that can change that decision.

4. Identify the critical dependency.
5. Confirm each owner's acceptance.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Combined progression works only when dependencies are connected and accountability is not blurred.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Support is not secured when an email is sent. It is secured when the route is eligible, accepted, owned, and moving through its required states.

What state proves that delivery is ready rather than merely requested?

activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether evidence supports another solution-area conversation. Usage alone does not authorize expansion, and an activation failure should not be relabeled as new pipeline.

activitySteps: 1. Start with customer evidence and priorities.
2. Distinguish an activation gap from a new opportunity.
3. Check existing opportunities and cross-solution ownership.
4. State a disconfirming fact for each hypothesis.
5. Validate one hypothesis before creating pipeline.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is an optional SME&C preview for enabled individual contributors, not Enterprise Sales Agent. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. activities.whyThisMatters: Evidence is most valuable when it improves the same customer's next decision without forcing an upsell.

activities.name: Build the renewal and contract-event action plan
activities.description: Connect contract timing, outcome evidence, risk, and solution-area expansion without taking over commercial renewal ownership.
activities.prompt: Use only authorized dated renewal, contract-event and outcome evidence I supply; do not assume CRM/calendar retrieval or persistent agent memory. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. For the agreement, use the supplied outcome and usage evidence, risks, owners, and current opportunities to prepare a renewal and expansion action plan with event date, transaction context, customer outcome, unresolved risk, bounded expansion hypothesis, distinct commercial and account owners, actions, and review date. Mark facts needing confirmation, make no construct or concession recommendation, and keep any recurrence as an unactivated proposal; future scheduling requires separate explicit approval of scope, sources, cadence, recipients, access and review/expiry.
activities.expectedOutput: A renewal and expansion action plan with timing, evidence, risks, distinct owners, and review date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS owns the solution-area evidence and expansion recommendation. The Commercial Executive or authorized commercial owner owns commercial construct, concessions, and negotiation; the account owner owns the customer path.
activities.requiredContext: Contract or renewal calendar event; agreement and transaction context; outcome and usage evidence; risks; owners; current opportunities.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the contract or renewal event and owner.
2. Assemble outcome, usage, risk, and open-opportunity evidence.
3. Separate solution expansion from commercial renewal decisions.
4. Assign actions and dates to accepted owners.
5. Set the next evidence review before the customer decision window.

Access/fallback: Scout is optional and preview/prerelease. Build the same dated action plan manually from supplied evidence; retaining a review date needs no scheduled job, connector or persistent agent memory. No scheduling, messages or record changes occur in this practice.
activities.whyThisMatters: Early calendar-driven action prevents renewal from becoming a late administrative event and keeps solution and commercial accountabilities clear.

activities.name: Reconcile the next opportunity, handoffs, CRM, and forecast
activities.description: Close the loop by making ownership and system state match the validated customer plan.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. Audit the opportunity against its validated next-opportunity or renewal plan. Return discrepancies and evidence-backed proposed changes for duplication, lead solution area, owner acceptance, stage, next customer action and date, partner or delivery handoff, amount or usage basis, renewal dependency, and forecast treatment, naming the authorized human for each; do not resolve or write changes autonomously.
activities.expectedOutput: A draft CRM/forecast reconciliation ledger with supported proposed changes, supplied acceptance status, next customer action, renewal dependency and re-entry signal; no record change.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS is accountable for solution-area pipeline accuracy. Account, commercial, and forecast owners approve their respective decisions; an AI audit may find inconsistencies but cannot resolve them autonomously.
activities.requiredContext: Validated next-opportunity or renewal plan; current CRM and forecast; accepted owner and partner handoffs. Supply authorized dated account/opportunity and required agreement, partner, usage, support or policy extracts. Optional Sales Home access is only for enabled SME&C individual contributors; supplied evidence and manual review suffice. No Deal Agent/renewal integration is assumed.
activitySteps: 1. Compare the validated plan with the current record.
2. Propose create, update, merge or close only with supplied evidence; authorized owners decide and no source record changes in this practice.
3. Confirm every handoff was accepted.
4. Reconcile stage and forecast with authorized owners.
5. Record the next review and re-entry signal.

Access/fallback: Sales Home is an optional SME&C preview for enabled individual contributors, not Enterprise Sales Agent. Use authorized dated account/opportunity extracts; required agreement, usage, support, partner-program, pricing or policy detail must be supplied by its authorized owner. No Deal Agent/renewal roadmap integration is assumed. Without access, review the same supplied evidence manually or in one already authorized general assistant.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expansion is operational only when owners accept it and CRM and forecast tell the same evidence-backed story.

activities.name: Build an approved proof point after serving the same account
activities.description: Turn one evidenced outcome into a reusable proof point only after the customer's next action and ownership are secure.
activities.prompt: Use only the authorized dated materials I supply for this bounded practice; do not retrieve unsupplied CRM, agreement, mailbox, telemetry, support or partner-portal records. If one essential detail is missing, ask one concise question. From the supplied verified outcome, evidence source, delivery ownership, and permission requirements, draft an anonymized proof point covering situation, action, evidenced measure, time frame, material context, and limits. Remove identifying detail and unsupported causation, list required account-owner, customer, delivery-owner, and partner approvals, and label the draft unapproved.
activities.expectedOutput: An anonymized, bounded proof-point draft with evidence citation, limitations, and approval state.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DSS decides whether the claim is useful and supportable. The customer and relevant delivery or partner owners control permission; anonymization is not permission and correlation is not causation.
activities.requiredContext: Verified customer outcome; evidence source; delivery owner; customer, account-owner, and partner permission requirements.
activitySteps: 1. Confirm the outcome and evidence owner.
2. Prioritize the same customer's next action before external reuse.
3. Draft only the evidenced claim and necessary context.
4. Test whether the customer could recognize themselves.
5. Obtain every required approval before reuse.

Access/fallback: Use the named assistant only if already available and authorized for these supplied materials; otherwise prepare the same bounded output manually. No second tool, connector or private-system access is required.
activities.whyThisMatters: Reusable evidence builds credibility only when it is accurate, bounded, and authorized by everyone whose work or data it represents.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The strongest evidence should first improve the same customer's next decision. Renewal, expansion, and reusable proof follow from that evidence and the contract calendar.
keyTalkingPoints: Use evidence to test a same-account next opportunity rather than force one. Keep renewal ownership distinct from solution-area expansion and commercial ownership. Reconcile CRM, stage, forecast, next step, and handoffs before closing the loop. External proof requires customer, account-owner, and where applicable partner permission.
discussionQuestions: What next customer problem does the evidence genuinely support?
Which contract event creates urgency?
Which record or handoff would currently surprise the next owner?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Select the same-account next opportunity from evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Move from the expansion or renewal hypothesis to the accepted handoff and reconciled system-of-record state. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Build the renewal and contract-event action plan', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Renewal and expansion follow verified outcomes and contract timing, with records, forecast and accepted handoffs reflecting the human plan. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one evidenced outcome or one contract or renewal event within your operating horizon, plus its current opportunity and forecast state.
facilitatorQuestions: What next customer problem does the evidence support?
What contract or renewal event affects timing?
Who owns solution expansion, customer path, commercial renewal, and delivery?
What must change in CRM and forecast?
What evidence has a peer used to decide that same-account expansion is not yet supported?
listenFor: Expansion inferred from usage alone, a reusable case study prioritized before same-account value, renewal ownership blurred, handoffs sent but not accepted, and forecast state inconsistent with the customer action.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one next-opportunity hypothesis: same-account evidence, unsupported assumption, renewal event, accountable role and CRM/forecast reconciliation question. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Did the evidence support expansion, or were you trying to make it support expansion?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate an expansion or renewal hypothesis and agree the next evidence check; authorized humans control CRM or forecast changes. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized hypothesis revised, retained or rejected and whether it made the plan more realistic. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on converting technical work into a decision rather than another technical conversation.
keyTalkingPoints: Use relayed communication only when direct customer access is unavailable; preserve qualifications and identify the person authorized to accept.
Current execution: Use the technical decision record, customer review, and accepted evidence.
Fallback: Run a live decision review and capture explicit acceptance when no workflow exists.
System of record: The technical decision record is authoritative for the recommendation and acceptance.
Optional AI boundary: An approved assistant may format DSE-authored conclusions; it must not soften qualifications or mark acceptance.
discussionQuestions: Does the evidence meet the agreed criterion?
What qualification must travel with the recommendation?
Who is authorized to accept the technical decision?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Evaluate every agreed criterion'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Record acceptance and relay-safe summary', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Technical closure preserves criterion results, alternatives and residual risk. Sign-off exists only after actual authorized acceptance. Treat the next use as a small test of better work; share the benefit or correction, not just the draft.
preparationChecklist: Bring one technical criterion, approved proof/architecture results, recommendation qualifications and the accepting customer or delivery owner. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which agreed criterion is supported, contradicted or still untested? What residual risk limits the recommendation? How would a peer communicate a technical hold without claiming customer acceptance?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Solution Engineer absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one technical criterion review: agreed criterion, supported/contradicted/untested evidence, residual risk, conditional recommendation and acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which result or residual risk changed proceed, revise or hold?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review a deciding criterion or risk with the technical owner and record their actual proceed, revise or hold; sign-off is not an exercise quota. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized decision clarification and whether it improved confidence or made the hold explicit. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

activities.description: Confirm whether the intervention restored the intended path.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on acting on one risk while it is still an intervention rather than an escalation.
keyTalkingPoints: Only covered/material accounts qualify; product incidents route to support/CxE, material design changes to DSE, and commercial issues to DAE/CE.
Current execution: Use accessible telemetry, milestone, deployment, and support evidence plus direct customer/partner input.
Fallback: Run a hypothesis review and customer/operator conversation; escalate when evidence or access is insufficient.
System of record: Committed-milestone/consumption record for intervention; support and technical systems retain their own findings.
Optional AI boundary: Researcher may check current technical documentation; DCSA validates customer applicability and owns the intervention decision.
discussionQuestions: What evidence distinguishes a cause from a symptom?
Which intervention can you own within coverage?
What issue must route to support, technical or commercial owners?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Validate the blocker hypothesis'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Close the customer loop and test movement', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Blocker diagnosis needs evidence and an owner able to act. Apparent cost stays a hypothesis until checked. Frontier Accelerator grows through repeated use and shared learning, not a polished artifact. Carry this judgment into the next work cycle.
preparationChecklist: Bring one covered milestone/adoption risk, dated telemetry/support evidence, the current plan and the unresolved cause or escalation question. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which blocker hypothesis explains the highest-cost delay, and what would disprove it? What smallest intervention has a willing owner? How does a peer test movement with the customer or operator without overpromising recovery?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Digital Cloud Solution Architect absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one blocker hypothesis card: observed delay, competing cause, disconfirming evidence, smallest intervention, proposed owner and movement check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which cause changed after checking customer or partner evidence, and who can act?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate a material blocker cause and agree bounded intervention or evidence check with its accountable owner. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share an anonymized diagnosis corrected and whether it focused intervention or prevented misdirected work. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.
