facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on turning partner cadence into a deal decision rather than a status meeting.
keyTalkingPoints: Use for a selected material partner deal; routine cadence without a decision remains outside this practice.
Current execution: Use reconciled pipeline evidence, partner input, and named DAE/DSS/DSE/CE/PDM/PSA/program owners as applicable.
Fallback: Run a short live clinic and manually record decision/acceptance if no shared workflow exists.
System of record: MSX for Microsoft opportunity actions; Partner Center/partner record for partner actions; authoritative systems for specialist decisions.
Optional AI boundary: Agent J.ai may help rehearse the partner conversation where available; it cannot identify the true blocker or assign ownership.
discussionQuestions: What decision would unblock this deal?
Which role can actually make it?
What acceptance or next evidence will show the clinic produced more than status?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Select the blocker worth clinic time'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Test whether the deal moved', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Deal clinics resolve specific evidenced blockers through reciprocal accepted actions, not broader action-register production. Keep the useful step in your normal rhythm and bring a permission-safe lesson back for the team to improve together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one stalled partner deal, reconciled pipeline evidence, partner comments, the blocked decision and known specialist/program owners. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Which single partner-deal blocker is worth clinic time? Who can decide it and what evidence do they need? How does a peer distinguish an accepted action from a discussion that changed nothing?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Partner Solution Sales absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one clinic decision card: single blocker, decision evidence, accountable role, proposed action, acceptance gap and next movement check. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What changed when partner and Microsoft actions were made explicit?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, review the deciding partner-deal gap and seek owner acceptance of a bounded action or explicit hold. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized blocker clarified and whether it improved reciprocal follow-through. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Focus on changing partner behavior using evidence and the partner's stated priorities, not invented economics.
keyTalkingPoints: Use for selected partners in PSS scope; do not present PSS as the sole Microsoft route to post-sale outcomes.
Current execution: Use MSX, Partner Center/Timeline, program records, partner-reported outcomes, and current joint plan.
Fallback: Build a dated review from the available sources and label partner-reported versus Microsoft-observed evidence.
System of record: Each system remains authoritative for its own record; accepted actions return to MSX/Partner Center/joint plan as applicable.
Optional AI boundary: Know Your Partner may assemble permitted context. PSS must not invent margin, capacity, or customer outcomes.
discussionQuestions: What partner behavior should change and why?
Which outcome is observed versus partner-reported?
What accepted action supports the stated partner priorities?
suggestedTransitions: A suggested starting point is 'Reconcile plan, pipeline, program, and delivery evidence'. Other Featured practices can be used as alternatives rather than additional live steps. Inspect one decision-changing evidence gap in the selected artifact, then compare a peer's approach and name the accountable next action. Drafts do not prove acceptance, approval or a completed system update. Optional Extended follow-up: 'Agree the next loop and expansion route', only if its prerequisites and role applicability are met; it is outside the live one-practice slot.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Partner review compares source-attributed outcomes with plan and forecast, then tests expansion rather than equating activity with value. Agree where this fits in recurring work and how a small, safe signal will help the team learn together.
preparationChecklist: Bring one partner review, approved joint-plan priorities, dated pipeline/outcome evidence and the prior accepted actions. Label source, scope and date; record access or evidence gaps. Use only approved material and tools.
facilitatorQuestions: Where do plan, pipeline, program and delivery sources disagree? What partner priority should the review resolve? How does another PSS record the next reciprocal action without inventing agreement or taking the broader partner strategy?
listenFor: Work starting without the stated trigger, partner involvement treated as universal, an unaccepted owner presented as coverage, AI output presented as system evidence, or Partner Solution Sales absorbing a decision outside this role boundary.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the selected tool, system or approved context is inaccessible, use a sanitized supplied example; if none is available, use a clearly labeled synthetic case. Work on paper to build one partner-review exception: plan/pipeline/program/delivery evidence, source conflict, partner priority, reciprocal next action and owner acceptance gap. Separate evidence, assumptions and unknowns. A synthetic case rehearses the method only; it cannot establish live status, eligibility, agreement or approval. Record the source/access gap and who must validate it before real use. Keep commercial, funding, staffing and publication authority with the authorized humans; a proposed owner is not an accepted assignment.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which variance changed the partner action or expansion hypothesis?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, validate a material variance with its source owner and agree your own follow-up plus separately accepted partner action; expansion may stay on hold. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot only for permitted drafting or analysis; otherwise review manually. Humans validate sources, accept work and control record changes or messages. If inputs are unavailable, use a sanitized example and name the gap.
bringBackEvidence: Share a sanitized variance checked and whether it improved the review or next action. A brief, anonymized verbal summary is enough; keep restricted details in approved systems. If blocked or untested, share the gap and next check.

agents.ShortDescription: Agentic Microsoft 365 experience for longer-running, outcome-focused, multi-source work.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Plans and executes multistep work, invokes skills, and creates deliverables with checkpoints.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you want to hand off a multi-step piece of work and review it rather than do it. Complex tasks spanning Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 data, documents, presentations and recommendations, where it plans the work, runs the steps and checks in before it finishes.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid for a quick single answer when Copilot or a specialized agent is sufficient, and for work that should keep running on a schedule after you stop asking, which is Scout.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select Cowork beside Chat. Describe the outcome you want rather than a single question, then review the work at each checkpoint it presents.
agents.KeyBenefits: Executes multi-step work across Microsoft 365 instead of answering one question at a time. Built for delegation: it plans, invokes skills, works across data sources, and produces deliverables with review checkpoints.

agents.Name: Scout
agents.ShortDescription: Always-on agent that runs on your desktop. You set it up once and leave it running: it works to a schedule without being asked, remembers what it saw last time, and can reach work that sits outside Microsoft 365.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Recurring checks, follow-up nudges and work that reaches outside Microsoft 365. Watch a book of accounts for movement between reviews, catch commitments going quiet, notice a signal approaching its expiry, and carry what it found last week into this week rather than starting from nothing.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When the work should keep running after you stop asking. Set it up and leave it running for anything recurring, anything that needs watching between reviews, and anything that reaches outside Microsoft 365. The test is whether you want an answer now or want to be told when something changes.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for a quick single answer that Copilot would handle in the app you are already in, and do not use it for a multi-step task you want done once and handed back, which is Cowork. It sees the same Microsoft 365 content under the same permissions as the others, so reaching for it does not get you more access. Do not use it to bypass a human checkpoint because it can run unattended; anything it produces while running on its own still needs the same review.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Go to aka.ms/m, the internal Scout hub. Request the access package, complete the agreement, download and install Scout, then sign in with Microsoft 365 and GitHub as instructed. Start with a business outcome rather than a tool command.
agents.KeyBenefits: Keeps work moving between sessions rather than inside one chat. Monitors signals, coordinates follow-through, and prepares materials within organizational controls.

Researcher is also reachable inside Sales Agent, which uses it to answer research questions; call Researcher directly when you want the full sourced report rather than an answer inside a sales conversation.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid for quick summaries or lightweight drafting.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Researcher agent, then state the research question and sources.
agents.KeyBenefits: Produces source-cited research reports rather than unattributed summaries, combining work content and web research across multiple steps so claims can be traced.

agents.Name: Analyst
agents.ShortDescription: Data-analysis agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot for statistics, trends, outliers, charts, and reports.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Analyzes supplied data and produces understandable findings and visuals.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Multi-file quantitative analysis, trend analysis, and executive-ready data insights.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Avoid when authoritative operational reporting must come directly from a certified business system.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and select the Analyst agent, then attach the data you want analyzed.
agents.KeyBenefits: Turns supplied data into findings and visuals a non-analyst can act on, including trends, outliers, and executive-ready charts, without building the analysis by hand.

agents.Name: MSXI Assist V2
agents.ShortDescription: Assistance within MSXI for certified-report analysis, report discovery, KPI definitions and supported report actions.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Analyze certified MSXI data to investigate performance, pipeline or consumption signals; find relevant reports, understand KPI definitions and take supported report actions.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you need to analyze an enabled certified MSXI report, investigate its signals, find the right report or understand a metric before deciding what action to take.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: MSXI Assist V2 and the experience formerly called MSXI Copilot are the same Copilot experience inside MSXI, not two tools or a pending product merge. Proactive Insights is distinct: use its lightbulb entry point to subscribe to topic or report summaries; use the Assist robot entry point for questions and certified-report analysis. Do not imply that Assist retrieves information outside authorized MSXI data or is a general analytics tool for arbitrary datasets. Point participants to the experience the activity actually names.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens the MSXI home page. For the Assist copilot, select the robot icon in the top ribbon (tooltip "MSXI Assist") to open the sidecar. For Proactive Insights, select the light bulb icon on the same page, then choose a topic, detail level and sending preference to subscribe to emailed snapshots. No enrollment is required.
agents.KeyBenefits: Combines certified-report analysis with natural-language report discovery and KPI explanations, helping users investigate signals, inspect source evidence, apply supported report actions and identify where further validation is needed.

agents.Name: Agent J.ai
agents.ShortDescription: Text-based coaching experience grounded in Microsoft 365 context and curated content.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Helps users sharpen messages, rehearse conversations, anticipate objections, and plan next steps.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Customer conversation preparation and role-play, or de-identified rehearsal of a manager coaching conversation about business judgment where access and scenario support are confirmed. Do not use employee or HR data for rehearsal.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as the authoritative source for CRM or commercial data.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Agent J.ai in Microsoft 365 Copilot, then describe the conversation you want to rehearse and who you will be speaking to. For manager coaching rehearsal, use a de-identified scenario and review the suggested questions yourself. Related Manager Empowerment guidance: https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/MCAPSAcademy/SitePages/MCAPS-Manager-Empowerment.aspx
agents.KeyBenefits: Rehearsal before the real conversation. Sharpens messages, surfaces objections you had not anticipated, and coaches on clarity and next step, grounded in Microsoft 365 context and curated content.

agents.Name: Auto-Fix Pipeline Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Agent in MSX intended to resolve supported pipeline hygiene issues.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supports targeted pipeline cleanup inside MSX.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When a Practice explicitly addresses supported pipeline hygiene correction.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not generalize beyond supported issues.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens MSX. Auto-Fix has no standalone URL. Inside MSX, open the Pipeline Hygiene workspace and select Auto-Fixes, then choose which automated fixes to enable and review, accept or revert each change after it is applied.
agents.KeyBenefits: One-click cleanup for supported pipeline hygiene violations, with review and revert available so the seller stays in control of what changes.

agents.Name: MSXI Copilot
agents.ShortDescription: Copilot experience in MSXI reports for interpreting enabled business data.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Interpret enabled business metrics, report views, and signals in context.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Use when the job starts from an enabled MSXI report or certified business signal.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as a replacement for human interpretation of KPI scope, report filters, or customer context. MSXI Assist V2 and the experience also called MSXI Copilot are the same Copilot experience inside MSXI, not separate tools or a pending product merge. These two identifiers remain for model continuity; guide participants to the named MSXI experience and verify report availability.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open an AI-certified MSXI report and use the embedded Copilot panel to ask questions about the metrics and trends in front of you. Availability varies by report.
agents.KeyBenefits: Answers questions against certified report data without leaving the report. Explains what a metric means in the context of the filters and view currently applied.

agents.Name: Customer Success Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Teams-based customer success experience referenced in Customer Health Success Program dispatch guidance.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supports Success Program dispatch and customer-success workflow steps where available.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Customer Health Success Program dispatch or customer-success process steps that are explicitly supported.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use as authority for policy, delivery commitments or customer-facing claims.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens the Customer Success Agent app details page in Teams. Install the app once and it stays in your Teams rail, then follow the supported Customer Health Success Program dispatch workflow.
agents.KeyBenefits: Connects Customer Health Success Program execution to CSAM workflow steps in Teams, so dispatch and follow-through happen where the team already works.

agents.Name: MSX Deal Assistance
agents.ShortDescription: The investment request front door inside MSX. Consolidates ECIF, ACO, Azure Access, and Solution Assessment requests that were previously spread across separate tools.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Create, submit, and track investment requests against an opportunity, with ROI calculation and opportunity data prepopulated rather than retyped.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When an investment request needs to be created or submitted, or when you need the current status of one you already submitted.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for building the workscope itself, which happens in ECIF Central, and not for policy or eligibility judgments, which stay with the accountable owner.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open an MSX opportunity, go to the Deal Assistance tab, select New Request, then choose the request type such as ECIF, ACO, or Azure Access.
agents.KeyBenefits: One front door instead of several legacy request tools. Opportunity data and ROI calculation carry over, so the request starts mostly complete.

agents.Name: ECIF Central
agents.ShortDescription: Where the workscope is built and where delivery actually runs, including supplier collaboration, milestones, and change requests.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Create a workscope against an opportunity, add suppliers and scope detail, calculate the spend plan, and track execution and milestones once funding is approved.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you need to build or revise a workscope, onboard or work with a supplier, or check delivery progress and milestones.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not the submission point. The completed workscope is submitted through MSX Deal Assistance.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open ECIF Central, create a workscope using the MSX Opportunity ID, add suppliers and scope detail, calculate the spend plan, then generate the completed workscope for submission. Suppliers collaborate through partner.ecifcentral.microsoft.com.
agents.KeyBenefits: Keeps workscope, supplier collaboration, and delivery tracking in one place instead of email threads and spreadsheets.

agents.Name: Investment Tracker
agents.ShortDescription: The status view inside MSX Deal Assistance showing where a request sits, who holds it, and what is blocking it. Sometimes called the Pizza Tracker.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: See request stage, current owner, blockers, and recommended next steps without asking someone for a status update.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When a submitted request has gone quiet and you need to know where it is and who holds it.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not a substitute for contacting the owner when a request is genuinely stuck. It shows status, not urgency.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens MSX Deal Assistance. The Investment Tracker is a view inside it rather than a separate site: open your submitted request and read the tracker view for stage, ownership and blockers. FY27 material describes proactive at-risk alerts; confirm current availability with the ECIF program team.
agents.KeyBenefits: Replaces the status-chasing email with a view. Makes ownership visible so the next action has a name attached.

agents.Name: Azure Offer Navigator
agents.ShortDescription: The front door for Azure investment offers, including Azure Accelerate, with eligibility guidance and nomination support.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Find which Azure offers an opportunity is eligible for, choose the right one, submit the nomination, and track its status.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When the investment is Azure-specific and you need to identify and request the right offer.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for non-Azure ECIF requests, which go through MSX Deal Assistance.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open the Navigator, enter the MSX Opportunity ID, review the eligible offers it returns, select the appropriate one, and submit through the Navigator workflow.
agents.KeyBenefits: One place to see what an opportunity actually qualifies for, with recommendations and next-best-action guidance rather than reading offer documentation.

agents.Name: MCAPS Help for ECIF
agents.ShortDescription: Support, guidance, and ticketing for ECIF and investment process questions.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Get help when a request is blocked, access is missing, or the process itself is unclear, and raise a case when self-help does not resolve it.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When you are blocked on process, access, or tooling rather than on a business decision.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not for eligibility, policy, or funding decisions, which belong to the accountable owners rather than support.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open MCAPS Help for ECIF, search the guidance first, and raise a case if the answer is not there. Have the opportunity ID and request ID ready.
agents.KeyBenefits: A defined path for process and access problems, so a blocked request does not sit waiting on an informal ask.

agents.Name: Consumption Manager
agents.ShortDescription: Consumption plan information used inside Global ECIF and ACO request flows.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Supply and review the consumption plan detail that a Global ECIF or ACO request requires.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When submitting a Global ECIF or ACO request that needs consumption plan information.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Not a standalone consumption reporting tool. For consumption trends and ACR, use Sales Agent or MSXI.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens ECIF Central. Consumption Manager is not opened directly - it is reached from inside the Global ECIF and ACO request flow as part of a submission. Confirm current behavior with the ECIF program team.
agents.KeyBenefits: Keeps consumption planning attached to the investment request rather than tracked separately.

agents.Name: Sales Home
agents.ShortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
agents.WhatItIs: SME&C Seller surface within Sales Agent
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Sales Home is in preview for SME&C sellers who use MSX, and is enabled for individual contributors only - managers will not see it. Renewal, Campaign, Planning, Realization and Deal Agent integration are roadmap, not available today, so do not build an activity that depends on them.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens Sales Agent. Sales Home is the seller surface inside it - My View for alerts and quota attainment, Prospecting for signals, account research, contacts and outreach, and Pipeline for opportunities, forecast comments, close plans and deal risks. It is not a separate product and has no separate link.
agents.KeyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

agents.Name: Know Your Partner
agents.ShortDescription: SME&C partner briefing agent. Assembles partner performance from Partner IAP (ACR, CSP, Copilot seats, net new revenue) and program utilization from Activities Utilization ROB (Azure, Copilot and Security Accelerate), then adds web-sourced partner news and situational fluency. Type a partner name or PartnerOne ID; name several to compare. States placeholders rather than inventing missing data.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Prepare or compare partner briefings using permitted partner-performance and program-utilization data, with partner news kept distinct from operational evidence.
agents.WhenToUseIt: Before a partner planning conversation, deal clinic, readiness discussion, or performance review when permitted partner context is needed. Enter a partner name or PartnerOne ID; compare named partners only where access and comparable data support it.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat a briefing as proof of current staffing, delivery capacity, customer intent, partner economics, eligibility, or approval. Verify dates, scope, and source differences; retain missing-data placeholders rather than inventing facts. Do not bypass partner-data sharing or role-access rules.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Opens the Know Your Partner app details page in Teams via the owner-maintained alias. Install the app once and it stays in your Teams rail.
agents.KeyBenefits: Reduces partner-context gathering for a preparation or review conversation, making available performance and program signals easier to compare while preserving evidence gaps for human follow-up.

agents.Name: GitHub Copilot
agents.ShortDescription: AI coding assistant available in an IDE, GitHub Copilot CLI, and the GitHub Copilot app. Repository or working-folder context supports code and configuration work rather than acting as a CRM source of record.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Write, explain, refactor and test code; scaffold infrastructure-as-code and deployment artifacts; build the smallest spike that proves or disproves an architecture assumption; generate sample data and validation scripts; and reproduce a reported failure so you can see it rather than describe it.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When the next step is to build something rather than to plan or describe it. Validating an architecture assumption with a spike, standing up a demo or workshop environment, iterating a proof of concept, reproducing a deployment or integration failure, or packaging a reusable asset with tests and setup steps.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not use it for customer, market or account research; that is Researcher. Do not use it to assemble a customer-facing document or deck; that is Cowork. Do not point it at production without the review your team already requires, and do not paste customer data into it. It works on code and configuration, not on the CRM record.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Choose the Copilot extension in your IDE, GitHub Copilot CLI for terminal work, or the GitHub Copilot app for coordinating agent-driven development. Open or select the relevant repository or working folder so the task has context. Start with: Explain what this deployment does, then write the smallest test that would prove the assumption I am least sure about. Review proposed commands and edits, run the relevant tests, and follow your approved environment and data-handling rules.
agents.KeyBenefits: Creates reviewable code and test evidence to validate an architecture assumption or reproduce a failure, giving technical and account teams a more concrete basis for the next decision. Human review and testing remain required.

agents.Name: Deal Agent
agents.ShortDescription: Deal Agent is surfaced through Sales Agent. It is not a standalone agent to install or select; it triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.WhatItHelpsYouDo: Support enterprise renewals and deal work: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions. Retrieve agreement, enrollment, license-estate, and consumption context through Sales Agent.
agents.WhenToUseIt: For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
agents.StepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot and use the agent picker to select Sales. Start a new chat with a renewal or deal question, such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically; there is nothing separate to install or select. Lead with a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number, keep one chat thread per deal, and review returned facts and proposed actions before using them.
agents.KeyBenefits: Brings deal facts, renewal context, Deal Books, and proposal work into the Sales Agent conversation instead of gathering them across separate portals. Keeps the capability visible while retaining one entry point and human review of commercial decisions.
agents.AccessLinkLabel: Open Sales Agent for Deal Agent

agents.Name: Frontier Accelerator App
agents.ShortDescription: App used by designated Frontier activities.
agents.WhatItIs: An operational system and access destination, not an AI agent.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When an activity directs you to open the app, including Week 9 reflection and next-focus activities.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not select it as an AI agent or for activities that do not direct you to the app.

agents.Name: Team Member Impact Survey
agents.ShortDescription: Survey used by designated Team Member Impact Survey activities.
agents.WhatItIs: An operational survey and access destination, not an AI agent.
agents.WhenToUseIt: When an activity directs you to open the survey, including Close and complete the Team Member Impact Survey.
agents.WhenNotToUseIt: Do not select it as an AI agent or for activities that do not direct you to the survey.
